THE FIRST ROUND WITH A POOL, AND WHY NO SAT STILL MOVED (2026-09-21, round `b35f6e48607102f5`).

Two players, two browsers so neither renderer is throttled, both on the same paid round, both stakes 98000
msat HELD. One driven to the gate, one rolled out and left alone. Both seats agree, word for word:

  b9aad72c  DELIVERED / score 174   hold CANCELLED   <- handed back by the committee, not by a timeout
  e7b78420  FAILED / 0              hold SETTLE_REQUESTED

That CANCELLED is the first hold on the Daily ever resolved by a decision: `[custody] b9aad72c CANCEL ->
CANCELLED: handed back to its owner`. §23.2 gives a delivered player their own stake back, so it is right.

The loser's stake is the pool, and it did not get there:

  [verify] lncli settleinvoice refused: invoice already canceled

WHY, READ OFF THE INVOICE'S OWN HTLC RECORD rather than inferred:

  accept_height    93748
  expiry_height    93895          (the 144 blocks this node now asks for, plus 3 of route)
  resolve_time     1789977656     = 08:00:56, and the chain was at height 93878 then
  state            CANCELED

**lnd gave up 17 blocks before the expiry it was asked for, having held the HTLC for 130 of its 147.** The
chain never reached 93895 - that block was mined at 08:03:29, two and a half minutes later. There is no
`IRPC: Canceled invoice` line for this hash either, so it was not this node asking; the winner's hash
(410ed05a) has one, which is §23.2 handing that stake back, and the preimage this node offered for the
loser hashes to the loser's own payment hash, so it was the right preimage on the right invoice.

The whole race, measured from the moment Lightning accepted the HTLC:

  accepted                        07:48:46 (height 93748)
  round closed                    07:52:22
  lnd gave up                     08:00:56 (height 93878) - 730 s of usable hold
  the objection window closed     08:02:38 - 830 s after acceptance

**730 s of hold against 830 s of round. Short by 100 s.** So the budget a door-side check must use is not
the 144 blocks the contract names: it is 144 less lnd's own safety margin, measured at 17 blocks here, and
it is counted from acceptance, not from the round opening.

  payouts 0, payout_signatures 0    - no payout table formed, so no sat moved between the two players

AND A LOOSE END WORTH ITS OWN LINE: both seats still hold that entry at **SETTLE_REQUESTED**, "about to
settle; if this node dies here, ask Lightning", while lnd says CANCELED. `custody.reconcile()` runs only at
startup (`server.js:1539`) - it is built for a daemon that stopped, not for a call that came back refused -
and `settleHeldInvoices` will not touch a MID_ACT state ("reconcile it against Lightning first"). So a
settle lnd refuses on a live node leaves an intent nothing clears until the next restart, even though lnd
answered in plain words what happened.

AND THE TWO CLOCKS ARE WITHIN 4% OF EACH OTHER, which is why it is not always the same answer. Read on the
live rounds (scratchpad `fits.mjs`, read-only), one line per quantity the node would need at its own door:

  the chain           200 blocks in 1124 s = 0.178 blocks/s
  a hold of 144       lives 809 s
  the run             10800 ticks = 180 s at the core's 60 a second
  the objection window 600 s (the contract's own `objectionWindowMs`, §13A's reference 10 minutes)
  nothing settles before 780 s                    -> FITS by 29 s at that rate

At the 0.200 blocks/s measured an hour earlier the same arithmetic gives 720 s against 780 - SHORT by 60 -
and the DELIVERED run lost by a measured 90 s. So the margin is a few percent of the requirement and the
outcome flips with the block rate. Whatever is ruled, a rehearsal this close to its own limit will keep
producing both answers.

THE START WINDOW NOW OPENS AT THE TICK THE PLAYER HAD REACHED WHEN THE STAKE WAS HELD (2026-09-21).

This replaces the version committed earlier in this letter, which converted `stake_seen.seen_ms` with
`ticksForMs` against `startTimeMs` - a wall-derived "round tick" that the measurement showed is not a
protocol quantity at all. The origin is now in the ONE clock the protocol uses: the player's own run ticks,
the same stream the batches and the marks are numbered in.

  new table `stake_seen_tick (entry_id, tick, seen_ms)` - the house idiom, "a table of its own so a store
  written before it existed gains it", beside `stake_seen` and `hold_expiry`.

  `putStakeSeen` writes it in the same breath, once: the highest tick this node has ALREADY RECEIVED from
  that player, read off the last stored batch. Not a number the client asserts - a player cannot name a late
  origin to buy itself an unbounded window - and pinned by the same replay as every other tick.

  `startWindowOrigin` returns that tick; an entry with no such row keeps `joinTick`, word for word, which is
  what a free round and an entry that never played get.

  a player who has sent nothing when the hold appears gets 0, which is where its run starts anyway.

CORRECTION: THERE ARE NOT TWO CLOCKS. THE MARK AND joinTick ARE THE SAME CLOCK (2026-09-21).

Read out of the seat's own store, for the paid entry 6742d644:

    batches 602, covering ticks 0 .. 10799      (the whole 10800-tick block)
    first batch: seq 0, firstTick 0, previousHash GENESIS
    the first mark's tick, 5220 -> INSIDE the submitted inputs
    the busiest entry in the store: 2048 batches, its first firstTick also 0

So the player's transcript is numbered from 0 for the entry, the marks are numbered in that same stream -
`replay.js` matches marks to replayed inputs BY TICK, and runs do settle, which they could not if the two
were different clocks - and `joinTick 0` is therefore CORRECT. It is tick 0 of the player's own run.

WHAT I GOT WRONG, AND IT RAN FOR SEVERAL LETTERS. I compared the mark's tick against a ROUND tick I derived
myself from wall time (`(now - startTimeMs) * 60/1000`). Nothing in the protocol computes that number. From
that bad comparison came "the mark carries core tick 5220 while the round is at 4891", the "2257-tick offset
spread", "no node can convert", "the carrier cannot be a bare tick", and the shares 88/7.6/4.4. The
subtraction on both sides of §13B was always in one clock; the mismatch was mine.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE, and it is simpler: the player played 5220 ticks OF ITS OWN RUN before planting a first
mark, and the rule asks for one inside 900. The run starts at tick 0 when the session opens, and the entry
then waits about 87 s for the stake to be paid while its own run is already counting. By the time the client
will sign anything, 5220 of its ticks are gone.

SO THE ORIGINAL RULING NEEDS NO NEW CLOCK, NO NEW FIELD AND NO CLIENT ASSERTION. The origin should be the RUN
tick at which the stake was seen HELD, and the node can have that without trusting anybody: it is the highest
tick the node has already received from that player when Lightning shows the hold - node-observed, and pinned
by the same replay that pins every other tick. `stake_seen` is already written at that moment; what it does
not record is the tick, and that is a one-column question rather than a protocol one.

Nothing was built on this turn. The origin move committed earlier reads `stake_seen.seen_ms` and converts it
with `ticksForMs` against `startTimeMs` - that conversion is the same wall-derived number this entry says is
not a protocol quantity, so IT IS WRONG AND MUST BE REPLACED by the received-tick origin. 900, §13B, close,
payout and the Daily pin are untouched.

  protocol/test/first-mark.test.js    5 / 5
  protocol/test/stopped.test.js       2 / 2
  blwp-node/test/first-mark.test.js  14 / 14

A CLIENT-REPORTED ORIGIN WOULD HAND THE START DEADLINE TO THE PLAYER (2026-09-21).

(b) says the client reports its own core tick at HELD and the node uses it as the origin. Before building a
door for that number, one property of it was checked, and it is the deciding one.

A MARK'S TICK IS NOT FREE - IT IS PINNED BY REPLAY. `replay.js:155` builds
`want = new Map(marks.map((m) => [m.tick, hex(m.stateHash)]))` and then walks the player's own inputs,
comparing `a.stateHash(st)` at each tick and recording `divergedAt` (`:173`, `:194`). A player cannot put an
arbitrary tick in a mark: the state at that tick has to be the state the core produces from the inputs the
player also signed.

A BARE REPORTED ORIGIN HAS NO SUCH BINDING. Nothing would pin it to anything - not to a state, not to an
input chain, not to a hash the player is already committed to. And the player's interest is to report a LATE
one: origin + 900 is their window, so a dishonest client reports its core tick as far forward as it likes and
is never late. That empties §15, whose whole purpose is that a player cannot wait, watch the world, and then
start with information others did not have. The rule that currently says "a late start is the player's own
act" would become unenforceable, and it would be the player who decided it.

THE SHAPE THAT CLOSES IT, named and not written: the reported origin is only accepted if the player's own
transcript COVERS it - the tick must appear in the inputs and marks the node replays, so the same machinery
that pins a mark's tick pins the origin. A number the player asserts is worthless; a number the player must
later prove is not.

So (b) is still the right origin and still needs a carrier, but the carrier cannot be a plain "here is my
tick" door. Nothing was built on this turn: no door, no node-side default, no conversion, and §15's
late-start rule is left exactly as it is rather than quietly defanged.

  protocol/test/first-mark.test.js    5 / 5
  protocol/test/stopped.test.js       2 / 2

(b) IS RIGHT AND NEEDS A NEW CARRIER: NEITHER THE ENTRY NOR THE CHECKPOINT HAS ROOM (2026-09-21).

Step 1 said to measure the field before writing, and preferring the existing `joinTick` is closed by three
measurements, not by preference:

  1. JOINTICK IS INSIDE THE ENTRY'S HASH. `contracts.js:318` writes `w.u32(e.joinTick)` into
     `encodeEntryContract`, and `entryId = taggedHash(TAG.entryContract, encodeEntryContract(e))`
     (`contracts.js:393`). The entry is built, signed and POSTED before the stake is paid - the hold invoice
     is derived from it - so a value known only at HELD cannot go in it. Changing joinTick changes the entry
     id, and with it the handout and the invoice the player already paid.

  2. JOINTICK IS ALREADY LOAD-BEARING FOR THE RUN'S END. `contracts.js:461-466`: "THE LAST TICK A RUN MAY
     CARRY, for an entry that joined at `joinTick` ... whose ticks reach `joinTick + BLOCK_TICKS`". Moving it
     to mean HELD would move the last tick of the run as well - a second rule changed silently.

  3. THE CHECKPOINT HAS NO SPARE FIELD. `CHECKPOINT_BYTES = 1 + 2 + 32 + 32 + 4 + 32 + 32 + 32`, a fixed
     record, and `SIGNED_CHECKPOINT_BYTES = CHECKPOINT_BYTES + SIGNATURE_BYTES`. Adding a tick changes every
     checkpoint's size and its `PROTOCOL_VERSION`.

So both carriers the ruling named - "on the entry or checkpoint" - are unavailable as they stand. (b) is
still the right answer: the origin must be the player's OWN core tick at HELD, because the mark is numbered
in that clock and no conversion exists (offset spread 2257 ticks). What it needs is a THIRD number the client
sends after the stake is held - a new door, or a checkpoint version bump - and the letter's own instruction
is "until that field is present, do not invent a node-side default or a conversion". So none was invented.

WHAT IS ALREADY IN PLACE, and unchanged by this: the origin moves to HELD in `round.js` (from
`stake_seen.seen_ms`, committed), `firstMarkOutcome` takes an `originTick`, free rounds keep the old
behaviour word for word, and §13B still VOIDs two first marks. What is NOT in place is the origin being
expressed in the player's clock, which is exactly the carrier this entry is about.

  protocol/test/first-mark.test.js    5 / 5
  protocol/test/stopped.test.js       2 / 2
  blwp-node/test/first-mark.test.js  14 / 14

900 untouched, §13B text untouched, close and payout untouched, the Daily still pinned at df66c6d1. No Unity
was touched; if the field lands on the checkpoint the WebGL page becomes its sender and the pin still holds.

NO SERVER-SIDE CONVERSION IS POSSIBLE: THE CORE-TO-ROUND OFFSET SWINGS 2257 TICKS (2026-09-21).

If the node could convert the mark's core tick into a round tick, the clocks would reconcile without touching
the protocol. It cannot. The same four traces, each pairing a core tick with the round tick at that instant:

  run       core tick   round tick   core - round
  origin         5100         4223          +877
  slices         5280         6475         -1195
  clocks         5220         4891          +329
  held           5220         4158         +1062

  spread: -1195 to +1062, a range of 2257 ticks

The offset is not a constant to subtract: the page's core starts when the PAGE loads and the round rotates
every three minutes, so the same core tick means a different round tick on every run. A node that guessed a
conversion would be inventing the number the whole letter exists to stop being invented.

AND THE PROTOCOL ALREADY SAYS WHICH CLOCK IT WANTS. `firstMarkOutcome` refuses a mark before the join tick:

    if (!Number.isInteger(firstMark.tick) || firstMark.tick < joinTick)
      throw new Error(`a first mark is at a tick at or after the join tick ${joinTick}`);

so `joinTick` and the mark's tick are the SAME clock - the player's core clock - and `joinTick + 900` was
always meant to be a window in the player's own ticks. What breaks it is that the client never fills it in:
`blwp-client/src/join.js:761` declares `entryFor(round, { ..., joinTick = 0, ... })` and the page passes
none, so every paid entry says it joined at core tick 0 while its core is already past 4000.

SO THE DECISION IS NOW WELL POSED, and it is one of two, both of which put the anchor where the mark's clock
is - in the client:

  (a) the client fills `joinTick` with its core tick at join, restoring the design the validation already
      assumes. The window then opens at join, which is before the money, so on its own it still forfeits a
      paid entry - it fixes the clock but not the origin.
  (b) the client reports its core tick at the moment it sees the stake HELD, and the node uses that as
      `originTick`. That is the ruling already made - the window opens at HELD - expressed in the clock the
      marks are actually numbered in, and it is the only one of the two that satisfies both.

Neither is written. Both change what a client must send, which is a protocol decision about the entry or the
checkpoint, not a node-side patch. 900 untouched, §13B untouched, close and payout untouched, the origin move
as committed, and the Daily still on its pinned checkout.

THE MARK CANNOT BE JUDGED IN THE ROUND CLOCK, AND THE SUITES SAID SO (2026-09-21).

FIRST, A CORRECTION I OWE. The ruling rested on "the mark already carries a round tick (4223 / 6475 / 4891 /
4158)". It does not. Those four numbers were MINE - a column I computed from the wall time of the attempt and
labelled "mark (round)". `encodeCheckpoint` writes exactly one tick, and it is the player's CORE tick:

    w.u8(TYPE_CHECKPOINT); w.u16(PROTOCOL_VERSION); w.bytes32(roundId); w.bytes32(entryId);
    w.u32(tick); w.bytes32(stateHash); w.bytes32(inputChainHash); w.bytes32(previousHash);

WHAT WAS TRIED. The only round-clock stamp the node has for a mark is WHEN IT ARRIVED, taken the same way the
HELD origin is - wall ms against the round's `startTimeMs`. Implemented, and against the four traces it is

  origin    4094   4223         4994      129        no forfeit
  slices    6175   6475         7075      300        no forfeit

  held      4102   4158         5002       56        no forfeit

than the ten reds. ARRIVAL IS LOCAL. Two seats receive the same mark at different moments, so they would
reach different verdicts from the same transcript - identical inputs, different results - and whether a
player "started late" would depend on the network instead of on the player. That is the one rule this whole
project is built on, and no start-deadline convenience is worth spending it.

second. This is not one mark delivered twice: two payloads, two signatures, two ticks.

THE MECHANISM IS IN THE CLIENT, AND IT IS NAMED. `client.js:947` and `:986` both build with
`previousHash: this.head`, and the file says what moves the head: "The head is advanced only when the node
says it STORED the mark ... `readReceipt` counts the signer and moves the head only when the mark is live."
So a first mark that is not stored leaves `this.head` at NO_PREVIOUS, and the NEXT mark is another first.
That is exactly the shape of A and B.

AND THE OBVIOUS CAUSE IS RULED OUT BY THE DATA, not by argument. The theory was: the page marks before the
stake is paid, the node refuses with STAKE_NOT_SEEN (`server.js:1791-1792`), the head never advances. But
that door RECORDS its refusals - `round.putRefusedFirstMark` - and for this entry:

    refused_first_marks: 0 rows at seat a, 0 rows at seat b
    offered_marks:       0 rows at either seat

So these marks were not refused for an unseen stake. Something else left the head unadvanced, and no fix is
written on a theory the store contradicts.

THE NEXT INSTRUMENT, and it is the client's own answer: `mark()` already computes `answer`, `refused`,
`unreached` and `live` per mark and returns them - nothing logs them. Saying those four out loud, plus
whether the head moved, names the condition in one run. That is the measurement; the fix follows it.

THE 2% WAS NEVER INVOICED ON TESTNET4, AND THRESHOLD_LN HAS NO OBJECT TO CARRY IT (2026-09-21).

MEASURED, NO WRITES. The fence stays up: nothing was minted, claimed or spent for this.

WHERE THE 20000 MSAT WENT: nowhere. It was never asked for.

  the stake                     1000000 msat
  §22A's 2%                       20000 msat
  the hold A actually issued     980000 msat      = netStakeMsat = stake - fee - donation

`netStakeMsat` (protocol/payout.js) subtracts the fee BEFORE the invoice is written, so the only invoice that
ever existed was for the net. The 20000 msat never left the payer's balance, and no seat was paid it.

  A's invoices    39 total, 30 CANCELED, 9 SETTLED
                  requested amounts  {980000: 36, 100000000: 1, 1000: 2}
                  settled amounts    {980000: 8, 100000000: 1}
                  invoices for 20000 msat:  NONE
  B's invoices    1 total, SETTLED, 20000000 msat - that is 20000 SAT, the inbound purchase, not the 2%.
                  (20000000 msat and 20000 msat differ by a factor of a thousand; the fee is the small one.)

  the channel     A local 87840 sat, B local 108690 sat, unchanged by this letter - no writes were made
  historical      8 settles x 980000 = 7840000 msat moved A-ward, which is the whole observed delta.
                  Had the fee been taken it would have been 8 x 1000000 = 8000000 msat.
                  THE DIFFERENCE, 160000 MSAT, IS THE FEE THAT WAS NEVER INVOICED ACROSS EIGHT LIVE SETTLES.

WHY IT CANNOT BE TAKEN ON THIS CUSTODY. `server.js:2039` guards the whole fee-lock door with

    if (rc.custody === 'FEDERATION' && rc.federationId.some((x) => x !== 0))

and the live round names `custody: 'THRESHOLD_LN'` with `federationId: new Uint8Array(32)`. BOTH halves are
false, so the door is skipped: no fee lock is required of an entry, none is minted, none is verified and none
is claimed. The entry contract still carries a `feeLockOutpoint` field, but under THRESHOLD_LN nothing reads
it. There is no object on this custody that could hold the 2%, and the fee is already gone from the only
invoice that exists.

THE OPTIONS, WITH NUMBERS, NONE IMPLEMENTED:

  (a) A FEDIMINT FEDERATION ON TESTNET4. This is the shape the tests already prove: at a 1000000 msat stake
      with two seats and a zero base fee, `feeLockPays` mints a 20000 msat lock and pays both seats - measured
      in lock-settlement as "fee locks 2, 40000 msat, paid 2 signer nodes 36000 msat". It needs a non-zero
      federationId, a reachable stake-lock port, and guardians - and GUARDIANS ARE PARKED BY RULING. It also
      meets the measured fedimintd default of 1000 msat base, which §22A's own guard refuses.
  (b) THE FEE OVER LIGHTNING, AS ITS OWN HOLD. The size is not the problem: 20000 msat is far above the
      channel's min_htlc of 1 msat, and the usable 106690000 msat would take thousands of them. The problem
      is WHO. A seat is a BLWP signer-node pubkey, not a Lightning node; of the two seats in the live round,
      exactly ONE has a Lightning port at all, so only 1 of 2 could be paid today. And a fee invoice is not
      §22A's fee lock - changing the shape of how the 2% is carried is a ruling, not a repair.
  (c) THE WRITTEN REASON, which is this entry: on THRESHOLD_LN the 2% cannot be taken live, because the fee is
      deducted before the invoice and no fee-lock object exists on this custody path.

BOTH DIRECTIONS, NOT JUST INVOICES. The first pass only read invoices, which would have missed a fee paid as
an outgoing payment rather than requested as one. Closed:

  A's payments   1   {20000000: 1}              = A buying inbound from B, matching B's single invoice
  B's payments   9   {100000000: 1, 980000: 8}  = the inbound purchase, and the eight holds B paid
  payments of 20000 msat, either node:  NONE

B's eight 980000 msat payments match A's eight 980000 msat settled invoices exactly, which confirms the
7840000 msat delta from the other end of the channel independently.

AND THE 2% FIGURE IS THE CODE'S, NOT AN ASSUMPTION. `entryFeeMsat(1000000n) = 20000`; also 100000 -> 2000 and
200000 -> 4000. The tool's `donationMsat` is 0n, so the whole of the 20000 msat gap is the fee and nothing
else comes out of the stake.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT SAY. It does not say the fee path is broken - it is green in test and the arithmetic is
proved there. It says the LIVE custody has nowhere to put it, which is a different sentence, and it is the
remaining one of M3's three clauses: the federation hold and the payout on a rebuilt key both have live
evidence, and this does not.

INBOUND RE-MEASURED, AND A 980000 MSAT HOLD FITS 108 TIMES OVER (2026-09-21).

A correction of the DONE line of 2026-09-20, not a new item: that line's figures no longer described the
channel, because settles since have moved money A-ward.

  channel dce6199b, capacity 200000 sat, ACTIVE at both gateways, 0 pending HTLCs, 0 unsettled, commit_fee 2810

                          2026-09-20 (the DONE line)   2026-09-21 (now)     moved
  A 0274e261 inbound              116530 sat               108690 sat      -7840
  B 025f17c2 inbound               80000 sat                87840 sat      +7840

THE 7840 IS ACCOUNTED FOR, NOT ASSUMED. A's invoice list: 39 invoices, 9 SETTLED, and the settled amounts are
`{980000: 8, 100000000: 1}` - EIGHT settled holds of 980000 msat, which is 7840000 msat exactly, plus the one
100000 sat invoice that bought the inbound in the first place. Two of those eight are this session's live
reconstruction runs; the other six are earlier custody runs. 30 are CANCELED, which is the qualifier's hold
handed back each time.

WHAT A HOLD OF 980000 MSAT MEETS ON A. The hold is the NET stake - the 1000000 msat stake less §22A's 2% -
and that is the number that has to be receivable, not the gross. (The Daily advertises a 100 sat PAID round,
a different and smaller number; this is sized for 980000 msat because that is what a real settle has moved.)

  A's inbound                     108690000 msat     the hold is 0.90% of it
  B's side, less its 2000 reserve 106690000 msat     108 such holds fit
  max_pending_amt_msat             198000000 msat    202 x the hold; 101 x the two the tool takes at once
  min_htlc_msat                            1 msat    the hold is far above the floor
  max_accepted_htlcs                     483         with 0 in flight
  channel reserve                 2000 sat a side    both sides hold it comfortably

NO GAP, AND NO CHANGE INVENTED. Every limit clears the hold by two orders of magnitude, so the accept probe
was not run - the instruction was to stop at the measurement if the numbers say it would succeed. The
prediction put on the record before measuring - "A's inbound is about 108690 sat, so a 980 sat hold is
roughly 1% and I expect no gap" - is what landed, to the sat.

WHAT WOULD BITE FIRST, which local_balance alone would not have shown: B's side funds the HTLC, so the
binding number is B's local balance less B's channel reserve - 106690 sat - not A's inbound as such. At 980

A TESTNET4 HOLD SETTLED ON A PREIMAGE THE SEATS REBUILT (2026-09-21).

  shares asked of the peer   1   (GET http://127.0.0.1:46649/share)
  shares that formed P       2   = A's own + 1 from the other seat
  settle preimage            a6ef8e3fa4ea9be7eb17ae333fd17b95...
  equals the dealt secret    true
  hashes to the stake commit true
  channel A   before 86860000 -> after 87840000 msat   moved +980000
  channel B   before 109670000 -> after 108690000 msat  moved -980000
  pending HTLCs on A         0      (the hold did not sit and expire back)
  lncli settleinvoice runs   1
  threshold                  receiptsNeeded(2) = 2

TWO OF TWO IS NOT FIVE OF SEVEN. `receiptsNeeded` knows exactly two shapes - 2 slots need 2, 7 need 5 - so
this pair can only ever be a 2-of-2. BOTH seats had to answer, which is what makes it a reconstruction rather
than a lookup, but it does not demonstrate surviving the loss of a seat. That is what five of seven buys and
it is exercised in process by `five-of-seven.test.js`.

WHAT THE TOOL WAS, AND IS. `custody-testnet4.mjs:123` handed the bytes in - `preimageFor: (id, e) =>
preimageOf(e.pubkey[31])`, fabricated as 0xc0 + run nonce + player number - and `:236` did the same for the
restart section. Both are gone; nothing in the file can put a fabricated preimage on a settle. It now stands
up two real signer nodes with `serve()`, names THEIR pubkeys as the round's settlement seats (it named the
placeholders b32(8)/b32(9), which no process held), deals a handout per entry so shares are published, and
settles through `fromTheCommittee`.

FIVE THINGS THE DESIGN REFUSED ON THE WAY, each one measured rather than argued with:
  1. "this node holds stakes and has no preflight" - a paying round will not open until Lightning is shown
     able to hold one. The live run uses the real `lndPreflight` over the two testnet4 gateways.
  2. "that randomness names no time, so nothing says it came after committee_time" - the round needs a real
     beacon. It is lnd's own tip: block hash, height and header time.
  3. "no stake moves: the operator would keep 980000 msat: a pool of 980000 against 0 handed out" - a round
     whose only entry is FORFEIT was refused outright. So the walk-away has a qualifier beside it.
  4. "this node has replayed nothing for that run" - B KEPT ITS SHARE when asked early, and A stopped at
     "1 of 2 shares: a stake nobody can open stays in flight". A seat does not hand over a share for a run it
     has not judged, so asserting finality to A alone cannot move it. The qualifier has to actually play.
  5. "that round closes entry at ..., before its committee forms at ..." - testnet4's header timestamp ran
     1.8 HOURS ahead of this machine's clock, so a committee time taken off the beacon landed in the future.

AND THE WORLD IS CHOSEN, NOT ASSUMED. The beacon changes every block, and a world that delivers under one
wrecks under the next: under 00000000bd4c..62a3 the fixture's own 0x5e secret ends FAILED at tick 336 while
0x55 DELIVERS at 993 with score 176. The tool drives candidates against the core before joining anything and
takes one that arrives under today's beacon, by the same GATE_X aiming rule `window-fixture` uses.

TWO ASSUMPTIONS ARE STATED OUT LOUD IN THE FILE, not smuggled: `recordSignerNodes` (there is no live testnet4
census) and `putStakeSeen` on B (the hold is an invoice on A's node; who watches the HTLC for the other seats
is a real question and not this letter's).

the Lightning port swapped for a fake. Every refusal above was found dry. Two live runs were made: the first

RULING (Daniel 2026-09-21): §22A'S 2% IS SEAT COMPENSATION FOR A ROUND THAT ACTUALLY RAN.

It is not a qualifier's prize and it is not operator profit. In the spec's own shape:
  1. A VOID round - a technical failure - claims NOTHING. Stakes and fee locks unwind, and the operator must
     not profit from a failure. Unchanged by this letter.
  2. A FINISHED round with a loser and no qualifier: the stakes expire back to their players, no stake is
     paid to a qualifier because there is none, and the FEE LOCKS STILL SETTLE TO THE SEATS. That settlement
     is ACCEPTED, not NONE.

WHAT THE SETTLER ACTUALLY DID with such a round, printed rather than guessed at (min_score 1000000, the
delivered run scores 5, so nobody qualifies):

  state                ACCEPTED           submissions 2
  stake locks held     2 of 2             <- neither stake claimed; both expire back to their players
  fee locks held       0 of 2             <- both claimed, to pay the seats
  claimed outpoints    the two fee locks (outIdx :1), once per submission
  payouts              2000 msat to 021080c4fa, 2000 msat to 02af15b892
  seats                021080c4fa, 02af15b892      <- exactly the round's two sitting signer nodes
  winner key           020a0a0a0a         loser key 0205050505      <- NEITHER is paid

The arithmetic is §22A's: two players staking 100000 msat is 200000 gross, 2% of it is 4000 msat, and this
round's two seats take 2000 each - 1% GAME/VERIFY and 1% SETTLEMENT, both pools.

THE TEST WAS SPLIT, NOT RETUNED. It asserted `NONE` and zero submissions, which was true only while the
fixture's entries brought no fee lock; on a federation BLWP would accept the round mints them. The
expectation moved because the fixture is the production shape now. What it pins is strictly MORE than before:
  - the settlement is ACCEPTED and something was submitted;
  - NO payout reaches either player's key, and BOTH stake locks are still held (they expire back);
  - each sitting seat is paid exactly 2000n to its own key;
  - both fee locks are claimed, so the seats really were paid out of them.
The title says what is true now: "a round with a loser and no qualifier pays no stake and still pays the
seats: both stake locks expire back, both fee locks settle the 2%".

THE DRIVER NOW AIMS AT THE GATE THE CORE PUBLISHES, in the core's own units. Heading is a fraction of a turn
in Q16.16 (0.25 = +x, measured off the spawn pose), so the desired heading is `atan2(GATE_X + LEAD - x, -z)`
and the steering word is the wrapped error times a gain. `LEAD` is 20 m PAST the gate, because a truck that
turns toward a point it is already on steers into the doorframe; 20 m was the shortest lead measured that
still arrives. Nothing is hand-tuned to a tick count: the day the world moves again, this follows it.

THE FAKE FEDERATION IS ONE BLWP WOULD ACCEPT (2026-09-21). `test/lock-fixture.js:60` 1000n -> 0n.

WHAT THE 1000 WAS STEERING, measured with `feeLockPays` on the fixture's own `contractFor` before anything
was changed:

  stake   nodes  feeLock  rule                          pays   why
  100000    2     2000    base 1000 (the fixture)       false  locks hold 4000, inputs alone cost 2000
  100000    2     2000    base 1500 (lock-settlement)   false  locks hold 4000, inputs alone cost 3000
  100000    2     2000    base 0, disable_base_fees     TRUE   every one of 2 paid more than nothing
 1000000    2    20000    base 1000                     TRUE   <- the 1000 only bites on SMALL rounds
   10000    2      200    base 0                        TRUE
  100000    2     2000    base 0, ppm 1000000           false  fees take the whole fee

So it steered exactly one branch - "the federation's per-input/output cost exceeds the 2% fee, mint nothing" -
and only on small rounds. On a legal federation that branch is UNREACHABLE: with base 0 every round measured
mints, down to 10 sat. The 1000 is not invented either: `protocol/test/lock-settlement.test.js:201` keeps it
as REAL_RULE, "measured on fedimintd 0.12.0". It is that daemon's DEFAULT; §22A's `disable_base_fees` is an
operator setting. The fixture was modelling a federation as it ships, which BLWP refuses until configured.

THE FIX, without weakening the guard and without loosening one assertion:
  - `lock-fixture.js` is legal AT REST: `{ ppm: 0n, baseMsat: 0n }`.
  - `lock-settlement.test.js` applies fedimintd's measured default AT THE CLOSE (`closeRound`), by which time
    every entry is in. Settlement arithmetic is still run against 1000 msat base; the door never sees an
    illegal federation. That mid-test mutation is the one this suite already used at :349/:401/:508.
  - `forfeit`, `outage`, `first-mark`, `one-signer-node-refused` now DEAL a fee lock: a secret, an outpoint,
    the lock put on the port and handed to each signer node beside the stake lock. `lockAndPlay` in
    lock-settlement defaults `feeLock` to true for the same reason.
  - `one-signer-node-refused`'s handed-out `lockOn` hands BOTH locks: a stake is only seen when both are in,
    and handing one left B with one receipt where the test asks for two.

THE TWO HALVES NEVER MEET. Every assault the player was told about had NO armour in the camera's horizontal
field, and every assault whose armour was in the field was one he was never told about. That is the whole
16:22 complaint in one table, and neither half is a camera problem on its own.

THREE THINGS THE WITNESS HAD TO BE TAUGHT, each measured rather than assumed:
  - `AssaultWatch.Keep` is 6. A full log stops growing and only shifts, so a LINE COUNT would have been false
    too; the signature is per-line (colour class + text-pixel total), and a new line rewrites the sequence.
  - A line's pixel total drifts up to ~9 % between ticks while the words are unchanged (anti-aliasing over
    whatever the world does behind it). An exact compare called every tick a new line. The rule is therefore
    a different number of lines, or two or more slots differing by over a quarter. Background contamination
    measured at 8 matching pixels across 130 non-text rows.
  - A real line carries 62 to 135 quantised units; the bay panel sliding in threw a single 16-unit blob that
    scored two false YESes in the bay. A 40-unit floor removes it and sits well below the smallest real line.
  - The HUD can draw BEFORE the probe reads: round 2's t+68 declaration was on screen at t+67. The baseline
    is taken three ticks back and the search starts at -2 s. Without that, a true announcement read "no".

HALF TWO OF §23.4: THE CLAIM KEY *IS* THRESHOLD-SIGNED, AND ITS PROOF IS HIDDEN THE SAME WAY (2026-09-20)

Read before writing anything, as ruled. §23.4 asks for two things: reconstructing P from 5 of 7 shares (half
one, now demonstrated 7/7) AND "the committee's threshold signature". §23.6 names the shape: "the claim key
is a FROST (RFC 9591) BIP-340 key, which the federation checks like any other key."

IT EXISTS. `blwp-node/src/forfeit.js` signs with real FROST:
  - each seat holds `{ id, share }` and publishes hiding/binding nonce commitments;
  - `signShare340({ id, share, groupPublicKey: claimPk, nonces, message, commitments, curve })` produces that
    seat's BIP-340 signature share;
  - the threshold is the round's own: `receiptsNeeded(contract.nodes.length)`, and a list shorter than that is
    refused - "N commitments, and this round's key signs at M";
  - a seat signs ONE list per message and keeps no second pair - "this signer node signed that forfeit over
    another list, and keeps no second pair";
  - a combined signature handed over by a peer is kept only if `schnorr.verify(signature, message,
    claimPk.subarray(1))` passes against what THIS seat rebuilt - x-only BIP-340, the federation's own check.

So neither half of §23.4 is missing code. What is missing is the same thing half one was missing: EVIDENCE.

  settle-threshold    0/2     all three fail with "a stake dealt at the round's own threshold was refused:
  pool-threshold      0/4     this node holds no such round" - the stale `blockTicks: 9000` again, one per
  handout-threshold   0/2     fixture, exactly the chain reconstruct.test.js was stuck behind
  forfeit             NOT MEASURED - no stale ticks in it; it exceeds 300 s here and was terminated twice.
                      Cause unknown; not claimed as red and not claimed as green.

THE GAP THAT IS NOT A FIXTURE, AND IT IS WORTH NAMING PLAINLY: the shares are DEALT. `server.js` says so in
its own words - "THIS NODE'S OWN SHARE OF THE POOL, and nobody else's. `{ id, share }`, dealt today because a
dealerless DKG is its own letter." A dealer that splits the key has held the whole key. FROST signing and
five-of-seven reconstruction are both real; the key's ORIGIN is not yet trustless, and until a dealerless DKG
lands, custody rests on whoever dealt.

AND ON TESTNET4 IT IS STILL SINGLE-NODE: `custody-testnet4.mjs` and `custody-lnd.mjs` both inject
`preimageFor`, so the live-pair run never exercised reconstruction or threshold signing. That is not a claim
this letter makes.


FIVE-OF-SEVEN RECONSTRUCTION IS DEMONSTRATED, NOT ASSUMED (2026-09-20, M3 §23.4 half one)

§23.4: "Claiming a loser's stake lock requires the committee's threshold signature and reconstructing `P`,
which requires 5 of the 7 shares, which the mechanical rule releases only against a FINAL result - and
finality requires 5-of-7 game/verify signatures plus an objection window that anyone in the world may use to
disprove the result by replay (§13A)." (§23.5 is "No pool wallet" - a different rule, kept distinct.)

RECONSTRUCTION WAS NEVER MISSING, and that was the first thing measured. `server.js:323` wires
`preimageFor: preimageFor || fromTheCommittee`, and `fromTheCommittee` reads the round's `settlementSlots`,
derives `roundThreshold(...)`, calls `preimages.open({ roundId, entryId, needed })` and returns null with a
logged reason if the threshold is not met. Its own comment: "An operator may still inject one - the regtest
tool does - but the DEFAULT is the committee, because a default that settles alone is the custody this letter
exists to end."

WHAT WAS MISSING WAS THE PROOF. `reconstruct.test.js` - seven tests that speak §23.4's own sentences - was
0/7, and both of its causes were stale fixture values rather than anything about custody:

  blockTicks: 9000          `Round.open` refuses a contract disagreeing with the core (10800 since c01cc655),

  objectionWindowMs: 0n     a zero window was legal when this fixture was written; it is refused now, because
                            it erases §13A's replay veto. The spec sets NO FLOOR, so the smallest legal
                            window is 1ms - which has passed by the time these tests ask. Nothing asserted in
                            the suite is about the window's length.

  before  reconstruct 0/7        after  reconstruct 7/7

AND WHAT THE SEVEN NOW SAY, once a round can open:

  one node alone opens nothing, four refuse by name, five reconstruct
  a stranger asking for a share is refused, and a signer node gets an envelope only it can open
  a delivered run never gives up its preimage, and neither does one that is not final
  a hold settles on a preimage five signer nodes opened, and on nothing less
  with four signer nodes reachable the loser's stake stays in flight
  a player who committed to one secret and dealt another opens nothing
  a signer node that never replayed the run hands over nothing

That is §23.4's half one, demonstrated: the threshold is real, four is not enough, a non-final result releases
nothing, and a hold settles only on a preimage five seats opened.

A ROUND CANNOT NAME A ZERO RESULT WINDOW (2026-09-20, M3 the result window)

THE FIELD ALREADY EXISTED AND WAS ALREADY USED, which is the first thing measured and the reason this letter
is a bound rather than a feature.

  key            `objectionWindowMs` (the spec's `objection_window_W`)
  units          milliseconds, u64 on the wire - contracts.js:67 writes it, :217 reads it
  who writes it  the round's creator, in the Round Contract
  opens          at the round's close (`closed_ms`); for the objection window, when the result is
                 PROVISIONALLY_FINAL
  closes         `closed_ms + objectionWindowMs`

  §13A  "After a result is PROVISIONALLY_FINAL, the window W (reference: 10 minutes, contract-defined) runs."
  §13   "The result window equals the objection window - same duration, a field on the contract. A seat that
         cannot retrieve the transcript in that window treats the entry as VOID."

Already implemented against it: the objection window itself (`protocol/src/objection.js`), finality timing
(`finality.js`, `server.js:1042/1059`), §13C's no-quorum outcome (`payout.js:noQuorumOutcome`, a `no_quorum`
table read by `finality.js` and `forfeit.js`), and the result window itself - `verify.js:#unretrievedPastWindow`
is the spec sentence nearly verbatim: inside the window it answers null and the seat waits, past it the
no-quorum rule decides and the reason records "could not retrieve the transcript within the result window".

WHAT WAS MISSING WAS ANY BOUND. `roundWindowsAreValid` checked committee time, start time and entry close and
never mentioned the field, so a contract could name 0. That is not a short window, it is none:

  - finality is instant, so §13A's replay veto - which the spec calls "the cheapest defence in the whole
    design" - could never be exercised by anyone;
  - `verify.js`'s own test is `now >= closed_ms + objectionWindowMs`, true the moment the round closes, so a
    seat that had not yet retrieved the transcript would void the entry immediately.

NO FLOOR IS SPECIFIED, AND NONE WAS INVENTED. §13A gives "reference: 10 minutes, contract-defined" - a
reference, not a minimum - and no sentence in BLWP v4.6.1 states a floor or a ceiling for W. So the check
refuses only what the spec's own words rule out: a duration that is not positive. Measured:

  600000ms -> opens      1ms -> opens      0ms -> REFUSED      -5ms -> REFUSED      absent -> REFUSED

Any positive window opens, 10 minutes or otherwise, because the field is contract-defined. A missing or
non-bigint field is refused rather than defaulted, since defaulting would fix the number the spec declines to.

PROVED RED: with the `roundWindowsAreValid` call deleted from `Round.open`, "THE CALL SITE ITSELF" fails
(6 pass, 1 fail). Restored, 7/7.

A ROUND MAY NOT SEAT MORE SIGNER NODES THAN IT HAS SLOTS (2026-09-20, M3 fee locks / 22A node slots)

§22A pays the node fee to "the round's sitting seats - the seats the census seated for this round, its
`nodes` - however many there are: two in a 2-of-2, seven in a 5-of-7", and warns in its own words: "Not seven
census slots when the round is 2-of-2." §22A again: "A fee lock is sized for the same seats the settlement
pays."

MEASURED BEFORE, with `feeLockPays` on full contracts:

    round                       slots   nodes   pays   seats sized   lockMsat
    2-of-2, 2 seats (correct)   2/2     2      true   2            20000
    2-of-2, SEVEN seats         2/2     7      true   7            20000      <- the fault
    5-of-7, 7 seats (correct)   7/7     7      true   7            20000
    5-of-7, TWO seats           7/7     2      true   2            20000

`feeLockPays` reads `contract.nodes` and never looks at the slot counts, so the fee lock was sized for whoever
the contract named and the settlement paid the same set. Seven shares out of a committee of two.

AFTER: `sittingSeatsFitTheSlots` (protocol/src/contracts.js, beside `publicationRelaysAreValid`) is called in
`Round.open` - the node's own open path - and throws before the contract is stored. The 2-of-2 naming seven
seats is refused with "that round seats 7 signer nodes on 2/2 slots: 22A pays the seats the census seated, and
a fee lock sized for more of them pays seats that never sat". The other three rows are unchanged.

IT IS AN UPPER BOUND, NOT AN EQUALITY, and that was a measurement rather than a preference. Contracts in this
tree run 2, 3, 4, 5 and 7 slots and the two pools are NOT always equal (settlementSlots 4 appears once), so an
equality rule would have invented something the spec does not say and broken them. The spec's number is
"however many there are"; a slot a census left unfilled is a round with fewer seats than slots and is
legitimate. Only naming MORE is the fault 22A warns about, and only that is refused. The bound is the larger
pool, because both pools draw on the same sitting seats.

THE CLAIM HASH WAS ALREADY RIGHT and was not touched. The table's `payment_image  Hash(H(F))` is a KIND tag,
not a double hash - it reads against `Point(stake_point)` on the stake row, and §23.1 step 5 says it outright:
"whose payment_image is the entry's stake_point (resp. H(F))". `stake-lock.js:74` computes `sha256(F)` and
requires `image.kind === 'hash'` with those bytes. F5 is implemented too: it refuses when H(F) equals the
entry's stake commitment, "claiming the fee would publish P".

round.test.js 0/12 and checkpoint.test.js 1/21 are RED AND WERE ALREADY RED: stashing this change back to HEAD

THE FEDERATION'S FEE IS ZERO, AND THE NODE NOW REFUSES ONE THAT IS NOT (2026-09-20)

THE RULE, QUOTED, so the next reader does not re-open the arithmetic. §22A "Node fee and developer donation":

    gross_round_volume = Σ stake of every financially activated entry      (ENTRY_VOID and VOID excluded)
    node_fee = 2.00% of gross_round_volume
    1.00% -> GAME/VERIFY pool     (the round's sitting seats)
    1.00% -> SETTLEMENT pool      (the round's sitting seats)

  "The 2% stays. Fedimint's own base fees are 0: the federation runs with `disable_base_fees`. Lightning
   `min_htlc` / routing is not a federation fee."
  "Unearned shares are redistributed pro rata among the other eligible nodes in the same role pool, keeping
   the total at 2%."
  "Calculate in millisatoshis, floor each base share, and distribute the remaining msat in ascending
   H(round_id ‖ node_pubkey) order."
  §17: "Node fees and the player-selected donation are INCLUSIVE in the wallet commitment; the pool is the
   sum of net stakes, and entitlement is weighted by net stake."

WHO PAYS the player, inclusively, inside the wallet commitment - never on top. WHO RECEIVES the round's own
sitting seats, 1% for game/verify and 1% for settlement, split by however many seats the census seated (1%/2
in a 2-of-2, 1%/7 in a 5-of-7); a seat in both roles earns both. WHEN at settlement, out of the round's own
volume. UNITS millisatoshis, floored, remainder by hash order.

SO "THE FEDERATION'S FEES" HAS NO ARITHMETIC LEFT IN IT: the federation's own fee is ZERO by rule, and the
only fee in the chapter is 22A's node fee, which is already implemented and green.

    protocol/src/fee.js            16/16   gross volume, 2%, the 1%/1% split (the second pool taken as
                                           `fee - first` so two floors cannot lose a msat), per-seat floor,
                                           remainder in H(round_id ‖ node_pubkey) order, and a self-check
                                           that throws unless paid + unallocated === fee
    protocol/src/lock-settlement.js 17/17  pays those seats from the fee locks

And it is already visible on the live pair: the testnet4 hold invoices were 980000 msat against a 1000000
msat stake - the 2% withheld because it is inclusive and travels in a fee lock, not in the stake hold.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY MISSING was the other half of the zero: the CLIENT refuses to lock against a federation
that charges a base fee (`page-lock.js`), and nothing on the NODE did. A signer node would have taken entries
into a round whose stakes were being shaved on every input and output - money the operator did not earn,
which is the operator-must-not-profit rule arriving from the other side.

`federationTakesNoBaseFee` in `blwp-node/src/stake-lock-signer-node.js`, called on POST /entry where the node
already reads the federation's fee rule, before `round.enter`:

    baseMsat 0      accepted, "that federation charges no base fee"
    baseMsat 1000   refused 409, naming the amount, disable_base_fees and the players' own pool
    baseMsat 1      refused - there is no threshold in the rule
    ppm 10000       accepted - a per-million rate is not a base fee, and min_htlc / routing never were
    no rule known   accepted - the client's own "no fee rule known: no lock"; an unreadable port is not an
                    accusation, the round simply mints no fee lock

PROVED RED RATHER THAN ASSERTED: with the call deleted from server.js, "THE CALL SITE ITSELF" fails - it
checks the import, the call, the 409, and that the call sits on the /entry path BEFORE `round.enter`.

SUITES: no-base-fee 6/6, fee 16/16, lock-settlement 17/17, custody-daemon 9/9,
paying-round-needs-gateways 7/7. No Unity, no WebGL, no deploy, no testnet4 fee-lock spend.


A HOLD INVOICE ON TESTNET4 GOES ACCEPTED -> HELD, AND SETTLES OR CANCELS FROM THE CORE'S WORD (2026-09-20)

`custody-lnd.mjs` proved these rules on an isolated regtest it spawns and MINES. `custody-testnet4.mjs` runs
the SAME `Custody` - same four operations, same outcome mapping - against the two gateways that exist, and
mines nothing, because nobody mines testnet4. A is the custodian and issues the hold; B is the player's wallet
and pays. The outcome word is handed to `custody.settleHeldInvoices`; the script never decides it.

    channel before        A local 84900000 msat, B local 111630000 msat
    three holds           1000000 msat stake each -> invoices of 980000 msat
                          (the hold is the NET stake: the stake less 22A's 2%)
    B pays all three      lnd says ACCEPTED x3, this node says HELD x3, 980000 msat paid each

    winner   DELIVERED  -> CANCEL   -> CANCELLED
    loser    FORFEIT    -> SETTLE   -> SETTLED
    voided   VOID       -> NOTHING  -> EXPIRED

    after the acts        A local 85880000 msat  (+980000, exactly one forfeited net stake)
                          B local 109240000 msat
    channel afterwards    A 85880 sat + B 110650 sat = 196530 sat, 0 pending HTLCs - the whole usable
                          capacity, nothing kept and nothing lost

THE VOID ROW IS AN ABSENCE AND WAS MEASURED AS ONE. Of the 12 lncli calls the port actually made - recorded
from the real invocations, because `lndPort` keeps no log of its own - the void hash appears in ZERO settle or
cancel. lnd still says ACCEPTED, and its HTLC expires at height 153354 against a tip of 153271: 83 blocks
away. THE REFUND ITSELF IS A LATER PASS, by ruling - on regtest the tool mined to force it, and on testnet4
that is real hours.

AND THEN THE TOOL CLEANS UP, WHICH IS NOT THE PROTOCOL PATH AND SAYS SO IN THE OUTPUT. A paid hold left until
its CLTV is one lnd force-closes the channel to resolve - and that channel is the gateways' only inbound. So
the third hold is cancelled AFTER the numbers are taken, labelled housekeeping, and nothing in the VOID row is
read from it.

A SETTLE IS REFUSED BEFORE LND IS ASKED, TWICE, and both were proved with money actually in flight:

    no preimage      -> HELD, 0 settleinvoice calls, "this node has no preimage for that stake"
    wrong preimage   -> HELD, 0 settleinvoice calls, "that preimage is not the one this hold was made for"

A LONE FORFEIT IS REFUSED FOR A DIFFERENT AND CORRECT REASON, found on the way: "the operator would keep
980000 msat: a pool of 980000 against 0 handed out". So each guard needed a winner beside it for the pool to
reach. That refusal is the operator-must-not-profit rule firing on its own, unprompted.

FOUR THINGS WENT WRONG IN THIS TOOL BEFORE THE NUMBERS WERE RIGHT, and none of them were in the rules:
  - it waited for the GROSS stake to arrive and reported "the payments never arrived" while all three sat
    ACCEPTED. The hold is for the net stake; the wait now reads the invoice's own amount.
  - the entries handed to the settlement named only their stake, not their fee and donation, and were refused.
  - `preimageFor` was handed the settlement entry, whose key is `pubkey`, not `playerPubkey`.
  - fixed preimages collided with the invoices earlier runs had left: "this endpoint already had an invoice
    for that hash and it is CANCELED, not a hold still in flight". Every run now mints its own.

STILL SINGLE-NODE CUSTODY, NOT §23.5. One endpoint issues and settles, and `preimageFor` is handed in rather
than reconstructed from five of seven shares. FROST closes that gap; this does not.

The mismatched-invoice refusal (`invoiceMatchesEntry`) is covered by `lnd-port.test.js` and was not re-proved
against the live pair. Gateways after all of it: 2 usable, YES - A inbound 110650, B inbound 85880.


A PAYING ROUND NOW REFUSES TO OPEN WITHOUT TWO INDEPENDENT GATEWAYS (2026-09-20, M3)

§23.6: "deposits and withdrawals through any of at least two gateways ... No gateway holds a round's money or
is needed by it", and §22: a gateway may refuse a deposit, never keep one. `gatewaysAreIndependent` was
written and proven against the live pair in the previous letter and then CALLED BY NOTHING, so a paying round
would have opened with no gateways at all.

THE CALL SITE. `lightningPreflight` (`blwp-node/src/preflight.js`) is the one gate the server consults on the
paying-round open path: `server.js` POST /round, inside `if (contract.stakeMsat > 0n && custody.reaches)`,
before `round.open(contract)` - so before any invoice exists and before the round is advertised as payable.
There is no second open path: `preflight` appears in server.js only there (and in its own option comment),
and a node that holds stakes with no preflight already answered 503. The browser is not asked.

Everything above that line in `lightningPreflight` asks ONE node about itself - synced, an active channel,
inbound >= needed, addholdinvoice. That is what let a single endpoint through.

FAIL CLOSED. `gateways` absent, not an array, or unreadable is a REFUSAL, not a pass: "this node was shown no
gateways, so it cannot open a paying round". A round that asks no stake still returns early and needs neither
Lightning nor a gateway (M3.3-19), which is the earlier letter's rule and is guarded here too.

WHAT "INDEPENDENT" MEANS HERE IS NARROWER THAN THE LAW'S, and it is written into the code rather than blurred:
§23.6 wants "different operators"; this M3 step (RULED 2026-09-20, named pick A) is the operator's own two
testnet4 nodes with the same host allowed, so the predicate counts distinct identities at distinct rpc
addresses that are synced and hold inbound, and does not read the host. Different-operator gateways are a
later letter.

`askGateways` / `askGatewaysRegtest` gather each node with its own `readonly.macaroon` - the same read-only
key the preflight already used, so the gate still cannot move a satoshi. A node that will not answer is
reported as unsynced with no channels rather than dropped, so a stopped gateway counts as one that cannot
receive instead of vanishing.

PROVED RED RATHER THAN ASSERTED. With the call site deleted from `lightningPreflight`, 5 of the 7 tests fail,
including "THE CALL SITE ITSELF: delete it and this goes red" - written so a green suite cannot hide an
unused predicate, which is the exact fault this letter found. Restored: 7/7.

SUITES: paying-round-needs-gateways 7/7, protocol/gateways 9/9, lnd-settings + gateways together 13/13.

THE SIX custody-daemon REDS ARE NOT THIS LETTER'S, and that was checked rather than assumed: the suite is
3 of 9 with this change AND with `preflight.js` stashed back to HEAD, the same six either way. The symptom is
`POST /entry` answering 400 where the test expects 201 - the ROUND opens fine (these tests stub the preflight
ready), so it is not the gateway gate. The failing six are:

  a joined player is quoted the hold invoice their own entry names
  a daemon with no Lightning still signer nodes, and says why it quotes nothing
  closing a round on the daemon reaches the money path, and moves no stake
  the committee agreeing on a round nobody finished still moves no stake
  a daemon asks Lightning about an act it died in the middle of, on start
  closing a round makes the daemon sign what it owes, and serve that signature

The cause is NOT diagnosed and is not guessed at here: the entry fixtures and the /entry validation need a
letter of their own. DEPENDENCY: nothing in M3's gateway or hold-invoice work waits on it, but the hold-invoice
letter will touch the same daemon, so it is worth clearing before that rather than during it.

THE ASSAULT HORN ACTUALLY SOUNDS (2026-09-20, the 16:22 half nobody can see)

The banner and the desktop log are on screen and were measured there. A sound cannot be screenshotted, and
Unity's own audio bookkeeping is out of reach: the framework declares `var WEBAudio = {...}` inside its own
closure, so it is on neither `Module` nor `window`, and asking the page for it answers "no Unity WEBAudio
module" - which says nothing either way. That answer was nearly written up as "audio is missing"; it was not.

Measured at the Web Audio API instead. `probe-assault-horn.mjs` wraps `AudioBufferSourceNode.start` before
Unity loads and records the moment and the buffer's DURATION. `DriveHud.AssaultHorn` builds a 0.55 s clip in
code, and nothing else in this build is that long - over a whole run, of 1070 buffers started:

  1.100s x616   0.200s x244   2.000s x136   0.160s x52   0.000s x10   1.000s x8   0.550s x4

Four 0.55 s buffers, two chimes, and both pairs inside 1.5 s of a banner:

  t+40s  chime 1  "BEARS ASSAULT LOW"    window [0.55, 0.55, 2, 2, 0.2, 0.2, 1.1, 1.1, 1.1, 1.1]
  t+54s  chime 2  "BULLS ASSAULT HIGH"   window contains 0.55, 0.55 among 40 battle sounds

(Every length arrives in pairs because the hook sees each start twice; the ratio is what matters, and it is
exactly two horn buffers per chime and none anywhere else.)

THE FIRST VERSION OF THIS PROBE REPORTED "NO HORN" TWICE AND WAS WRONG. It compared a horn count taken at the
poll that noticed the chime with one taken a second later - but the horn is started in the same frame the
chime is counted, so it was already in the first number. A window either side of the banner, and a census of
every length, answers the question the count could not.


THE ROUND TIMER, AND THE CLOCK THAT LIED ABOUT IT (2026-09-20, Daniel's 16:21 letter)

"When the round timer hits 0, the game must end and return to the lobby by itself. It used to. It no longer
does." Two causes. The second one is what he was actually looking at.

1. THE CLIENT'S GATE AND ITS CLOCK ASKED DIFFERENT QUESTIONS. In `SplashScreen.Update` the result-hold clock
   was started from `RunHasEnded` - the core's word OR the client's - while the lobby gate was still handed
   `BlwpNet.Ended` alone. A round the CORE ended with no session word started its five seconds and then never
   took them. Both go through `ShouldReturnToLobby(core, runState, netEnded, ...)` now. PROVED RED first: put
   the old wiring back and 3 of the 5 new tests fail - the timer-alone case, every-outcome-comes-back and the
   hold - while the live-round guard and the client's-own-word case stay green.

2. THE HUD CLOCK WAS NOT THE CORE'S CLOCK, AND THIS IS THE ONE ON SCREEN.

     BlockClock.RunTicks      9000    hand-written in C#
     gate.js BLOCK_TICKS     10800    changed in c01cc655, "a round is three minutes"

   `Remaining = CoreSecondsLeft(elapsed)` counts `RunTicks - elapsed`, so the clock reached 0:00 at elapsed
   9000 and the core does not call the run MISSED until 10800: 1800 ticks - thirty seconds - of every round
   with a timer showing nothing left and a truck still driving. Nothing threw and nothing was red. It is the
   SECOND time this clock has told him the same thing (2026-09-16 15:36, quoted in the file), and the first
   fix was right in shape - make it the core's count - while the number it counted stayed a copy.

   `BLOCK_TICKS` and `RUN_LIVE/DELIVERED/WRECKED/MISSED` are GENERATED into `Blwp.Layout` now, from gate.js,
   the same way the word offsets are. `BlockClockIsTheCoresTests` pins the HUD length against the generated
   one, 0:00 on the ending tick, and three minutes.

   `RunEndsAtDeliveredTests.TheRunClockIsTheCoresOwnCount` had 9000 in five assertions and was GREEN while
   describing a round that had not existed for days. It reads `Blwp.Layout.BLOCK_TICKS` now; every assertion
   means what it meant, and only the duplicated number is gone. That is the shape of this whole entry: a
   number two engines both need is not a number either of them may type.

WHAT THE BROWSER SAID, AND WHY THE FIRST DRIVE SAID NOTHING

  SwiftShader, 1280x800     23 ticks/s     round closed by the node at tick 4588, run VOID at 5004 of 10800
  SwiftShader,  640x400     41 ticks/s     still short of the 60 a round keeps
  ANGLE/Vulkan (RADV RENOIR) 61.4 ticks/s  the core reaches its own block end

  The Beelink has an AMD Renoir the headless browser was not using. On SwiftShader the page walks at most
  `MostTicksPerFrame` = 8 ticks a frame at ~3 fps, so the run always died VOID by the CLIENT's word - the
  path that already worked - before the clock could reach zero. The first drive therefore proved nothing
  about this fix, and said so rather than being written up as a pass.

  On the GPU browser, one round joined and then left alone:

    clock 0:06 at elapsed 10424      (tdrive-before-zero.png)
    clock 0:00 at elapsed 10800      state 0 -> 3 MISSED at the same tick
    lobby back by itself 5 s later   (tdrive-lobby-back.png)
    page: "run ended FINISHED: the core said MISSED at tick 10800"

A PLAYMODE TEST CANNOT CARRY THIS, AND I WROTE ONE BEFORE CHECKING. `BlwpCore.Available` is set by an extern
that exists only in a browser build, so in EditMode and PlayMode there is no core at all and
`TimerEndsTheRoundInThePlayerTests` failed on its first assertion - "the core did not come up". PRIORITIES

THE OTHER HALF OF ITEM 4: CAN A TANK STAND IN THE DRAWN CABLE? (2026-09-20, measured before changing anything)

The item says two things: the truck's roof passes through the tunnel, and "a tank can stand in a drawn cable".
The truck half is fixed and shown on Daily. The tank half needed its own measurement, because the fix for the
truck does nothing for it:

  `st.solids` is consumed in ONE place - `resolveSolids(v, st.solids, ...)` at sim.js:1412, where `v` is the
  vehicle. `resolveArmour` pushes the TRUCK out of tanks, not tanks out of the map. Army units are pushed out of
  CRATERS and off the MAP EDGE (army.js) and nothing else. So the 41 new boxes, `power_cable_0/1` among them,
  cannot stop a tank: armour is not resolved against map solids at all.

SO IS IT REACHABLE? `tools/measure-tank-in-miner.mjs`, 3 seeds x 60 s:

  living tank-ticks                 217757
  standing east of x 100            0   (0.000%)
  inside a drawn miner part         0   (0.000%)

Not one tank in 217757 tank-ticks gets within 8 m of the miner's westernmost drawn part, let alone into a cable.
The army fights at the seam and the seam never reaches the miner's end of the map.

RULED, and this is evidence rather than parking: nothing is missing from item 4. Making armour resolve against
the map's 78 boxes would change tank movement over the WHOLE map - the post office, the edges, every lane - to
close a case that happens 0 times in 217757 tank-ticks. That is its own item if it is ever wanted, with a
whole-map cost, and it is not a hole in this one. The measurement is kept so nobody has to re-derive it.

BOTH ENGINES, in numbers, one more time: C# `DeliveryGate.Slab()` builds 5 BoxColliders and still does; the core
now carries 46 at the miner. The difference is deliberate and safe because NOTHING harvests those colliders -
`WorldSolids.Gather` is called nowhere outside its own file, `BlwpCore` records "SetSolids IS GONE", and
`CoreDrivenTruck` forces the Rigidbody kinematic while the core drives. PhysX has not become the simulator.

THE RUN-STOPPED LINE IN THE BAY: FOUR CAUSES AND THREE BAD INSTRUMENTS (2026-09-20).

A truck still choosing cargo when the block closes is the path that ends VOID, and it is the path where the
player was told nothing. Measured at 1280x800 against the mempool panel's own band (PackageYard panelTop 0.10,
panelBottom 0.51, so y 80..408):

  before   RunStoppedBox y 325.9, height font*2.8 = 67 px   -> inside the panel band, and never drawn anyway
  after    road (panel shut)  y 325.9, height from CalcHeight (>= font*4.4 = 106 px)
           bay  (panel open)  y 422.4 = panel.yMax + font*0.6, height from CalcHeight

FOUR CAUSES, all on the existing DrawRunStopped path - no new card, no second draw, no new ending API:
  1. `OnGUI` returned early on the loading branch - `if (loading) { DrawWasted(); return; }` - so in the bay the
     row was NEVER DRAWN. My first diagnosis was that the panel covered it; the rect arithmetic was true and
     irrelevant. The call simply never happened.
  2. The box sat inside the panel's band, so it needed somewhere to be once it was drawn.
  3. The height was a guessed multiple of the font: font*2.8 cut at "error the round" and lost "is closed";
     font*4.4 reached "cannot publish" and cut there. It is now `style.CalcHeight(line, width)` with the old
     value as a floor - the copy is the client's and is not shortened to fit.
  4. The reason reached the HUD on a 0.5 s poll into a window of 0.6 s, and the result hold was timed from
     `BlwpNet.Ended`, which flips BEFORE the reason exists. So whether the player was told was a coin toss:
     bay-04.png has the line, bayok-27.png and bayfull-29.png are the same state with nothing on screen. Fixed
     by fetching the reason the moment the run ends and starting the hold when the reason is known, with a 2 s
     guard so a reason that never comes can never strand anyone.

I HAD REVERTED (4) EARLIER THE SAME DAY on the strength of a ROAD frame, where the window was 1.2 s and the poll
happened to land. The bay is where it bites. Restored, with the measurement that earns it.

THREE INSTRUMENTS THAT LIED, and they cost more than the code did:
  - the probe never pressed ROLL OUT, so every capture for hours sat in the BAY by accident - which is also how
    the bay case was found at all.
  - it triggered on `BLWP_RUN_ENDED`, set by BLWP_RUN_OVER at onEnd, while C# reads `endingLine()` earlier: the
    hold had already run before the probe saw a word. Replaced by a rolling ring of frames.
  - 20x CPU throttle renders Unity at about 1 fps, so a 0.6 s window drew ZERO frames and produced two "absent"
    pictures that meant nothing. At 5x the page draws and the answer is unambiguous.

"THE VOID REASON IS INVISIBLE" WAS ALREADY DONE, AND THE PREMISE WAS MINE (2026-09-20).

The item said a returned player is never told why a VOID run ended, and that `BlwpNetEnding()` carries the line
while nothing draws it. Both halves are false, and the second one was my own inference from an unmeasured
premise - the same mistake as the lobby "regression" earlier the same day.

WHAT THE PICTURES SHOW. A VOID was forced on purpose by starving one tab (20x CPU throttle) until its round
closed under it, on both builds, same doors, same sequence:

  daniel-screens/before-26.png   build 0.0.1815, BEFORE any change of mine, run ended, lobby still down:
      "RUN STOPPED - the node refuses this run's inputs at tick 9406: error the round"
  daniel-screens/ring-11.png     build 0.0.1818, after a change I later reverted, the same frame:
      "RUN STOPPED - the node refuses this run's inputs at tick 7957: error the round"

Large amber, centred under the block headline, readable at a glance, visible for at least 1.2 s before the lobby
takes the screen - IDENTICAL on both builds. `DriveHud.DrawRunStopped` has been drawing it all along, fed by
`NetSession.Ending` from `BlwpNet.Ending()`. Nothing needed fixing.

WHY I COULD NOT SEE IT, and it took five captures to find out: my probe never pressed ROLL OUT. It clicked AUTO
to load and held the throttle, so the run never started and the truck sat in the BAY for every capture - and in
the bay the LIVE MEMPOOL cargo panel covers exactly the region `RunStoppedBox` occupies, because that box hangs
off `BlockTimerBox` at the top left. A player is on the road, where that region is clear. Load, ROLL OUT, drive
clear, THEN starve the tab.

FOUR PROBE FAULTS IN A ROW, written down so the next one does not repeat them:
  1. polled `BLWP_LOBBY_VIEW`, which only exists while the lobby is up - every sample read "?".
  2. read `BLWP_UNITY_LOBBY.showing` at t+0, which still held TRUE from the page being replaced.
  3. triggered on `BLWP_RUN_ENDED`, which `BLWP_RUN_OVER` sets at `onEnd` - by then the hold has already run,
     because C# reads `endingLine()` earlier. Fixed by a rolling ring of frames instead of a trigger.
  4. stopped on ANY ending, so a run that merely FINISHED was taken as the before-frame for a VOID.

WHAT I CHANGED AND THEN REVERTED. Believing the row absent, I made `NetSession` fetch the reason the moment the
run ends instead of on its 0.5 s poll, and made the result hold start when the reason is known rather than when
`BlwpNet.Ended` flips, with a 2 s guard so a missing reason could never strand anyone. Both are defensible
readings of the code and NEITHER changed what the player sees: before-26 and ring-11 are the same picture. Per
the ruling - if the line is already readable, commit nothing extra - the change is reverted and the Daily rebuilt
from the tree, so what is served is what is committed.

LISTED, SMALL, NOT FIXED HERE: the line is CLIPPED mid-sentence on both builds. It ends at "error the round" and
loses "is closed", because `RunStoppedBox` is `font * 2.8` tall and the third line is cut. Placement on the
existing path, worth a line of its own rather than being smuggled into a closed item.

THE VOID FIX, MEASURED LIVE (2026-09-20, Daily 0.0.1815, two real browser tabs, cache cleared, Network on).

  number                        before (0.0.1812)      after (0.0.1815)
  tab A back at the lobby       ~t+300 s               t+225 s / t+290 s
  tab B back at the lobby       NEVER                  t+235 s / t+275 s
  runs ending VOID              1 every run            0
  round two joined              never reached          BOTH tabs, POST /round 201 + POST /entry 201 on both doors
  round two, each sees the other -                     others 1 on both; A drew 173 pictures, B drew 165
  overlay age in round two      29564 ms and climbing  12-632 ms (A), 13-617 ms (B)
  loadingFailed                 0                      0

Two runs after the fix, and the tab that comes back first is not fixed: A then B in one, B then A in the other.
Nothing voided in either. Round two now publishes from both sides - `others 1` with pictures accumulating on each
tab - which is the number the parked item named as 0 at ticks 300 through 1500.

STILL THERE, SMALLER, AND NOT THIS FIX'S TO CLOSE: the clocks still drift. In round two A reads B at -399 to -631
ticks and B reads A at +601 to +793 - about 10 to 13 s, against the 33 s that used to strand a tab. The drift is
what put a client past its round's close in the first place; the fix stops it STRANDING anyone, it does not stop
it happening. Both pages report `this frame 333 ms` - two headless browsers and two WebGL cores on one MacBook,
about 3 fps each - so a share of it is the measuring rig, not the protocol. Left listed rather than guessed at.

THE FIX ITSELF: SplashScreen started the return-to-lobby clock only from the CORE's word, or from a page with no
core at all. A VOID is neither - the core is present and silent at RunState 0 - so `_endedAt` was reset every
frame, `sinceOutcome` stayed 0, `BackToLobby` could never come true, and the tab sat with its truck locked.

  RunHasEnded(coreAvailable, runState, netEnded) => (coreAvailable && runState != 0) || netEnded

Settlement is untouched and VOID is not an escape hatch: the run is already over and already VOID by the time
this is asked; it only decides when the screen comes back. The 5 s result hold stays a separate rule and is
asserted separately. Guarded by VoidReturnsToLobbyTests (5 tests) and PROVED RED first - the old rule fails
exactly AVoidRunEndsEvenThoughTheCoreNeverNamedAnOutcome and leaves the other four green.

THE GHOSTS BUG IS A CLOCK, NOT A FETCH (2026-09-20, two reproductions on Daily 0.0.1812).

The parked line said one tab's round-two session "died on Failed to fetch - a call refused outright". Measured,
that is false, and it is corrected in PRIORITIES rather than left standing.

METHOD, after three probes that measured nothing and are worth naming so the next one does not repeat them:
  - probe 1 polled `window.BLWP_LOBBY_VIEW`, which only exists while the lobby is up, so every sample read "?".
  - probe 2 clicked PLAY blind: both tabs sat in the free world, 0 requests to either signer door, console at
    tick ~45000 reporting 27434 ticks jumped. Nothing about a round could be concluded from it.
  - probe 3 read `BLWP_UNITY_LOBBY.showing` at t+0, which still held TRUE from the page being replaced, and
    clicked into a still-booting page. `rows=none` beside `showing=true` was the contradiction to catch.
  - probes 1-3 also all used a cache-busting query string, which is its own fault - see the separate item.
  The working shape: bare URL, `Network.clearBrowserCache`, settle 15 s, require `showing` AND at least one round
  row on BOTH tabs before clicking, then VERIFY the join by counting requests to the trycloudflare doors before
  believing anything.

WHAT TWO CLEAN RUNS SHOW, two real browser tabs, cache cleared, Network on:

  requests                     1151 (A) / 940 (B),  signer-door requests 1001 / 811
  loadingFailed                0 / 0        "Failed to fetch"   0 / 0
  non-200 from a signer door   POST /name 409 (join-time name conflict, retries to 201)
                               POST /round 201, POST /entry 201 - nothing else

  A reads B   own tick 10800, newest other picture 8807, BEHIND 1993 ticks
  B reads A   own tick 9900,  newest other picture 10799, behind -899 - its own FUTURE
              collapsed 19, then silenced 1, overlay age 1974 -> 11449 -> 20640 -> 29564 ms
  B ends      [blwp] run ended VOID: the node refuses this run's inputs at tick 8576 (9708 in the first run):
              error the round is closed - and it still refused after resyncing, so this client cannot publish
  A returns to the lobby at about t+300 s. B never returns at all.

So the node ANSWERS. Nothing is refused outright. A client that has fallen about 33 s behind keeps playing past
the round's close, its inputs are refused for that reason, the run is VOIDed, it publishes nothing more and it is
left on a dead screen while the other player is already back in the lobby choosing round two. That is the whole
"round two has one invisible truck": there is no second truck publishing, because that client never left round
one.

Deterministic, not a flake: identical across both runs, the same tab stuck, the same shape - A back at the lobby
at ~t+300 s, B never.

THE LOBBY WAS NEVER BROKEN; MY VIEW OF IT WAS (2026-09-20, after the 0.0.1812 deploy).

I reported a regression - "the lobby has no infographics" - and offered three fixes for it. There was no
regression, and the report was wrong. What happened:

  - The headless Chrome on the MacBook had been parked on the Daily since BEFORE the deploy, and `shot.mjs` never
    cleared the cache. `Network.setCacheDisabled` in a later probe only covers requests made after it is set.
  - That view could not reach the signer doors, so the lobby came up with NO ROUNDS: no identity line, no FREE
    row, no PAID row - only the how-to text and PLAY/SPECTATE. A lobby with nothing to join still looks like a
    lobby, and I read the empty one as the whole one.
  - One `Network.clearBrowserCache` on the SAME build and the same URL produced the whole lobby: daily.json 200,
    both trycloudflare doors 200, four `round?id=...` 200, the four how-to panels drawn, the identity line, and
    FREE / PAID rows. Daniel's phone had been showing that all along.

THE LESSON, and it is a probe lesson, not a product one: clear the browser cache before screenshotting a page to
judge a deploy by. A stale Unity build plus unreachable nodes is indistinguishable from a regression at a glance.

WHAT IS NOW GUARDED (Assets/Tests/EditMode/LobbyShowsUpTests.cs, 4 tests, EditMode 261/265):
  - `TheLiveDailyPayloadComesUpAsAWholeLobby` - the fixture is `window.BLWP_LOBBY_VIEW()` read off the LIVE Daily
    at 0.0.1812 over CDP, ids and hostnames as they came. It asserts the lobby comes up whole: from daily.json,
    the identity and its fingerprint, exactly one FREE and one PAID row, both 2-of-2 agreed and joinable with
    entry time left, no refused and no silent node - and that PLAY picks the FREE round.
  - `ALobbyThatReachedNoSignerNodeIsEmptyAndSaysSo` - the shape I misread. It still parses as a lobby, because the
    player must get a screen, but rows are empty, nodes is 0, the silent nodes are NAMED, PickDefault is -1 and
    `UnansweredLine` is not empty. The two states are now pinned apart.
  - `ARoundOneSignerNodeShortIsNeverWhatPlayJoins` - a 1-of-2 round with more time left is still never joined.
  - `TheLobbyKeepsItsHowToArt` - the how-to sheet is in Resources.

HONEST LIMIT OF THOSE TESTS: they are parse-level and run on a fixture. They pin the healthy lobby's shape and
separate it from the empty one, so a future screenshot showing no rounds can be diagnosed instead of guessed at.
They CANNOT tell that the live Daily's signer nodes are down - only a cleared-cache load against the live page
does that, which is what should have been done before calling it a regression.
