§11.4 ON SCREEN: THE SINK IS GONE IN A BROWSER, NOT ONLY IN THE FIXTURE (2026-09-20).

A green EditMode guard is not an on-screen check, so the letter was not closed on one. Two WebGL builds were made
from the same tree, differing only in `SoldierLift`, and both were read over CDP on the MacBook against the live
feed. The renderer reads the value back OFF THE TRANSFORM (`t.position.y - Ground(at.x, at.z)`) rather than
restating the arithmetic, and logs it beside the count that was already there:

  BEFORE  [render] downed men sit -0.73 m over the ground, worst -0.75 m; standing men 0.12 m; prefab yes
  AFTER   [render] downed men sit  0.02 m over the ground, worst  0.00 m; standing men 0.13 m; prefab yes

  `worst` is a MINIMUM over every downed man on the field, so 0.00 is the stronger statement a per-kind mean would
  not give: no man is under the ground anywhere - candle lip, crater rim or wreck - which are the same three kinds
  the fixture measured at 0.74 / 0.74 / 0.68 m.

  Standing men sit +0.12 m and that is not an error: a walking man BOBS (|sin(tick x 0.08 + i)| x 0.16, mean about
  0.10) and is seated on the highest ground his feet cover. A downed man does not bob - by design, the bob is a
  walking cue - which is why his number falls to ~0.00 rather than ~0.12.

  `prefab yes` is in the line on purpose. The scene ships `soldierPrefab: {fileID: 0}`; `Bootstrap.cs:879` copies
  its own unset field, and the only other writer is `ModelStreamer.cs:166-168`, which fetches `model/soldier` and
  calls `SetSoldierPrefab`. So a build STARTS on the centre-anchored box path and switches to the sole-anchored
  prefab path once the model streams in. Without that flag the same reading could have been taken on the box, at
  its legitimate +0.15, and proved nothing. This was checked BEFORE the build, not after.

THE SUNK MEN ARE THE PRONE DROP, NOT THE CRATER BOWL (2026-09-20, measured before any code change).

The named first blocker was "Unity carves a crater bowl the core does not, so men correctly standing in holes draw
below the mesh". Measured, that cause is FALSE in both halves, and the entry above dated with the cover letters is
wrong where it says otherwise.

1. UNITY CARVES NO BOWL. `MempoolTerrain.HeightAt` (MempoolTerrain.cs:302) returns `Blwp.BlwpCore.TerrainAt`
   whenever there is a core, and `terrainAt` in the core already has `craterCut` subtracted (sim.js:745). The
   crater-reveal loop (MempoolTerrain.cs:386-393) then assigns `h = BlwpCore.TerrainAt(wx, wz)` - the value it
   already held. It is a no-op, and the mesh is the core's terrain everywhere, not only inside a revealed crater.
   `BlwpCore.CraterAt` never exposes C_D at all, so Unity cannot know a bowl depth even if it wanted one.

2. THE THREE HEIGHTS, under men standing on a hole, 2 seeds x 40 s, 20550 man-ticks (`scratchpad/heights.mjs`):

     place kind    n       core ground   Unity terrain   visible surface   man drawn Y   sunk below visible
     candle lip  19187        0.87           0.39             0.87            0.12            0.74 m
     crater rim   1251       -0.02          -0.02            -0.02           -0.76            0.74 m
     wreck         112        0.55           0.55             0.55           -0.13            0.68 m

   Unity terrain equals core ground exactly except under a candle lip, where the 0.48 m difference is the candle
   ribbon - and the candles are drawn by their own mesh standing up to `surfaceAt`, so the VISIBLE surface there
   is the core ground too. The sink is the same 0.74 m on all three kinds, including the 93.4% of on-hole men who
   are nowhere near a crater.

3. THE CAUSE. ArmyRenderer.cs:929-940: `lift = soldierPrefab != null ? 0f : 0.9f`, then `if (down) lift -=
   soldierProneDrop` (0.75, ArmyRenderer.cs:53). ArmyRenderer.cs:265 wraps the prefab with `WrapOnItsSole`, so the
   transform origin is the man's SOLES, and Bootstrap.cs:879 assigns that prefab in a real build. A standing man
   is therefore at ground + 0, and a DOWN man at ground - 0.75: his feet are driven underground instead of his
   body being laid flat. The 0.75 was tuned for the fallback BOX, whose origin is its centre and whose standing
   lift is 0.9 - there the same subtraction lands at +0.15, which is about right. The scene itself has
   `soldierPrefab: {fileID: 0}`, which is also why ImportedModelTests.SoldiersStandOnTheGroundAndAreAnimated fails
   on its FIRST assert ("die Szene hat kein Soldatenmodell zugewiesen") and never reaches its sink check.

4. THE SHARE, in the form asked for: the crater-bowl mismatch accounts for **0.00 m of the 0.74 m** that is
   missing - 0% of it. It is not most of the sink; it is none of it. 98.9% of men standing on a hole are DOWN, so
   the prone drop accounts for essentially all of it.

5. THE FIX (ruled the same day, prefab path only). `ArmyRenderer.SoldierLift(down, hasPrefab, proneDrop)` is now
   one pure function: sole-anchored prefab men get 0 whether they stand or lie, and the centre-anchored fallback
   box keeps 0.9 standing and 0.9 - 0.75 = 0.15 down, exactly as before. The same fixture re-run, 2 seeds x 40 s:

     place kind    n      core ground   Unity terrain   visible surface   drawn BEFORE   sunk   drawn AFTER   sunk
     candle lip  19187       0.87          0.39             0.87             0.12       0.74      0.87       0.00
     crater rim   1251      -0.02         -0.02            -0.02            -0.76       0.74     -0.02       0.00
     wreck         112       0.55          0.55             0.55            -0.13       0.68      0.55       0.00

   The probe MIRRORS the renderer's arithmetic rather than observing it, and that is why the guard matters:
   Assets/Tests/EditMode/SoldierLiftTests.cs calls `SoldierLift` itself, needs no core, and therefore runs where
   PostureDrawTests has to Assert.Ignore. PROVED RED BEFORE IT WAS KEPT - restoring the old
   `(hasPrefab ? 0 : 0.9) - (down ? drop : 0)` fails ASoleAnchoredManIsDrawnOnTheGroundStandingOrDown and
   NoManIsEverDrawnBelowTheGroundHeStandsOn while TheFallbackBoxKeepsTheNumbersItWasTunedFor still passes.

   EditMode 257 of 261, 3 skipped, 1 red (the long-listed CombatFx rifle flash), 0 error CS - three tests more
   than before, which are the three new guards. PlayMode 230 of 257, 14 skipped, 13 red - one FEWER than before,
   PostOfficeTests.TheGogglesAnimate being green this run. ImportedModelTests.SoldiersStandOnTheGroundAndAreAnimated
   is still red and still cannot see this fix: it stops on its FIRST assert because the scene carries
   `soldierPrefab: {fileID: 0}`, and in the editor the core is stubbed and no men are drawn at all.

   This letter did not create the fault and did not deepen it. It made it more visible: man-ticks on a hole went
   2.9% -> 6.4%.

NOTE ON WHY UNITY CANNOT MEASURE THIS ITSELF: in EditMode and PlayMode `BlwpCore.Available` is false, the core is
stubbed, `HasSurface` is false and the terrain falls back to the mempool relief while ArmyRenderer draws no men at
all - the same reason the pose test is Assert.Ignore. The three heights above are computed from the core plus the
renderer's own arithmetic, with every term read out of the files and cited by line. They are not sampled from a
running editor, and that is stated rather than glossed.

§11.3 OCCUPANCY - THE POST THE CLAIM PASS MEASURED FROM WAS NOT THE POST THE STEP WALKS TO (2026-09-20).

The row stood at 64.6% against a 70% bar that was not loosened. Daniel's accepted sequence was: cite the printed
failing-tick split, measure the 12 m reach per man, measure a claim from take to end, and only then - if they name
a SINGLE cause - a core fix.

1. THE SHARE, already printed and not re-litigated: of the 1698 failing ticks, 100% hold an UNPINNED man with a
   claim about 8.9 m from his hole, and freezing every crawler clears none of them. Crawl is a ceiling of 24.1
   points and is not the cause.

2. THE 12 m REACH FROM HIS POST, unpinned men on failing ticks, 2 seeds x 40 s, 89240 man-ticks
   (`tools/measure-reach-and-claims.mjs`):

     NO place within 12 m of his post          8800  ( 9.9%)
     a place in reach, and he HOLDS a claim   31866  (35.7%)
     a place in reach, he holds NOTHING       48574  (54.4%)
     nearest place to his POST                mean 7.5 m, median 7.4 m

   So reach is NOT the binding constraint: nine men in ten have a place inside 12 m of their post. The refusal
   splits three ways, and the third is the one that matters:

     outside his clamp [seam - 40, seam + 8]  16222  (33.4%)
     inside 3 m of a living tank                239  ( 0.5%)
     ELIGIBLE and still not claimed           32113  (66.1%)

3. A CLAIM FROM TAKE TO END, every man over the run (144 men):

     men who never held a claim at all          42  (29.2%)
     men who NEVER once arrived on a hole      132  (91.7%)
     claims taken, per man that took any       mean 1.6, overwritten under him 0.0
     share of a man's living ticks holding one 38.4%,  ON a hole 2.9%

   One column in that print was badly chosen and is reported as such, not as a finding: "could he cross it this
   tick" is 0 for everyone by construction, because a gait of 0.046 m a tick can never cover a remaining distance
   in one tick. It measures the tick length, not the man.

4. THREE CANDIDATE CAUSES MEASURED AND CLOSED before the real one was named:
     - a PHANTOM wreck (the core calls a hull a wreck on U_STATE alone, the row's place list also wants HP <= 0):
       30 of 14756 wreck claims, 0.2%. Of 115200 hull-ticks, 22298 were state 0 and NOT ONE had HP left. Closed.
     - the place MOVING under him (a candle lip's world x is CL_X less the scroll): 0.0000 m a tick for all three
       kinds, and the gap to it CLOSES at 0.024 to 0.035 m a tick. He walks in. Closed.
     - the walk being too slow: no. The gap closes; he simply never gets there in time.

5. THE CAUSE, and it is one thing. §11.3 measures eligibility "from his POST, not his feet" - the ruling Daniel
   kept - but the claim pass and the step did not mean the same post. The pass took the man's OWN squad anchor at
   a bare RIFLE_STANDOFF; the step walks him to his FIRE TEAM's anchor (§9.2) at his own scattered stand-off less
   §12.1's push. Measured, 2 seeds x 40 s, 318644 man-ticks:

     man -> the point the claim pass called his post   median 46.3 m, mean 47.3 m, p90 79.7
     man-ticks ever within 2 m of it                   783  (0.2%)
     men who ever came within 2 m of it once           6 of 144
     POST -> the place, while he holds one             mean 25.6 m   (the rule admits 12)
     man -> the place, while he holds one              mean 39.7 m, median 38.9

   So "within 12 m of his post" drew its circle round a point no man stands on, and handed him a hole a median
   38.9 m from his feet - a 14 to 28 s walk. A claim lives 12.8 s. It ends: the man died 60.2%, the place stopped
   existing 27.8%, a living tank came inside 3 m of it 12.0%, overwritten 0.0%. Nobody arrives, and that is the
   row.

6. THE FIX, in the right units and taking no draw: `rifleStandoff(index, infPush)` is now ONE function in
   army.js, called by the walk and by the claim pass, and the pass reads the fire team's anchor and `pushNear`
   exactly as the step does. Nothing about §11.3's rule changed - eligibility is still measured from his post,
   and a held claim is still not re-measured for distance. The post simply became the post he is walking to.
   DO NOT SPLIT THEM AGAIN, the same way chart.js and the war share `trendCandle`.

     §11.3 occupancy   64.6%  ->  91.7%   against a 70% bar, not loosened   (2 seeds x 40 s)

   AND WHAT THAT ROW IS NOT, said plainly: it counts a TICK in which ANY living man of a side stands within 0.5 m
   of any place of his side. It is not the share of men in cover. Per man over the same run the numbers moved but
   are far smaller - living ticks ON a hole 2.9% -> 6.4%, men who never once arrived 91.7% -> 84.7%, men who never
   held a claim at all 29.2% -> 24.3%. The bar the spec sets is the tick-level one and it is met honestly; a
   per-man bar would not be met, and nobody should read 91.7% as "91.7% of men are in cover".
     claims that ever reached 0.5 m of their place    7.5%  ->  15.1%
     failing ticks                                     400 of 4800, and every one holds a walker still closing

7. WHAT THE FIX MOVED, and neither number was tuned:
   - §4.12's assault witness 8 -> 10. Every clause of §4.12 still passed on the run that moved it; only the count
     did. Re-measured per seed: bulls 0/0/0/2/2, bears 2/1/2/0/1. More men reach cover, more men live, survivors
     hold objectives, and an assault clock reads the holder. The comment beside the assert carries the cause.
   - rules.test "replacements keep both armies in contact" went RED, and it is LISTED, NOT FIXED AND NOT TUNED.

THE CONTACT RED, measured rather than argued (seed 20260901, the test's own scenario):

     HEAD                                  5 bull tanks v 11 bear at t=90   (floor is 4 a side: passes)
     with this fix                         3 v 12                           (fails)
     the same fight with the trend neutral 6 v 12                           (would pass)

   The test flattens the tape - `st.tape.fill(st.tape[0])` - to get a symmetric fight, because "comparing a fight
   offset by twenty-seven metres against a symmetric one is not a comparison". But it steps with no market tick,
   so `readMarket` never runs, and MK_TREND keeps the value `init` gave it from the SEEDED tape: DOWN, strength 2,
   unchanged for all 90 s. The bears are favoured for the whole run - a 30-60 s assault clock against 45-90, +1
   lane weight, a ceiling raised by 8 x strength. The bull side was already collapsing at HEAD, 12 tanks to 5;
   this fix makes the men better at using cover, which amplifies the side already favoured, and 5 becomes 3.
   RULED AND DONE (Daniel, 2026-09-20): fix the SETUP only. `tactics.readMarket(st.i32, O_TACTICS, st.tape)` now
   runs once after the fill, so both sides see the same flat market. The floor of 4 is untouched, nothing the test
   asserts is changed, and the only line added is the one that makes the fixture's own stated premise true.

     with the trend frozen as init read it   3 bull tanks v 12 bear at t=90   RED
     with the trend read off the flat tape   6 bull tanks v 12 bear at t=90   GREEN,  rules 50/50

   The general lesson, which is not confined to this fixture: flattening the tape does NOT neutralise §4.14.
   `init` reads MK_TREND off the seeded tape, and a fixture that never ticks the market never revises it. Any
   test that wants a symmetric fight has to read the trend off the tape it actually runs on.

§11.3 COVER - THE MEASUREMENT BEFORE THE WORK (2026-09-19, on the tree deployed at 0.0.1739).

WHAT THE OLD ARMY DOES ABOUT COVER: nothing, and that is a statement, not a run. §11.3 is a declared GAP ("GAP,
all of it"), the earlier no-cover ruling is overruled, and the only C# artefact in this area is `AvoidWrecks`,
which pushes a man OUT of a crater - the inverse of this letter. It is already in the core, where it belongs, for
tanks: it is what the crater-post rule of 15:57 works against. Porting it for men would port the fault the ruling
overturned. There is nothing to compare because the recording has no cover; spending a run to measure zero would
be theatre.

1. MEN LOST PER SIDE PER 60 s, five seeds x 180 s, by cause (`tools/measure-fodder.mjs`):

     no nukes submitted      mean 34.0 a side      fire 23.2%   bomb 76.8%   nuke 0%
     a nuke every 30 s       mean 43.1 a side      fire  9.2%   bomb 39.4%   nuke 51.4%

   §0's bar is <= 20. The 2026-09-16 figure in the spec (26.5 to 41.5, mean 32.7) is NOT today's: it predates the
   seeded tape, the hull rectangle, the dock clamp, the world grown east and the lethal nuke. Today's number is
   34.0 without nukes and 43.1 with them, and the shape has changed more than the total - three quarters of
   infantry deaths are now the gunships' bombs, and with nukes landing half are the nuke.

2. COVER'S ROOM, three seeds x 120 s with a nuke every 30 s (`tools/measure-cover-baseline.mjs`):

     places standing, mean per tick                    30.5
     ticks with a place within 12 m of a man           96.9%
     ticks with a man ON a place (within 0.5 m)         1.0%   <- the GAP, and the 1% is accident
     men killed by fire                                  54
     ...with a free place within 12 m when they died      21   (38.9%)

   Two simplifications, both stated, both making the denominator LARGER than the spec's, so the conclusions below
   are ceilings: candle lips are not counted as places (their geometry scrolls with the chart), and the 12 m is
   measured from where the man stands rather than from his post.

3. THE SHARE, in metres rather than adjectives. Cover is one of three (§11.3 cover, §11.4 posture, §11.5
   suppression) and §0 grades the three with two rows.

   - "Wrecks and craters are used" (>= 70% of the ticks where a place is free within 12 m of a post, a man is on
     one): today 1.0% against a 70% bar, with the room available on 96.9% of ticks. THIS LETTER CAN CLOSE IT, and
     it is entirely undone.
   - "Not cannon fodder" (<= 20 lost a side per 60 s; and STAND deaths >= 2x PRONE + COVER together): the second
     clause cannot exist before §11.4 writes the postures and their hit thresholds. The first clause is 34.0 / 43.1
     against 20.

   What cover can reach of today's losses: fire is 23.2% of deaths without nukes and 9.2% with them, and 38.9% of
   fire deaths had a place within 12 m. So cover alone touches at most 9.0% of infantry deaths in the quiet world
   and 3.6% in the world a player drives through. The rest is bombs and nukes, which clear circles: §11.3 itself
   says a bomb "does not wound a rifleman, it clears the circle", and the nuke kills everything in its blast by
   the 15:55 ruling. NO AMOUNT OF COVER BRINGS 43.1 UNDER 20. Saying otherwise before building it would be the
   stale-number fault in a new coat.

4. THE PORT PLAN, and it is not a port - there is nothing to port. All of it in packages/core, integer fixed-point,
   no draw, no truck:

   - `TAC_COVER`, 72 words appended to O_TACTICS, laid out ONCE with §11.4's posture bits reserved in the high
     bits, so the next letter does not reshape the state and regenerate goldens a second time.
   - Places as pure functions of the state: a wreck's two, a crater's four (four sin/cos constants in Q16.16), a
     candle lip's one every 4 m. Each a function of (state, side) alone, so every node computes the same bits.
   - Eligibility as §11.3 states it: within 12 m of the man's POST (18 m for the side the trend runs against),
     inside his clamp, not within 3 m of a living tank.
   - Claims: the living men of a side visited in `mix(seedHash, 600 + index)` order, each keeping an eligible free
     claim or taking the nearest, ties by the place's own order. No draw is taken, so no stream shifts.
   - The walk: his own gait to the place when his fire team's clock says rush; COVER once within 0.5 m; the place
     is his post while he holds the claim.

   WOULD THE PLAYER SEE IT? Not yet, and that is worth saying plainly: with the hit thresholds of §11.4 absent, a
   man in cover is shot exactly as often as a man in the open, so the only visible change is where the men stand.
   The row goes green, the killing does not change, and the value arrives with §11.4.

§11.5 SUPPRESSION - WRITTEN, NOT CLOSED (2026-09-20). The pin row is INSIDE its ceiling at 43.8% per team;
what is open is §0's 0.01 m clause and the cover row this letter knocked down. Five seeds x 180 s, frozen tape, a
nuke every 30 s, `tools/measure-suppression.mjs`.

THE WRITE. TAC_SUPP, one word per fire team, 18 appended after §11.3's cover words: TAC_WORDS 212 -> 230. No new
bit in TAC_COVER and no posture value changed. +60 per round aimed at a team's living man (hit or miss), -1 a
tick, clamped [0, 600]; under fire above 0, pinned at 120. A pinned team does not rush; a pinned man crawls at
0.5 m/s toward his claimed place or his post, which is the same walk to the same target at a sixth of the pace and
not a second movement path - at 0.0083 m a tick it sits under §11.4's 0.01 m step probe, so a pinned man is never
STAND by the number already in the core. A pinned man's reload draw is taken as always and doubled. A suppressing
round takes the look-again draw he was already taking, so the draw count does not move. A bomb adds 300 to every
team with a living man inside 16 m.

3. THE RESIDUAL AS IT WAS FIRST READ - SUPERSEDED BY 3a, kept because the arithmetic in it is true and useful even
   though the conclusion was wrong. NOTHING WAS RETUNED THEN AND NOTHING IS NOW. The arithmetic is the reason and it is in §11.5's own
   numbers: decay is 1 a tick, which is 60 a second, and one round is +60. So a SINGLE shooter landing one round a
   second on a team holds that team at break-even forever, and the pin threshold is only two rounds. The half-rate
   doubles a pinned man's RELOAD, but a suppressing round is fired on the LOOK-AGAIN clock (0.4-1.1 s), which
   §11.5 does not halve - so a pinned man with no target still suppresses roughly once a second. With men of both
   sides inside 34 m of each other along the whole seam, the word saturates and never decays below 120.

   +60, -1 and 120 are §11.5's own numbers and are left exactly as written. The row stays LISTED as over its
   ceiling with this cause. Changing any of the three to paint it green would be tuning the rule to the row.

3b. TWO THINGS I RAISED AGAINST THIS WRITE, and BOTH ARE NOW ANSWERED (2026-09-20) - one was a real fault, the
   other was my misreading. Kept in full because the second is the more useful record.

   (a) A PINNED MAN READS STAND ON FOUR TICKS IN FIVE. §0: "a pinned man is never STAND and never steps more than
   0.01 m in a tick (a crawl)". The crawl is 0.5 m/s = 0.00833 m a tick and §11.4's probe is 0.01 m, so the write
   claimed a pinned man is never STAND "by the number already in the core". That reasoning was wrong: x and z are
   steered by SEPARATE controllers and the probe reads |dx| + |dz|, so a diagonal crawl spends the budget twice.
   Measured, two seeds x 40 s:

     pinned man-ticks                   133536
       stepped more than 0.01 m         105381  (78.9%)
       written STAND while pinned       106402  (79.7%)

   Every suite is green through it because nothing asserts that row. WOULD MEASURE AFTER A FIX: cap the crawl on
   the STEP rather than per axis (|dx| + |dz| <= 0.00833), then require 0 pinned man-ticks over 0.01 m and 0
   written STAND, excluding respawn walk-ins - the 166.8 m worst step in the table above is a replacement entering
   from the back edge, not a crawl - and re-read the pinned share and rifle volume, since a slower effective crawl
   moves where men end up.

   (b) RETRACTED 2026-09-20, AND IT WAS NEVER A HOLE. I read §11.5's "it may halt when the pinned team's CLOCK
   says halt" as "the neighbour test must read the clock, not the pin", and called the code wrong. Daniel ruled the
   other reading and it is the right one: the covering team is the one ON THE GROUND, so a pinned team must LOOK
   HALTED to its neighbour even when its own timer would have it rushing. The clock sentence is permission to halt
   during the covering phase, not an instruction to ignore the pin.

   MEASURED rather than argued (tools/measure-pin-profile.mjs, five seeds x 180 s):

     pinned team-ticks                                426193
       seen as halted by the neighbour                426193  (100.0%)
       NOT seen as halted                                  0  (0.0%)
       ...of those, the clock would have had it RUSHING 368547 (86.5%)

   The last line is the rule working: on 86.5% of pinned team-ticks the timer says rush and the pin holds the team
   down anyway. No code changed. My diagnosis was the error, not the core.

   A third, latent and harmless today: `u.pinned` is written only inside the !armour branch of a reused scratch
   object, so for a tank it holds the previous man's value. The gait tests `u.armour` first so nothing reads it,
   but it is a stale field waiting for its first reader.

3g. IS §11.5 DEPLOYABLE, AND IS IT PLAYABLE ON ITS OWN? No to both, and the second answer matters more.

   NOT SEPARATELY SHIPPABLE. The goldens are deliberately stale and the core hash unpinned, so signer nodes would
   refuse the round; that regeneration is ruled to belong to the deploy which ships cover, posture and suppression
   TOGETHER, so §11.5 cannot go out by itself even when it is finished.

   NOT VISIBLE EITHER, which is the part worth writing down. The renderer does not read TAC_COVER, so a PINNED man
   crawling on his belly at 0.5 m/s is drawn walking upright, exactly like a man who is not pinned. Suppression is
   entirely in the numbers: a player watching the field would see men move more slowly and die less, with no
   posture, no going to ground, and no sign of why. Men in holes also still draw below the mesh, so the one thing
   cover DOES change on screen currently reads as broken.

   So on screen today §11.5 changes nothing a player could see, while the cover row it knocked down IS visible as
   fewer men in holes. That is the wrong way round, and it is the argument for the renderer work being the next
   player-facing thing after this block closes - it is listed as a deploy stop, not as part of any letter.

3j. THE COURIER SHELL PINS TOO (2026-09-20), and the first test I wrote for it was worthless.

   §11.5 pins "a man" within 8 m of where a shell lands and never asks what it was aimed at. It names the truck
   exactly once, to keep a SUPPRESSING ROUND off it - the opposite case - which is how the section says so when it
   means it. The core's connect split into an onCourier branch and the rest, and the pin went only into the rest,
   so men standing beside a truck under tank fire were completely unsuppressed.

   NO DRIVE COULD SHOW IT. Every 180 s drive passes zero input, so `rolledOut` is false, `onCourier` is never true
   and the branch never runs. The case had to be constructed.

   THE FIRST CONSTRUCTED TEST PASSED WITHOUT THE RULE, which is worth more than the fix. Men stood beside the
   truck in the middle of the line were also inside 8 m of other tanks taking shells and inside rifle range of the
   enemy, so +60 arrived from somewhere else on every connect. Clearing the field - one firing tank, one distant
   foe to give its gun a target it would pass over for the truck, four men of one team, everything else dead - it
   STILL passed, because latching `rolledOut` also lets the gunships fly and a blast is +300. Only when the assert
   was narrowed to exactly one round's worth did it fail, and the rises it printed said why:

     rises seen: 0,0,300,0,0,0,0,0,0,300,-1,-1,-1,300,-1,0,0

   Three bombs and a lot of decay; never a 60. With the rule in, the same test passes.

   THE RULE IS NOW ONE FUNCTION. `pinTeamsWithin(s, x, z, reach, amount)` marks every team with a living man in
   reach and adds the amount ONCE PER TEAM; the hull shell, the courier shell and the blast all go through it, so
   they cannot drift apart. The blast's own test was `blastReach`, which is axis-reject then length2 against
   BOMB_RADIUS - identical to the helper's, so unifying it changed no behaviour.

   candles+chart+spawn 18/18, canonical group 22/22, vectors+bundle 2/20 with goldens deliberately stale.

3m. THE PIN IS NO LONGER INVISIBLE (2026-09-20). ArmyRenderer read neither TAC_COVER nor TAC_SUPP, so a man
   crawling on his belly at 0.5 m/s was drawn walking upright and the whole of suppression was invisible.

   WHAT CHANGED, all of it client-side and read-only: the layout generator now emits §11.4's posture constants and
   §11.5's suppression constants to BlwpLayout.cs; BlwpCore gains `UnitPosture(i)` and `UnitPinned(i)`, which read
   words and decide nothing; ArmyRenderer poses from `posture != STAND` - the man drops `soldierProneDrop` and
   pitches `soldierPronePitch` along the way he was facing, does not bob, and his animator Speed goes to 0. The
   Rigidbody stays kinematic with gravity off and there is no PhysX knock; nothing was taken from Army.cs.

   NO CORE FILE CHANGED. `git status` shows packages/core/src and packages/core/test untouched this turn, so
   cover occupancy and STAND-while-pinned cannot have moved - they are the same 64.6% and 0.2% as before, by
   construction rather than by re-running them.

   THE MEASUREMENT CORRECTED ITSELF TWICE, and that is the record worth keeping:
     first tool: looked one tick after a cab hit and reported 8 of 8 men drawn UPRIGHT, reading as a renderer
       fault. It was not. A shell is +60 and the pin line is 120 - §11.5's own "two rounds to pin from cold" -
       so ONE cab hit never pins anybody. The tool was measuring a team under fire, not a pinned one.
     second tool: waited for the word to cross 120 and found NO men at all, because two shells must land inside
       60 ticks of each other and one tank reloads in 150-270. A SINGLE TANK CANNOT PIN A TEAM BY SHELLING THE
       CAB. It takes a second shooter, or a word already part-way up.

   So the dramatic case - a man pinned by a shell on the cab - is real but needs two shells inside a second. The
   chain the renderer depends on is the general one and is already measured: of 138119 pinned man-ticks, 214

3o. WHAT THE OCCUPANCY COUNTER HOLDS ON THE TICKS IT FAILS (2026-09-20). The story "pinned men crawl and cannot
   reach their holes" had been printed twice without being broken down. Broken down, IT IS NOT THE STORY.

   The counter, read from tactics.test.js rather than assumed: a tick counts when ANY living man of a side is
   within 0.5 m of ANY place of his side. A failing tick is one where NOT ONE man on the field is on a place.

     ticks with a man on a place    3102 of 4800   64.6%     bar 70%
     ticks with NOBODY on a place   1698           35.4%     5.4 points under

   EVERY LIVING MAN ON THOSE FAILING TICKS (110134 man-ticks):
     on a place                            0   (0.0%)   - the check on the classification itself
     CRAWLING in, claim held, team PINNED  8522   (7.7%)
     walking in, claim held, NOT pinned   34680  (31.5%)
     in the bowl he claimed, off the lip      0   (0.0%)
     no claim at all                      66932  (60.8%)

   A man-tick share does not convert into points on the row, because a tick fails only when EVERY man is off. What
   converts is which failing ticks hold a man who could have been on a place:

     hold at least one CRAWLER    1157 of 1698  (68.1%)   nearest such crawler 18.2 m from his place
     hold at least one WALKER     1698 of 1698 (100.0%)   nearest such walker   8.9 m from his place
     hold NEITHER                    0 of 1698   (0.0%)

   SO: THE CRAWL ACCOUNTS FOR AT MOST 24.1 OF THE POINTS AND CANNOT CLOSE THE ROW, because 100% of the failing
   ticks also hold an UNPINNED man with a claim who is only 8.9 m from it. Freeze every crawler on his place and
   those ticks still fail on the walkers. The 5.4 points under the bar are not a crawl problem; the crawl made an
   existing problem worse, which is a different sentence from the one this letter has been telling.

   WHAT THE 8.9 m SAYS. A claim is eligible within 12 m of his POST and he takes the nearest to that post, so a
   man 8.9 m from his place is about that far from his own post too. Men are not standing on their posts - the
   same thing measured at §11.3's close, where a claim-holder stood a median 23.4 m from his line post against
   7.3 m for a man without one. The men are permanently in transit, and cover measures whether anyone is standing
   still in the right spot.

   NOT PROPOSED, NOT CODED: nothing here is changed on a guess. The claim rule is §11.3's ("nearest eligible place
   to his POST, not his position, so a man does not wander to cover"), and moving that is a doctrine change, not a
   fix. The bar is untouched and the test asserts what it always asserted.

   GUARDED, in the JS core suite where the rules live, each PROVED RED before it was kept:
     the posture word §11.4 derives, for every living man every tick, including §0's "a pinned man is never
       STAND" and "COVER means he is within 0.5 m of the place he claims"
       RED PROOF: pose writer made to ignore the pin -> 14348 of 120563 man-ticks written STAND while pinned
     the suppression word: +60 a round, no pin on one, pinned on two, decay exactly one a tick, clamp 600 and
       480 ticks back under the line, and no leak to the next team or across the seam
       RED PROOF: decay changed to two a tick -> "the decay is one a tick, not more"
     the courier shell pinning the teams beside the cab (added earlier)
       RED PROOF: rule removed -> rises 0,0,300,... and never a 60

   NOT GUARDABLE IN UNITY, and the reason is structural rather than a gap in effort: the core is the JS bundle,
   `BlwpCore.Available` is set by `BlwpInit` - an extern present only in a browser build - so in EditMode and
   PlayMode the core is stubbed, its state is zeros, every unit reads dead and THE RENDERER DRAWS NO MEN AT ALL.
   `_state` is private static with no setter.

   TWO TESTS WERE WRITTEN FOR IT AND BOTH WERE WORTHLESS. The first asserted the renderer's down-count against the
   core's and failed at once on "the core is not running". The second asserted that with no core word nothing may
   be laid down - it PASSED, and went on passing when `down` was forced true for every third man, because there is
   no man to draw. Only breaking the renderer on purpose exposed that; a green over an empty set is not a guard,
   and the second one would have shipped as coverage.

   RULED: NO TEST-ONLY STATE SEAM ON BlwpCore. It is production surface added for editor testability, and a seam
   would either fake the men the editor does not have or open the core's API. The test stays Assert.Ignore with
   its reason, in the SKIPPED count and never a green pass, and neither dead end is revived as coverage. The pose
   is held by the renderer's own count over CDP from a running build - 4 to 20 of 69 men drawn down on 0.0.1791 -
   and that is recorded as a hand measurement, not as a suite result.

3f. THE TWO CLAUSES OF §11.5 THAT ARE ACTUALLY OPEN (2026-09-20, found by reading the section against the write
   at the close-out, not by measuring). Neither is coded.

   (a) THE SHELL CLAUSE DOES NOT EXIST. §11.5: "A shell (§4.4) that lands - hit or miss - inside 8 m of a man adds
   60 to his team's word too; a tank's fire pins infantry, which is what infantry hides from." Nothing in the core
   does this. Tank guns fire today and a connecting shot lands on the target hull, so the HIT half is buildable
   now - men within 8 m of a hull that was just hit take +60. The MISS half needs a landing point the core does
   not model at all: a gun shot either connects or does not, and a miss goes nowhere in particular. That half
   belongs with §4.4, which owns the shell.

   (b) A BOMB ADDS 300 PER MAN, NOT PER TEAM. §11.5 says a blast "adds 300 to every TEAM with a living man inside
   16 m of it". The call sits inside the per-man loop (sim.js, the blast pass), so every man of a team inside the
   circle adds his own 300. With the clamp at 600, a team with two men in one blast is pinned at the ceiling.

   IT IS NOT COSMETIC, by the decay arithmetic already recorded above: from 600 the word needs 480 ticks (8.0 s)
   to fall under the pin line, against 180 ticks (3.0 s) from 300. So a team caught with two men in a blast stays
   pinned about THREE TIMES as long as the section says. Bombs open 36.4% of all pinned episodes, so this sits on
   a live path rather than in a corner - and it is one of the reasons the crawl is starving cover.

3d. THE PIN, PROFILED - which of threshold, duration or fire density is the overage (five seeds x 180 s).

   THE ARITHMETIC THE RULE IS BUILT FROM: a round is +60, decay is 1 a tick = 60 a second, the pin line is 120 and
   the clamp is 600. So two rounds inside a second pin a team from cold; one round a second holds the word level
   exactly; and from the clamp the word needs 8.0 s to fall under 120 and 10.0 s to clear.

     team-ticks                    972000
       under fire (word > 0)       534707  (55.0%)
       pinned (word >= 120)        426193  (43.8%)
     the word, once a second       mean 182, median 49, p90 575, max 600
     rifle rounds                  3878 = 4.3 a second across both sides
       per team per second         0.24        break-even is 1.00
     pinned episodes ended         797
       length in seconds           mean 7.9, median 3.0, p90 22.5, max 96.8
     pinned episodes opened by a BLAST  305 (36.4%)   by rifle rounds  533 (63.6%)

   THE ANSWER IS NONE OF THE THREE. Fire density is a QUARTER of break-even. The threshold is reached by two
   rounds, which is the section's own intent. Duration is short in the median - 3.0 s - and only its tail is long,
   because a blast puts the word at 600 and 8.0 s must then decay off it.

   RULED 2026-09-20, AND THE OVERAGE IS RETRACTED. The 70% ceiling is the SHARE OF TEAMS actually pinned -
   pinned-teams / 9, or the matching fraction of riflemen in the pin state where the row is read on men. It is NOT
   the fraction of time at least one of nine teams is pinned.

     the pinned share          43.8% per team        INSIDE the 70% ceiling
     the retracted figure      96.0% / 95.6%         the OR saturating, not a share

   At 43.8% per team, at-least-one-of-nine is 99.5% if the teams were independent and 96.0% / 95.6% as measured -
   which says nothing about how much of the front is pinned, only that nine chances rarely all miss. Reading an OR
   as a share is the same class of misread as hole 2 above, and it was mine both times.

   So §11.5's pin is INSIDE its ceiling and was never over it. +60, -1 and 120 stand untouched; two rounds pinning
   a team and a median episode of three seconds are the section's intent and are working.

§11.4 POSTURE - THE BITS WRITTEN (2026-09-19). Before and after, five seeds x 180 s, a nuke every 30 s.

THE WRITE. COVER_POSTURE_SHIFT now carries STAND 0 / PRONE 1 / COVER 2 in TAC_COVER's reserved high bits. No new
word, no layout change, no draw. STAND is 0 on purpose: a tick before the first write reads as the most exposed
posture, so nothing moves for a reason other than the rule. The pass runs last in the movement step, after §8.3's
hull clearance and the truck's clear-out, so a man's FINAL position decides COVER while his OWN step - captured at
his write-back, before anything can shove him - decides STAND.

THE RIFLE READS IT ONE TICK LATE, DELIBERATELY. Men fire and move in the same pass, so reading a posture written
mid-pass would make the outcome depend on unit order. The written word agrees with the rule's own derivation on
97.2% of man-ticks; the 2.8% is that lag, and every node pays it identically.

       written PRONE or COVER                            0  (0.0%)    1004637  (52.3%)
       written STAND                                     all          917304   (47.7%)

   Before the write the word was unwritten, so every man read STAND whatever he was doing. The 47.7% still STAND
   after it is not a fault: §11.4 says running men run upright, and a man walking to his hole is stepping. What
   changed is that a man who has arrived is now written down as being there.

       PRONE                             14.5        16.1

     STAND / (PRONE+COVER) rifle deaths per man-tick    0.17 -> 0.35    the row wants >= 2.0

   No threshold was retuned to reach it. The cause is the row's denominator, not the rule: STAND is dominated by

§11.4 POSTURE - THE MEASUREMENT BEFORE THE WORK (2026-09-19, on HEAD 359ba8a3, no bit written).

Posture is DERIVED, not chosen (§11.4: STAND = own step over 0.01 m, COVER = within 0.5 m of his claimed place and
not stepping, PRONE = everything else that did not step), so it can be computed from state the core already has
and every row it grades can be given a number before a single bit of TAC_COVER's high bits is touched.
`tools/measure-posture.mjs`, five seeds x 180 s, a nuke every 30 s, on both drives.

1. THE POSTURE MIX

                        frozen tape (the §11.3 assert drive)   live scrolling tape (the game)
     STAND                   2494745  70.6%                        2598274  74.2%
     PRONE                    489561  13.9%                         454332  13.0%
     COVER                    548529  15.5%                         450296  12.9%

   A PUSH IS NOT A STEP: §8.3 stands a man 3 m off a hull after his own step, and counting that as a step would
   have inflated STAND by 20189 man-ticks on the line (53200 over all men). The tool corrects it.

2. §0's "MEN HIDE" ROW IS A TAUTOLOGY, and that has to be said before it is claimed as a win. It grades men on the
   line who did NOT step and wants >= 85% of them PRONE or COVER. By §11.4's own derivation a man who did not step
   is COVER if he is on his place and PRONE otherwise - there is no third outcome. Measured: 549202 of 549202 on
   the frozen tape and 460049 of 460049 scrolling, 100.0% on both, before any code. Its second clause ("a man in
   the open who did not step is PRONE") is definitional in the same way: 107436 of 107436, and 69089 of 69089.

   So the row goes green the moment the bits are written and proves nothing. The letter's worth is NOT here. (The
   "under fire" qualifier needs §11.5's suppression word and cannot be read at all yet.)

3. §0's SECOND FODDER CLAUSE - rifle deaths per man-tick of STAND >= 2x PRONE and COVER together - IS NOT REACHED
   BY THIS LETTER'S OWN THRESHOLDS, and the gap is a factor of four.

     rifle deaths per 100k man-ticks      frozen              scrolling
       STAND                               3.1  (77)           3.6  (94)
       PRONE                              14.5  (71)          20.2  (92)
       COVER                              22.4 (123)          19.3  (87)
       STAND / (PRONE+COVER)               0.17                0.18      <- the row wants >= 2.0

   A man in cover is today shot at SEVEN TIMES the rate of a standing man, and that is not an anomaly: STAND is
   dominated by men walking in from the back edge who are never shot at, while a man on his place is on the line in
   contact. The row compares rates on wildly unmatched exposure.

   Applying §11.4's own thresholds to the measured split (STAND 45 per mil unchanged, PRONE x 22/45, COVER x 11/45)
   gives 0.17 -> 0.50 frozen and 0.18 -> 0.49 scrolling. It moves a quarter of the distance and stops.

   A FIRST TOOL FAULT, caught and named: the claim was first read AFTER the step, and a dead man's claim is cleared
   the tick he dies (§11.3), so COVER was structurally impossible for a casualty - it printed 0 COVER deaths in
   548070 COVER man-ticks and filed every man killed in a hole under PRONE. The tool now grades a man on the
   posture he HELD while he was being shot at. The 0.17 above is the corrected figure; the faulty one was the same
   0.17 for the wrong reason.

Everything for M2 and beyond is further down, under "The milestones", and
none of it should be started while item 2 is open. M2 needs stage 3
(`blwp-node`) before it can begin at all, and starting a lobby on top of
a simulation that still disagrees with the game is work built on sand.

**Governance code is tested to 100%, and it is the only thing here that
is.** Everything to do with voting, consensus and forks - proposals, the
tally, thresholds, turnout, schedules, bond re-affirmation, the fork
certificate chain - must have full branch coverage before it ships, with
the adversarial cases written as tests and not as comments.

The reason it is singled out: **a governance bug cannot be fixed by
shipping a fix.** A wrong tally that activates a config is not a crash you
patch and redeploy - the network has already moved, the change is live,
and the mechanism you would use to undo it is the one that just proved it
does not work. Every other bug in this repo costs a session. A miscounted
threshold costs the network. Details in M3.1B.

The rule that has cost the most time here, written down so it is not
learned a fourth time: **when a number does not move across several
attempts, stop forming hypotheses and print what the code is actually
holding.** The whitepaper sat at exactly 22% through four changes; one
Debug.Log showed Fit had been given a 9.4 x 12.2 plate while the test
measured 73.8 x 52.3, because the streamed building swaps the mesh under
a node that keeps its name. Four rounds of guessing, one line to see it.

## 1. Clear the red tests  -  M1  -  DONE

165 green, one known flake left (`TheGogglesAnimate`, which passes alone
and depends on a network fetch inside a two-second animation window).

Both failures were mine and neither was where I first looked. Dumping
what was on the wall settled it in one run: the band was fully populated
with English ages and correct heights - the test was reading the caption
STRIP, which I had deliberately blanked when the number moved onto the
face of the block. The claim it makes is unchanged; only the place the
number is written moved, so the test now reads the face.

The other was the streamed building swapping meshes under nodes that keep
their names, so any plate size read at wiring time can describe something
that no longer exists. Every display is re-fitted against the mesh that
is there now.

## 2. The army into the core  -  M1  -  DONE

The last thing standing between here and M1.

The core RECEIVES the army today: Unity simulates it and sends x, z and
kind every tick, which is why danger, collision and score are correct.
M1 asks for enemies that come FROM the core.

`PhysxReferenceTests` is the pattern and `ArmyReferenceTests` is the
recording: test/vectors/csharp-army.json.

  a. Movement and squads - DONE. Armour closes at 6.8 m/s, infantry at
     2.6, armour arriving first, both within a third of a metre of the
     recording at five seconds. Units hold a squad post rather than
     wandering; free wandering spread them from 57 m to 87 m of standard
     deviation where the C# army holds 36-45, and two armies that drift
     apart sideways simply stop meeting.

  b. Firing and death - DONE. The gap that looked like a firing fault was
     the reference: the C# army REPLACES its dead. Measured, both sides,
     same seed, replacement switched off (`passes` in csharp-army.json) -
     the C# army collapses exactly as the core does. See "What the
     reference was actually saying" below.

  c. Retreat - IN. Back off inside 24 m, fall right back when overrun by
     14 (Army.OverrunDepth), held to |x| < 88.

  d. Reinforcement - DONE. Replacement was not a garnish on the army; it
     is what holds the front up. Without it the first exchange decided
     the round and the survivors stood still for the remaining sixty
     seconds; with it both armies are still fighting at t=90 on every
     seed. Numbers under "Reinforcement, and what it cost the golden
     vectors" below.
     Gunships and bombs - DONE. Sorties, gunships, ballistic bombs and
     the blast are in `rules/air.js`, and the core's air war replays
     from the seed, which the C# one cannot. Fifteen of the recording's
     seventeen published quantities overlap; the two that do not are
     both the GROUND line's doing and are named under "The air arm"
     below.
  e. Delete the C# army; Unity renders from core state only - DONE.
     The C# army is not built, not stepped and not drawn. Position,
     damage, enemies and delivery all come FROM the core, each with a named
     reader, and the picture was proved in a browser rather than argued.
     What is left over is presentation and has its own lines: item 7
     (CombatFx and the combat audio) and (r) the turret.

     ITEM 7, THE COMBAT HALF - DONE. `CombatFx` was never dead: measured in
     the player build it ticks every frame with `army=null` and drew
     `pieces=0` for a whole drive, while `GameAudio` was asked for
     `combat=0` sounds. All five things it drew - `Shot`, `Fired`,
     `Killed`, `Destroyed`, `Bombed` - hung on a C# army that is never
     built.

     The core raises no events either, and does not have to. Each of the
     five is a transition in the buffer Unity already polls, and the core
     steps once per Unity frame so none is missed:

       a tank fired      `U_TARGET`, the armour's reload counter, rises -
                         it only counts down otherwise
       a rifleman fired  `U_COOLDOWN` rises to 150 or more; the reload band
                         is 150-269 and the "looked, found nobody" band is
                         24-65, so a look draws no flash
       somebody hit      `U_HP` fell while still alive
       somebody died     `U_STATE` went 1 to 0
       a bomb went off   `B_STATE` went 1 to 0

     Nothing here decides anything: no roll, no damage, no range test that
     costs anyone. The tracer's end is picked by re-running `pickTarget` /
     `pickRifleTarget`'s own rule - nearest enemy of the same arm inside
     46 m and 26 m - on the core's own state, and a slot that changed
     alive-state this frame is skipped so a spawn's staggered reload cannot
     read as a shot.

     Measured in the player build, one drive, before against after:

       pieces drawn      0 for the whole drive   ->  peak 65 at once
       shots seen        -                       ->  160
       hits seen         -                       ->  48
       deaths seen       -                       ->  16
       combat sounds     0                       ->  233

     TWO MORE HOLES, FOUND BY PLAYING A SECOND ROUND. Everything above is
     about one round. A session has more than one, and the second one was
     broken in two separate ways - neither visible to any suite, both
     measured in a browser.

     1. THE CORE NEVER STARTED A SECOND ROUND. `outcome` latches: once a
        run leaves RUN_LIVE nothing brings it back, and only `init` does.
        `BlwpCore.Init` ran once, in `Start`. All three endings - delivered,
        written off, block missed - go through `TruckController.Respawn`,
        which calls `teleport`, and `teleport` moves the truck and clears
        its momentum and touches no score word. Round two against a fresh
        `init(0x5eed1234)`, same words, read out of the browser:

          S_STATE      0    ->  1          Armee lebend  96 -> 91
          S_EXPOSURE   0    ->  214.5      Armee tot      0 ->  5
          S_ELAPSED    0    ->  0.020      Nachschub  [0,0] -> [89640, 48144]
          S_BESTX   -100.4  ->  114.1      Luft       [0,0] -> [581454, 525784]
          S_DELIVERED  0    ->  1050       T_X     -100.400 -> -100.337
          S_PRACTICE   0    ->  1          tick        0    -> 1440

        Twelve of thirty words. `S_STATE` alone withholds damage, danger,
        delivery and score, all of which are gated on RUN_LIVE - so round
        two was unplayable and looked normal. Fixed by `restart` IN THE
        CORE, reached at roll-out (`LoadoutPanel.Confirm`) because the score
        card is read out of the core after a run ends. The uploaded relief
        and solids are round SETUP and are carried across. After the fix,
        round two at tick 40 is word-identical to a local `init(seed)`
        stepped 40 idle ticks - all four RNG words and both sortie clocks
        included.

     2. THE GATE BANKED A LEVEL, NOT AN EDGE. `RunState == RUN_DELIVERED`
        stays true after the arrival, so `DeliveryGate` re-banked the same
        run on the first frame the bed held anything. Instrumented: AUTO
        took 8 parcels, fill 0.86, loaded True - and the next frame showed
        0 parcels, NOTHING LOADED, the truck back in the bay and the camera
        flying the arrival again. The player could load but never roll out,
        so the reset in (1) could not be reached at all. The gate now banks
        the transition into delivered and waits for the core to be live.

     AND THE LAST C# VETO IS GONE. `TruckHealth.WriteOff` returned early on

       before   road: WASTED, truck burning     apron, bay open: intact, run continues
       after    road: WASTED, truck burning     apron, bay open: WASTED, truck burning

     Removing it needed the same lesson the delivery gate had just learned:
     RUN_WRECKED latches, and `IsDestroyed` is the BURN TIMER rather than
     the condition, so a level read would have exploded the truck again
     every time the respawn cleared the timer. `ApplySnapshot` now applies
     the core's verdict once per write-off and clears on the core going
     live, which happens only in `restart`.

     Two more PhysX-era lines went with it: the respawn handed the body back
     to PhysX (`isKinematic = false`) although the core drives and writes the
     transform, so after the first write-off the truck was a dynamic body
     being teleported sixty times a second for the rest of the session.

     `DeliveryGate` read `health.IsDestroyed` as a LEVEL in front of the

     `RUN_MISSED` had no reader at all. `Bootstrap` wired
     `clock.BlockClosed` straight to `MissTheBlock`, so the third outcome
     was a Unity stopwatch. The two clocks do not measure the same thing:
     the core counts 9000 ticks from ROLL-OUT, `BlockClock` closes on wall
     time for everybody at once, so a run starting ten seconds before the
     block closes has missed it in C# and has 140 s left in the core.
     Measured: with the core's own clock wound to 8900 and the core left to
     decide, S_STATE went to 3 at exactly S_ELAPSED 9000, the card read
     BLOCK MINED WITHOUT YOU and the bed was thrown away - while the Unity
     block clock still showed 2:17 left. The next round then ran to a
     delivery. The decision is read; `MissTheBlock` was not rebuilt.

     Worth writing down while measuring it: the core is stepped once per
     Unity FRAME. In this headless browser that is about twelve ticks a
     second, so BLOCK_TICKS - "150 s at 60 Hz" - was twelve minutes of wall
     clock here. Determinism is unharmed, the tick stream is the input
     stream, but a round's LENGTH IN SECONDS depends on the frame rate of
     the machine playing it. Not this letter's to fix; listed.

     NEW ITEM, NOT PART OF 2e - THE CARGO NEVER REACHES THE CORE. Found
     while answering whether `RunScore` filters a core quantity. It does
     not: `Exposure` and `Projected` read the core unconditionally. But the
     breakdown card does not add up, and the reason is worse than the card.
     One delivery, read both sides:

       card   load 0.86  x  danger 1.00  x  speed 1.50  x  1000   SCORE +1,050
       core   E 1.001                      T 3900/817 ticks clamped = 1.500

     Danger and the time factor agree. But 0.86 x 1.00 x 1.50 x 1000 is
     1290, and the score banked is 1050 - which is 0.70 x 1.00 x 1.50 x
     1000. `S_CARGO` and `T_CARGO` are written once, in `sim.js:248/250`,
     to 45875 - 0.7 of a bed - and NOTHING ever writes them again. There is
     no cargo call in the jslib or in `BlwpCore`. So what the player loads
     reaches neither the score (`sim.js:1056`) nor the danger
     (`sim.js:1045`): every run is priced as a 70% bed, and the card prints
     the C# bed fill beside a number that ignored it.

     This is a MISSING HOST-TO-CORE INPUT, not a veto - which is why it is
     not 2e - but it changes what a run pays, so it is not cosmetic either.
     Both halves are needed: a call that hands the bed to the core, and the
     card then reading the core's cargo rather than `bay.Fill`. Also
     related: the time factor agreed only because both sides were sitting
     on the 1.5 clamp; a run slower than 65 s would be needed to tell them
     apart, and that has not been measured.

     ALSO LISTED WHILE MEASURING: the core is stepped once per Unity frame,
     so a round's length in SECONDS follows the frame rate. Twelve ticks a
     second in a headless browser made BLOCK_TICKS - "150 s at 60 Hz" -
     twelve minutes of wall clock. Determinism is untouched, the tick
     stream is the input stream, but the clock the player feels is not the
     clock the rule was written against.

     WHO OWNS THE SCREEN, read off the player path and not off a test:
     the picture is C#. `ArmyRenderer` holds a `public Army army` and walks
     `army.Armour` and its soldier lists; it names `BlwpCore` nowhere.
     `BlwpCore.UnitAt(i)` exists and has NO caller - the only readers of
     `BlwpCore.State` are `CoreDrivenTruck` for the truck's transform and
     `DriveHud` for a diagnostics panel. And `Battlefield.Update` calls
     `Army.Update(dt)` unconditionally whenever `Army != null`, with no
     gate on whether the core is driving.

     So two armies run and neither can see the other. Since `c6cc689` took
     `UploadArmour` out, the C# army feeds the core nothing at all: the
     player watches an army that decides no outcome, while the truck is
     shot at and blocked by an army nobody draws. The cutover is therefore
     RENDERER PLUS OFF-SWITCH - point `ArmyRenderer` at core state and stop
     stepping `Army` - and not a rules port.

     THE CUTOVER, IN NAMED STEPS. Not started; this is the plan.

       1. The mirror must be able to describe a unit. `UNITS` (96) lives in
          `sim.js` and `ARMOUR_MASK` (3) is private there, and
          `BlwpLayout.cs` is generated from `state.js` - so neither
          reaches C#. A drawer would iterate `MAX_UNITS` 256 and hand-copy
          the kind rule, which is the drift the generator exists to
          prevent. Move both into `state.js`, regenerate the mirror, and
          add accessors beside `UnitPosition`/`UnitHealth`: `UnitSide`,
          `UnitAlive` (`U_STATE != 0`), `UnitIsArmour` (`(i & ARMOUR_MASK)
          == 0`), `UnitHeading` (`U_HEADING` is mirrored already). Facing
          is bound here because the hash already carries it.
       2. DONE, with 3, because they cannot be separated without a broken
          build. `Battlefield.Update` no longer feeds Flow, Courier or Heat
          and no longer calls `Army.Update`; `Battlefield.LaunchSorties` is
          gone with it, the core running its own on the same schedule.
          `Bootstrap` builds and populates no army, binds none to CombatFx,
          and hangs no audio off its events. `Battlefield.Army` is still
          DECLARED and never assigned - removing it means re-sourcing
          fourteen test methods across four files, which is its own step -
          and nothing in the product reads it.
       3. DONE. `ArmyRenderer` has no `army` field. Units come from
          `UnitPosition`, `UnitSide`, `UnitAlive`, `UnitIsArmour` and
          `UnitHeading` over `Layout.UNITS`; gunships from `HeliAlive`,
          `HeliSide`, `HeliDir`, `HeliPosition`; bombs from `BombAlive`,
          `BombPosition`, `BombVelocity`. `DriveHud`'s counts read the core
          too. NOT BUILT, and named rather than discovered later: the
          turret follows the hull, helicopter yaw and bank are derived from
          `H_DIR` in the renderer, a man is one size and always walking -
          height and the halt are (q) - and the bob comes off the tick.

            no core in the editor, so nothing is drawn to look at -

     STEP 0 DONE - the bridge, measured rather than read.
     `tools/measure-bridge.js` prints all of it.

     Three uploads run in `CoreDrivenTruck.Update()`, and only one of them
     is per-tick host input. `UploadGround` returns early unless
     `terrain.Revision` moved; `UploadSolids` returns unless a second has
     passed AND the box count changed. `UploadArmour` is guarded by
     nothing: every frame, straight out of `field.Army`. And `setUnits`
     has NO caller anywhere - not Unity, not the tools, not the tests - so
     the host branch of the score's danger at `sim.js:881` is dead code
     today and the score already reads the core's own army. That is one of
     the three worries in "What (e) actually has to move" answered: it is
     not a preference to remove, it is a setter to delete.

     The collision is worse than that entry says, and this is the finding.
     It is not that `resolveArmour` PREFERS the host's tanks - it is that
     the core has no armour of its own to give it. Nothing inside `step()`
     ever writes `st.armour`; only `setArmour` and `setUnits` do, and
     neither is called in a headless round. Measured over all six golden
     vectors, `st.armour.n` is 0 at every tick of every one. The core
     simulates twenty-four tanks and the truck can drive through all of
     them.

     And the round really is not replayable today, which was an argument
     and is now a number. Feeding one host tank at the truck's own
     position from t=600 of `straight`:

       no host                      hash 32e819e7...  ends x = +130.0
       host tank on the truck       hash 7d961a75...  ends x = -130.0

     So (e)'s collision work is an ADDITION, not a deletion: `st.armour`
     has to be built inside `step()` from the core's own armour, and only
     then can `setArmour` go. Doing it the other way round removes a
     collision the game currently has.

     STEP 1 - the truck's two owners. Half measurable here, and the half
     that is not is the important half.

     What IS established. The two are not merely separate, they are on
     different SCALES: `TruckHealth.Damage` takes `amount / armour` with
     `armour = 1.5` (`TruckHealth.cs:121`), and the core takes the shell's
     full amount off `T_HP` with no divisor at all (`sim.js:829`). Same
     maxHealth of 100, same hits, and the core spends them half again as
     fast - which is why its truck dies at t=15-20 s in the courier pass.
     And `BlwpCore.TruckHealth` (`BlwpCore.cs:239`) really does have no
     consumer: grepped, the only references in the whole project are the
     two lines of the measurement below. The core's health is a ghost, as
     this entry said.

     What is NOT measurable in this loop, and it is a fact about the
     project rather than about the truck: THERE IS NO CORE IN THE EDITOR.
     `BlwpCore` compiles every call to a stub unless
     `UNITY_WEBGL && !UNITY_EDITOR`, so in the editor, in PlayMode tests
     and in a standalone build `Available` is false and `_state` stays
     zeroed. The measurement was written, run, and came back
     `core=0.00 game=100.00 tick=0` at every one of 120 samples with the
     truck never leaving x = -100.4. Its own guard caught that, which is
     what the guard is for.

     Two consequences worth having in writing. The two owners cannot be
     shown to disagree anywhere but in a browser, so `MeasureTheTwoTruck
     Healths` is `[Explicit]` and waits for a WebGL run. And every PlayMode
     figure this file quotes as a guard - 174/164/2/8 included - is a
     measurement of the C# path, NOT of the core: it can prove the game
     still works, and it can never prove the core does. The core's own
     guard is the 47 node tests and the golden vectors, which is the split
     the class doc calls deliberate.

     STEP 2 DONE - what `RunOver` and `ClearPath` are worth, sized before
     the file that holds them is deleted. `MeasureRunOverAndClearPath`,
     PlayMode, `[Explicit]`. It runs on the C# path deliberately: these are
     C#-only rules and the editor has no core anyway.

     Driving AT the infantry for a round: 18 men run down, the corridor
     holding up to 13 men and 0.92 on average, and never more than ONE man
     inside the 3.6 m kill radius at a sample. `RunOver` is worth about 18
     men - a tenth of the 180 on the map - to a player who aims at them.

     CORRECTED IN STEP 2 OF THE PORT: this entry went on to say that
     `ClearPath` "is what keeps that number as low as 18", easing thirteen
     men out of the corridor. It eases nobody out of anything. Its
     corridor branch never runs - the only call is
     `YieldTo(u, 0f, 0.9f, false, 1.6f)`, `stepsAside` false and `rate`
     zero - so `halfWidth` 7.5 and `ahead` 26 are dead parameters in the
     game they sit in. Why at most one man was ever inside 3.6 m is
     unexplained by that rule and stays unexplained here.

     It took three runs to get a number, and the two failures are the same
     failure this project keeps finding. The first drove with
     `externalThrottle` alone and never moved - `useExternalInput` has to
     be set or the control path ignores it - and reported a tidy zero. The
     second drove the full width of the map at 20 m/s with `corridor` at
     ZERO the whole way, because straight ahead from the bay is z ~ 10 and
     the infantry are not there. Both are null results from a test that
     could not have fired, and neither is evidence that the rule is
     cheap. The measurement now steers at the nearest living rifleman,
     which is the upper bound a port has to cover.

     WHAT THIS MEANS FOR (e). Neither rule can simply go. `RunOver` is a
     tenth of the infantry a round on a route that seeks them; `ClearPath`
     is load-bearing for `RunOver`'s own size and for not leaving a man
     standing in the cab. Both are outcomes the player produces, so both
     have to exist in the core before `Army.cs` goes - which, with the
     collision from step 0, makes THREE core additions that must land
     before the deletion: `st.armour` built in `step()`, run-over, and
     path-clearing.

     THE AUDIT FOUND ONE, AND IT WAS MY OWN DAMAGE. `Army.Update` opens
     with `Separate(Armour[i], Armour[j])` over every pair, before
     anything moves, holding 8.5 m between friends and 7.5 m between
     enemies. The core had no such rule - `Separate` appeared in it only
     in comments explaining that the infantry has none - and nothing
     recorded it, because in C# it is true by construction and a recording
     of a constant is not worth taking.

     It was tolerable until e5dabe8 gave an engaged tank its enemy's x to
     close on. That is what C# does, but C# does it WITH the separation;
     two tanks closing on the same enemy converge on bitwise the same x,
     and with nothing to push them apart they end up occupying one point.
     Found by looking at an actual pair: units 52 and 68, both alive, both
     Bear, x identical to the last bit and 0.018 m apart in z.

       8 seeds, sampled every second        too close  nearest median  closest ever  bitwise x
       before the chase (6398783)              2.16%         3.61 m        0.00 m       0.03%
       chase, no Separate (d1e84ec)            7.25%         0.03 m        0.00 m      10.51%
       chase + Separate (now)                  4.18%         8.22 m        7.46 m       2.01%
       C#, by construction                     0.00%       >= 7.50 m     >= 7.50 m         n/a

     The number that matters is the last-but-one: the closest two tanks in
     eight rounds went from ON TOP OF EACH OTHER to 7.46 m, four
     centimetres inside the 7.5 m the rule allows. The "too close" column
     rising from 2.16% to 4.18% is not a regression and should not be read
     as one: before the chase the armour was spread on a ladder and rarely
     near anything, and now it is packed at about 8 m, so many pairs sit
     just under 8.5 m while NONE overlaps. The bitwise-x residual is the
     same story - the separation runs at the top of a tick and the chase
     re-aligns x at the bottom of it, which is exactly C#'s own ordering.

     Ported with its own units, not with a leftover number: `push` is
     `(min - d) / 2`, a distance, halved with `>> 1` which is exact in
     Q16.16; the normal is dimensionless; and C#'s `d2 <= 1e-4f` is a
     separation of 0.01 m, which is 655. Nothing was scaled to make a
     column match. It is called at the top of the army's step because that
     is where `Army.Update` calls it - a separation applied afterwards
     would resolve last tick's overlap against this tick's positions.
     Alive is `U_STATE` rather than `U_HP`, which is what `reinforce`
     counts and what the crowding scan skips on; C# never has to ask,
     since it removes its dead from `Armour` before this runs.

     The army balance is unmoved: at t = 90 s inRange 2.00 against the
     reference's 1.70, xspread 37.4 against 34.8, alive 19 against 20.
     Vectors regenerated and `dist/` with them, core 47/47, guard 19 files
     clean, node vs bundle-node identical, stage 0 PASS. PlayMode is NOT
     re-run for this and that is deliberate: it only ever exercised the C#
     path, `BlwpCore` is stubbed outside WebGL, and this round moved core
     JS, the vectors and `dist/` - none of which PlayMode can see.

     STEP 3 - the port order, and it is dictated by the measurements
     rather than by taste. Each step is a rule change, so each moves the
     golden vectors and `dist/` with them, and each is its own commit.

          DELETED - three members were: `setArmour` and `setUnits` from

          Four core tests moved with it and none was weakened.
          `clearTheField` empties the slots but `reinforce` refills them
          within seconds, which was harmless until the core's own armour

          Core 47/47, guard 19 files clean, node vs bundle-node identical,

       2. DONE. Path-clearing, and it is a smaller rule than this list

          rifleman back out to 1.6 m if he is inside it, and nothing else.

          Measured, 8 seeds, truck driven AT the nearest living rifleman
          for 90 s each - straight ahead is z ~ 10 and meets nobody, which

                                    before        after      C# recording
            penetration, total      1773.3 m      0.000 m       0.000 m
            deepest single          1.590 m       0.000 m       0.000 m
            man-ticks over 2 cm     3253          0             0

          The core and the C# game now agree exactly on the quantity this

          Only `handbrake` moved of the six vectors, which is the only one

          A WRECK CLEARS NOBODY - the hole this step was closed on, and it
          was found by reading the C# call site for the ordering question
          rather than by a test. `Battlefield` wraps the whole block in
          `if (courier != null && (health == null || !health.IsDestroyed))`,
          so once the truck is written off C# stops BOTH running men down
          and pushing them out. The first port had no such guard and went
          on shoving riflemen out of a hulk the game considers gone.

          The core's quantity for "written off" is `T_HP`, and NOT
          `S_STATE`: the state word is recomputed in the score section,
          after this, so here it still holds last tick's value and would
          let a wreck clear for one more tick. `T_HP` is current at this
          point because the courier damage has already come off it. It is
          not `TruckHealth` and not its `armour` divisor - that is the
          two-owner question, and it is NOT decided here. Run-over goes
          inside the same brace when it is ported, because it shares this
          `if` in the game rather than merely sitting next to it.

              unguarded          16409     0.011 m     0.000 m      0

              unguarded          26791     0.013 m     0.000 m      0

          Counted separately, all three measured on this tree: Core 47/47,
          guard 19 files clean, node vs bundle-node identical, stage 0
          PASS. EditMode 124/123/1. PlayMode 176/164/2/10.

          The 3.6 m peak from the step 2 sizing is a SAMPLING ARTEFACT of
          my own instrument and 0% of the open M1 gap - no investigation.
          18 men fell in about 18 s at 10-14 m/s; a man is inside 3.6 m for
          about 2*3.6/12 = 0.6 s, so the expected number inside at any
