## M2.36, why 19:27 and 19:31 both told the truth: the replay is flat

The 19:27 look measured each tab's picture of the other against that truck's own
core at (0.000, 0.000) m. The 19:31 look watched P2's chip crawl -100,-3 to
-97,-3 while P1 was out in the tank field. Both happened, and the difference is
the ground.

`init` leaves a core "flat until the host uploads the relief". The PAGE uploads
one - `CoreDrivenTruck.UploadGround` calls `BlwpCore.SetGround` with
`MempoolTerrain.HeightGrid`, and `UploadSolids` does the same for the boxes.
THE DAEMON'S REPLAY DOES NEITHER: `RunInProgress` calls `init(seedWord)` and
steps. Counted rather than remembered: files in `src/` that give a replay a
ground, 0.

Measured, one seed, one drive, six hundred ticks, the only difference being the
ground the core was given:

    after 20 ticks, still on the apron        0.000 m apart
    after 600 ticks   flat    (-77.322, -45.794) m
                      relief  (-65.947, -14.285) m
                                             33.500 m apart

The apron is level by construction - `MempoolTerrain.HeightAt` flattens both
ends of the map on purpose, "a metre of remaining relief anywhere under it is a
metre of daylight under one end" - so the two worlds agree EXACTLY while the
truck is standing at its bay or rolling off it. That is the whole of the 19:27
measurement: it was taken on the apron, over 3.6 m of it. The moment the truck
is on relief the replayed truck drives a different map, which is a chip that
crawls while the real truck is in the field.

IT IS NOT ONLY THE GHOST. The same replay decides the outcome and the score the
round pays on, so a run that leaves flat ground is judged in a world nobody
drove.

AND THE GROUND HAS NO HOME IN THE PROTOCOL. Checked: `contracts.js`,
`transcript.js`, `batch.js` and `checkpoint.js` carry nothing about heights,
terrain or relief. A replay cannot ask for it because there is nowhere to ask.
Worse, it is not derivable: `MempoolTerrain.HeightAt` is `Mathf.Log10` of a
LIVE mempool fee profile plus `Mathf.PerlinNoise` - a host's live data through
Unity's own float maths, which NIGHT-RUN already measured as the thing the
fixed-point core exists to avoid. No other party can reproduce it, and the page
telling the core what the world looks like is the simulator leaking back into
Unity by a door nobody was watching.

## M2.36, closed: the committee walks the same seeded hills the player drove

THE PICK WAS DANIEL'S: the core generates the relief from the round's seed, in
integer fixed-point, and Unity draws it. Trusting a client-uploaded heightfield
was rejected as an attack - a player who publishes their own hills chooses the
world they are scored in - and pinning Unity's Perlin/mempool float grid was
rejected because that is still C# simulating the ground.

WHAT WAS BUILT

  - `rng.js` gains `hash2(seedWord, i, j)`: splitmix32's finaliser over the
    three, `Math.imul` and shifts only. A FUNCTION and not a stream, because a
    stream depends on how many times it has been drawn from and the ground is
    asked about corners in whatever order a caller walks them. It lives in an
    arithmetic file because it multiplies.
  - `rules/ground.js` gains `groundFromSeed`: a 12 x 8 lattice of corner
    heights from `hash2`, bilinear across it, a second octave at half the scale
    and a quarter of the height, peak 6 m. Both ends levelled into an apron -
    level out to 86 m, easing to full relief by 66 m, with 3t^2 - 2t^3 so the
    join has no crease. `MempoolTerrain` already levelled its aprons and said
    why: an apron slab is one plane at a single height, and a metre of relief
    under it is a metre of daylight under one end. The bays are on it - 24
    doors across 156 m - and a door on a slope is a truck that rolls out of it
    sideways.
  - `sim.js`: `init` calls `groundFromSeed` where it called `flatGround`. That
    one line is the fix: the player's core and every committee's replay are the
    same function of the same seed, so they agree by construction rather than
    by agreement. `restart` no longer carries the previous ground over unless
    it was uploaded, because the seed makes a generated one again.
  - `setGround` survives for ONE caller that is not a host: the reference
    tests, which reproduce a published dataset and need the field it was
    measured on. A ground put there is marked `uploadedGround`.

WHAT WAS TAKEN AWAY, which is the half that makes it a rule

  - `BlwpSetGround` deleted from `blwp.jslib`.
  - `SetGround` deleted from `BlwpCore`.
  - `UploadGround` deleted from `CoreDrivenTruck`.
  - `HasRelief` is set by `Init` now. It used to mean "a host has uploaded
    one" and was false until it did; a core that is up always holds the round's
    hills.
  - `MempoolTerrain.HeightAt` returns `BlwpCore.SurfaceAt` when a core is
    answering. It is the one place the mesh, `SampleSurface` and the seat all
    read from, so redirecting it moves all three at once. The mempool relief
    stays below it as the answer when there is no core - the Editor, where
    PhysX drives - so the game still looks like something without a browser.

THE NUMBER

    after 20 ticks, still on the level apron    0.000 m apart   (was 0.000)
    after 600 ticks   page    (-70.212, -32.048) m
                      replay  (-70.212, -32.048) m
                                                0.000 m apart   (was 33.500)

And the world they agree on is not a table: 10176 of 15360 cells carry relief,
up to 6.930 m. Two seeds differ in 10172 of 15360 cells, so it is the ROUND's
ground and not the game's. Every bay in both rounds stands on level ground.

WHAT THE FIXTURES COST, re-measured and not adjusted. On the new ground the
daemon fixture's drive DELIVERED where it used to wreck, and those tests are

## 2026-09-09  M3.3 item 18 - the daemon asks the chain and pays the winner

`payWithCommittee` had zero callers in `src/`. Measured at the start, by
reading the source rather than remembering it: one file could ask the chain
about outputs (`pool-watch.js`), and nothing called the payer, so a close wrote
PAYOUT_QUEUED and stopped. Every winner in every test was paid by the test
handing the daemon an outpoint.

`Payouts.settleQueued` is the caller. `PoolSigning.owes` is split out of
`spendFor` so the asker can size an output before it has one, rounded UP -
`payoutOutputs` floors each row and drops sub-floor ones, so the transaction
pays at most the bound, and a bound a satoshi short costs a whole signing round
to discover.

WHO ASKS: `askerFor(roundId, seats)`, seats in store order (by pubkey, which no
seat chooses), indexed by four bytes of the round id. 200 rounds asked all 7
seats. A round id of 0xfffffffe would have picked seats[-x] without the `>>> 0`.

ON AN ISOLATED REGTEST (`tools/settle-regtest.mjs`), seven daemons on seven
sockets, one share each, and no outpoint given to anybody:

    the round names seat 7 of 7, and 7 of 7 seats agree
    unfunded pool         refused: 0 confirmed outputs cover the 1000 sats
    funded, in a mempool  refused: the same sentence, and it is the right one
    1 conf against 6      refused: 1 output with fewer than 6 confirmations
    6 of 6 other seats    waited; 0 transactions sent
    the asker             sendrawtransaction -> a txid, block 202 carries it
                          the winner's key holds 1000 sats, the row says PAID
    asking again          already PAID, no second spend of one output

THE FAULT THAT MATTERED was in a fixture and only a real chain could find it.
The shallow-output message was written believing an unconfirmed pool would read
as "too shallow"; `scantxoutset` scans the UTXO SET, so a funding transaction
still in a mempool is not in the answer at all and reads - correctly - as a
pool holding nothing. The code comment, `pool-watch.test.js`,
`pool-settle.test.js` and the harness all said the wrong thing until that run.
The branch is real, but only for `minConfirmations` above one.

WHAT CAME OUT OF IT and is its own line: item 19, nobody takes over when a
round's asker is down. The round stays PAYOUT_QUEUED and its own start-up sweep
pays it when it returns, so nothing is lost - but a seat that never returns
strands the round, and a takeover needs a clock.

## 2026-09-09  M3.3 item 19 - a payout outlives its asker, and one spend lands

MEASURED BEFORE ANY OF IT WAS WRITTEN, because the answer decided the design.
Two askers over one output, `PoolSigning.live` still a Map:

    asker A and asker B, same process     signature SAME, raw bytes SAME
    asker B after a RESTART               signature DIFFERENT, raw DIFFERENT

Same txid both times, because a segwit txid does not cover the witness - so
this is witness malleability rather than a lost satoshi, and the money would
have gone to the same outputs either way. It is still two valid transactions
for one input, which is what a takeover must not create. The nonce pair is a
`pool_nonces` row now; the same probe after the change reads SAME / SAME.

THE CLOCK. The round's beacon height, which is not a new time source: a round
with no randomness beacon cannot be seeded, so every seat already holds the
same number. TAKEOVER_BLOCKS = 2. Seat k in `askerOrder` may ask at
beacon + k*2. The order is the seats the store keeps sorted BY PUBKEY, rotated
by four bytes of the round id - a hash of a contract signed before the round
ran, so a node cannot grind its way up. 7 seats, one eligible at the beacon and
one more every 2 blocks; handing the list round the other way gives the same
ring.

Rejected and why: wall clock (per-node; two seats a minute apart both take
over) and the pool output's own confirmations (a pool funded before the round
closes is already deep, so every seat is eligible at once).

TWO FAULTS CAME OUT OF THE WIRING, neither foreseen:

  THE COMMITMENT LIST WAS WHOEVER ANSWERED FIRST. `payWithCommittee` broke out
  of its loop at the first five, so two askers assembled two different lists -
  and the list goes into the binding factors and therefore into the challenge,
  so every seat that had already signed refused the second by name ("has signed
  under another commitment list"). All seats are asked now and the five are the
  lowest ids: one list whoever asks, at the cost of two more requests. The
  chosen ids printed 1,2,3,4,5 for every asker afterwards.

  A SEAT THAT HAD PAID REFUSED TO COMMIT AT ALL. `spendFor` demands
  PAYOUT_QUEUED, and the seat that broadcasts marks its own row PAID - so the
  takeover could not reassemble the same five, and a spend dropped from a
  mempool would have stranded the round. A seat holding a pair for that round
  answers about it whatever its row says; the sighash is still checked against
  the pair, so it relaxes nothing about starting a spend.

  And a third, one layer up: after the five became the lowest ids, the asker's
  own seat was asked for a share even when it was not in the list it had built,
  and "this seat is not in the commitment list" was reported as a withdrawal.

ON AN ISOLATED REGTEST (`tools/settle-regtest.mjs`), the asker never run:

    beacon block 200; 7 of 7 seats agree who asks
    the order survives being handed round the other way: true
    height 201   6 of 6 seats waited, nothing broadcast, row still queued
                 "may ask at height 202; the chain is at 201, 1 block past"
    height 202   the next seat took over, 5 of 5 signed
                 sendrawtransaction -> a txid, block 203 carries it
                 the winner's own key holds 1000 sats
    same instant the seat behind, that spend still in the MEMPOOL:
                 "that output is already going: the chain holds no such
                 unspent output" - `gettxout` sees a mempool, `scantxoutset`
                 does not, which is why the takeover re-reads through it
    its own turn the seat behind: refused, the pool holds nothing
    after a restart  the asker came back and spent nothing
    on the chain the winner's key holds 1000 sats - ONE payment, not two

TWO HARNESS CHECKS WERE TRUE SENTENCES ABOUT THE WRONG THING and were fixed

    five of seven interpolate to the secret nobody held

alone from the parity of a key computed from public data, and it is the move

because a test that only saw even keys would pass with the normalisation

caught it.

THE BUDGET IS WALLET-SIDE POLICY (§24, §24A.1), so it is asked for. Three
read-only calls over the same relay and encryption a payment uses:

    get_info      first, because `methods` is the wallet saying what it
                  implements. `get_budget` is a later NIP-47 addition; asking
                  blind turns "not implemented" into an error a player reads as
                  a fault.
    get_budget    where offered
    get_balance   where it is not

Measured against the fake relay and wallet:

    with get_budget       get_info then get_budget, get_balance NOT asked
                          "750 of 1000 sat budget left"
    without it            get_info then get_balance
                          "wallet balance 4200 sat"
    reporting neither     1 call, "this wallet does not report a budget"
    budget set to nothing "this connection has no budget set"
    every one of them     0 invoices paid

A BALANCE IS NOT A BUDGET. A balance is what the wallet holds; a budget is what
THIS connection may spend before the player is asked again. On a screen somebody
is about to spend from, showing one where the other is meant is the wrong number
in the worst place - so the line names which it is, and no branch renders a bare
figure: "not asked for yet", "budget unknown: …", "this wallet does not report a
budget" are all words.

`paintWallet` is driven off the shipped page as before: a connected wallet with
an allowance renders the client's own line, one that cannot say renders the
words, and a DISCONNECTED wallet renders nothing at all - "not asked for yet"
beside an empty box is noise.

Display only. No new spend path; the pin refusing lnbc, bolt11, payInvoice,
nwcCall and pay_invoice in the page's code is unchanged. PlayMode and EditMode
were not in this letter - no C# and no jslib.


M3.2 ITEM 6b - THE SET 27A.4 SPECIFIES DOES NOT EXIST. Pinned before any code
was written for it, and the numbers are the reason the letter is worth writing.

27A.4 gives the object:

    DonationSet {
      network_id
      serial          monotonic; the highest validly signed one wins
      entries[]       lnurl + share_bps, summing to 10000
      valid_from      block height
      signature       by donation_authority_pubkey
    }

`donation.js` implements ENTRIES AND NOTHING ELSE. Counted in the file:
occurrences of serial, validFrom or signature, 0. So what the repo calls a
donation set is the third line of a five-line object, and every property the
other four carry is missing:

    no serial       nothing orders two sets, so there is no "highest wins"
                    and no rollback to refuse. A thief's older set and an
                    honest newer one are indistinguishable objects.
    no valid_from   nothing says from when a set applies, so two nodes
                    paying at different moments can pay different lists.
    no signature    ANYBODY CAN PUBLISH A SET. The bytes stand or fail on
                    their shares alone; nothing ties them to the authority
                    key whose whole job in this protocol is to sign this
                    one object.

AND THE AUTHORITY KEY HAS NO CODE AT ALL. `AUTHORITY_PUBKEY_REGTEST`,
`RECOVERY_PUBKEY_REGTEST` and their testnet4 twins are in `genesis-ids.js` and
are hashed into `network_id` by `computeNetworkId`. Readers of those four
constants outside `genesis-ids.js`, `make-genesis.mjs` and their own test: 0.
Occurrences of AuthorityRotation, authorityRotation, donationAuthority or
donation_authority anywhere in `packages/*/src`: 0, all of them in a comment
quoting 27A.4. The two keys define the network and neither can do anything.

27A.4's recovery path is the sharper half of that: "recovery CAN name a new
authority", "from valid_from, sets signed by the old authority are rejected and
only the new one is accepted, whatever serial the old key publishes". None of
those sentences is code. PRIORITIES 6b says why that is not acceptable to
defer - "a key with no exercised revocation path is a key whose revocation does
not work" - and the row it answers is the one that matters: authority stolen,
the thief signs a higher serial pointing at their own LNURLs, and the remedy is
a rotation with no fork and no census lost.

CALLERS OUTSIDE donation.js AND ITS OWN TESTS, counted across every package,
the client bundle and the served page:

    donationSetStands        0
    splitDonation            0
    donationAfterFailures    0
    donatedMsat              0
    encodeDonationSet        0
    canonicalLnurl           0
    decodeDonationSet        0
    donationSetMatchesRound  0
    donationSetId           17   the contract field only
    anything paying an LNURL 0

Six helpers with a full test suite each and nobody calling them, which is the
same shape `heat()`, `payWithCommittee`, `feeMatchesEntry`, `invoiceMatchesEntry`
and `trustedDealerSplit` were all found in: rules written against a spec
paragraph, correct in isolation, wired to nothing.

WHAT THIS LETTER IS NOT. `donationMsat` is written `0n` by `join.js` and read by
nothing, and it stays that way here: no money moves, no LNURL is paid, no
donation touches the page's stake path, and `feeMatchesEntry` and the entry door
are not opened. Charging a donation at all waits on 6e, because the code
charges on top and 6b says inclusive.


M3.2 ITEM 6b, THE OBJECT AND THE KEY. 27A.4's DonationSet exists.

    packages/protocol/src/authority.js          new
    packages/protocol/test/donation-authority.test.js    12 tests, stub curve
    packages/blwp-node/test/donation-rotation.test.js     3 tests, real BIP-340

    protocol      444 -> 456
    blwp-node     406 -> 409
    blwp-client   184, core 89
    money guard   19 -> 20 files clean   (authority.js is on the list: its
                                          serial is the ordering a theft is
                                          undone by)
    determinism guard  21 files clean

WHAT THE FOUR MISSING FIELDS BUY, each measured as a refusal:

    network_id    a set for another network is refused. 27A.9's anchor is the
                  client's own built-in id, and someone who forks the code and
                  writes their own address in "has not captured the donations -
                  they have left".
    serial        the highest validly signed one wins; the same set re-offered
                  at an older serial after a newer one changes nothing, whatever
                  order the objects arrive in.
    valid_from    a set published for height 900000 is not in force at 899999
                  and is at 900000. Arrival is not a time two nodes agree on.
    signature     an unsigned set is refused (64 bytes expected, none present),
                  and one signed by a stranger is refused by key. Before this,
                  both stood.

TWO SETS AT ONE SERIAL. 27A.4 does not say, because an honest authority does
not do it. Two deterministic answers were available and the contested serial is
dropped rather than decided by bytes: picking the lower hash pays whichever
list a key that has already signed twice managed to shape, and does it
silently. So serial 5 signed twice leaves serial 4 in force, from either order
of arrival, and the refusal says which serial died. That is where 27A.4's "both
lost" row already puts the network - "the set freezes at its last published
serial" - and a frozen set is a bounded failure where paying a thief is not.

THE ROTATION, ON REAL KEYS. blwp-node/test/donation-rotation.test.js signs with
@noble's BIP-340, the same curve the daemon signs adverts and payout tables
with, because "the recovery key revokes the authority" is a sentence about a
signature and a stub cannot speak it.

    height 200, no rotation     the thief's serial 500 wins and lnurl1thief is
                                paid. The damage is shown before the remedy.
    height 299, rotated at 300  still the thief: a rotation applies from its
                                own height, not on arrival
    height 300                  ok false. EVERY set the old key signed is
                                refused - 2 of 2, the honest serial 2 included
    new authority republishes    serial 3, the network's own recipients
    old key tries serial 9000    refused, 3 of 4 by signature

A ROTATION BLANKS THE LIST, and that is the section's own reading rather than a
strictness of taste: "from valid_from, sets signed by the old authority are
rejected". The alternative was measured on paper and is worse - grandfathering
what the old key published before the rotation keeps the THIEF'S set alive too,
because the thief published before the rotation as well. A revocation that
leaves the stolen list in force is not a revocation. The price is that the
network pays nobody between the rotation and the new authority's first
publication.

WHAT THE TWO KEYS CANNOT DO, checked rather than stated: the authority key
signing its own rotation produces a real signature by the wrong key and is
refused, so the working key cannot promote itself; the recovery key signing a
donation set is refused, so the cold key cannot publish payees; and a rotation
has four fields, none of them a new recovery key - one theft of the cold key
cannot close the door behind itself.

CALLERS, the count this letter was opened on:

    encodeDonationSet        0 -> 1   (the body the authority signs)
    decodeDonationSet        0 -> 1   (a publication inherits every list check)
    donationSetStands        0 -> 1   (before the key, so the refusal names the
                                       actual fault)
    donationSetMatchesRound  0 -> 1   (the round's binding is unchanged: the
                                       contract names the RECIPIENTS' hash,
                                       which is a different id from the
                                       publication's)
    splitDonation            0 -> 1   (a zero donation, to pin that it stays 0)
    AUTHORITY_PUBKEY_*       0 -> 1   donationKeysFor(network)
    RECOVERY_PUBKEY_*        0 -> 1

AND NO MONEY MOVED. donationMsat is written 0n by join.js and read by nothing,
feeMatchesEntry and the entry door are untouched, no LNURL is paid, nothing was
mixed into the page's stake path, and a test refuses payInvoice, pay_invoice,
lnbc, fetch( and WebSocket in both donation files. Nothing in packages/core.
The shipped bundle grew 1387 bytes - the two new type bytes and the comment
that says why they are two - and the template's copy is the bundle again.
Deployed for that reason alone: btc-logistics-core.pages.dev serves
blwp-client.js md5 4a6805b9a72afa6d50130f0647c97a56, the repo's byte for byte,
HTTP 200. Nothing the page DOES changed in this letter.

STILL NOT BUILT HERE: publication. 27A.4 says a set is "published like an
advertisement - a marked output committing to H(DonationSet)", and nothing
writes one, so a node is handed sets rather than finding them. Parked with the
other data-availability limits, beside the set preimage nobody publishes.

THE 283/623 mm IS A CONSTANT 8-TICK OFFSET, not a wrong path: P2's ghost of P1
labelled 105 is P1's core pose at core tick 113 (-99.702) exactly, and 147 is
155 (-97.106) exactly; parked, t651 = P1's core (-91.520,-57.800). Both entries
join at tick 0 and the daemon numbers from the join tick. It is P1's PAGE:
core 632 while publishing 622 with 2 held (P2: 624 / 618 / 6 held).

WHY, read in blwp.jslib: when the round's seed resolves the core is re-inited
(`b.core.init(net.seedWord)`, tick 0), then four network round trips run -
Client.at, openRound, join, connect - before `setRound`. `net.tick` returns
while `!net.client` and `client.record` returns false while `!this.where`, so
every tick Unity steps in that window is simulated and never published: 8 on
P1's reload, 0 on P2's. `net.seen` counts only recorded ticks while `markNow`
hashes the live core, so a checkpoint from such a tab names the wrong tick too.

## Two-tab ghost, hole (b): checkpoints on the old and the new Daily (2026-09-10)

Same round, both tabs at 400 ms: P1 on the current Daily (fdd1562c), P2 on the
last deployment before the jslib relabel (164b5b2c, b3e81c4). A hook installed
before load wraps `Client.markNow` and records each call's label, the core's
own tick at that moment, and the node's answer; then each daemon is asked
`/checkpoints` for that seat. ~25 s after roll-out:

                         NEW Daily                      OLD Daily
    labels = core tick   4 of 4 (60/60 120/120 180/180) 0 of 4 (60/68 120/128 180/188)
    node's answers       1 receipted, 3 refused         1 receipted, 3 refused
    refusal              "error the checkpoint does not follow the chain head" (both)
    page counters        sent 1, skipped 0              sent 1, skipped 0
    stored A / B         1 / 0                          1 / 0

THE RELABEL IS RIGHT: every checkpoint now names the tick its core is on (the
old build's are 8 ticks off). THE CHAIN IS BROKEN ON BOTH BUILDS, and it is not
this letter's change: only a run's FIRST checkpoint is accepted; every later
one is refused for not following the chain head. The page's counters hide it -
`marksSent` counts receipts and a refusal is counted as neither sent nor
skipped, which is why "sent 1, skipped 0" read as quiet. Daemon B stores none:
checkpoints go to the socket's node only.

THE CAUSE, read in the code and the spec (not changed):
  - the client moves its chain head only on a LIVE checkpoint (client.js:629),
    and `receiptsForLive` is 2 on the Daily's 2-of-2 (gameVerifySlots 2) - both
    daemons must receipt it (13C: the canonical chain carries receipts from a
    quorum of the committee)
  - the client sends each checkpoint on its one socket, to one node (daemon A);
    B stored 0. Section 10's "receipt gossip" is committee members exchanging
    digests of receipts they issued - it does not carry checkpoints - and
    `recoverReceipts` asks the client's own node only
  - so the first checkpoint never goes live, `this.head` never moves, and every
    later checkpoint names the old parent: A refuses "does not follow the chain
    head". Both builds.
  - the spec's reading of delivery: section 10 "a checkpoint is accepted when
    enough nodes receive it ... nodes return a signed CheckpointReceipt";
    section 11 "the client periodically sends batches and checkpoints" - the
    CLIENT delivers checkpoints to the committee.
  - consequence: no Daily run builds a checkpoint chain with a quorum of
    receipts, so by 13C none has a canonical transcript; a paying round would
    end in the no-quorum rule until checkpoints reach the committee.

### (b) after: every checkpoint reaches both daemons, and the chain grows on A and on B (c3d8659, on the Daily)

The client now seats the entry on every node the round named and sends each
checkpoint to all of them at once, verifying each receipt; the head moves when
the mark is live. The node list reaches `Client.at` as `discovery.nodes` from
the page's own wrapper (`index.html`, `window.BLWP_NODES`); no client src file
reads the page (the source guard is unchanged and passes). Page counters:

### Both daemons hold the run's inputs, not only its checkpoints (ed5a517, on the Daily)

Every input batch this client's node takes is kept and fed, in order, to every
other node the page's node list names (the §11 send). A peer that refuses for a
missing seat is seated again; any refusal stops that peer's feed until the next
batch or checkpoint retries, and shows as "inputs refused N" on the status
line. A batch answer is an unsigned count of new ticks - the protocol has no
batch receipt - so what is checked is that each node answers a count for it.

### An honest next checkpoint no longer becomes a fork proof because a peer was down (cut (c) still OPEN on the funnel map)

The client keeps a checkpoint that some node stored but the committee did not
carry (`pendingLink`). Before any new checkpoint it re-sends those same bytes
to every node - a node that has it answers with the receipt it already issued,
a node that missed it stores it - and the new checkpoint chains onto it once it
is live. If it still is not live, the new checkpoint is NOT sent (it would name
the head before the pending link: the second child of one parent), it is
counted as skipped, and the line says "pending link T". "relinked N" counts
links carried after a re-send.

### A peer's closed connection is no longer counted as a refusal (cut (c) still OPEN on the funnel map)

A connection to a peer that could not be made or dropped now answers
`closed: ...`, never the `error ...` a node says. The input feed counts it as
closed and as one "peer drop" per time the peer went away; a checkpoint a peer
never received is "unreached", not "refused".

### MEASURED, NOT FIXED: the client's own socket closing mid-batch counts as the node refusing, and two such drops end an honest run VOID

One real daemon, the page's reconnect wired as the bridge wires it
(`client.onDrop = () => client.reconnect(...)`); the batch frame in flight is
swallowed and the socket closed 5 ms later (scratchpad/m-drop.mjs):

    baseline      batch answer 60, nextTick 60, ready
    drop 1        answer "error the socket closed" -> refusals 1, refusedWhy
                  "error the socket closed", resynced true, drops 1;
                  reconnect -> ready, "resumed 60", 30 held
    drop 2        (no batch landed between the drops) answer "error the socket
                  closed" -> refusals 2 -> ENDED VOID: "the node refuses this
                  run's inputs at tick 60: error the socket closed - and it
                  still refused after resyncing, so this client cannot publish
                  and nothing from here can be replayed"

The node refused nothing. `drain` treats every non-count answer as a refusal
and `#afterRefusal` resyncs once, then ends the run on the next; the main
socket's close answers its waiting batch with `error the socket closed`, the
same shape as a node's refusal. A disconnect is not a refusal, and VOID is
decided here for a player who only lost the link twice. The peer side was
split in 12ce726; this is the same mix-up on the client's own connection.

### The player's own socket closing mid-batch is a disconnect, not a refusal - two drops leave the run alive (cut (c) still OPEN on the funnel map)

The client's own socket, closing with a batch in flight, now answers with the
same `closed: ...` word the peers use, never the `error ...` a node says. The
drain holds the batch and counts it "interrupted"; it does not count a refusal
and does not resync towards VOID. On the reconnect, `resume` now drops from the
hold any words the node already took (a batch whose answer was lost) and feeds
the peers every batch the node holds.

One real daemon, the page's reconnect, two drops with no batch landing between
(scratchpad/m-drop2.mjs; pinned by test/own-socket-drop.test.js). Every tick
carries its own index, so a misplaced tick shows:

                              before (583c4a6)                 after
    A. frame lost x2          VOID at tick 60 ("the node       alive; refusals 0,
                              refuses this run's inputs ...    interrupted 2;
                              error the socket closed");       node 150 of 150
                              refusals 2; node 60 of 120       ticks, each in place
    B. answer lost x2         VOID at tick 90; node 150        alive; refusals 0,
       (node took the batch)  ticks for 120 recorded, tick     interrupted 2, landed
                              90 holding the input for 60      unheard 2; 150 of 150,
                                                               each in place
    a node that says no       -                                refused 1, interrupted 0,
       (wrong batch head)                                      one resync, run goes on

A node that keeps refusing still ends the run VOID by name (refused-batch.test.js,
unchanged and green). blwp-client 206/206 (81 + 78 + 47); blwp-node 422/422
(131 + 88 + 118 + 85). No C#.

### A checkpoint that wakes after the player's own link went is skipped, not refused and not half-sent - (c) now BLOCKED only on the funnel map

The last disconnect-vs-refusal path on (c): a mark waits for B; the player's
own socket drops; B returns and is fed without it (the peer feed needs no own
socket) and the mark wakes with no socket to its own node. Two real daemons,
no reconnect wired (scratchpad/m-wait-drop.mjs; pinned as checkpoint-quorum
test 8, which also reconnects and carries on):

                                                             client's own node went ..."
    counted as              refused 1                        skipped 1, refused 0
    sent to                 B alone (stored on B, pending)   nobody; A 0 B 0, no pending link
    after the reconnect     -                                mark 120 live on both, 1/1,
                                                             same chain, /equivocation 204/204

THE FOLLOW-UP, answered:
- Disconnect vs refusal, every path: the node treats a player's socket close as
  nothing but the end of its ghost watch. Client: batch in flight (71271bf),
  resync (only on a node's own "error ..."), hold and republish (resume trims
  what the node already took), peer fan-out and peer checkpoints (12ce726), a
  mark in flight on the own socket (unreached), and now a mark that wakes

it never saw stays queued" is unchanged and green (a failed send stays queued).

FOUND, AND IT IS NOT THIS LETTER'S TO DECIDE: THE OWED SATS DO NOT STAY IN THE
POOL. The spend on the chain is 900 sats in, 336 out to 1 output, fee 564 - the
252 owed sats go to the miner. Item 16's own rule (above) says they are "not
folded into the fee - the miner is not who the round owes" and "stay in the
pool with the debt recorded". `payoutOutputs` makes no change output on purpose
("the alternative is an output an operator chooses the destination of"), so
every sub-floor debt is recorded against money that has already left. A change
output back to the pool's own script is chosen by nobody - but it needs a fee
the committee agrees on, and there is no fee rate in the contract, the code or
the spec (grepped). That is a MONEY-class value: Daniel's ruling.

THE DAILY'S LAUNCHERS SHARE ONE LND BETWEEN TWO DAEMONS, and that is why they
are not wired. `run-2of2.mjs` and `round-2of2.mjs` start A and B in one process
against "one bitcoind/LND". The client posts each entry to every daemon's
`/entry` (`client.js` 513), and `/entry` calls `custody.hold` (`server.js` 626)
- so both daemons would `addholdinvoice` the same payment hash on the same lnd,
and the second collides. Handing both the same port is a design choice (which
daemon holds a stake, or one lnd per daemon), not a wiring step.

CORRECTION, SAME EVENING: the shared lnd is not a design question - the spec
answers it. §23.1 step 3: "The settlement committee's Lightning endpoint
(§23.6) issues a hold invoice for payment_hash"; step 5: STAKE_COMMITTED "once
>=5 settlement nodes have seen the held HTLC". One endpoint, several daemons,
which is exactly the 2-of-2's shape.

### A second daemon on the committee's one endpoint takes up the hold instead of colliding

Measured first, `custody-restart-lnd.mjs` with a second daemon (its own store)
holding each entry on bob's lnd right after the first:

    before   the run stopped: lncli addholdinvoice refused: [lncli] rpc error:
             code = Unknown desc = invoice with payment hash already exists

- thrown out of `custody.hold`, not even a refusal. `lndPort.createHeld` now
reads lnd's own "already exists" as the endpoint having issued it: it looks the
invoice up and takes it up only while it is OPEN or ACCEPTED, with lnd's own
`payment_request` and amount, so `invoiceMatchesEntry` still checks what comes
back. A SETTLED or CANCELED invoice for that hash is refused by name; any other
lncli error still throws.

Pins (lnd-port.test.js): an OPEN and an ACCEPTED hold are taken up, read back;
SETTLED and CANCELED are refused; "connection refused" still throws. Mutant
"take up whatever state" killed (5/6). lnd-port + custody 30/30.

After, on the real lnd, both kill points: the second daemon holds each entry
"HELD, the same invoice" (2 of 2 entries), and the rest of the run is
unchanged - point 1 HELD then SETTLED on the next close, point 2 SETTLED, bob
gains exactly 98000 msat once, "no problems" x2. blwp-node 432/432.

NOT YET: "seen by >=5" as a recorded STAKE_COMMITTED, and which daemon's hold
settles or cancels - both daemons now hold the same invoice, and 23.4's five of
seven decides the settle.

### No play on a stake nobody paid: a node signs nothing for an entry until its lnd shows the stake held in full

§23.1 step 5: "STAKE_COMMITTED is recorded once >=5 settlement nodes have seen
the held HTLC. Play begins only after this." §9 step 7 puts it between the
wallet paying and play.

Measured first: nothing gated play on payment. An unpaid OPEN invoice reads
HELD (lnd's OPEN and ACCEPTED both map to it), `paidMsat` had no caller outside
`lnd-port.js`, and test/stake-committed.test.js failed 0/2 - an input batch for
an unpaid stake was taken ('1'), and so was play in a paying round on a node
with no Lightning at all.

Now:
- `Custody.seenPaid(entryId)`: a free round (stake 0) passes without asking; a
  stake already seen answers from its row; otherwise it asks Lightning and passes
  only when the state is HELD and `paidMsat` covers the hold's amount, then
  writes that once (`stake_seen`, a new table, so a store written before it
  gains it).
- The socket gates every input batch and checkpoint for a seated entry on it,
  refused by name ("the stake is not paid and held: 0 of 98000 msat, Lightning
  says HELD"; "this node reaches no Lightning, so it cannot see this stake
  held"). THE FRAMES ARE ORDERED: every frame on a socket waits for the one
  before it, so a batch cannot overtake the batch it chains to because
  Lightning answered one faster.
- Each node gates its own receipts, so the spec's >=5 is the receipt threshold
  the client already needs.

After: stake-committed 2/2. Mutant "seen held whatever was paid" killed.

On a real lnd (custody-restart-lnd.mjs --point=1), both stakes: before alice
pays, "the stake is not paid and held: 0 of 98000 msat, Lightning says HELD";
after, "HELD, 98000 msat" - lnd's ACCEPTED with amt_paid_msat. The rest of the
run unchanged, "no problems".

THE FALLOUT WAS FIXTURES, AND EVERY ONE WAS THE GATE: 26 blwp-node and 38
blwp-client tests played a 100000-msat round with no stake paid, and each
failure read one of the two refusals above (sampled per group; no ordering
failure). They are about marks, ghosts and verdicts, not payment, so they

### The gate's own regression, found and closed: a player paying at wallet speed lost the run

The page pays from a button (`payTheStake`, WebGL index.html) and nothing
stops the player driving first, so ticks go out before the HTLC is accepted.
The client treats a refused batch as a disagreement: resync once, and a second
refusal ends the run. Measured, test/stake-wait.test.js (blwp-client), before:

    the node refuses this run's inputs at tick 0: error the stake is not paid
    and held: 0 of 98000 msat, Lightning says HELD - and it still refused after
    resyncing ...                                                -> VOID

So 1c0f9ed made a late payer lose the round. Now the wait has a word of its
own, `STAKE_NOT_SEEN` in protocol/src/constants.js, which the node puts on the
gate's refusal and the client matches - neither side reads the other's prose.
On the client's own drain the ticks stay held and are sent again on the next
drain (`stakeWaits`, not `refusals`, no resync); on a peer feed the feed stops
uncounted and the next batch asks again. A stake never paid still ends the run
when the hold is full - that rule is unchanged.

After: 60 ticks driven unpaid -> not ended, 0 refusals, 0 taken, 60 held; the
port reports paid -> the next drain publishes all 60. refused-batch 4/4
unchanged (a node that keeps refusing for a real reason still ends the run).
blwp-node 434/434, blwp-client 208/208.

### A hold invoice is paid long before the wallet says so: the page asks the node

`Client.payStake` believed only the wallet: `pay_invoice`'s answer with a
preimage, or nothing. A real wallet answers when the payment COMPLETES, and a
hold invoice completes only when the round settles or cancels it - minutes
later, and as a failure for every winner (whose stake is cancelled back). So
in a real round the page would have said "the wallet did not answer" (30 s
default) while the stake sat held, and the spending log would never have
counted it. The fixture that answered at once with a preimage is the unusual
wallet, not the usual one.

Measured first (wallet-nwc.test.js, a wallet that takes pay_invoice and never
answers, the node's port showing the HTLC paid once asked):

    before   ok false: "the wallet did not answer in 3000 ms"  (node: held)
    GET /stake                                                  404, no door

Now:
- `GET /stake?entry=` on the node: 200 {state, paidMsat} when this node has
  seen the stake held (`Custody.seenPaid`, the same answer the play gate
  uses), 409 "stake not seen: ..." when not, 404 for an entry it never seated
  and 400 for a malformed id - neither of those two asks Lightning.
- `payStake` races the wallet's answer against the node's: a stake the node has
  seen held IS paid (`held: true`, `preimage: null` - the wallet's preimage
  arrives with its answer, which for a hold may be minutes away), and the log
  records it. Before reporting a wallet failure it asks the node once more,
  because a wallet that timed out may have paid anyway.

After: the silent wallet -> ok, paid, held, 98000 msat, 1 request, 1 log
entry. A silent wallet with a node that never sees it -> still "did not answer
in 400 ms". The honest path (a wallet that answers with a preimage) unchanged.
stake-committed 3/3. blwp-node 435/435, blwp-client 210/210. Bundle rebuilt,
template copy equal.

### The hold's refund timelock is lnd's default, and sizing it is a ruling

§23.1: "CLTV is sized in days, comfortably beyond round + objection window +
result window + claim window, so that delay is never loss." The spec lists
`htlc_cltv_days` among the round contract's fields (line 1289).

What a hold gets today: `lndPort.createHeld` passes `--expiry` (the invoice's
own expiry) and nothing for the HTLC timelock, so lnd's default applies. The
real-lnd run (custody-lnd.mjs) measured it: the void HTLC expired at height
345 with the chain at 262 - 83 blocks, ~14 h at ten minutes a block. lncli
offers `addholdinvoice --cltv_expiry_delta`, so passing a value is mechanical.

WHY NOTHING WAS CHANGED. The old blocker - no tick rate - is gone:
`protocol/src/tick.js` converts `blockTicks` to milliseconds exactly, and the
contract carries `startTimeMs`, `entryCloseMs` and `objectionWindowMs`. But
two things remain a choice, not a derivation:
  - a CLTV counts BLOCKS, which can come faster than ten minutes; the spec's
    answer to that variance is a margin "in days"
  - the result window and the claim window are not in the contract, and
    `claim_window_days` is listed as unchosen
So `htlc_cltv_days` is a value for Daniel, like the node fee rate - not a
constant to invent in the money path. Named in PRIORITIES as a ruling.

### Where a loser's settled stake goes, and why the pool never receives it

Measured: nothing in `blwp-node/src` or `protocol/src` sends a settled
stake anywhere after `settleinvoice`. A grep for sendcoins, sendtoaddress,
sweep and any pool funding finds no code; every pool output ever spent
(payout-regtest, payout-committee-regtest, settle-regtest,
settle-crash-regtest) was funded by the HARNESS with `sendtoaddress` to the
pool address. So:

    a loser's stake     settled by lnd into ONE operator's channel balance
    a winner's payout   spent from the pool's P2TR output, 5 of 7
    between the two     nothing - no code, no letter

THE SPEC HAS NO SUCH GAP, and that is the finding. §23.2: a loser is
"Settle the HTLC -> stake enters the pool wallet", and a qualifier's payout is
"Lightning payment from the pool wallet". §23.5: "Settled loser stakes
accumulate in a wallet whose every operation requires a 5-of-7 threshold
signature". §23.6 builds that wallet as a threshold-signed Lightning node or a
Fedimint-class federation, "and the Round Contract names which construction it
uses". In the spec the Lightning endpoint that settles IS the pool.

Item 13 built the pool as an on-chain taproot output with no script path, and
custody as one lnd (`lnd-port.js`: "SINGLE-NODE CUSTODY, NOT §23.5"). A bridge
between them is not a send: settled sats are channel balance, and getting them
on-chain is a channel close or a swap that one operator performs - custody by
one party in the middle of the path the pool exists to make threshold-only.

So it is a construction ruling, named in PRIORITIES with three options: an
interim single-operator bridge said out loud, a federation (the spec's advice
for V1), or a threshold Lightning node. Nothing was built around it.

IMPLEMENTATION.md 9.4 (quoted in PRIORITIES item 8):

    AWAITING_INVOICE -> HELD -> (result FINAL)
       qualifying: CANCEL_REQUESTED -> CANCELLED -> PAYOUT_QUEUED -> PAID
       losing:     SHARES_REQUESTED -> PREIMAGE_READY -> SETTLE_REQUESTED -> SETTLED

Current labels, measured before the change:

    the moment before an invoice exists   not written at all - the first row
                                          was HELD, after the endpoint answered
    a cancel, before the call             ACTING
    a settle, before the call             ACTING  (custody.js called it "the only
                                          state in this file that is not 23.2's")

The settle seat is in this change because it wore the same stand-in: leaving
it on ACTING would leave the old label written, and no test could say "no seat
is left on it".

THE PIN (custody.test.js), red before on today's code - 6 of 19 custody tests:
- a cancel is on disk as CANCEL_REQUESTED and a settle as SETTLE_REQUESTED at
  the moment the port is called, and neither is ACTING;
- AWAITING_INVOICE is on disk when the endpoint is asked, HELD after the check;
- a node that died awaiting its invoice asks again and holds, rather than
  answering "already has a hold" with no invoice;
- the three mid-settle assertions read SETTLE_REQUESTED where they read ACTING.
Mutant "write ACTING for both acts": 4 red. Mutant "skip the AWAITING_INVOICE
write": 2 red.

WHAT ELSE THE NAMES NEEDED, each measured:
- STORES ALREADY ON DISK: ACTING is still READ, never written. `MID_ACT` is the
  three labels meaning "asked, never answered"; reconcile (on start and per

- A REFUSED INVOICE: writing AWAITING_INVOICE first turned an old test red -

- A CLOSE REACHING AN AWAITING_INVOICE ROW acts on nothing and says "no invoice
  was ever confirmed for that stake".
- THE CLIENT reads only the node's `x-hold` word, and a hold still answers
  HELD, a refusal `none` - unchanged.

ON A REAL LND (custody-restart-lnd.mjs, both kill points): the killed node's
row reads SETTLE_REQUESTED on disk (was ACTING), restart (a) leaves it,
restart (b) resolves it to lnd's own HELD / SETTLED, 98000 msat moved once,

custody-crash.mjs (fake port, SIGKILL inside a settle) had not reached its

### M3.3-21: the player sees how many settlement nodes have seen their stake held

§23.1 step 5: "STAKE_COMMITTED is recorded once >=5 settlement nodes have seen
the held HTLC." Each node already answered `GET /stake` from its own Lightning;
the page asked only the node it joined, and printed something else.

### A round for sats, rehearsed on regtest through the real daemons: where every msat went, and the holes

`tools/round-rehearsal-lnd.mjs`: its own bitcoind and two lnd v0.21.3-beta
(alice pays; bob is the committee's one Lightning endpoint). Two daemons from
`standUpRound` - bonded, censused, the beacon off this chain - both on bob
through BLWP_LND_* (the launchers' own parse), a 100000-msat round. Three
players take the page's own steps (settlement seats, stakeFor, postHandout,
entryFor, Client.at, join): P1 drives a world secret the verifier's own
`replay()` says DELIVERS, P2 one it says FAILS, P3 pays and never plays. Both
daemons close; the committee's own result decides. Nothing on testnet or
mainnet is touched.

THE FIRST GAP, as predicted, with its number: a regtest daemon given Lightning
had NO preflight (`askLnd` knows only a testnet4 lnd.conf), and a node with a
port and no preflight opens no paying round -

    POST /round 100000 msat  -> 503 "this node holds stakes and has no preflight"
    POST /round      0 msat  -> 201

Closed (code): `askLndRegtest` / `lndPreflightRegtest` ask the regtest lnd with
the port's own flags and `readonly.macaroon`, refusing any node that answers as
another network; `lightningFromEnv` hands it out on regtest. `standUpRound`
takes `stakeMsat` (default 0 - every caller unchanged). The rehearsal's round
opened at 100000 msat.

THE REHEARSAL (two runs; the second instrumented):

    settlement seats              2, agreed by 2 daemons
    P1 world                      #7 tried, DELIVERED by tick 1260 (score 33)
    P2 world                      #1 tried, FAILED by tick 480 (score 45)
    x-hold at the seat            HELD for all three
    stake seen (M3.3-21, real lnd) 2 of 2 (2 needed), committed - all three
    in flight after paying        294000 msat (3 x 98000)
    published                     P1 1260/1260, P2 480/480, 0 refused
    close                         "closed" on both daemons

    what each daemon's close saw (A and B identical):
      P1 replay   stored false - "no checkpoint of that entry is carried by 2
                  committee members: the first has 1"
      P2 replay   stored false - the same
      P3 replay   stored false - "that transcript carries no ticks"
      the close   "that round produced no result to pay on"; agreed []

    WHERE THE MSAT WENT
      P1 DELIVERED   lnd CANCELED -> back to alice (by expiry, not by the close)
      P2 FAILED      lnd CANCELED -> back to alice (by expiry, not by the close)
      P3 VOID        lnd CANCELED -> back to alice (HTLC expiry 366, chain 283)
      alice 996530000 -> 996530000 msat (0); bob (the operator) +0

So today a real round settles NOTHING: the loser keeps the stake, the winner is
paid nothing, and every hold goes home on its own timelock. The safe direction,
and not settlement.

THE HOLES, each with its kind:
- [code, OPEN, the next piece] NO DAEMON EVER CARRIES A CHECKPOINT'S RECEIPTS
  ACROSS THE COMMITTEE. Each daemon stores only its own receipt, so 13C's
  canonical transcript ("receipts from at least T committee nodes") never
  exists on any node, and no run is ever replayed to a signed result. The
  client COLLECTS both receipts (every mark went live at the client) and
  forwards none; the node ACCEPTS a peer's receipt on the socket (`takeReceipt`)
  and serves its own on `GET /receipts`, and nothing in any daemon ever fetches
  a peer's. The only receipt gossip in the repo is a test handing one over by
  hand. It belongs on the daemons, not the client: a losing player who simply
  did not forward receipts would reach no-quorum and a VOID refund, which 13C
  says a player cannot manufacture. Every earlier settlement proof handed the
  node its second receipt or result directly.
- [code, CLOSED] the regtest preflight, above.
- [ruling] how a settled stake reaches the pool - unchanged, and NOT reached by
  this rehearsal: nothing was settled, so nothing was owed and no seat asked
  for a spend. The earlier measurement (a loser's settle lands in the
  operator's lnd; the pool is harness-funded) stands.
- [ruling] the owed-sats fee rate and htlc_cltv_days - unchanged; this hold
  again carried lnd's default timelock (expiry 83 blocks past payment).
- [inbound] the same round on testnet4 needs 196000 msat of inbound on the
  operator's node, which has 0.
- NOT YET MEASURABLE, behind the receipts hole: two daemons settling ONE
  invoice on the shared endpoint (the second settle), the objection window
  before finality, and the pool payout path.

### M3.3-27: the Client.at flake is a dead kept-alive socket, reused after a held event loop

THE SHARE. Every rehearsal that stopped before play since the committee-time
wait was this refusal: rehearsal-3, the first M3.3-25 AB run, 8-AB and 10-BA
(rehearsal-4, the other pre-play stop, was the committee time, fixed then).

INSTRUMENTED FIRST, NO BEHAVIOUR CHANGED. `discover` already handed back each
provider's refusal; `Client.at` dropped it and threw only "only 1 of 2
providers gave a chain". It now carries it (`refused`), and the chain check
carries the fetch's `cause` - Node's fetch says only "fetch failed" and puts
the socket's words there. The harness and a new probe
(`tools/client-at-probe.mjs`: its own bitcoind, the two daemons, no lnd, a
free round, N asks of `Client.at`) print, per provider, its error, how long
that origin had been idle, the tip it answered straight after, how long the
event loop was held, and - `tools/socket-watch.mjs`, undici's diagnostics
channels joined to the daemons' own server sockets - which socket the failed
request rode.

    probe, 50 asks, gaps 0-10000 ms slept (loop free)       0 of 50 refused
    rehearsal batch 12-15, AB and BA side by side          3 of 8 stopped before play,
      12-BA  provider 0: fetch failed: ECONNRESET, idle 6537 ms before the ask
      14-BA  provider 0: fetch failed: ECONNRESET, idle 9582 ms
      15-AB  provider 0: fetch failed: ECONNRESET, idle 6052 ms
      straight after, both /headers 200, 3 headers, the same tip - the chain
      was never in question
    probe, loop HELD synchronously 6000 ms before each ask   20 of 20 refused,
      every one ECONNRESET (10 provider 0, 1 provider 1, 9 both)
    probe, loop held 3000 ms                                0 of 20 refused
    probe held 6000 ms, socket watcher                     5 of 5 refused: every
      failed request rode a REUSED socket (usesBefore 1) idle ~6000 ms; the
      daemon's side closed 0 ms before the error or was closing it

(The first stall gauge, `monitorEventLoopDelay`, read 0 ms on the held probe
too - a hold is recorded only when the loop next runs - so it proved nothing
and was replaced by a 100 ms tick's open gap, which reads 6000.)

WHY THE REHEARSAL HOLDS IT: between a player's last fetch (`worldSeedFor`)
and `Client.at`, the harness runs `worldFor`, a synchronous replay search -
seconds, longer beside a second rehearsal. Node's server lets an idle socket go
after 5 s; the client's pool cannot notice while its loop is held, and the
first read after the hold rides the dead socket. A browser asks again by
itself, so the page never met this; Node's fetch does not.

THE SHAPE, on a bare server (default 5 s keep-alive, loop held 6 s): one
pooled socket reads fine (3 of 3); three pooled sockets to one origin, the
next read resets (3 of 3); a shorter keep-alive (2 s held 3 s, 1 s held 2.5 s)
does not reset. Asked once more after the reset: 5 of 5 answered on the
second attempt.

THE FIX (`blwp-client/src/reread.js`): a READ whose connection was already
gone - ECONNRESET, EPIPE, UND_ERR_SOCKET - is asked once more, and only once.
Never a write (a round, an entry, a handout posted twice is a second act),
never a refused connection (a server that is down is down), never an HTTP
answer, never a read its caller aborted. Every idempotent read in the client
goes through it: the headers and bond providers `Client.at` weighs, the
round, randomness, settlement seats, stake-seen, advertisement, receipts,
invoice, entry, transcript and checkpoint reads. The two sources and the
most-work rule are unchanged: the same source is asked the same question.

    stale-socket.test.js (real sockets, 6 s hold)   red before: both
      "fetch failed", cause ECONNRESET; green after
    reread.test.js (stubs)   a lost connection asked once more; a second loss
      is the answer; a POST never twice; ECONNREFUSED, an HTTP error and an
      aborted read never again

### M3.3-29: the second daemon to close is left HELD on a stake lnd settled - measured, then fixed

THE 6 OF 21, TIMED from the close stamps already in the logs. In every one the
second closer turned P2 final - and its settle asked the first for a share -
about 1.8 s before the first closer turned P2 final on its own re-gather:

    run        order  closes (ms)  second closer's P2 final  first closer's P2 final
    12-AB      AB     0 / 353      B +1766                   A +3596
    16-AB      AB     0 / 348      B +1853                   A +3643
    17-AB      AB     0 / 406      B +2009                   A +3881
    19-AB      AB     0 / 349      B +1755                   A +3863
    20-BA      BA     0 / 353      A +1858                   B +3685
    forced-fix-BA BA  0 / 354      A +1835                   B +3660

The first refused ("no share is handed out before the result is final: 1 of 2
agree on any one run"), the second wrote HELD ("this node has no preimage for
that stake"); the first then settled through lnd, the operator +98000 msat -
and the second never asked again: `watchFinality` stops when no run is short of
final and the table is signed, and on the second closer P2 was final at its own
close. `Custody.reconcile` looks only at rows caught mid-act, never at HELD.
No player money was stuck in any of the six; the second closer's row was wrong,
and a first closer that died after its close would have left the loser's stake
to expire back to the loser.

THE RACE NEEDS ASYMMETRY, and gap 0 removes it. The harness takes
`--close-gap=MS` (the second close sent MS ms after the first, not waiting for
its answer). At 0 ms both daemons store their own P2 result before either
gathers (A +1539, B +1838; A gathers +1709, answered +2101), so both are final
at their first gather and both open the stake with 2 shares - pair 1 at gap 0,
AB and BA: 0 HELD. The race needs the first closer's one gather to miss the
second's result (the second stores ~1.4 s after its own close) and the second
to ask before the first re-gathers (~2 s later): a gap of roughly 0.5-1.6 s.
The natural ~350 ms sits at its lower edge, which is 6 of 21. So the forced
race is `--close-gap=800`; gap 0 is kept as the check it cannot regress.

THE FIX (`server.js`, `watchFinality`): a SETTLE on a FINAL run whose hold is
still HELD - the settle found no preimage - keeps the watch going on its
existing cadence (2 s) inside the same objection window, and each tick runs the
round's own close logic again: the settle asks for the shares again, and a
hold that moved meanwhile answers "already moved". The share is asked again;
nothing is copied from lnd - with one lnd per daemon the other's settle would
never be seen - and a repeated `settleinvoice`, which lnd answers "already
settled" with success, is only the safety net.

### M3.3-30: a VOID stake's timed-out hold is written EXPIRED on the daemon's own chain

BEFORE: 35 of 35 played rehearsals (both close orders) - P3, seated, paid and

THE RULE, the daemon's own: when a hold is first seen paid (`seenPaid`), lnd
supplies one fact - the earliest expiry height among the HTLCs it accepted -
and it is written once (`hold_expiry`, a table of its own). A HELD row whose
recorded height this node's own chain is PAST is EXPIRED (`Custody.expire`);
at the height itself it can still be claimed. lnd is not asked after
seen-time. The height comes from `chainTip`, or from the pool's own bitcoind
call when a launcher gives one (`main.js` does); a sweep every 5 s.

### M3.3-30, the unpaid invoice: it runs out on the daemon's own clock and number

`Custody.hold` writes HELD - "in flight, in nobody's balance" - the moment an
invoice is issued, and for an invoice nobody paid that stayed true forever
while lnd cancelled it at the expiry the daemon asked for (`--expiry 3600`).
Now the daemon records, when it issues the invoice, its issue time plus that
expiry (lnd-port's own `expirySeconds`, never read back from lnd) in
`invoice_expiry`, and a HELD row it never saw paid, past that time, is
EXPIRED: "its invoice ran out unpaid ...: nothing was ever sent". Paid holds
keep the chain-height rule.

THE GUARD, logically required: "never seen paid" is not "never paid" - a
player can pay and be seen by nobody, and that HTLC stays held in lnd past any
invoice expiry. So before the clock expires a row, the sweep asks the one
seen-time question (`seenPaid`: is it paid?). Paid - it is seen, its HTLC
expiry recorded, and the chain decides. "Not paid and held" - EXPIRED. An
answer the node cannot get - left alone.

`funded`, so `serve`'s default `NOTHING_IS_FUNDED` answers every round and every

(:780). Only harnesses pass `funded`, always `() => true`: the rehearsal's

### M3.3-32: settlement waits for the objection window - measured first

THE RULE, 13A: a result the threshold signed is PROVISIONALLY_FINAL; "it
becomes FINAL when the window closes without a valid objection", and "taking a
player's stake requires a final result, an elapsed objection window, and a
threshold quorum". `protocol/src/objection.js` had `finality()` and
`objectionHolds()`; no file in `blwp-node/src` imported either. The daemon
took the gather's quorum as final: `settleTheStakes` settled and cancelled,
`mayRelease` handed out shares, the payout queued - all at the close.

BEFORE, objection-window.test.js on the old code (contract window 3000 ms):

      after the close, on both daemons (three runs: [[977,811],[914,745]],
      [[918,752],[826,668]], [[811,586],[816,610]])
    seven seats: a share of a run the threshold had just signed was released

    the late-objection control passed (nothing to fix there)

M3.3-32 AFTER. `src/finality.js`: `resultFinality(round, roundId, entryId)`
calls `finality()` with the committee's threshold (a new `needed` passthrough,
so 2 of 2 is agreed at 2, not the flat 5) and answers null,
PROVISIONALLY_FINAL, FINAL or SUSPENDED.
  - The window opens when THIS node held the threshold: the `seen_ms` of the
    agreeing record that completed it, off the store. A restart does not open
    it again, and no message opens it earlier.
  - An objection holds per `objectionHolds`: the committee's receipts (this
    node's stored ones) and a replay that contradicts the signed result. The
    replay a daemon has is its own, so a filing at `/objection` holds only on
    a node whose own result is not the run the threshold signed. A filing
    alone suspends nothing - it would let anybody hold every stake past its
    window and hand it back.
  - Gated on FINAL: custody's settle and cancel (`finalFor`), `mayRelease`
    (the share door), and the pool payout (no table is queued while a run of
    the round is inside its window or suspended).
  - The finality watch keeps going while a run waits, reruns the close logic
    once a window has closed, and its deadline moves to a whole window past
    the latest close, so a settle short of shares keeps its old budget.
  - `stakes()` reports `agreed` (the quorum, as before), `final`, `waiting`
    (with each run's `closesAtMs`) and `suspended`.

### M3.3-33: a daemon restarted inside the objection window - measured first

FOUND BY RE-READING M3.3-32's own work: `watchFinality` has one caller, the
close (server.js, the `close ` text door), and it lives in memory. On start the
daemon reconciles only rows it died in the middle of an act on (custody's
SETTLE_REQUESTED / CANCEL_REQUESTED, the payouts). Since M3.3-32 a close moves
nothing for a whole window - ten minutes at the reference - so a daemon that
restarts inside it has nothing left to settle that round.

BEFORE, a new pin in objection-window.test.js: two daemons on file stores, a
3 s window, a winner and a loser, both closed and agreed, both restarted
inside the window on their own stores and the same lnd. 10 s past the window
A's lost stake still read HELD ("in flight, in nobody's balance, until every
condition is met") - it would have expired back to the loser, and the
winner's back on its own timelock rather than by a cancel.

M3.3-33 AFTER. The close's work is one function, `afterClose(roundId)`: replay
and gather (`verifier.settleRound`), the money (`settleTheStakes`), the watch.
The close door calls it, and so does a start: once custody's `reconcile` has
answered, every CLOSED round with a stake still HELD on this node runs
`afterClose` again, one round at a time (`resuming`, on the returned node).
A replay after a restart re-signs nothing - the store keeps the first result
per seat - and a hold that moved is left alone. A daemon shut down while it
replays acts on nothing afterwards.

### How a settled stake reaches the pool - step 1, measured; step 2 blocked

Daniel's pick (2026-09-11): after the window, the settled loser stake funds
the pool that pays the winner, so the operator does not keep it and the
winner is not paid from a side purse.

THE CURRENT PATH, measured on b100863:
  - blwp-node/src: no file sends anything TO the pool output. pool-watch.js,
    pool-signing.js and payout.js only find and spend it. Only harness tools
    fund one (payout-committee-regtest.mjs, labelled STAND-IN).
  - lnd-port.js: four acts - createHeld, look, settle, cancel. No payment and
    no on-chain send, so the daemon cannot move a satoshi out of lnd at all.
  - The real-lnd rehearsal (--mine-before-round=6, AB and BA): 0 of 4 acts
    before the window, VOID rows HELD 0, HELD after lnd settled 0; the
    loser's 98000 msat is in bob's CHANNEL balance (bob +98000, alice
    -98000); both daemons' payout PAYOUT_QUEUED, "this node reaches no
    chain, so it spends nothing".
  - What the round owes, from the protocol's own code for this rehearsal
    (100000 msat stakes, fee 2%): table P1 196000 msat, P2 0, pool 98000;
    `winnings` - what the pool itself pays after P1's cancel returned its
    stake - one row, P1 98000 msat.
  - Dust, on a throwaway regtest bitcoind (bitcoin 31.1): sendtoaddress to a
    taproot address - 98 sat "Transaction amount too small", 329 sat the same,
    330 sat accepted.

WHY STEP 2 STOPS. Three facts, each measured above:
  1. The settled stake is Lightning money in one lnd's channel balance; the
     pool is an on-chain taproot output. Moving one into the other is an act
     by the operator of that lnd - an on-chain send from its wallet, a channel
     close or a swap. That is PRIORITIES' option (a), "an interim bridge, one
     operator", the choice the standing ruling reserves.
  2. At this round's stake the hop cannot be a transaction: 98 sat is under
     the 330-sat dust floor, and so is the winner's 98-sat payout out of the
     pool. An on-chain pool needs a stake floor far above today's, or stakes
     batched across rounds - money rules nobody has set.
  3. The spec pays the winner over Lightning (§23.2: "Lightning payment from
     the pool wallet"; §23.5/23.6: the pool is a 5-of-7 wallet built as a
     threshold LN node or a federation, named in the Round Contract). On one
     shared lnd that is a payment only that lnd's operator can make - single
     custody again, and a winner's invoice the client cannot ask its wallet
     for today (it only pays).

THE FINDING. The standard path SETTLES AT ONCE. After the invoice is paid and
long before any window, the 1000 sats are a completed settlement in bob's
channel - the gateway's lnd, one operator's balance, spendable by bob. What
the "pool" received is 990 sat of ECASH, swapped from the gateway's own
pegged-in ecash; the federation's on-chain custody did not move (walletv2
1000000 sat before, after the payment and after the window). Nothing in the
path waits for anything but the guardians' automatic threshold decryption of
the incoming contract's preimage - which is where a hold would have to live.
  So by Daniel's test - "not spendable by bob, not already a completed
  settlement in bob's channel" - the stake is not held, and after the window
  the stake's sats sit in one lnd, not in federation custody.

WHAT IS NOT DONE, ON PURPOSE: no custom Fedimint module, no delay, no test
changed. The next named piece is a hold: the incoming contract's preimage
decrypted by the guardians only after the round's result is FINAL and its
window has closed - the same rule our preimage shares follow today.

A DECISION IT RAISES: 0.12.0 will not run a 2-guardian federation, so the
rehearsal's two seats cannot be a Fedimint federation; 4 is the smallest
(threshold 3).

### Routing round stakes through the federation - what LNv2 decides first (source)

Daniel's sequence (2026-09-11): the rehearsal's round stakes through the
patched federation, measured with the hold table; then a release keyed to
the round becoming final; then winner-cancel. Read before any routing code,
v0.12.0 modules/fedimint-lnv2-client:
  THE SECRET IS THE RECEIVER'S. lib.rs create_contract_and_fetch_invoice
    (1009-1017): `encryption_seed` from an ephemeral tweak of the receiver's
    static key, `preimage = sha256(encryption_seed)`, invoice hash
    sha256(preimage) (1061). No call takes a caller-chosen secret or hash.
    A round entry commits to sha256 of the PLAYER'S secret and deals that
    secret to the settlement seats - so a stock LNv2 invoice cannot carry an
    entry's own hash.
  THE RECEIVER CLAIMS WITHOUT THE GUARDIANS. lib.rs recover_contract_keys
    (1130-1160) derives the aggregate decryption key from the receiver's own
    seed (1151); receive_sm.rs transition_incoming_contract (111-134) claims
    as soon as the incoming contract is confirmed funded. The guardian hold
    delays the gateway's settle of the payer's HTLC - it does not, by this
    reading, delay the receiver taking the gateway's ecash.
  The hold table's "receiver ecash 990 only after the hold" was read with
  `fedimint-cli info`, which exits before a claim can run: to be measured,
  not assumed.

MEASURED - THE RECEIVER'S CLAIM IS NOT HELD, AND AN EARLY CLAIM STRANDS THE
GATEWAY UNDER HOLD PATCH v2. The probe now drives the receiver inside the
window (its own await-receive, 8 s max, one client process at a time).

    alice's payinvoice         gave up after 180009 ms, still IN_FLIGHT
    AFTER PAY / AFTER WINDOW   (+186 s / +220 s) bob channel 1000000, invoice

  CORRECTION: the hold table's "receiver ecash only after the hold" was a

HOLD PATCH v3 - the funded-at record keeps the contract too (value
(u64, IncomingContract)), because a claim runs `remove_entry(&IncomingContract
Key)` in process_input; the share is still not made at funding. Release build

v0.12.0 tree. Same probe, receiver driven inside the window, hold 30 s:

  The payer's leg is held for the window and the gateway settles after it,
  whether or not the receiver has claimed. The pool's leg is not held.

WHAT ROUTING THE ROUND'S STAKES THROUGH THE FEDERATION STILL LACKS - the
share that decides what comes next:
  1. THE HASH. An LNv2 invoice's secret is its receiver's; a round entry
     commits to sha256 of the player's own secret, dealt as shares to the
     settlement seats. Either the entry commits to the federation invoice's
     hash (the invoice comes first, and the dealt shares have no job for a
     federation round), or the incoming contract is built around the
     player's secret (the page, or a patched receiver, encrypts it to the
     guardians' key). Protocol either way.
  2. THE POOL'S LEG. The receiver claims the gateway's ecash at funding
     (measured, inside the hold), with a key only it holds. 23.2 needs that
     claim held until the round is final - a guardian CONSENSUS rule on the
     claim, on consensus time, not the per-guardian clock the share hold uses
     - and a claim key that is not one party's.
  Until 1 and 2 are settled, the round's stakes cannot pass these guardians
  and close still acts on bob's own hold invoices.

SIZING THE TWO DECISIONS (read from the v0.12.0 source; nothing built):
  1a  THE INVOICE COMES FIRST: the node's receiving client makes the LNv2
      invoice and the entry commits to its hash. No cryptography to port;
      the join order changes, and the player's dealt shares have no job in a
      federation round.
  1b  THE PLAYER'S SECRET: the page encrypts it to the guardians' key.
      crypto/tpe/src/lib.rs encrypt_preimage (49-69) needs, bit for bit,
      `Scalar::random(ChaChaRng::from_seed(seed))` (83-85) and
      `G2Projective::random(ChaChaRng::from_seed(sha256("FEDIMINT_TPE_
      BLS12_381_MESSAGE" || ct || pk || commitment)))` (97-123) - Rust's
      ChaCha generator through the bls12_381 crate's own sampling, not RFC
      9380. @noble/curves 2.4.0 (installed) has BLS12-381 arithmetic,
      pairing and the standard hash-to-curve, not these. So: a bit-exact JS
      port of three Rust routines, or a WASM build of the tpe crate; one
      wrong bit and the guardians refuse the contract. Then POST
      /create_bolt11_invoice {federation_id, contract, amount, description,
      expiry_secs} (lnv2-common gateway_api.rs 131) to the gateway.
  2   THE POOL'S LEG: a claim is authorised by one secp256k1 key,
      `claim_pk` (lnv2-server process_input: `verify_agg_decryption_key`,
      then claim_pk or refund_pk). A FROST group key - the pool key the
      daemons already make - signs in that shape, so a committee-held claim
      key fits; the new work is building and signing the Fedimint claim
      transaction, and a guardian consensus rule that refuses the claim
      until the round's hold has passed (on consensus time, deterministic).

    AGAINST THE WINDOW      run 3, instrumented: paid 11470 ms before the first
                            close; released at close +19328 / +19499 / +19562
                            ms; the round's window closes at +31800 (P1) and
                            +31309 (P2) - RELEASED 12472 AND 11810 ms BEFORE THE
                            WINDOW CLOSED
  THE FINDING: on the round path the payer's HTLC is NOT held for the window.
  The guardians' hold counts 30 s from the PAYMENT; the round's window counts
  from the CLOSE. Bob could spend about 12 s before the window closed. Not
  tuned: raising HOLD_SECS would be moving the number, not the rule.
  And so: every stake - winner and VOID too - is settled into bob's channel
  by the gateway (+2940000 msat, 3 x 980), the daemons' P1 cancel meets
  "invoice already settled" and throws out of the close (money summary

  EXPIRED past the HTLC height while lnd says SETTLED (HELD AFTER LND SETTLED 6).
  Those are steps 3 and 4's to fix; they are reported, not hidden.

THE SUITES (this tree, run two at a time): blwp-node 485/485 (+3),
blwp-client 236/236 (+3), protocol 464/464, core 91/91; Unity not touched.
In an earlier 4-way parallel run two timing tests fell (second-closer 800 ms;
