## 13:13 - NO CENTRAL PAYMENT ENDPOINT: where each Lightning act stands (2026-09-11)

Daniel 13:13: a single lnd gateway is forbidden; invoice, hold, settle and
pay need the same quorum as the mint (5 of 7, or 2 of 2). "No threshold-LN
until it hardens" is gone from the letter.

STOPPED: keying the guardians' release to the round's deadline (entry close
+ run length + window). It was half written (a protocol deadline function, a
node door serving an entry and its round contract by payment hash, the
guardian patch asking it) and is out of the tree, kept in scratch. Whatever
clock the guardians used, the payer's HTLC would still sit in bob's lnd, and
bob's gateway would settle it - the construction 13:13 forbids.

WHO CAN DO EACH ACT TODAY, from the code and the measured rehearsals:
    act       daemon path (M3.3)                    federation path (step 2)
    invoice   one daemon asks one lnd (bob),        one gateway (bob) makes it
              custody.js:181
    hold      the HTLC sits in bob's channel        the HTLC sits in bob's
                                                    channel (the gateway's)
    settle    PREIMAGE: 2 of 2 shares               PREIMAGE: 3 of 4 guardians
              (custody.js:305); the act and the     (decryption shares); the
              msat: bob's lnd (+98000 msat)         gateway settles, bob's lnd
                                                    (+2940000 msat)
    cancel    one daemon, on its own FINAL check    bob's lnd; the gateway
              (custody.js:318), no second seat's
              signature - 23.2 asks 5 of 7
    pay       none over Lightning; the pool pays    the gateway
              on-chain by FROST 2 of 2
  Only the settle's preimage is quorum-bound. Anything with bob's macaroon can
  issue, cancel, and spend what was settled.

WHAT EXISTS TO BUILD ON:
  - Fedimint 0.12.0: modules ln, lnv2, mint(v2), wallet(v2), meta, and one
    `gateway`. Every Lightning payment in or out passes one gateway's node;
    there is no federation-run gateway in the tree.
  - lnd v0.21.3 (the one here): --remotesigner.enable (all key operations in
    another process) and --protocol.simple-taproot-chans (MuSig2 channel
    funding keys). That signer is one process today; a committee signer
    behind it would be 23.6's threshold-signed Lightning node.

DECISION NEEDED (Daniel), which quorum-run Lightning:
  (a) a threshold-signed Lightning node: lnd with its remote signer answered
      by the settlement committee (FROST for Schnorr/MuSig2 paths, taproot
      channels), so no invoice, HTLC settle or payment is signed without the
      quorum. 23.6 calls it emerging; nothing here does it yet.
  (b) the federation's own quorum without Lightning in front: stakes pegged in
      (on-chain or ecash), no invoice at all. Meets "no single node", drops
      Lightning hold invoices (M3's stated path).
  (c) something else Daniel names.

## A COMMITTEE-SIGNED LIGHTNING NODE: CAN lnd's REMOTE SIGNER BE ANSWERED 2 OF 2? (2026-09-11)

Daniel's pick: lnd's remote-signer interface answered 2 of 2 (not Fedimint
hold patches, not waiting). Invoice / hold / cancel may sit on one replaceable
node; the settle and the spend of settled money must not. (FEDERATION.md,
a024628, predates this pick.) Measured before any FROST, threshold node or
Fedimint work.

  bash packages/blwp-node/tools/remote-signer-probe.sh     (149 s, run 2; run 1 145 s)

Own regtest, ports 30301-30312. Bob's lnd v0.21.3 is WATCH-ONLY
(--remotesigner.enable, InitWallet watch_only over REST - `lncli
createwatchonly` needs a terminal); a signer lnd (nochainbackend, no peers,
RPC log at debug) holds every key; a private TAPROOT channel alice -> bob
(--protocol.simple-taproot-chans, commitment type TAPROOT). The invoice and
the settle go through the daemons' own port (src/lnd-port.js, via
tools/remote-signer-acts.mjs). Bob's health check on the signer is off - his
switch, so he keeps every power his credentials allow.

WHAT THE SIGNER HOLDS: one seed. It exports 259 xpubs and nothing private:
m/49', m/84', m/86' (one on-chain account each) and m/1017'/1'/0'..255' -
lnd's key families (0 funding, 1-5 revocation/htlc/payment/delay bases and
revocation root, 6 the NODE KEY). Bob's node key 03717641...54d75a is not in
bob's lnd.

WHAT EACH ACT ASKS THE SIGNER FOR (requests the signer served, run 2):
    open (taproot)  DeriveSharedKey 1, MuSig2CreateSession 3, MuSig2Sign 2, MuSig2CombineSig 1
    idle 10 s       SignMessage 4 (noise floor)
    INVOICE         SignMessage 1
    hold            DeriveSharedKey 2, MuSig2CreateSession 2, MuSig2Sign 1, WalletKit/SignPsbt 1
    SETTLE          MuSig2CreateSession 2, MuSig2Sign 1        (alice SUCCEEDED)
    cancel          MuSig2CreateSession 2, MuSig2Sign 1        (alice FAILED = refunded)
    spend 500 sat   MuSig2CreateSession 4, MuSig2Sign 2, WalletKit/SignPsbt 1
  Runs 1 and 2 asked the same requests for every act.

THE INVOICE'S SIGNATURE, read off the BOLT11 request: 65 bytes, recovery id 1,
  r 05b60be6702cd1f194c02286b8f35ead96096e8eb7b9d5f77ec0202895126dd1
  s 6062f9fd2a5a3f4ee1243a42b68b9299413afe727329e598b0ef3081751bb5e3
  recovers to bob's node key, and verifies as ECDSA (secp256k1, not prehashed
  again). BOLT11 requires this recoverable ECDSA signature.

THE ANSWER: NO. The two-seat committee cannot answer this signer 2 of 2 for
either act, as the tree stands:
  - invoice create needs an ECDSA signature by the node key. The committee's
    only signature is FROST over BIP340 Schnorr (protocol/src/frost-bip340.js);
    there is no ECDSA anywhere in blwp-node/src or protocol/src.
  - settle needs a MuSig2 partial signature, in a session with alice, over the
    channel's funding key (family 0). The committee has no MuSig2, and a
    FROST group acting as one MuSig2 signer is not a procedure this tree or
    lnd has.
  - and the committee's door refuses by construction: pool-signing.js takes
    a round and an output and signs only a spend it rebuilt itself -
    "nothing here accepts a sighash, a transaction, or a table". lnd asks for
    exactly that: a message, a session, a partial signature.

CAN ONE MACAROON STILL SETTLE? YES, with the signer up: bob's one
admin.macaroon plus the preimage settled (invoice SETTLED, alice SUCCEEDED),
and the signer signed the MuSig2 share without any second party - the signer
is itself one lnd behind one macaroon (bob's lnd holds the signer's
admin.macaroon). A remote signer moves the keys to a second process; it adds
no quorum.

WITH THE SIGNER GONE, bob's own node and credentials: the invoice is refused
("error signing message in remote signer instance ... connection refused"),
and bob's lnd SHUTS ITSELF DOWN on that first signing failure:
  13:38:51.291 [CRT] RPWL: [RPC signing server not available: ... dial tcp 127.0.0.1:30311: connect: connection refused]
  13:38:51.291 [INF] RPWL: Sending request for shutdown
  13:38:51.419 [INF] LTND: Shutdown complete
Then hold (alice's payment FAILED), settle, cancel and spend: connection
refused - nothing. Invoices 4 and 5 stay ACCEPTED in flight (alice
IN_FLIGHT); 23.2's default, the CLTV, is what returns them.

THE LEFTOVER, in the same table:
    act       signer up                      signer gone, bob's credentials only
    invoice   signer: ECDSA by the node key  refused, and bob's lnd shuts down
    hold      signer: ECDH + MuSig2 + PSBT   no (lnd down)
    settle    signer: MuSig2                 no (lnd down)
    cancel    signer: MuSig2 - the same      no (lnd down)
              requests as a settle
    spend     signer: MuSig2 + PSBT          no (lnd down)
  So a remote signer takes every act away from bob's node alone - the gap
  it would close is all five acts - but ONLY IF the signer is the quorum,
  and on this lnd the quorum cannot be the signer: it is asked for ECDSA and
  MuSig2, and the committee has neither. Also measured: a settle and a cancel
  reach the signer as the same requests (MuSig2CreateSession 2, MuSig2Sign 1),
  so a signer that lets a replaceable node cancel alone but not settle would
  have to read the commitment it signs - it cannot tell them apart by name.

Not touched: FROST, a threshold node, Fedimint, Unity, §22, the parked items.

## A LOSER'S STAKE INTO THE COMMITTEE'S POOL BY A SUBMARINE SWAP (2026-09-11)

Why: the committee-signed lnd measured NO (above). Daniel's rule keeps
invoice, hold and cancel allowed on one replaceable node; the settle and the
spend of settled money must not be. A submarine swap - Lightning Loop Out's
shape: an off-chain payment for an on-chain HTLC under ONE hash - is a
recognised procedure that asks nothing of lnd but a hold invoice and an
on-chain send. MEASURED ONLY; not a pick, not wired into the daemons.

  bash packages/blwp-node/tools/swap-into-pool-probe.sh [stake-sats=980] [claim-fee=200]
  (tools/swap-into-pool.mjs builds the output, the claim and the refund)

The swap output (P2TR, internal key BIP-341's NUMS point - NO key path):
  claim leaf   OP_SIZE 32 OP_EQUALVERIFY OP_SHA256 <stake hash> OP_EQUALVERIFY
               <committee group key x> OP_CHECKSIG
  refund leaf  <height> OP_CHECKLOCKTIMEVERIFY OP_DROP <operator key x> OP_CHECKSIG
  claim pays   the pool's own key-path output (pool.js), the committee's 2 of 2

Two runs, own regtest (ports 30321-30332), 39 s each, identical results:
  alice pays a 980-sat hold invoice on bob's lnd     ACCEPTED; bob's channel 0 msat
  bob locks 980 sat on-chain to the swap output      1 confirmation
  bob's refund BEFORE the height (263 < 406)         REJECTED: non-final
  committee claim signed 1 of 2                      REJECTED: Invalid Schnorr signature
                                                     (verifies locally: false)
  committee claim 2 of 2, a WRONG secret             REJECTED: Script failed an
                                                     OP_EQUALVERIFY operation
    - after all three: alice's invoice still ACCEPTED, bob's channel 0 msat
  committee claim 2 of 2 with the secret             ACCEPTED, mined; the output is
                                                     780 sat at the POOL key
  bob reads the secret from the claim's witness      sha256 = the stake's hash
  bob settles with it                                invoice SETTLED, alice SUCCEEDED

WHERE THE MONEY IS, both runs:
  bob's channel    0 -> 980000 msat     (alice's stake, for the coins he locked)
  bob's on-chain   1000000 -> 998710 sat  (980 locked + 310 his own send fee)
  the pool         +780 sat at the committee's 2-of-2 key (980 - 200 claim fee)

WHAT THIS SHOWS:
  - The settle's secret reaches the chain only by the committee's 2-of-2
    claim, and the claim puts the stake's value in the pool. Bob alone has no
    secret, so he cannot settle; his locked coins come back to him only by
    the refund leaf, after the height.
  - After the claim, bob's settle only repays his own coins; the stake's
    value is at the pool key, which only the committee spends (the payout
    path, measured in payout-regtest and the --pool rehearsal).
  - Invoice, hold and cancel stay on bob's replaceable node, as allowed.

WHAT IT DOES NOT SHOW (the next pieces, if chosen):
  - A harness committee (trusted dealer) and a harness-supplied secret; the
    daemons' pool-signing signs only key-path payouts it rebuilt, and nothing
    in blwp-node yet claims a script path or asks the operator to lock.
  - The timing rule: the refund height must fall before alice's HTLC expires,
    with the committee's claim inside that gap - else a claim after the HTLC
    expiry takes bob's coins while alice is refunded. Not measured.
  - Fees: 310 sat on bob's lock at 2 sat/vB and a 200-sat stand-in claim fee
    taken from the stake (the owed-sats fee-rate ruling, parked). At 100-sat
    stakes (98 net) there is no swap output at all: under the 330-sat floor.

## THE SWAP'S CLOCKS: A TIMING WINDOW EXISTS (2026-09-11)

Daniel: the submarine swap IS how a loser's stake reaches the pool. Before
any src change, the hole the first run named - the operator's refund height
must fall before alice's HTLC times out, with the committee's claim in
between - measured in the same tool, one scenario per run:

  bash packages/blwp-node/tools/swap-into-pool-probe.sh <normal|late-before-timeout|far-refund|bob-refunds>

Alice's hold invoice has the daemons' own shape (addholdinvoice --expiry 3600,
no --cltv_expiry, as src/lnd-port.js). Four runs side by side (PORT_OFF 0/20/
40/60), 55-106 s each; no process left. Regtest mines on demand, so seconds
are at the 600 s block target, not measured.

THE CLOCKS (identical in all four runs):
  CLOCK 1  alice's HTLC   paid at 262; invoice final CLTV 80; expiry_height 345
                          = +83 blocks = 49800 s. lnd CANCELS the held HTLC at
                          327, 18 blocks before its expiry (alice's payment
                          FAILED, her channel back to 1996530000 msat).
                          The rehearsal's own: expiry 366/367 with the chain at
                          283/284 at the close (+83), cancelled at 353/354.
  CLOCK 2  bob's refund   nLockTime = alice's expiry - 20 = 325 (+63 from the
                          payment); lock confirmed at 263. Spent before 325:
                          "non-final", every run.
  CLOCK 3  the claim      2 of 2 + the secret, into the pool key:
    normal                confirmed at 264 - 61 blocks before bob's refund,
                          81 before alice's expiry. Bob settles from the
                          chain: alice SUCCEEDED, bob's channel +980000 msat,
                          pool +780 sat.
    late-before-timeout   bob does NOT refund; the claim after his refund
                          height confirmed at 327 (2 past it, 18 before
                          alice's expiry). Bob still settles: alice
                          SUCCEEDED, bob's channel +980000 msat, pool +780.
    bob-refunds           bob's refund confirmed at 326 (alice still
                          ACCEPTED); lnd cancels alice at 327; the late claim
                          at 327: "bad-txns-inputs-missingorspent". Pool 0,
                          alice refunded, bob on-chain 1000000 -> 999490
                          (310 lock fee + 200 refund fee).
    far-refund            bob's refund at payment + 144 = 406, 61 blocks
                          PAST alice's expiry (the first run's choice). lnd
                          cancels alice at 327; the claim confirmed at 328;
                          bob's settle: "invoice already canceled".
                          ALICE REFUNDED, BOB -1290 sat on-chain and 0 in his
                          channel, POOL +780: A LATE CLAIM DRAINS BOB.

THE WINDOW, on these clocks:
  - A claim confirmed at any height up to lnd's cancel (327 = expiry - 18)
    leaves bob whole: he reads the secret from the chain and settles.
  - The drain needs BOTH bob's refund height past lnd's cancel AND a claim
    after it. With the refund height before the cancel (expiry - 20 = 325),
    bob's refund confirmed at 326 and a claim after alice's timeout found
    the output spent.
  - So: lock height < claim <= lnd's cancel height, and bob's refund
    nLockTime < lnd's cancel height. Here: the committee has 263 -> 325, 62
    blocks (37200 s at the target); bob has 325 -> 326, the blocks between
    his refund height and lnd's cancel, to get his refund in. The refund
    margin trades one against the other (20 here); it is not chosen -
    htlc_cltv_days is the parked ruling.
  - On the rehearsal's own timeouts: 83 blocks from payment to expiry and
    lnd's cancel 13-18 before it, with the round's 30 s objection window
    (10 min reference) well inside one block - the window exists.

WHAT THE DAEMONS WILL HAVE TO KEEP (named, not built):
  - the operator's refund nLockTime from alice's HTLC expiry, below lnd's
    cancel height; the committee's claim before that nLockTime;
  - the operator refunding at its height rather than waiting.
Dust and fees stay listed: 100-sat stakes (98 net) cannot be this output
(330-sat floor); the claim fee (200 here) out of the stake is the parked
owed-sats ruling; bob's 310-sat lock and 200-sat refund fees at 2 sat/vB.

FEDERATION.md step 1: "deposit into a lock with claim_pk = the FROST key; the
guardians accept it". Stock released fedimintd 0.12.0, unpatched; four
guardians, threshold 3 (Fedimint's rule: total - (total-1)/3,
fedimint-core peer_id.rs:82-102); one gateway on bob's lnd; own regtest.

and fedimint-cli has no way to name another; the guardians insert an
outgoing contract without checking its keys (lnv2-server lib.rs:548). So

crates only) opens the player's client as fedimint-cli does and funds ONE

## THE STAKE LOCK, REHEARSAL STEP 3a: ONE COMMITTEE-SIGNED SETTLEMENT OF TWO LOSERS' LOCKS (2026-09-11)

FEDERATION.md step 3: "one settlement transaction: losers' locks and fee
locks in, payout contracts out; accepted; a 1-of-2 signature refused". 3a is
that without the fee locks (their claim hash and the §22A node slots are not
decided). Stock released fedimintd 0.12.0, unpatched; four guardians,
threshold 3; one gateway; the 2-of-2 committee key.

  FEDIMINT_BIN=<released builds> LOCK_BIN=<blwp-stake-lock> \
    bash packages/blwp-node/tools/stake-lock-step3.sh

What the source says:
  - one BIP-340 signature PER INPUT over the txid, each under that input's key;
    the count must equal the inputs (fedimint-core transaction.rs,
    validate_signatures). Both locks name the committee: one signature,
    listed twice.
  - funding: inputs >= outputs + fees from core consensus 2.1 (this build is
    2.1; fedimint-server consensus/transaction.rs, verify_funding).
  - LNv2 fee per input and per output: base + amount * ppm / 1e6
    (lnv2-common config.rs), read here off the federation's own config.
  - a submission whose txid is already accepted answers Ok(txid) without
    processing it again (fedimint-server consensus/api.rs:173-181).
The committee cannot hand the stock builder a Keypair, so tools/stake-lock
--mode settle builds the raw Transaction: both locks in as Claim(P), one

## THE STAKE LOCK, REHEARSAL STEP 4: THE PLAYER'S REFUND AFTER EXPIRY (2026-09-11)

FEDERATION.md step 4: "`Refund` after expiry by the player's key; before
expiry refused". Stock released fedimintd 0.12.0, unpatched; four
guardians, threshold 3; one gateway; the 2-of-2 committee key.

  FEDIMINT_BIN=<released builds> LOCK_BIN=<blwp-stake-lock> \
    bash packages/blwp-node/tools/stake-lock-step4.sh

What the source says: Refund passes only when the lock's expiration is at
or below the guardians' block count, and the transaction must be signed by
refund_pk (lnv2-server lib.rs:466-497); the guardians' block count is the
third-highest of four votes (lib.rs:746-765). So the run mines past the
expiry and then WAITS until the guardians' own count reaches it.
Tool: tools/stake-lock --mode redeem --witness refund (the stock Refund
witness, no signature in it; the transaction signed by the given key), and
--mode status to poll the guardians' count and the lock.

## THE STAKE LOCK, REHEARSAL STEP 7: NO SINGLE KEY AND NO MACAROON MOVES A ROUND'S MONEY (2026-09-11)

FEDERATION.md step 7, the last of the 7. Stock released fedimintd 0.12.0,
unpatched; four guardians, threshold 3; two gateways; the 2-of-2 committee.

  FEDIMINT_BIN=<released builds> LOCK_BIN=<blwp-stake-lock> \
    bash packages/blwp-node/tools/stake-lock-step7.sh

A. NO MACAROON HAS A PATH (source, not a submission): a stake lock is removed
   only at process_input (lnv2-server lib.rs:468) - inside a Transaction whose
   witness needs claim_pk and/or a tx signed by refund_pk. The only lnv2 admin
   endpoints are add/remove-gateway (lib.rs:705-724); neither spends. gatewayd
   has no command touching a foreign contract. Live: a guardian admin
   credential answered `admin audit` (module summaries, no spend), a gateway
   credential answered `info` (1 federation, no spend). A macaroon is never an
   input to a lock's witness; one guardian is 1 of 4, below threshold 3.

      not be: the check is against refund_pk, so any non-player key fails the

                    Construction: the dishonest seat takes the honest A0 it was
                    sent, publishes A0' = X - A0_honest for a key X it owns
                    (never knowing A0''s secret), picks the honest seat's share
                    r, and solves A1' = (rG - A0') / j_honest as a POINT, so the
                    honest share lies on the published polynomial.
  PROTOCOL FACTS    acceptContribution: accepts | honest share (openMyContribution)
                    still verifies | combineShares emits the attacker's X as the
                    group key | the attacker ALONE signs a BIP-340 signature that
                    verifies under the group key. All four true.
  DAEMON ORDER      (real honest daemon, dishonest peer on its own socket, logged)
                    1 honest dkg.run starts and DEALS
                    2 honest POSTs its contribution to the peer - the peer holds
                      the honest A0 and has dealt nothing
                    3 honest GETs the peer's contribution -> 404
                    4 run() returns ok=false: "1 of the committee's 2 seats have
                      contributed"
                    5 peer POSTs the rogue contribution -> 201 taken
                    6 honest finish() ok=true, group key = the attacker's X
                    and the pool's output key (poolOutput) is spendable by the
                    attacker alone. GET /dkg serves a node's own contribution to
                    any caller; POST /dkg takes a committee member's any time.
  WHY IT WORKS      Feldman checks only that each honest share lies on the
                    published polynomial; with honest seats < threshold (2-of-2:
                    one honest seat) the dealer can fix those shares and solve
                    the remaining commitments as points. combineShares guards
                    one-contribution-per-seat, not dealing last.

                    suite's HDKG), refusal without a valid one, checked against

                    from the DKG commitments every seat already stores.

M3 W5 STEP 1: THE SEATS MAKE THE ROUND'S CLAIM KEY
  WHY FIRST         W5b's forfeit is a threshold signature by the round's claim
                    key, and every lock rehearsal (W1a, W1b) had handed the seats
                    that key (claimKeyFor, keys.json). Measured before anything:
                    does a round the daemons seat themselves have one?
  BEFORE            fresh Daily 2-of-2 (standUpRound), nothing injected: neither
                    seat held a group key ("this node has no share of that
                    committee's key yet"), /claim-key 409 and 409; dkg.run by
                    hand, twice on both: "1 of the committee's 2 seats have
                    contributed". So on a daemon-seated round the page counted 0
                    of 2 and would lock nothing: W1b's shipping path rested on
                    the injected key.
  CAUSE             nothing in server.js or main.js ran the key generation; its
                    peers were a daemon-wide list, [] on a launched daemon (the
                    tests set dkg.peers by hand); and once the peers were given,
                    Dkg.finish still asked the daemon-wide list for the other
                    seats' agreements ("1 of the committee's 2 seats have said
                    which contributions they combined").
  FIX               a seat that seats a round from its census runs its half of
                    the key generation with the round's own committee endpoints
                    (endpointsOf, the rule the verify and payout paths use), and

                    key"; B's /entry-void 404; B holds no mark; B's round open.
                    Forfeit asked 20.8 s: none - A "1 of the 2 seats the forfeit
                    needs", B 409 "no forfeit before the result is final ... 0 of 2
                    agree on any one run"; kept by neither seat.
                    X before the expiry: redeem through the seats refused (no
                    forfeit); a forfeit A signed alone over the lock's contract id:
                    forfeit_verifies false, the guardians "The forfeit signature is
                    invalid"; refund: the guardians "The contracts locktime has not
                    yet passed". X's lock HELD at the end, 146 blocks left.
    (2)             B: 409 {entryVoid: true} "offered the on-time first mark only
                    after the start deadline had passed; ... 1 of 2"; B records
                    ENTRY_VOID (closed); round open. Forfeit 431 ms, verifies under
                    the round's claim key, kept by both seats; lock held, 150 left.
                    The real forfeit with a stranger's key and with seat A's node
                    key, at the guardians: both refused, "The transaction's
                    signature is invalid" (signer is not the refund key); lock held.

  WHAT IT MEANS     A seat's own word and receipt void nothing: the paid lock stays
                    held and no key opens it before expiry. A seat that really holds
                    the player's signed first mark can still close it early and push
                    "closed" - a 2-of-2 veto, which either seat always has by
                    withholding receipts - and the forfeit then pays only the
                    player's refund key: not a stranger, not a seat.

M3.3-34 ENTRY_VOID PIECE: THE WALK-AWAY (§15), READ AND MEASURED - NO CODE CHANGED (2026-09-12)
  THE SPEC (multiplayer_p2p.md, header "BLWP v4.6")
    §15 Disconnect rule: "After stake commitment: A transcript that stops becomes
        a deterministic result. Missing inputs follow the neutral-input policy; if
        checkpoints stop beyond tolerance, the valid run ends at the last receipted
        checkpoint; replay determines the final state; the player normally becomes
        FAILED or FORFEIT. Closing the browser does not escape a losing stake."
    §16: "Before stake commitment: no financial entry exists; no loss." ENTRY_VOID
        only "after commitment, before the first financial tick" when fewer than the
        threshold of game/verify seats are available - a seat outage, not a player.
    §13C: VOID only when no result reaches quorum and the fault is the operator's.
    §14: VOID / ENTRY_VOID reachable only from PROVISIONAL.
    In a player's words: once your stake is committed, walking away is not a
    refund - the round replays what you sent and you normally lose (FAILED or
    FORFEIT); only the seats failing you before your first tick refunds you
    (ENTRY_VOID), or the committee failing to agree (VOID). PLAYER_LOST is not an
    outcome in the spec or the code (DELIVERED, FAILED, FORFEIT, VOID, ENTRY_VOID).
    NOT DEFINED ANYWHERE: "neutral-input policy" and "tolerance" appear only in
    §15's sentence (lines 1754-1755). No old C# path exists (no disconnect, idle
    or neutral-input code in unity-proto/Assets/Scripts): intent is §15 alone.

                    closed-claim harness), deadline 900, both seats close:

        no ENTRY_VOID, no FORFEIT; /forfeit 409 "0 of 2 agree on any one run";
        lock held, expiry 1200 > height 1000 -> the player's key refunds it.
    (B) paid, first mark at tick 60 (receipted at both), then nothing:
        both "that run is still LIVE at its last stored tick, so it came to
        nothing yet" (verdict.js resultFrom) - no result; the same refund at expiry.
    (C) free, seated, sends nothing: "that transcript carries no ticks" - no result.
    What the other seat and the operator see: a seated entry with no result,
    no record, no board row; the money path does nothing and the lock expires
    back to the player. "Closing the browser does not escape a losing stake" is
    not true today - before the first mark or after it.

                    not VOID. Tolerance: a missing first mark is stopped when the
                    round's start deadline (900 ticks) passes with no receipted mark;
                    a run with marks is stopped when checkpoints cease before the
                    round's close, and ends at its last receipted checkpoint.
                    Outcomes: no first mark = FORFEIT, score 0, empty receipted
                    transcript (the late start's family); a mid-run stop = FAILED
                    at the last receipted checkpoint. No PLAYER_LOST; core
                    unchanged; neutral input is not a sim rule this turn; no W4.

M3.3-34 ONE SEAT REFUSED: §13C'S VOID AFTER THE RESULT WINDOW (2026-09-12)
  RULED             (Daniel) a seated entry whose on-time first mark is receipted
                    below the threshold, every seat it is short of having been up
                    and REFUSED it: both seats HOLD until the result window has
                    passed (not at the close), then record explicit VOID - final,
                    not HOLDING; the lock held (no act: it returns at its expiry),
                    forfeit door 409, out of the pool and the payout table; Daily
                    stake 0: recorded VOID only. The refusing seat holding a
                    different first mark: FORFEIT. Unanswered / down: ENTRY_VOID,
                    unchanged. A seat unreachable at the close: hold, no VOID. A
                    refusal made good in time: 2 of 2, the run's own outcome. A
                    FINAL result is never voided. No live fault injection: a live
                    Daily refusal is a named gap.
  LAW               §13C: no result at the threshold after the result window -
                    proven equivocation -> FORFEIT, otherwise the operator side's
                    fault -> VOID, "refunded by letting the HTLC expire ...
                    excluded from the pool and from the payout table". §23.2:
                    VOID = do nothing. §14: VOID only from PROVISIONAL. Protocol
                    payout.js noQuorumOutcome / settlementAction already said so;
                    nothing in blwp-node called it.
  BEFORE            refused-probe (scratchpad, first-mark's lock-round fixture), B
                    up and refusing every mark of the run: A 1 receipt, the offer
                    to B "refused"; at the close both HOLDING - 3 attempts at 2 s,
                    12 and 11 at 10 s - "no checkpoint of that entry is carried by
                    2 committee members" / "no checkpoints for that entry"; no
                    result, finality null, no Void, forfeit 409 at both, lock
                    held: a hold for ever, nothing ever decided.
  CHANGE            blwp-node only. store: refused_first_marks, no_quorum. round:
                    putRefusedFirstMark (kept only for the player's own signed,
                    on-time first mark of an entry seated here, this seat holding
                    none), refusedFirstMark, putNoQuorum, noQuorum. server: the
                    forward door keeps what it refused (stake not seen, or the
                    mark not taken - never FORFEIT or "the round is closed");
                    /closing shows the decided outcome; the retry filter and the
                    start-up resume leave a decided entry alone; /results says
                    x-no-quorum. verify #keep -> #noQuorum: the evidence above, no
                    seat unreachable, not ENTRY_VOID, not a late start; held until
                    this seat's close + the round's objection window; then
                    protocol noQuorumOutcome, equivocation proven from this
                    seat's own store or a peer's /equivocation, each pair checked
                    with provesEquivocation. finality: the no-quorum outcome where
                    no quorum is. forfeit: a VOID entry is refused by name (409).

M3.2 ITEM 6e, COMMIT 1: 22A PICK A IN computePayoutTable (rulings 2026-09-13)
  RULE              within the paying ranks a player's weight is its §18A rank weight
                    (3^(i-1) * 4^(K-i)) times its own net stake; the pool is split in
                    proportion, each share floored; the leftover goes out by §18A.6,
                    ascending H(round_id || pubkey) (remainderOrder), unchanged. The
                    refusal of mixed nets is gone. holdSettlement, the slash check's
                    recompute (slash.js) and the leaderboard all call this one
                    function, so they follow it.
  THE LIMIT         accepted: with one paying rank - every round of four qualifiers or
                    fewer - the winner takes the whole pool whatever it donated.
                    22A's "no double reward for donating" bites only when two or more
                    ranks pay; no second-rank effect is added.

                    96000; B, C 98000 deliver; D 98000 fails):

                        every hold expired to its player - A 96000, B 98000, C 98000,
                        D 98000 back; pool 0 of D's 98000.

                        B CANCEL 98000, C CANCEL 98000 back to the players; table A
                        194000 (own 96000 + the pool), B 98000, C 98000, D 0; A wins
                        98000. Donations 0 msat collected (production writes 0).
                    two paying ranks (pinned in inclusive.test.js): donor first at net
                    93000, second at 98000, pool 98000 - weights 4 x 93000 and

  other recipient, no raised donation minimum, no share rewritten in the protocol. A
  2% donor on a 100000 msat stake is owed 1334/666; the 666 NO_ROUTE is lnd's default

  will not carry. The 5% pair (3334 + 1666 SETTLED) is the proof both recipients work
  on a paid local round. Closed.

                    (1) A RELOAD ONTO THE ROUND LINK STARTS A NEW JOIN - measured, run 8: after the
                        reload the page, holding 1536 msat, set out to fund a second 980000 + 20000
                        msat of lock, i.e. to show a second deposit invoice for a round the player
                        already stakes. Cause: index.html reuses a kept lock only when no seat has

                        resume path (its session key is the Client's). The collect itself is not
                        affected (it works from the kept record). Depends on: a resume of a
                        committed entry on reload (W1b's reload, extended past the commit).

                        lock in it is verified - measured, run 8 (every stake waits for its lock's
                        expiry). A client that does not mint (or whose /fee-lock never lands) makes
                        this happen. Depends on a ruling: refuse such an entry at the door when the
                        round's gate mints, or settle the stakes and leave that fee out.

                    pasting an invoice; it stays in the federation under their key. A Lightning address

M3 W6: A SEAT KILLED INSIDE A LOCK SETTLEMENT RECOVERS TO THE RIGHT STATE ON RESTART (2026-09-15)
  PREMISE CORRECTED identical settlement bytes sent again are ACCEPTED (stake-lock-step3.sh c1), so a
                    resubmit of the same txid is not the failure. The failure is a restart that cannot
                    rebuild the signed bytes.
  TEST              blwp-node/test/lock-settlement.test.js, "W6 ...": two seats on store files, each
                    reaching the federation through a port that dies with the seat - after the guardians
                    answered (a) or before the settlement went (b); both seats started again on their
                    files and ports; (c) the plan rebuilt differs (the federation's fee rule 1000 -> 1500
                    msat per input/output) or cannot be rebuilt (seat B stays down, no loser's P opens).
  MEASURED BEFORE   in all six cases both rows stayed SUBMITTING after the restart with the note "about to
                    submit; if this seat dies here, ask the federation for the claimed locks", and no
                    submission followed: (a) the payout at the signed txid stored and the loser's lock
                    gone - the money had moved; (b) the lock still held, no payout, 0 submissions - never
                    sent, the losers' locks would go back to them at expiry. Not REFUSED: nothing asked
                    again. CAUSE: at start a closed round's close runs again only for a round with a run
                    short of FINAL (server.js, M3.3-34), and a lock settlement happens only once every run
                    is FINAL - a settlement the seat died inside was never picked up.
  BUILT             the claimed outpoints and the payout count of the signed transaction are kept with its
                    intent (lock_settlement_moves); settle() on a SUBMITTING row asks the federation first
                    - IN: a payout contract of that txid stored and no claimed lock held -> ACCEPTED, no
                    rebuild; OUT: every claimed lock held and no payout -> rebuilt, the kept signature only
                    for the same txid, else signed afresh; anything else stays SUBMITTING with the reason,
                    no retry; at start, after the resumed closes, every SUBMITTING row goes through
                    settle(), and again every 60 s (the timer unref'd).
  MEASURED AFTER    (a) same plan: both ACCEPTED, "found in the federation ...: 1 of 1 payout contract(s)
                    ... stored, 1 of 1 claimed lock(s) gone", 2 -> 2 submissions (none new).
                    (a)+(c) fee rule changed: both ACCEPTED from the federation, 0 signatures over other
                    bytes. (a)+(c) seat B down: seat A ACCEPTED without a rebuild.
                    (b): both ACCEPTED, the same txid submitted, the lock claimed, the payout at the
                    signed txid. (b)+(c) fee rule changed: signed afresh - txid 7ce9... -> 9ca1..., the
                    winner paid 95000 msat under the new rule (was 96000), ACCEPTED, 0 signatures over
                    other bytes. mixed (the loser's lock gone by itself, no payout): SUBMITTING, "neither
                    in nor out - not settled here, not submitted again: 0 of 1 payout contract(s) ...",
                    0 new submissions.
  COUNTS            lock-settlement 15/15 (the six W6 cases in two runs of 3, the other 9 in one).
  ALSO FOUND        blwp-node client-hash 2 red: the known-good list lacked the blwp-client.js the Daily
                    serves (it had not been re-pinned since c6fca4c, 09-12, through several bundle commits
                    of 09-14, mine among them); pinned with tools/known-clients.js - client-hash 3/3.
                    Two long node --test runs of one shell at once were SIGTERMed (143); the long runs now
                    go in their own systemd units.
  NAMED LIMITS      a seat killed before any row of the settlement reached it keeps none and is not
                    picked up at start (it answers NONE, not REFUSED); once every payout of a settlement
                    has been collected and its claimed locks are gone the federation shows no proof, and
                    the row stays SUBMITTING with the reason.
  LIVE (a)          settle-live W6_KILL=1, 2026-09-15 00:40-00:47, stock fedimintd 0.12.0 (4 guardians, 3 of 4),
                    a 1000 sat round, two seats on store files: seat 1 combined the signature and submitted;
                    the real guardians answered accepted: true (txid 26a3b889...); the driver process was
                    SIGKILLed before any seat wrote it (settle-live-regtest.mjs, dyingAfterAnswer).
                    What the kill left: both rows SUBMITTING at 26a3b889...; the federation: 3 of 3 claimed
                    locks gone (the loser's stake lock and two fee locks), 3 of 3 payout contracts stored
                    (the qualifier and two seats).
                    Both seats started again on their stores, ports and lock clients (settle-live-w6-resume.mjs):
                    both ACCEPTED in 2.18 s, "found in the federation after this seat was inside it: 3 of 3
                    payout contract(s) of 26a3b88918e9 stored, 3 of 3 claimed lock(s) gone".
                    THE REAL GUARDIANS ANSWER AS THE TEST PORT COPIES THEM: the claimed locks gone and the
                    payout contracts at (txid, i) stored, read with blwp-stake-lock --mode status.
  SUITES            blwp-node 641/641: six chunks 605 (without lock-settlement and, for chunk 2's cap,
                    forfeit + frost-bip340 11/11 and five-of-seven run on their own), lock-settlement
                    15/15, five-of-seven 21/21 (11, then name groups of 3, 5 and 2 - the file runs past

M3 - WHICH GUARDIANS: RULED (Daniel 07:33, 3701038), MEASURED BEFORE ANY CODE (2026-09-15)
  RULING            every guardian / node has its own bond or takes no part; federationIsBonded stays: a paying
                    federation is valid only if its own threshold of guardian keys are advertised by distinct
                    census nodes bonded >= the round's minimum. None bonds today, so every paying federation is
                    refused until they do.
  THE CHECK         protocol federation.js federationIsBonded({ federationId, guardianKeys, threshold, census,
                    bondMinSats }) - exactly the ruling; 4 tests (federation.test.js). Callers: 0.
  ITS INPUTS        census: the seat derives one per round from blocks (roster.censusFor; entries carry pubkey,
                    bondSats, advert.guardianOf) and seats a round from it at POST /round (seatRound, synchronous)
                    only where it has a chain view; a seat without one seats nothing, and an unseated round gets
                    no claim-key attestation (409), so no stake lock can name its key. In production chainFor
                    fills a round's view asynchronously on first sight.
                    guardianKeys / threshold: fedimint 0.12 GlobalClientConfig.broadcast_public_keys (33-byte
                    secp256k1 per peer) and NumPeers::threshold = n - floor((n-1)/3) over api_endpoints. The
                    federation id is consensus_hash(api_endpoints) - the source comment says "broadcast public
                    keys", the code hashes the endpoints - so the id fixes n and the threshold but NOT the keys:
                    they come only with the config the stock client downloads. Neither federation client exposes
                    them: blwp-stake-lock has modes lock/settle/status/fees (+ forfeit/refund witnesses), the
                    wasm lock client join/lock/feeRule/...; both read only the LNv2 fee rule off the config.
                    The client (page) derives no census: directory.js checks single adverts against their bond
                    proofs over agreed headers (acceptAdvert, askForBond), for a round's committee.
  TOOLCHAIN         none on this machine: no cargo or rustc anywhere (the scratch toolchain of 2026-09-11, Daniel's
                    go, is gone); the built blwp-stake-lock and the wasm-node3 lock client remain, and wasm-bindgen.
  WHO WOULD BE HIT  the four live tools seat by assumeSeated (no chain view), as do the 9 node tests on the lock
                    fixture; 4 node tests derive a census from bonded blocks (seated-committee, roster,
                    close-peers, receipt-carry) - every advert there writes guardianOf: [].

  RULING            seats replay a named core (sim_wasm_hash); they embed no truck, cargo or map; a later game is a

  THE DOOR          blwp-node imports the core in ONE file, replay.js: init, step, submitLoad, submitLiquidation,
                    runScore (core/src/sim.js), hash and the truck's state words O_TRUCK, T_X, T_Z, T_HEADING, O_SCORE,
                    S_STATE, S_HEAT (state.js) for the ghost picture, RUN_LIVE, RUN_DELIVERED, BLOCK_TICKS (gate.js).
                    The contract names simCoreHash; nothing picks the core by it - there is one, imported.
  THE TRANSCRIPT    five input words per tick (INPUT_WORDS) and two truck-game event kinds the seat stores in their
                    own tables and replays before a tick: loads (fee, btc - the war's heat) and liquidations (size).
  THE CONTRACT      six game fields: blockTicks, exposureReference, corridorHalfWidth, spawnFreeRadius, timeFloor,
                    timeCeil. Read by seats/protocol: blockTicks only (a batch's limit, a run's length, and
                    runLengthIsThisCore against the core's BLOCK_TICKS); the other five are encoded and flagged
                    (exposure_ignored, time_factor_degenerate), never used by a seat. minScore and the rank curve
                    are economics over a score, not truck.

                    hash/tx/shares/bond-spend use core's sha256 and tick.js its tick (generic, not the game).

## SPAWNMARK: PARKED IS 2-D, AND THE CASE THE DAILY NEVER PRODUCED (2026-09-16)

  THE ITEM          "SpawnMark re-seats a parked truck by teleport (not measured)". Measured, then fixed,
                    then the fix's own unexercised case closed by construction.
  THE WRITER        Named from source, not inferred: SpawnMark.LateUpdate sets spawnPosition from
                    post.BayFor(SoloBay) and calls TruckController.Respawn, which - only if
                    externallyDriven - calls BlwpCore.Teleport, the sole caller in the tree.
                    CoreDrivenTruck holds the Rigidbody kinematic and rewrites the transform from core
                    words every frame, so nothing else can move a core-driven truck.
  LIVE, BEFORE      Daily lobby/practice, build 0.0.1375. Five terrain rebuilds, four fires: mark
                    unchanged, 2-D 0.00 m, 3-D 0.24 m of 12.0 m, teleport TAKEN and the core moved
                    0.00 m each time. v1 - the one rebuild whose mark height moved, 4.11 -> 1.40 - had
                    the truck 80.73 m away, identical in 2-D and 3-D, parked False, no fire.
                    So the jump the working list suspected is 0.00 m.
  LIVE, AFTER       Same path, build 0.0.1377: line for line identical. The 2-D guard admitted no
                    rebuild the 3-D rule had rejected. Correct and SILENT, said plainly.
  THE HOLE, CLOSED  A height-only rebuild with the truck ALREADY in the bay never occurred live, so it
                    was built: SpawnMarkParkedTests.AHeightOnlyRebuildStillCountsAsStandingInTheBay.
                    The lift uses feeHeight, which scales the one flat term the dead-level apron is made
                    of - the bay stands at postX + bayStandoff = -100.4, u = 0.06, inside
                    apronLevelFraction 0.19 - so the mark's y moves and its x and z do not.
                    MEASURED: ground lifted 17.59 m, mark 5.36 -> 22.95;
                      3-D to the mark      17.59 m   - EXCEEDS the 12 m budget, so the old 3-D rule
                                                       would have refused the re-seat
                      2-D to the mark       0.00 m   - x and z did not move: still in its bay
                      commanded x/z         0.00 m   - the teleport is a no-op across the ground
                    parkedWithin stays 12 m; the 3-D number is recorded, not accommodated; no assertion
                    loosened. A second test, ATruckThatHasDrivenOffIsNotDraggedBack, shows the widened
                    rule did not start dragging a driven-off truck back: 80 m out, moved 0.00 m.
                    NOTE ON THE MEASUREMENT: PlayMode has no core (BlwpInit stubs to 0), so Teleport
                    returns false and cannot report core movement. The third number is what the code
                    COMMANDS in x/z, labelled commanded rather than dressed up as core movement.
  RESIDUAL, LISTED  The 0.00 m teleport still fires on EVERY terrain rebuild while the truck is held -
                    four times in ~4 minutes, every 35-107 s - writing into the core on a cadence driven
                    by mempool polling. Left alone by ruling: not suppressed unless the 2-D guard
                    produced a wrong fire, and it produced none. Listed here, not a working-list letter.

## THE DRAWN TERRAIN FOLLOWS THE ROUND'S WORLD (Daniel 2026-09-16 12:38: "truck buried in dirt, only the cab roof showing")

  THE FAULT         The core's relief is made from the round's seed, and the drawn terrain was not rebuilt when
                    it changed. Two ways it changes: C# Init/Restart, and the page's own session start
                    (blwp.jslib: `b.st = b.core.init(net.seedWord)`), which C# never heard about. The mesh was
                    rebuilt only on a crater change or the mempool poll every 20 s - skipped outright when no
                    host answered - so the truck rode the new round's ground through the old round's hills.
                    Two seeds' reliefs differ by up to 5.59 m (core init(1) vs init(2), 1683 points).
  NOT THE FAULT     The mesh's own triangles against the core: at most 0.001 m over ~5000 route samples, five
                    seeds. The truck census could not see this - it compared the hull with the same ground it
                    computed; `SampleSurface` recomputes from HeightAt and never reads the drawn vertices.
  BEFORE (live)     Measured by the fix itself, the moment each change was seen, on the drawn vertices:
                      page start     up to 4.88 m ABOVE the core, 3366 of 3840 vertices off by > 0.5 m
                      round start    up to 5.26 m ABOVE the core, 1810 of 3840 vertices off by > 0.5 m
                    Daniel's screenshot was 16 s into a round (2:14 of 2:30) - inside the 20 s stale window.
  THE FIX           BlwpCore.ReliefEpoch = C#'s count of Init/Restart + the page's count of session-start
                    inits (BlwpReliefEpoch). MempoolTerrain rebuilds in the same frame the count moves.
  AFTER (live)      0.0.1385 at 40b5d409: drawn terrain vs core under the truck +0.00 m at every sample,
                    including hills at 2.60, 2.23, 4.36, 4.90, 5.73 and 4.64 m.
  SUITES            EditMode 211: 207 pass, 3 skipped, 1 red (rifle flash, listed). PlayMode 241: 215 pass,
                    13 skipped, 13 red - the 12 listed plus RampReadyTests.TheRealTransactionsReplaceThe
                    StandInsWhileNothingIsLoaded, the recorded flake: 3/3 RampReadyTests pass run alone on this
                    code. The deployed bundle is the committed one - the uncommitted M3 contracts.js was set
                    to HEAD for the build and restored byte for byte after.

## THE WAR NO LONGER RACES TO CATCH UP (Daniel 2026-09-16 12:26 / 14:24: "tanks go very fast, not instant, to another place - just open the game")

  THE FAULT         CoreDrivenTruck.Update steps the core in whole ticks, at most 8 a frame, and kept the rest of
                    the time owed with no end. A frame is at most 1/3 s (Unity's maximumDeltaTime) = 20 ticks, so
                    every slow frame left 12 ticks owed; fast frames paid them back at 8 a frame, and the whole
                    war ran at up to 8x its speed until caught up. Loading is slow frames, so: on login.
  NOT THE FAULT     The core. Replayed idle (no input, as in the lobby), 3 seeds x 3600 ticks: a live tank moves
                    more than 0.5 m in one tick only at tick 1 (armies spawning, 1-7.6 m) and once 0.51 m; every
                    other big move is a respawn, which is instant. The protocol defines no tick rate against
                    wall time, so letting time go changes no replay.
  BEFORE (live)     0.0.1386 at 4bd615ee, headless Chrome on the AMD GPU (Vulkan), lobby, nothing pressed, 250 ms
                    samples. Just loaded: up to 115.1 ticks/wall s. After 40 s CPU-throttled, the first 10 s:
                    p50 115.8, max 138.6 ticks/wall s, 23 samples over 70; fastest tank p50 20, p90 30.4 m/s
                    (ordinary 10). Software GL earlier: 5.5-10.6 ticks/wall s, ~11,000 ticks owed after 229 s.
  THE FIX           TicksDue: at most 8 ticks a frame, and time a frame cannot step is dropped, keeping under one
                    step for drawing between ticks. The drop is logged every 10 s ("the page is slower than the
                    core").
  AFTER (live)      0.0.1387 at b0aeaae5, same probe: just loaded max 79.4; after the throttle, first 10 s p50
                    60.1, max 66.5 ticks/wall s, 0 samples over 70; fastest tank p50 9.7, p90 10.6, max 11.7 m/s.
                    The page said it let go 375 ticks (6.25 s) during the throttle instead of racing them.
  SUITES            EditMode 214: CoreBacklogTests 2/2 (3 runs alone, all pass) - 20 s at 3 fps then 60 fps steps
                    at most 1 tick a frame; 45 fps loses nothing. PlayMode 241: 215 pass, 13 red - the 12 listed

## A RUN STARTED FROM A ROUND'S LINK COMES BACK TO THE LOBBY (Daniel 2026-09-16 14:24: "RUN STOPPED, cannot pick the next round")

  THE FAULT         PLAY leaves the address as the round's link with `&play=1`. Opened again - a reload, a
                    restored tab, a phone bringing the tab back - that address joins the round with no lobby
                    behind it (a named round skips the page's lobby), and Unity's auto-play starts the run on
                    the fourth frame, before the first lobby poll, so `_fromLobby` was false. At DELIVERED
                    nothing went back anywhere: the banner stayed over a truck that cannot drive.
  NOT THE FAULT     PLAY pressed in the lobby: measured on 0.0.1386, DELIVERED -> lobby 0 ms, second PLAY in the
                    same tab joined and ran (both signer nodes held its signed DELIVERED result, score 276).
                    Nor the finish wait: 68139fb (08:12) was already in Daniel's 0.0.1377.

                    "RUN STOPPED - the core said DELIVERED at tick 1273", lobby not showing 0 s, 3 s and 30 s
                    after (screenshot hang-play1/4-lobby.png).
  THE FIX           Page: BLWP_RUN_OVER on a page with no lobby sets the address back to the link's lobby (the
                    query without `round` and `play`) and starts the lobby in place. Unity: a run the address
                    started counts as started from the lobby (SplashScreen.StartedFromLobby).
  AFTER (live)      0.0.1391 at 3fa756a8, same `&play=1` run, DELIVERED at tick 1417: lobby showing 0 ms after,

## THE CHART FIGHTS THE WAR: ASSAULT TAKT, LEAD, TREND, SUPPLY IN THE CORE (WAR_TACTICS.md §4.12 / §4.14 / §3, 2026-09-16)

  WHAT              tactics.js: the ASSAULT CLOCK (§4.12, TAC_ASSAULT 6 words): first assault 20-40 s hashed (seed, side), then
                    45-90 s after the last ends (30-60 s for the trend's side), target hashed (seed, side, n) among objectives
                    the side does not hold, 30 s push or until the holder flips, then 15 s consolidation; a side holding all
                    three re-arms 20 s. While pushing: w 3 (4 for the trend's side), rest +16, ceiling 40 on the lane; w >= 2,
                    ceiling 32 beside. The LEAD and TREND (§4.14, TAC_MARKET 6 words: open, samples, trend, strength, lead,
                    momentum): submitSample() shifts the tape one sample (world input) and re-reads them; trend = green minus
                    red over the last six finished 10 s candles (two samples each; a body under 3 bp of the open is a doji),
                    |net| < 2 SIDEWAYS, else strength 1/2/3 at 2-3/4-5/6 - it changes only on a candle close. Trend effects:
                    the trend's side w + 1 and rest + 8 on every lane, ceiling 24 + 8 x strength; the other side rest - 8,
                    ceiling 24 - 8 x strength; the other side's assault clock paused (an assault already running runs out);
                    gun hit 550 +- 50 x strength and rifle 45 +- 5 x strength per mil for shots at a unit (a shot the truck
                    outranks keeps the plain threshold: the truck exception is untouched). SUPPLY (§3): reinforce wait x 4 /
                    (4 + supply), supply = objectives held - held by the other side + the lead's momentum for the side above
                    the open - the trend's strength for the side it runs against, -3..+3. Chart -> war only; nothing reads the
                    truck. The seeded tape reads SIDEWAYS on seeds 1-5 (no samples in a SIM round: both sides on the normal
                    clock).
  ASSAULT PROBE     tools/measure-assault.mjs, 3-minute runs (10800 ticks) x seeds 1-5, no samples:
                      takt alone -> with trend and supply: assaults per side 2.0 -> 1.9; target unheld by the attacker at the

THE LAST CANDIDATE HOLE: DO TWO TABS EVEN LAND IN ONE ROUND? (2026-09-18 07:20; the 19:15 two-tab gate)
  WHY IT WAS ASKED    every ghost number on this letter was measured with BOTH seats pinned to one round id - the
                      probe reads the lobby once and hands the same round to the driver and the watcher. A player
                      does not: two tabs each pick a round out of their own lobby listing, a minute apart. If the
                      first tab's round stops being offered in between, the second joins the NEXT one, neither is
                      ever shown the other, and nothing in the draw path is wrong. That would fail the gate with
                      every number on this letter still green.
  MEASURED            `tools/measure-two-tab-join.mjs`, eight minutes of the Daily lobby through the same
                      `fetchLobby` the page reads, seating nobody:
                        looks that found NO joinable free round      0 of 92
                        free rows offered at once                    1, every look
                        how long one round stays the offered row     106-205 s (four rounds)
                        gap between one round and the next          -48 to -53 s, i.e. they OVERLAP: the next round
                                                                     is offered about 50 s before the current one
                                                                     closes, so the row rolls over rather than empties
  THE ANSWER          no hole. A second tab that presses PLAY while the same row is offered - a window of at least
                      106 s, and there is always a row - joins the round the first tab is in. And a tab that has
                      pressed PLAY carries `?round=<id>&play=1` in its own address (index.html), so the second tab
                      can be opened on the first tab's link and join that round by name whatever the lobby is
                      offering. The only way to split the pair is to press PLAY in the second tab more than a couple
                      of minutes after the first AND let it pick from the lobby.
  NOT CLOSED          Daniel's two tabs on 0.0.1580. No host-side hole is left to name.

## Desktop pads, measured (2026-09-18 20:22 letter)

Daily 0.0.1613, MacBook headless Chrome over CDP, one seat joined from the lobby, every window started from a
standstill and read off the PAGE'S OWN core (`unityInstance.Module.blwp.st.i32`, T_VX/T_VZ, heading in 1/65536 turns,
O_SCORE+S_STATE for the run word). Tool: packages/blwp-client/tools/measure-desktop-pads.mjs.

  devicePixelRatio 1   nothing held 0.00 m/s | UP pad held with the mouse 10.86 m/s | keyboard W 13.55 m/s
  devicePixelRatio 2   nothing held 0.00 m/s | UP pad held with the mouse  6.36 m/s   (canvas 2560x1600)

So a held mouse press on a pad already drives the truck on the shipped build, at both pixel ratios. The UP pad's
centre computed from TouchPad.RectFor matched the page's own debug line exactly (padUp=1092,438,160,160 -> css
1172,518), so the rectangle was never in doubt.

Two false trails, both mine, withdrawn:
- Run 1 measured a truck still parked in the LOADING BAY - pads drawn, nothing moving, and the page had refused to
  join at all ("no proven endpoint: only 1 of 2 providers gave a chain, provider 1: no answer in 10000 ms" - a stale
  tab; both signers answered from the Mac in 0.08-4.4 s when asked directly). The probe now presses the bay's own
  computed rects and proves the run is live with the keyboard before it believes any pad number.
- Run 2 compared metres travelled. A coasting truck covers 20 m with nothing held, which read as "the pad drives".
  Speed replaced distance.

The fault that was real: TouchControls.Visible hung on Touchscreen.current existing, so the pads - and the mouse read
behind them - were on or off by accident of the browser. TouchControls.Shown is now "a pointer exists", and
DriveHud.PadsShown asks it instead of asking about touchscreens.

### What the pads-shown question turned up, measured and NOT fixed here

Pointing DriveHud.PadsShown at "anything that can press a pad" instead of "Unity found a touchscreen" is the honest
question, and the HUD cannot answer it yet. With the pads on screen (EditMode probe over ManifestBox / StreamingBox /
SendOffBox / TouchPad.RectFor, desktop, no overrides):

  1024x768   score column x 611.58 w  55.30   model list 352.26..624.62   handbrake pad x 676.48   chart 739..997
  1000x360   score column x 765.29 w  56.71   model list 338.00..628.00   handbrake pad x 827.00   chart 775..986
   844x390   score column x 563.41 w  98.59   and it grazes the send-off card by 5x2 px at (563.4..568, 245..246.9)
  1920x1080  score column x 1167.24 w 250.56  - the only one of the four with room

The column is pinched between the model list and the handbrake pad. There is nowhere else on those screens: above the
pad block the band under the chart's own row is 191 px where the column needs 218 at 1024x768, and 49 px against 131
at 1000x360. Two ways out were tried and both were wrong - taking room from the left puts the column on the model
list (32.7 px left at 1024x768), and taking the pads' own room puts SCORE across the throttle arrows, which
TheChartIsTopRightAboveTheButtonsOnEveryScreenWithPadsOrWithout catches by name (8512 px on the Up pad at 1280x800),
and which Daniel's 2026-09-17 12:35 HARD forbids in so many words.

## The whitepaper was fitted to the wrong box, twice (2026-09-18 22:16 letter, shipped 0.0.1617)

Daniel photographed it from spectate: the six lines sprawled across the depot, off the plaque.

  model file, mempool_post_office.glb   whitepaper_print is a quad 9.4 x 12.2 (portrait), backing 9.6 x 12.4

Fault 1: PostOffice.Show batches every renderer not named by IsLive, and whitepaper_print was not named.
StaticBatchingUtility.Combine swaps the batched renderer's mesh for the combined building, so after it ran the
plate's own renderer - and the TextMesh hanging under it - answered with the building's box. Fixed by naming the
whitepaper live: anything carrying drawn lettering stays out of the batch, whether or not the words change.

Fault 2: Face() returned (largest axis, middle axis) as (width, height), which turns every portrait plate into a
landscape one. The plate is 9.4 wide and 12.2 tall; it was read as 12.2 wide, so the fit was allowed 11.4 m of width
on a 9.4 m plaque - 21% over on one axis and short on the other, and the lines were shaped for a landscape page that
does not exist. Face now drops the THIN axis and keeps the remaining two in their own order, and both Room and Fit
measure in the plate's local axes times what it is drawn at, never a world-axis box round a wall at an angle.

Why the old test passed while the screen was wrong: TheLetteringFillsItsPlates measures the text against
PostOffice.Room, and batching had replaced both with the same combined mesh - two wrong boxes agreeing with each
other, the third time this shape of answer has been recorded here. TheWhitepaperIsInsideItsPlaque refuses it: the
plaque must be under a quarter of the building it hangs on, the text inside the plaque's own face, still filling it.

## The refused call at the round boundary, named (2026-09-18 22:5x, two runs on the MacBook)

Two two-tab runs on the Daily, both tabs real browser pages, CDP Network capture in each tab beside the page's own
fetch log, and a paired latency sampler hitting the signer nodes DIRECTLY on the LAN and through their tunnels at the
same instants. 19 minutes of play, both runs joined, drove and pressed PLAY again into a second round.

THE CALL, from the browser rather than from JavaScript:

  page says      GET https://honolulu-...trycloudflare.com/names?round=bbd65101... -> TimeoutError: signal timed out (8816-9421 ms)
  browser says   GET honolulu-...trycloudflare.com/names -> net::ERR_ABORTED / canceled after 9196-10056 ms
  also, run 1    GET tramadol-... and honolulu-.../rounds -> AbortError, net::ERR_ABORTED / canceled after 11542 ms
  also, run 1    POST honolulu-.../name -> net::ERR_ABORTED / canceled after 12750 ms
  counts         tabA 627 calls / 12 refused and 409 / 8; tabB 616 / 10. Both nodes appear; honolulu more often.

`net::ERR_ABORTED / canceled` is the browser saying the PAGE dropped the call, not that anything refused it. The
timeout is ours: index.html:1339 `AbortSignal.timeout(8000)` on the names lookup (`namesOf`, identity.js:149).

WHY THE PAGE HAD TO WAIT, measured with Cloudflare taken out of the picture - curl to 100.74.66.98:18080/18081 and to
the tunnel, same second, 28 samples:

  direct-a  median 0.017 s  worst 15.00 s (curl's own cap)  over 5 s: 3 of 28
  direct-b  median 0.011 s  worst 15.00 s                   over 5 s: 4 of 28
  tunnel-a  median 0.137 s  worst 12.87 s                   over 5 s: 2 of 28
  tunnel-b  median 0.125 s  worst 15.00 s                   over 5 s: 1 of 28

  21:12:41  direct-b 14.98 s while tunnel-b answered in 1.59 s
  21:13:40  direct-a  9.12 s while tunnel-a answered in 0.14 s
  21:15:08  direct-b 13.95 s while tunnel-b answered in 0.14 s
  21:14:06  everything timed out at 15 s, direct and tunnelled alike

So the signer node process itself blocks for seconds at a time - up to and past 15 s - on the LAN, with the tunnel
answering beside it in a tenth of a second. The tunnel is not the hop that fails. A page whose names lookup waits 8 s
gives up first, and that is every "refused" line above.

NOT THE 10 s CHAIN TIMEOUT that 0.0.1604 fixed, with both numbers: these calls die at 8.8-12.8 s on /names, /rounds
and /name, while `/headers` - the call `agreedChain` waits 10 000 ms for - answered http 200 in 1925 and 1941 ms in
both tabs at the same round boundary, and both tabs kept a proved chain of 3 headers.

WHAT DID NOT REPRODUCE: the exact `Failed to fetch` of the 12:02 letter. Zero occurrences in either run. That string
is a network-level failure, where everything measured here is an abort we asked for. Both tabs also SAW each other in
round two this time - 15.6 s and 16.2 s after PLAY in run 1, 35.5 s in run 2 - so "others 0 at ticks 300 through
1500" did not reproduce either. The Network capture stays in measure-ghost-in-page.mjs, so the next occurrence is
caught with its cause attached.

## What blocked the signer node, and what it cost the page (2026-09-18 23:2x, fixed live)

The node's own log already carried the answer once it was read the right way: `[lag]` lines say how long the loop was
held, what ran in it, and whether the process was merely unscheduled.

  BEFORE (4193 lag events in the log)      AFTER the fix (22 events, 238 KB of log)
  waiting for the machine        0 (0%)    0 - it was never the box, and never my Unity runs
  worst loop hold          26151 ms        1872 ms
  median lag                  ~300 ms      309 ms
  in the worst hold        134 close phases totalling 64785 ms
  close gather on loop     n=4727 median 381 ms worst 1318 ms
  finality   on loop       n=3116 median 399 ms worst 1319 ms

The finality watch (`server.js` `ticked`) awaited `retryClose` and then `gather` for every entry back to back. Each of
those holds the loop for its own synchronous share, so a round's worth of entries chained into one wall where nothing
was served - 26 s of it at the worst. That is what the page met at the round boundary: its 8 s `AbortSignal.timeout`
on `/names` fired at 8.8-9.4 s, `/rounds` at 11.5 s, `POST /name` at 12.8 s.

THE FIX, scheduling only - same work, same order, no outcome touched: the watch yields to the event loop between
entries, and the peer `/results` call gets the 2500 ms deadline it never had ("a peer that is down is not a fault"
was already that function's rule).

MEASURED ON THE DAILY, same probes, same box:

  paired LAN vs tunnel, /rounds     before                      after (93 samples)
    direct-a                        median 0.017 s worst 15.00 s, 3/28 over 5 s   median 0.022 s worst 1.25 s, 0/93
    direct-b                        median 0.011 s worst 15.00 s, 4/28 over 5 s   median 0.025 s worst 0.38 s, 0/93
    tunnel-a                        median 0.137 s worst 12.87 s                  median 0.124 s worst 0.42 s
    tunnel-b                        median 0.125 s worst 15.00 s                  median 0.122 s worst 0.26 s

  two tabs through a round boundary  before                     after
    calls refused                    tabA 12, tabB 10 (and 8)   tabA 0 of 507, tabB 0 of 541
    the other truck in round two     15.6 s / 16.2 s, once 35.5 s   12.4 s / 12.6 s
    on joining                       one tab had client NO      both "join joined, client yes, ghosts yes"

WHAT IS LEFT: one phase still holds the loop 1853 ms (`finality` / `close`), which is inside the page's 8 s budget but
is the next lever if the boundary ever tightens again. And `second-closer.test.js` is red - HELD where it expects
SETTLED - measured red on HEAD before this change as well, so it is not this fix; it is named here so it is not an
unnamed red, and it waits for the letter that owns settlement.

H1 asks that, of tank-ticks with both of a pair alive, >= 50% have the tank within 1.5 m of its post. It measures

What that settles, and what it kills:
- The post does NOT chase the scrolling seam. The hold is stationary between swaps, so "tanks chasing a seam-moving
  line" is not what keeps them off it. I had that hypothesis and the measurement killed it.
- The miss is in z, not x: tanks are in their lane (0.7 m) and 12 m behind their hold.
- And most of it is walking in: 53% of misses are tanks that have not once stood on a post since they spawned, with a
  tail to 71 m - the length of the field from the back edge. A force this heavily attrited spends much of its life in
  transit, and every transit tick is an H1 miss by the row's own words.

So the lever is not "follow the line better". It is either the walk-in (how long a respawn takes to reach its first
post, and whether the budget or the halt cycle slows it) or the row's own reading of a tank that has never yet been
on post. The next measurement is the walk-in itself: time from spawn to first post, and how much of it is spent
standing.

  the hold under them           jumped on 0.4% / 0.3% of those ticks: the post is stationary, they simply are not on it

### H1 is measured against a line the core does not use (2026-09-19 01:1x)

The steady state first, so the walk-in is not blamed for this: in the last third of a 60 s run 73-74% of pair
tank-ticks are settled, and only 40-43% of those are on post. So the gap is the settled tanks, not the arrivals.

Then what a settled tank off its post is doing, from fields the hook actually carries: standing still 63%, halted
(the §11.2 halt cycle) 12%, holding a budget grant 37%, a median 4.4 m from a hold that had not moved under it. A tank
standing still four metres from a stationary post is a tank that believes it has arrived.

It has. The probe and the rules are measuring two different places:

  the row's hold against the mover's own    median 1.37 m, q3 2.70 m, max 22.80 m
  H1 against the row's own hold             31.16%
  H1 against the MOVER'S hold (the hook)    53.3%      - over the doctrine's 50% bar
  on-post radius                            1.50 m     - smaller than the median disagreement

Where the difference is NOT: the hull-down crest. §4.1 rules that an overwatch tank holds its crest and switches only
for 0.3 m more rise, while the probe rescans the five candidates every tick - so the probe was swapped to the
doctrine's own `crestHold`, and H1 got WORSE, 31.16% -> 27.53%, with the gap to the mover's hold unchanged at 1.40 m.

Where it is: the SEAM. The probe's line is frontlineZ(st.tape, x, ...); the core's is seamAtX - the glided tape, on
this tick's scale, with the scroll and the window (st.glide, samplesTaken, seamScroll, seamLo/seamHi). Both the
bounding post and the crest scan hang off that line, so every hold the probe computes is shifted by whatever those two
readers disagree by.

Left as it is on purpose: the probe still measures the old way, so the table's numbers keep their meaning until the
seam is fixed properly - the harness patches the core COPY at named anchors, so the honest repair is to hook the
core's own seam out and use it, not to re-derive it a third time. That is the next step on this row, and it is
bookkeeping, not doctrine: H1 may already be met.

Two of my own probes were wrong before this and are named so they are not repeated: reading `crowded`, `crowdedLoose`
and `tacWait` off the hook returned undefined and printed a tidy "0%" for all three, and an earlier version measured a
"tank standing still" without separating walk-ins from settled tanks.

measure-war.mjs now patches the core COPY to export its own seam reader (`seamOfCore` -> `seamAtX`) and every row uses

This is not a test tuned green: the row asks whether a tank stands within 1.5 m of ITS POST, and a post is what the

The row wants every 60 s window to contain a team whose push word is negative. Measured with --verdicts (seeds 1,2 x
3600, 86400 team-ticks):

  the push word          min 0 m, p05 0, median 0, p95 8, max 16; below zero 0.00%

  push STEPS             28 in the whole run - 12 down, 16 up, none landing below zero
  steps from 0 downward  0

So the direction is not broken: teams do read GIVE (1022 tick-readings, 1019 with the reading before agreeing), and
PUSH_MIN is -8 m, so a negative push is allowed. What is missing is the RATE. The push word is re-read about once per
team-minute, and GIVE is the standing reading on 1.2% of ticks, so the chance a re-read lands on one is about a
hundredth: over the 24 team-minutes of this run the expected number of GIVE steps is under one, and zero were taken.

That is a doctrine question, not a bug in the mover: either §4.10's re-read cadence is too slow for "giving ground is
a normal part of the front", or the GIVE condition (foe >= own + 1 + weight inside the reach) is too strict for the
densities this game has. Both are Daniel's to rule. It is written here rather than guessed at, and the instrument
(--verdicts) stays in the harness so the next attempt starts from the step count.

### A9's remaining gap is the seam's own climb, not the army (2026-09-19 03:3x)

With the army deployed, every short metre has two or more guns within reach (median 8), so the question became where

The hulls are not lopsided: bull hulls run min -88 / q1 -59 / median -6 / q3 49 / max 88 m, 30% past +40 and 33% past
-40, and the slots they are sent to span -81..+81 with 32% past +40. Bear the same. So the frontage is manned on both
flanks and the gaps still sit on the +x one.

The mechanism, in the row's own arithmetic: a tank stands at its slot's x, a depth BELOW THE SEAM AT THAT X. A sample
40 m along a stretch climbing 0.7 m per metre is 28 m further up in z, so the distance from that tank to the sample is
sqrt(40^2 + (28 + 30)^2) = 70 m, past the 46 m reach - where on the flat side the same 40 m is comfortably inside it.
Each hull covers about +-25 m of x on the steep side against +-35 m on the flat.

RULING NEEDED, because every lever is pinned by another row or by the spec:

- the reach is 46 m (§4.2) and the depths are 14 / 26 / 30 m (§4.3), both spec;
- or A9's 95% bar is read as a bar on flat stretches and the steep ones are accepted as thin.
The measurement is done and the cause named; which lever moves is Daniel's.

leaves the lane that climbed to drift back down. O1 mean asks the objective lanes to average 6 m above the rest while
those two cadences run at the same rate.

pushes it must follow are these.

climbs with PUSH_STEP on the confirmed re-read clock, rule (a) skipping half, exactly as §4.10 and §4.11 are written.

the objective, and the failing seeds move it twice as often (35 against 18 lane changes in five minutes). That is 21

### A2's fidget row: the fix is one line, measured both ways, and HELD on a ruling (2026-09-19)

THE CAUSE, measured on the six seeds where the row fails (--cause, 12 fidgets of 318 flips = 3.77% against a 2% bar):
flips by axis x 4 / z 314; the hold had NOT moved on 9 of the 12; and by branch, 8 of the 12 were stepped by the
GIVE-GROUND branch, 4 by the walk-to-post one. That branch's deadband was the step's own length -
`abs(g) > mulFast(CROWD_WALK, dt)`, about 4 cm at 60 Hz - so a tank already inside its back-off point still stepped a
whole step, landed the other side of the point and reversed on the next tick. The walk-to-post branch eight lines
below records fixing exactly this with POST_DEPTH; the give-ground branch was left on the old band.

THE PATCH, one line in `stepUnit` (rules/army.js, the crowdedTight branch):
    -    const want = abs(g) > mulFast(CROWD_WALK, dt) ? (g > 0 ? ONE : -ONE) : 0;
    +    const want = abs(g) > POST_DEPTH ? (g > 0 ? ONE : -ONE) : 0;
Nothing else moves: the ground given is still BACK_OFF, the pace is still CROWD_WALK, a tank further out still walks.
Kept at scratchpad/a2-give-ground-band.patch.

WHAT IT DOES, canonical seeds 1-5 x 3600 ticks, the same table both runs:

  rows passing    before  27 of 39                      after  28 of 39
  other rows      not one changed verdict either way; the only diff in the whole table is A2's own line.
On the six failing seeds: 3.77% -> 1.60%, pass.

condition`, which parks the truck on the seam with the air held off and asserts 0 < hp < 100 after 15 s.

`holdLegs` pushes the team's role clock one tick later for every tick a leg boundary is due while the team is not on

living tanks are, so the off-post share H1 reports and this delay are the same fact twice.
