### The push cadence, measured against §4.10 and against the recording (2026-09-19, no core change)

THE ROW WHOSE ASSERTION IS THE PUSH RATE ITSELF IS A11b, NOT A11a. A11b counts 60 s windows in which no team of a
side held a negative push - the push word going below zero is the assertion. A11a counts hulls physically on the far
side of the seam (measure-war.mjs: `win.cross` counts tank-ticks past `seamOfCore` at the tank's own x), which
follows from the push but is not it. A11b is the probe row used here.

WHAT THE CODE HOLDS, printed from the code and not hypothesised (tactics.js `pressure`, seeds 1-5 x 3600):
  the 5 s clock       `mod(tick + mod(mix(hash, 300 + w) >>> 1, 300), 300) !== 0 -> continue`  - 300 ticks per team,
                      phase hashed per (seed, side, team). Due 720 over the run = 12 per team-minute.
  gate (a) 20:30      `if (!teamOnPost(...)) continue;`  - the re-read is LOST, not deferred; the next chance is the
                      next 300-tick boundary. On post at the due tick 410 of 720 = 56.9%.
  gate (b) 20:30      `const confirmed = s[base + TAC_VERDICT + w] === verdict; if (!confirmed) continue;` - and the
                      verdict word is written BEFORE this test but AFTER gate (a), so a skipped re-read leaves the
                      last verdict standing from however long ago it was taken. Confirmed 213 of 410 = 52.0%.
  delivered           steps 213 of 720 due = 29.6%, or 3.55 steps per team-minute against §4.10's 12.
  verdicts read       take 137, give 37, drift 236. The GIVE path: 37 reads, 12 confirmed, 31 of the 37 already at a
                      push <= 0; steps that landed below zero 11. The push word is below zero on 1.85% of team-ticks.

§4.10 AS RULED HAS NEITHER GATE. "Re-read every 5 s (300 ticks) per team, on a tick hashed from (seed, side, team)",
then own >= foe + 2 takes, foe >= own + 2 gives, otherwise one step toward 0. No on-post condition, no confirmation.
Both gates are the 2026-09-16 20:30 re-ruling, and the six rows were written against the 12-a-minute cadence above
them.

THE C# RECORDING HAS NO PUSH WORD AT ALL. In Army.cs `pressure` is the market's signed trade flow, not a line depth:
it scales speed (`7f + pressure * 2f`) and rate of fire (`Rand(1.4f, 3.2f) / (1f + max(0, pressure) * 0.45f)`), and
every tank simply steers to `front - Dir * 9f` ("push up to the line") EVERY FRAME. So the recording's intent is a
continuously adjusted line at 60 readings a second, with no step, no ceiling and no confirmation. Neither §4.10's
12-a-minute nor the core's 3.55 is a C# leftover: the push word is a doctrine invention (§4.10 "RULED HERE"), and
there is no C# fault to copy here.

TWO OF THE THREE NEVER READ TAKE BECAUSE THEY WERE OUTNUMBERED AT THEIR OWN SLOTS. Seeds 2 and 5 on side +1 read

THE THIRD IS A DIFFERENT FAULT AND IT IS THE INTERESTING ONE. Seed 4 side +1 was LEVEL - own - foe +0.05 - and met
the take lead 12 times of 42 readings, more often than seed 4's own side -1 (6 of 36), which DID cross. It still

at 8 m. Climbing 0 -> 8 -> 16 -> 24 needs THREE CONSECUTIVE CONFIRMED TAKE readings on the SAME team, and on a level
stretch the readings alternate: a take confirms a take, then a drift confirms a drift and §4.10's drift rule steps the
push back toward its rest. So a team that wins its stretch half the time oscillates around 8 m and never reaches the
ceiling. Level odds cannot climb, however many re-reads they get.

spread, not the cadence, not the gates.

AND THAT PUTS THE ROW AGAINST ITS OWN RULE. §4.10 says in its own words: "A team that is winning its stretch takes
ground across the seam; a team that is losing it gives ground." A11a asks that in every 60 s window at least one team
of EACH side crosses. On a seed where one side is three hulls down, the rule forbids exactly what the row requires -
and the give readings are there in the odds print (12 and 14 of them on the two outnumbered sides). This is the same
shape as A4a: the row or the rule. NOT declared a wait here; it is written down for Daniel to pick.

THE LEVEL-OSCILLATION WINDOW stays a rule fact, as ruled: seed 4 +1 was level at +0.05, met the take lead 12 times of
42, and still never climbed, because three consecutive confirmed takes on one team are needed and a take is followed
by a drift that steps the push back toward rest. Layout does not explain it either - seed 4 +1's slope is 0.003 m/m.

Nothing changed: no gate dropped, no cadence constant, no assertion, no A9/H1/B3/A4a lever, no C# copied and no 2-D
coupling introduced - the elevation columns are printed beside the odds, never multiplied into them. Tool only
(--a11geom).

Daniel's pick, recorded: a side three hulls down is losing its stretch, so it gives ground - the 12 and 14 give
readings on the two outnumbered sides are the rule doing what it says, not a fault in the gates. A11a asking a team
of EACH side to cross every 60 s is therefore the row against §4.10, the same shape as A4a's quiet-window bar against

### B4: the infantry's following accounts for 2 of the 7 misses (2026-09-19)

The row: whenever a squad's `pushNear` changes, the mean on-post z of its men must move at least half of that change,
the same way, inside 600 ticks. 7 of 41 changes are not followed; the bar is 0.

WHAT THE SNAPSHOT HOLDS, because it decides what a miss can mean: the squad reading is built ONLY from men who are
standing still this tick (`if (!u || u.dx !== 0 || u.dz !== 0) continue`). A squad still walking is absent from it
altogether, so a miss with almost no readings is a squad that never stood, not a squad that stood in the wrong place.

  what the miss was                            of the 7
    the push moved again inside the window        3
    the push came back before the 10 s were up    1
    stood and did not follow at all               2
    never stood still (unreadable, 9 readable ticks of 600)  1

  group     n   mean readable ticks   mean men standing   mean push change   best follow, as a share of the half owed
  misses    7        162.7 of 600           3.95              -2.29 m                      0.00
  follows  34        201.2 of 600           4.42              +6.12 m                      1.90

SO: THE INFANTRY'S FOLLOWING ACCOUNTS FOR 2 OF THE 7. The remainder, with cause and not with a second hypothesis:
  - 4 of 7: the push moved again inside the 10 s the row allows, one of those coming back to where it started. The
    squad was asked for a move that was then altered or withdrawn; standing still is the right answer to a push that
    returns. This is §4.10's stepping oscillating under the squad - the same take-then-drift already measured on
    A11a's level window - and not the infantry.
  - 1 of 7: the row's own instrument could not see the squad. It stood still for 9 ticks of the 600, so there is
    almost no reading to judge; that is evidence about neither side of the claim.

AND THE FOLLOW IS BIMODAL: a squad that follows overshoots the half it owes, 1.90x on average, while every miss
achieved 0.00 - nothing moved at all. There is no population of squads following slowly. Recorded as measured, not
built into a cause: both genuine misses were WITHDRAWALS (want -16 m and -8 m), while the changes that were followed
average +6.12 m. Whether men follow a take but not a give is a further measurement, not a claim made here.

CORE AGAINST THE RECORDING: no C# path matters to this row. Army.cs `StepInfantry` steers every man, every frame, to
`front - Dir * (standoff + squadOffsetZ)` - the frontline at his x, plus a fixed standoff, with random rests of
0.4-1.8 s every 3-11 s. There is no push word for a squad to follow, exactly as there was none for the tanks, so
B4's claim is doctrine, not a recording behaviour, and there is no C# fault to copy. The per-frame steer stays out.

Nothing changed: no assertion loosened, no gate, no cadence constant, pressure() untouched, A13b and O1's lane still
red by the ruling, the truck-condition red still listed. Tool only (--b4why).

CORRECTION FIRST, same shape as B4's: the live value of this row is 4.00 m, not 3.87 m. The 3.87 came from the run

"unheld" figure survives unchanged, being 6 - 5.27 and independent of the baseline.

THE PROBE AGREES WITH THE ROW IT MEASURES: 6.60 - 2.61 = 4.00 m on 29886 + 61665 = 91551 lane team-ticks, which is
the row's own number and its own denominator.

  group                n       mean push   mean ceiling   mean rest   capped at 16   sitting ON its ceiling
  RIDGE's lane        29886      4.46 m       17.3 m        8.67 m       94.6%             19.8%
  the other two       61665      7.64 m       25.8 m        9.00 m        0.0%             19.4%
  the rest           124449      2.61 m       24.8 m        0.00 m        0.0%              4.9%

THE CAP: `goalOf` gives RIDGE's own lane a ceiling of RIDGE_GOAL 16 m where every other lane may reach PUSH_MAX 24.
RIDGE's lane sits on that ceiling 19.8% of its ticks, as often as the uncapped lanes sit on theirs, so it is a live
limit and not a formality. Counting only the two UNCAPPED objective lanes the row would read 5.04 m instead of 4.00.

  THIS ACCOUNTS FOR 1.04 m OF THE 2.00 m LIVE SHORTFALL = 51.9%.

It is also LARGER than the 0.73 m that had no holder, which means the cap and the cadence OVERLAP rather than add:
1.27 m (what removing both gates would give) + 1.04 m (the cap) = 2.31 m against a 2.00 m shortfall. Part of what the
cadence would deliver on RIDGE's lane is blocked by the cap whatever the cadence does. They are not independent
shares and must not be summed.

WHERE THE REST OF IT GOES, in the row's own terms. The rules price a lane 8.89 m of rest against the rest's 0.00 m -
comfortably over the 6 m bar if both sat still at home. The difference is given back at both ends:
  lanes sit 2.29 m BELOW their own rest   (RIDGE 4.21 m below, the other two 1.36 m below)
  the rest sits 2.61 m ABOVE its own rest (its rest is 0, and §4.10 lets any winning team push toward 24)
  8.89 - 2.29 - 2.61 = 3.99 m, which is the row.
So the non-objective teams erode this row slightly MORE than the objective lanes' own lag does. §4.10 lets a team
that is winning its stretch push to 24 whether or not it holds an objective; the row asks objective lanes to lead
that by 6 m. That is the same shape as A11a - the row against the rule - and it is written down, not acted on.

### Army.cs IsOverrun against the core's overrun path (2026-09-19, read not remembered)

Checked because a fixed distance sitting next to a push word is exactly where a unit error hides.

  C#     `IsOverrun(u, frontZ) => (frontZ - u.z) * u.Dir < -OverrunDepth`, `OverrunDepth = 14f`, and on overrun
         `goalZ = front - v.Dir * 34f`. Armour only: StepInfantry has no overrun at all, it walks to
         `front - Dir * (standoff + squadOffsetZ)`.
  CORE   `OVERRUN_DEPTH = 14 m` (commented "Army.OverrunDepth"), `FALL_BACK_LINE = 34 m` (§1.1), and
         `const overrun = u.armour && past > OVERRUN_DEPTH` - armour only, which army.js records as "C#'s own
         division, not a preference", with the measurement behind it: applied to riflemen it parked the infantry
         36.5 m behind the front against a FALL_BACK of 34.

Same quantities, same units, both distances in metres: 14 m of depth and a 34 m fall-back line. NOTHING IS PORTED AS
A PUSH. The one deliberate divergence is documented in the core and required by a rule the recording does not have:
C# measures overrun from `front` (the seam), while the core measures it from the team's PUSHED forward line -
`u.tacSeam + side * u.tacForward` - because §4.10 did not exist in the recording, and measuring from the seam would
throw back every push across the seam on the tick it arrived. That is a rule, not a leftover.

So the standing finding holds, now verified rather than asserted: Army.cs has no push word; its only giving-ground is
this fixed overrun fall-back, which the core holds separately with the same numbers in the same units. No distance
used as a speed, no 2-D coupling, and the per-frame steer stays out.

### A11b, core against the recording IN NUMBERS: the core gives more ground, not less (2026-09-19)

The code read said Army.cs has no push word. That is necessary but not sufficient: it says the two cannot be compared
on §4.10's word, not that they cannot be compared at all. What the word is supposed to PRODUCE can be compared, and
in the same units - a side's armour standing further back from the seam than it did five seconds ago.

csharp-army.json holds each side's mean armour z every 5 s for 90 s (seed 20260901, flat world, seam at 0, no trade
flow, no truck, 24 armour a side). The core was sampled at the same cadence for the same 90 s, its depth taken from
its OWN seam at each hull's x - the seam wanders with the chart, so a depth measured from z = 0 would be measuring a
line the army does not hold. An interval counts as giving ground when the mean depth grows by more than 0.5 m.

Read from t = 20 s, after the recording's army has closed: the recording walks in from 77 m and the core spawns on
post (ruled 2026-09-19), so the opening is not comparable by design.

  side    recording gave ground      core gave ground
  bull     7 of 14 intervals          5 of 14 intervals
  bear     4 of 14 intervals          9 of 14 intervals
  BOTH    11 of 28 = 39.3%           14 of 28 = 50.0%
  worst single fall-back   recording bull 5.7 m / bear 3.8 m      core bull 10.8 m / bear 11.9 m

SO THE CORE'S ARMY GIVES GROUND MORE OFTEN THAN THE RECORDING'S, AND IN BIGGER STEPS - 50.0% of intervals against
39.3%, and a worst fall-back of 10.8-11.9 m against 3.8-5.7 m. A11b is red while the behaviour it is named for
happens more in the core than in the thing the core was written from.

That is because A11b does not measure the behaviour. It measures the WORD: a 60 s window passes only if some team's
`TAC_PUSH` goes below zero, and that word is what the two 20:30 gates hold shut. The recording, having no push word
at all, would fail A11b in every window of every seed - 24 of 24 - while visibly falling back on 39.3% of its
intervals. The row is about the instrument, not the army's conduct.

CAVEAT, stated rather than buried: the two runs are not the same world. The recording is flat with 24 armour a side
and no chart; the core has 12 a side and a seam that wanders. The comparison is of the RATE at which each line falls
back, in metres of its own depth, not of absolute depths, and it is reported as such.

CORROBORATION, free and worth keeping: at t = 0 the core's mean armour depth is 23.0 m, which is exactly the mean of
§2.5's two lines, (16 + 30) / 2. The hulls stand on their posts at spawn, measured here in a file that has nothing to
do with that ruling - while the recording stands at 77.3 m and walks in, which is the spawn fault that ruling named.

### THE FIVE WAITS, RULED (2026-09-19, Daniel's delegation)

Daniel: *"Lies die war tactics specs und beantworte dir die Fragen, am besten was einem dynamischen Krieg
entspricht"*, then the five restated with *"Entscheide"*. So these are mine, made against §0's own definition of a
dynamic war and written into WAR_TACTICS.md beside the measurement that forced each.

ALL FIVE WENT AGAINST THE ROW, NOT THE RULE. That is a suspicious-looking result and it is why each one carries its
own arithmetic here. Three were arithmetic defects (a window sized for a leg length the doctrine had replaced; two
generator ranges copied onto a standard deviation; a coverage bar that dropped its own "at full strength"
qualifier); two were contradictions with a rule already ruled to stay (§4.10's give-ground, §0's own column rule).
NO DOCTRINE NUMBER MOVED on this pass: not the 27 m slot pitch, not the 46 m gun, not the 14/26/30 m depths, not
§2.6's 12-20 s leg, not §4.3's 20 s cool-down, not §3's respawn entry, not §11.1's standoff or spread or squad z,
not §4.10's gates, thresholds or ceilings. No core source file was touched at all - the diff is WAR_TACTICS.md,
PRIORITIES.md and the probe.

#### A9 - the cause is attrition, and the climb hypothesis was measured and withdrawn

The first ruling written was "the two-gun bar is a bar on flat stretches", from the earlier band table (gap share
23-24% where the seam climbs 0.57-0.73 m/m against 3-4% at 0.18-0.37). It was implemented at a 0.40 m/m threshold,
measured, AND IT FAILED: flat stretches still ran 10.85% short against a 5% bar. Per metre of x, seeds 1-3:

  climb m/m     0.0-0.1   0.1-0.2   0.2-0.3   0.3-0.4   0.4-0.6   0.6-0.9    0.9+
  under 2 guns    9.72%    11.72%     6.03%     6.90%    11.26%    20.94%   18.22%
  under 1 gun     1.12%     2.21%     1.35%     0.91%     1.05%     5.27%    1.16%

So the climb roughly doubles the shortfall at 0.6+ and is real, but the FLATTEST ground is still 9.72% - nowhere
near the bar. The climb was never the cause. The competing hypothesis, measured in the same run:

  living hulls      12      10-11      8-9      6-7
  under 2 guns    2.00%     9.70%   25.05%   33.20%
  under 1 gun     0.15%     1.47%    5.20%    7.42%

Monotonic in attrition and nothing else, and AT FULL STRENGTH THE ROW PASSES OUTRIGHT at 2.00% against its own 5%
bar. The row admitted any side with >= 6 alive and then demanded double cover; a 46 m gun on a 27 m pitch covers
163 m of seam twice over with twelve hulls and arithmetically cannot with six. §4.1's own kill-zone sentence already
carries the qualifier the row had dropped - "every metre of the seam between the outer slots is inside the reach of
at least 3 slots of a side AT FULL STRENGTH" - so the row contradicted the section it guards. RULED: two-gun bar at
full strength, one-gun floor at any strength. Canonical 5 x 3600: 1.71% and 2.88%, both green. A thinned army
leaving holes in its kill zone is losses biting (§0.1, §3's supply), not a fault to engineer away.

#### H1 - §3's entry stays; the row stops counting columns

Measured before: the walk-in share and the row move together and inversely on every seed - seed 7 settles near 30%
walking in and the row CLIMBS to 59.08%, seeds 1 and 8 reach 44% and 48% and the row falls to 49.77% and 48.15%.
The hold is stationary throughout, no post is abandoned, the settled hulls keep holding. §0's own reading rule
already says a hull more than 40 m from its post is a COLUMN and that line rows do not count it - it had been
applied to rows 2, 4b and 7 and missed on the hold row. Applied: canonical 65.69% against 60.48%, with 53248 of
321770 pair tank-ticks excluded as columns. §3's entry deliberately NOT changed: a replacement still enters 52-87 m
from its post, 137-176 times in five minutes, because that column is the one thing on the field that reads as
resupply from the cab, and it is worth more than the row was.

#### B3 - half ruled, still red, and the tempting answer measured false

z: the band 4-12 m is `RIFLE_STANDOFF` 4 + `RIFLE_SPREAD` 8, whose own comment reads "so 4 to 12" - a DISTANCE from
the seam, copied onto a STANDARD DEVIATION. Computed from the constants that write the posts, over a side's 36 men,
nobody dead and no push applied: sd 2.98 m on one side and 4.52 m on the other. One side was under the old floor on
every tick of every seed before a shot was fired. Corrected to 2 m, and measured PER SQUAD, which is §11.1's own
scope (the scatter it writes is per man inside a squad; the differences between squads are §12.1's push doing its
job, and a side-wide sd added the two together). Still red: 13.51% of 7296 squad-ticks out of band.

x: the obvious ruling was that the 20 m floor is a bar on a DRAW - three squad anchors, uniform on [-80, +80]
(`sim.js`), a man within +-8 m of his; over 200k draws the men's sd lands below 20 m on 19.6% of rounds. A relative
bar was written against that (>= 0.6 x the anchors' own sd) and MEASURED FALSE, so it was withdrawn: the layout
alone puts a side under a 10 m sd on about 3% of rounds, and the core does it on 46.5% of side-ticks - twelve times
as often. The knot is NOT the draw. Left measured for the next probe: a squad's centre sits more than 12 m off its
own anchor on 25.9% of squad-ticks (>24 m on 2.3%) and per-squad x spread is outside 2-12 m on 24.3%. The first
question is whether that drift is §11.3's cover claims (12 m), §12.1's follow, or casualties collapsing a side onto
one surviving squad. The 20 m floor STAYS until that is answered, and B3 stays red on both halves.

#### A4a - the row, restated to the leg the cadence actually delivers

The 10 s window was arithmetic under `period = 360 + (h % 240)` - a leg of at most 600 ticks puts a boundary inside
every 600-tick window, for every team. The 20:30 re-ruling doubled the leg to 720-1200 and §4.3's cool-down to 1200,
ON MEASUREMENT (at 6-10 s the new bounding tank reached its post on 56% of legs and a pair was on post together
17.5% of the time - the cadence was moving the tanks the spec calls hold), and left the window at 10 s. The row
carried the contradiction in its own middle column: "(a leg is 12 to 20 s)" beside a demand for a change every 10 s.
Restated to 20 s. Canonical: 0 of 30. The cadence does not go back - reverting it to green a window would break H2,
the hold row and §0's "Hold is the default" together.

#### A11a - the row, and §4.10 stays

The chain was already closed: no post across the seam in 3 of 3 failing windows <- no TAKE verdict (2 of 3
outnumbered, 1 of 3 level) <- fewer hulls alive, 8.48 against 11.25 where crossing windows ran 10.81 against 9.86.
§4.10 was RULED on 2026-09-19 to stay as written, and it says a side losing its stretch gives ground - so asking a
team of EACH side to cross every 60 s asks for what the rule forbids. It is also anti-dynamic on its own terms: a
test demanding both sides cross every minute is a front that oscillates symmetrically for ever, which is §0.1's
point 2 (the homeostatic war) written as a bar. A beaten side must be allowed to stay beaten. Restated to three
clauses: some side crossed in every window; a side that did not cross was outnumbered while it did not; and no side
crossed in no window of its whole run. Canonical: 0 of 5 windows with neither side across, and all 3 non-crossing
windows outnumbered.

ONE DEFECT IN MY OWN ROW, FOUND AND FIXED: at TICKS = 3600 each side-run holds exactly one 60 s window, so the third
clause restated the second and failed by construction with it (3 of 10 side-runs). It is now asserted only on a run
with a second window (>= 7200 ticks) and prints "not asserted" below that, rather than printing a red that is the
same fact twice.

#### The table

  canonical 5 x 3600, before: 28 of 39 rows, 11 red
  canonical 5 x 3600, after:  35 of 44 rows,  9 red
The count moved because three rows were SPLIT, not because the army changed: A9 into two bars plus an information
line carrying the old number (12.32%, unchanged), A11a into three clauses, B3 into its ruled half and its unruled
half. Reds 11 -> 9: A9, A4a and A11a's crossing bar green by ruling, B3 now two reds. The remaining nine are A11b,
A13b, O1 (two), O4, B2, B3 (two) and B4, each with the holder it already had.

#### The rulings at five minutes (3 seeds x 18000), which is where H1 failed before

The canonical is 5 x 3600 (§0), but three of the five rulings had to survive a longer run to mean anything: H1
passed at one minute before this pass and failed at five, and A11a's third clause has no meaning at a run length
that holds one window.

  A9    1.09% at full strength, 4.33% on the one-gun floor   green (the floor is closer to its bar here)
  A4a   0 of 90 windows                                      green
  A11a  0 of 15 windows with neither side across; 7 of 7 non-crossing windows outnumbered; 0 of 6 side-runs
        that never crossed - the clause that only bites at this length, and it is green
  H1    59.43% of 623288 pair tank-ticks, 228650 of 851938 excluded as columns (26.8%)   green
        - and this is the decisive one: seeds 1 and 8 read 49.77% and 48.15% at this length before the ruling,
          seed 1 is in this run, and the slip is gone because it was the columns all along

NOT GREEN AT FIVE MINUTES, listed rather than buried, none of them one of the five waits: A2 4.1% of flips are
fidgets against a 2% bar (canonical 0.42%), B1 74.48% against an 80% bar (canonical 84.11%), and B3 degrades
further (z 31.43%, x 64.35% against canonical 13.51% and 61.21%). B3 getting WORSE with run length is evidence for
its own named hypothesis - attrition collapsing a side onto its surviving squads - and is the first thing the next

DEPLOY POSITION: A9 was the named blocker and it is green, but B3 is a red §0 doctrine row whose x number is
unruled, and the standing rule is that nothing ships while a doctrine row is red. The army was NOT deployed on this
pass and the Daily stays 0.0.1617. B3's concentration bug is the next work and the shortest path to the ship.

### B3's real defect was its POPULATION (2026-09-19, after the five rulings)

Chasing B3's x knot - "the line is concentrated twelve times more often than the anchor layout explains" - found the
cause in the row again, and this one was the biggest of its three defects.

§11.1's row says "a side's men ON POST". §11.1's own body uses that word for where a man IS: "whenever a man is on
post AND his fire team's clock says halt" - two conditions. The probe implemented "on post" as `dx == 0 && dz == 0`,
which is §11.2's HALT clock, and §11.2 halts a fire team 0.4-1.8 s out of every 3-11 s. So the row measured the
spread of whichever men happened to be mid-halt on that tick. Measured, same run, same seeds:

  men counted per side-tick        8.3  of the 30.1 on the line  (of 36 a side)
  x spread out of the 20-60 m band    61.21%  ->  25.84%
  x spread under a 10 m sd            46.48%  ->   9.02%      (the layout alone gives about 3%)

A spread of eight men drawn from three squads is tight whatever the line is doing. AND THIS OVERTURNS A CONCLUSION
I PUBLISHED EARLIER TODAY: the relative x bar (>= 0.6 x the side's own anchor sd) had been written, measured at
61.21% against it, and withdrawn as "measured false" with the note that the knot is not the draw. It was the
population underneath. With it corrected the measured 25.84% sits against the 19.6% the three-anchor uniform draw
predicts on its own, so the floor IS very largely a bar on the draw, as first suspected. The relative bar is
restored and the withdrawal is recorded here rather than quietly dropped.

B3 STAYS RED ON BOTH HALVES, canonical 5 x 3600 with the population and both bands corrected:

  z per squad out of 2-12 m      22.58%  of 69007 squad-ticks
  x under 0.6 x anchor sd, or over 60 m   18.91%  of 29837 side-ticks (under a 10 m sd on 13.55%)

Sample sizes are 5x the old ones because a side-tick now qualifies whenever six men are on the line, not only when
six are simultaneously mid-halt.

THE LAST PIECE IS NOT RULED, deliberately. Both bars are ZERO-TOLERANCE, and B3 is the only spread-band row in §0
carrying no tolerance while every other distributional row here carries one (2%, 5%, 80%, 95%). §0's own sentence -
"a tolerance is a measurement allowance for respawns and transit, not a licence" - points straight at the men who
blow these bands, because 72% of the men on the line are in transit on any tick (8.3 halted of 30.1). But unlike the
other four rulings, no number falls out of the spec's own arithmetic here, and a tolerance chosen to clear today's
22.58% would be tuning to pass. Left open, named, with the measurement done.

Nothing in the infantry moved: not the standoff, not the spread, not the squad z, not the anchors, not the squad
count. Tool only.

### B3's remaining red, SPLIT before any hypothesis (2026-09-19)

Both halves measured on the current tree, population cut at §12.1's 40 m, bands untouched. Every failing tick asked
which clause it failed and what the code was holding when it did.

THE X HALF - 5615 of 28812 side-ticks = 19.49% missing.
  under the 0.6 x anchor floor      4627  = 82.4% of the failures  (16.06 points of the 19.49)
  over the 60 m ceiling              988  = 17.6%                  ( 3.43 points)
  of ALL failures, also under the old absolute 20 m floor   3585 = 63.8%  (12.44 points)
  the remaining                                             2030 = 36.2%  ( 7.05 points) fail ONLY because that
    side's own anchors were drawn wide - the men are inside 20 m but their anchors span more than 33 m.
  anchor sd, min/q1/med/q3/max   failing 6.5 / 32.6 / 46.8 / 55.6 / 66.7   passing 0.6 / 17.9 / 29.9 / 43.6 / 66.1
  men's x sd                     failing 1.4 /  8.2 / 12.9 / 27.4 / 76.8   passing 4.3 / 16.4 / 25.6 / 36.9 / 59.7
  the floor those anchors imply  failing 3.9 / 19.6 / 28.1 / 33.4 / 40.0   passing 0.3 / 10.7 / 18.0 / 26.2 / 39.7
  SO: a failing side-tick is one where the anchors were drawn nearly twice as wide as on a passing tick (median
  46.8 m against 29.9 m) and the men cover half as much (12.9 m against 25.6 m). Two thirds of the miss is men who
  are tight in absolute terms as well; one third is only the relative floor biting on a wide draw.

THE Z HALF - 12140 of 64753 squad-ticks = 18.75% missing.
  looser than 12 m   8978 = 73.9% of the failures  (13.86 points of the 18.75)
  tighter than 2 m   3162 = 26.0%                  ( 4.88 points)
  squad z sd on failing ticks, min/q1/med/q3/max   0.6 / 1.9 / 13.4 / 15.5 / 23.3 - the loose half sits just over
    the ceiling, not far beyond it.
  men per squad there 4 / 5 / 7 / 9 / 21, OF THEM HALTED 0 / 0 / 0 / 2 / 11.
  SO: the median failing squad has NOBODY standing still. Only 957 of the 12140 failures have four or more halted
  men - 7.9% - and of those, 310 = 32.4% would be inside the band if only their halted men were counted.
  The z miss is overwhelmingly squads in motion, and their depth spread is a squad walking, not a squad standing
  wrong. That is consistent with the population ruling (the whole line counts, transit included) and it is why
  counting the line made this half worse rather than better.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT YET SAY: whether the tight men of the x half, and the loose-in-transit squads of the z half, are
the core placing men wrongly or the row asking for something the movement rules cannot give while men are walking.
That is the named fork and it is not picked here. No band, floor, ceiling or doctrine number was touched, no
population changed, nothing tuned. Probe flag: --b3split.

### B3 step 5: the recording cannot be asked B3's question, and where it can, the core's line is TIGHTER (2026-09-19)

WHAT THE RECORDING ACTUALLY HOLDS, checked field by field before comparing anything. `csharp-army.json` rows carry,
per side every 5 s for 90 s: infantry `n`, mean `z`, and `spread` (the z sd). Its `density` block carries an
`xSpread` for the ARMOUR only. There is no squad structure anywhere in the file and no infantry x at all.

  B3 asserts (1) z sd PER SQUAD between 2 and 12 m and (2) the side's x sd against its own three anchors.
  THE RECORDING CARRIES NEITHER. It cannot be asked either half of this row. That is a fact about the reference,
  not a result, and it is why this comparison cannot decide the fork on B3's own terms.

WHAT CAN BE COMPARED is the side-wide infantry z sd, measured on both engines at the recording's own cadence, its
own seed (20260901), with the core's depth taken from its own seam at each man's x. From t=30, which the recording's
own comment calls the steady grind:

  recording, side-wide infantry z sd    17.78 m
  core,      side-wide infantry z sd     8.76 m
  core,      z sd per squad (median)      7.70 m
  core,      side x sd                   30.88 m

THE CORE'S LINE IS LESS THAN HALF AS SPREAD IN DEPTH AS THE RECORDING'S. And read side-wide against B3's own 2-12 m
band, the RECORDING would fail it at 17.78 m while the core would pass it at 8.76 m. The core's per-squad median,
7.70 m, is inside the band too - the row's 18.75% is a tail of ticks, not a line that stands wrong on average.

CAVEAT, stated: the two armies are not the same size. The recording fields 70-72 infantry a side; the core fields
16-35 living men a side over this run. A sd from 20 men is noisier than one from 70, so this compares the shape of
the line and not counts, and the direction of the difference - core tighter - is far larger than that noise.

THE FORK, against the criteria set for it:
  - "the recording is already this spread on z while walking, so the row asks for what the movement rules do not
    produce" - NOT supported: the recording is MORE spread, not less.
  - "the recording holds the band and core does not, so Core is placing wrongly" - ALSO NOT supported: the recording
    does not hold the band either, and misses it by more than the core does.
  BOTH MISS, and by the instruction that case stops here rather than turning into a rewrite. No mechanism is named
  against the recording because the recording has nothing to name it with.

B3 stays RED on both halves - z 18.75% of 64753 squad-ticks, x 19.49% of 28812 side-ticks - listed with this as the
state of the evidence. Nothing moved: no band, floor, ceiling, population, doctrine number or assert, no C# number
copied and no 2-D coupling introduced. The army does not ship. Probe kept: tools/measure-line-engines.mjs.

### B3 IS LISTED RED, with cause and dependency, and the zero tolerance stays (2026-09-19, ruled)

RULED: no tolerance is invented. Both B3 bars stay zero-tolerance. A number picked against today's 18.75% z or
19.49% x would be loosening the assert to fit the line, which is tuning a test green.

THE LISTING.
  z half - 18.75% of 64753 squad-ticks out of the 2-12 m band, population cut at §12.1's 40 m.
     73.9% of the failures are looser than 12 m, 26.0% tighter than 2 m; the failing squad's z sd has a median of

     with halted 0/0/0/2/11, and only 957 of the 12140 failures have four or more halted men, of which 32.4% would
     be inside the band counting halted men only. CAUSE: squads in motion, whose depth spread is a line walking and

The recording is MORE spread in depth than the core, would MISS the 2-12 m band where the core's 8.76 m and 7.70 m

### B3: the men ARE on the line the core writes; the x miss is the floor's reference frontage (2026-09-19)

Asked to fix B3, the first question is whether the core is placing men wrongly. Measured, and it is not.

  ARE THE MEN OFF THEIR POSTS? A rifleman's post is his squad's anchor plus a fixed offset within +-9 m
  (army.js riflePost, SQUAD_OFFSET 18 m). Distance from each man to his OWN post, on failing against passing ticks:
     mean |man - his post| in x     failing 0.2 / 6.6 / 10.0 / 13.0 / 34.8 m    passing 0.2 / 5.9 / 7.9 / 12.6 / 68.5
     share of men more than 5 m off failing 0.0 / 33.3 / 51.4 / 70.0 / 100.0%   passing 0.0 / 34.5 / 53.8 / 68.6 / 100.0
  THE TWO ARE THE SAME. Men on failing ticks are no further from their posts than men on passing ticks - 51.4%
  against 53.8% more than 5 m off at the median. The line is not leaving its posts on the ticks that fail.

  WHAT IS DIFFERENT IS WHICH POSTS EXIST. The posts' own x sd on failing ticks is 3.0 / 11.0 / 20.3 / 40.9 / 79.9
  against an all-three-anchor sd of 6.5 / 32.6 / 46.8 / 55.6 / 66.7. Posts are anchors +-9 m, so the posts' sd can
  only fall that far below the anchors' if the living men no longer come from all three squads:
     squads with a living man        failing 1 / 2 / 3 / 3 / 3        passing 1 / 3 / 3 / 3 / 3
     failures with a wiped squad     2695 = 48.0% of the failures, against 11.1% of the passing ticks
     sd of the LIVING squads' anchors failing 0.0 / 11.2 / 25.1 / 55.2 / 80.0   passing 0.0 / 17.5 / 29.4 / 43.6 / 66.1
  So the floor asks the survivors to span 0.6 x a frontage measured from THREE anchors, one of which may have no
  living man on it. Of the 5615 failing side-ticks, 2107 = 37.5% would PASS if the floor used only the anchors of
  squads that still have a living man.

  THIS IS THE SAME DEFECT CLASS ALREADY RULED TWICE ON THIS ROW - a bar measuring something that is not the line
  (the halt clock standing in for "on post"; the generator range standing in for a standard deviation). Here it is
  a dead squad's anchor standing in for frontage the side still holds. It is 37.5% of the x miss. The other 62.5%
  is genuinely tight men and the 60 m ceiling, as already listed.

  AND THE Z HALF CANNOT BE FIXED IN THE CORE EITHER. Its failures are squads in motion - median zero halted men -
  and the ruled population counts men in transit on purpose. Making the core spread walking men less, or halting
  them more, would be moving the army to fit the test.

SO B3 CANNOT BE MADE GREEN WITHOUT A RULING. The core places men where §11.1 says and the recording is twice as
spread in depth. Every remaining lever is the row's: the floor's anchor set, or the in-transit tolerance. Neither is
taken here - both were explicitly forbidden - and no band, floor, ceiling, population or doctrine number was moved.
The measurement is the answer; the change is a decision.

### B3 LISTED RED, final (2026-09-19, ruled: keep the bar, keep the measurement, change nothing)

RULED: B3 stays listed red on both halves. The floor, the in-transit tolerance, the band, the ceiling, the
population, every doctrine number, every assert and the core source all stay as they are. Dropping a dead squad's
anchor from the floor would be a row change made after the five-wait ruling, and it would leave the row red anyway -
about 12.2% x miss instead of 19.49%.

THE CAUSE, in the four numbers that carry it:
  1. THE RIFLEMEN ARE ON THE POSTS THE CORE WRITES. Distance from each man to his own post (anchor +-9 m) is the
     same whether the tick fails or passes: mean |man - post| in x, median 10.0 m failing against 7.9 m passing;
     share of men more than 5 m off post, median 51.4% failing against 53.8% passing. There is no placement fault.
  2. X - the floor spans squads that are dead. 48.0% of failing side-ticks have a wiped squad against 11.1% of
     passing ones, and 2107 of the 5615 failures - 37.5% - would pass if the floor used only the anchors of squads
     that still have a living man. The remaining 62.5% is genuinely tight men and the 60 m ceiling.
  3. Z - squads in motion. The median failing squad has ZERO halted men; 73.9% of failures are looser than 12 m at
     a median z sd of 13.4 m, just over the ceiling. The ruled population counts men in transit on purpose.
  4. THE RECORDING IS MORE SPREAD THAN THE CORE - side-wide infantry z sd 17.78 m against the core's 8.76 m from
     t=30, with the core's per-squad median at 7.70 m, inside the band. So there is no C# rewrite to make, no
     spread or halt number to port, and no reason to change what the core does.

NO LATER ITEM IS OPENED TO "FIX B3 IN THE CORE". The residual is the row's, not a placement fault, and moving the
army to fit a bar would be worse than tuning the bar. The dependency stands where the letter named it: the
in-transit tolerance §0 gives every other distributional row and B3 alone does not carry.

STATE: z 18.75% of 64753 squad-ticks, x 19.49% of 28812 side-ticks, both red, both zero-tolerance. 35 of 44 rows
pass. The army does not ship while B3 is red.

So a side declares, runs and consolidates assaults, and it declares them at lanes it is already on.

§4.13 THE TAPE IS THE GENERAL - IN for a fed tape, STILL GAP for its own Rule 1. Seed 3, a sample every 5 s:
  rising tape (+0.4% a sample)   trend 0 -> +1, strength 1 -> 2 -> 3, seam z 2.05 -> -16.39 -> +19.40
  falling tape (-0.4%)           trend 0 -> -1, strength 1 -> 2 -> 3, seam z 2.05 -> -15.81 -> +21.98
  NOTHING SUBMITTED             seam z 2.58 -> 2.05 and there it stays; trend 0 at every reading of a whole round
The market moves the front, and the direction it moves is the tape's. But §4.13's "Rule 1 - seeded (GAP)" is not in:
the init tape should be mix(seedHash, 0x7e5a1c3d + i) per sample, walked, so that a SIM round with no live feed
still has a tape. With nothing submitted the seam is frozen for the whole round and the trend never leaves 0 - a SIM
round has no general. LISTED, not built: this letter ships what is ruled and measured, and a seeded tape is its own
piece.

### The path to coax, as its own letter (2026-09-19)

§4.4's coax cannot be written from the spec as it stands, because the spec writes it in terms of two things the core
does not have. Measured: `TAC_COVER` appears nowhere in tactics.js, there is no suppression word, and §11.4/§11.5
appear nowhere in army.js or sim.js. §4.4 sets the coax's hit by posture (STAND 400 / PRONE 200 / COVER 100 per mil)
and adds +60 to the man's fire-team suppression word, so writing coax first would mean inventing thresholds against
postures that do not exist.

THE ORDER, and it is the only honest one: §11.3 cover claims (still GAP) -> §11.4 posture, derived and written into
the TAC_COVER word's high bits, which is a state-layout change -> §11.5 suppression -> then §4.4 coax. Not started on
this letter by ruling.

### §4.13 Rule 1 in: the init tape is seeded, and three tactics rows now see a trend at open (2026-09-19)

RULE 1 IS IN. The init tape's step was `(i + 1) * 2654435761 >>> 20`, a function of the SAMPLE INDEX alone, so every
round of every seed drew the identical tape. It is now `mix(seedHash, 0x7e5a1c3d + i)`, the rule's own words. The
walk's shape, magnitude and starting level are unchanged and no doctrine number moves.

  MEASURED: eight seeds, eight different fronts - seam z -15.9, +27.43, +8.28, +17.21, +13.56, -1.17, -1.18, +11.17.
  Seed 1's tape and seed 2's share 0 of 64 samples. Before: every seed opened on the same front.

THE GOLDENS ALL MOVED, as a deliberate world change must: 9 of 9 regenerated, vectors 8/8 again, asserts untouched.

TWO rules.test.js FIXTURES NEEDED THEIR SETUP RE-MEASURED - setup, never an assert:
  "nothing accrues while the truck is still on the apron" - the ground this run crosses is the round's own now and
    the same throttle covers it more slowly: 16.8 m at tick 180 as ever, but 22 m with exposure only at tick 276.
    The second leg goes 60 -> 100 ticks.
  "a second round starts where the first one did" - this seed's seam runs +25.8 m at x -60 to -31.0 m at x 120 while
    the truck starts at z 10.2, so driving straight it never comes inside anyone's reach: 3000 ticks of full throttle
    and the exposure word is still 0. The drive steers now (-16000), first exposure at tick 211.
  "the seam banks more than the quiet lane" - its lanes were pinned at z 0 / 20 / 62 from when the seam sat near 0.
    Measured for this seed, exposure by lane in metres: z -80 0.0, -60 1.1, -40 31.3, -18 62.8, 0 45.9, 20 58.7,
    40 37.7, 62 1.4, 80 0.0 - the seam lane is still the busiest, at the seam. The lanes are taken from `frontAt`
    now and the rim from the field edge away from it, so the test reads the round it is given.

AND THREE TACTICS ROWS ARE RED, LISTED, NOT REWRITTEN - this is a rule question and not mine:
  "push moves one 8 m step on its re-read only"      seed 8 tick 3103: team 11 push moved off its re-read tick
  "a team rests at +8 m on an objective's lane"      seed 1: team 0 on slot 2 rests at 8 m
  "an assault starts only on an objective ..."       seed 1 tick 1: team 0 outside the assault lanes has weight 2
  THE CAUSE, measured: with a seeded tape some rounds OPEN with a market trend. trendFor at tick 0 is +1 on seeds 1
  and 2, 0 on seed 3, where with the old flat tape it was 0 on every seed always. §4.14 gives the trend's side +1
  weight on EVERY lane and moves rest and ceiling with it, so a team outside the assault lanes legitimately reads
  weight 2. The three rows compute their expectation as `objectiveWeight(slot)` alone - they omit §4.14's trend term,
  which was invisible while every tape was flat.
  The spec settles the neighbouring word and not this one: "Round open ... in SIM the seeded tape's newest sample at
  init ... every LATER sample against it is the lead", and the lead does read 0 at tick 0, as measured. The trend is
  not the lead: it comes from the tape's own candles, and 64 samples is far more than §4.14's six closed ones, so a
  trend at open is defensible. Whether the rows should model the trend term or the seeded tape should open without
  one is the row-or-rule call, and it is written down rather than taken.
NOT DEPLOYED: three doctrine rows are red, so nothing ships on this.

## The pool left twelve seconds after the close, and only into an open tab (2026-09-21, round ec9bd34e)

The 13:54 ruling's own measurement, run on the Daily against `4e9d7244`, and it passed:

    both seats     paid the stake and the fee from alice, NO NWC string anywhere in the run
    winner         named win@127.0.0.1:18778 in the page, once
    core           DELIVERED at tick 2240
    alice           996016 -> 996114 sat          (+98 sat, the pool's share)
    committee      1000216 -> 1000122 sat          (-98 out, +2000 +2000 msat of fee in)
    endpoint log   payRequest asked (x2, one per seat), callback asked for 98000 msat -> lnbcrt980n1p4tzgjf...

Two things in that run were wrong, and neither shows in the totals.

WHEN IT MOVED. The `[money]` print for this round:

    [money] ec9bd34e +12125ms after close, window 600000ms
      | 613218ca FAILED    agreed=y live=PROVISIONALLY_FINAL settle=not-final hold=HELD
      | c2ab63f3 DELIVERED agreed=y live=PROVISIONALLY_FINAL settle=not-final hold=HELD

At +12125 ms both fee holds were SETTLED to the committee and the winner was written down as owed
98000 msat - which the page then collected. The stakes were right to wait ("waits for its objection
window, which closes at 1789994144399", 588 s away) and both were still HELD, in flight and in
nobody's balance. So the 98 sat left the committee's own channel against money that had not arrived,
on a result still PROVISIONALLY_FINAL. §13A: FINAL is the window's word.

WHY IT MOVED AT ALL. The address lived in the tab's sessionStorage and travelled at payout time. The
probe's Chrome happened to still be up - I looked for it on the wrong debug ports (9222/9333; the
probes use 9351/9352) and wrongly read that as "no tab". Had it been down, FINAL would have arrived
ten minutes later with 98000 msat owed and nobody to post it. "Winnings are always sent" cannot mean
"sent if the player is still sitting there".

FIXED IN 56bec67a: a fee settles only once every entry of the round is final; the pool is owed only
once this node's own acts on the round are done, every stake that had an act having had it. And the
address goes to the door the moment it is named, signed by the session key, kept as a standing
instruction (202 NAMED while nothing is owed), with the settle LNURL-paying it itself.

FOUR REDS CLEARED WITH IT, all of them the fee hold's arrival at entry, none of them cosmetic:
  close-order x2   JSON.stringify of a BigInt threw inside an assertion's MESSAGE, so neither test
                   ever looked at the answer it was written to check. The settle's answer now leaves
                   `settleTheStakes` as decimal strings.
  second-closer x2 compared a port's whole settle log with one stake preimage and saw the fee's too
                   (sha256 of 32 zero bytes). Fee releases are separated and asserted on, not filtered.
  void-expiry x2   the fake port kept ONE amount for the whole port, so an entry's second invoice
                   overwrote the first: "not paid and held: 2000 of 98000 msat" on a good stake.
  close-at-end     built a round "over" 200 s back when the span is 2*1400 + 10800 ticks = 226.6 s,
                   so the round the test is named after was never built.

## The network id no longer commits to the rules being played (2026-09-21, listed - a rule call)

Found closing out the winnings letter, running the whole board rather than only the suites I had touched:

    protocol/genesis.test.js  game config hash matches the committed id
      computed b0f1c33846f1383f2146a73411075ddbecc702e14fec1a3168c56f59080f2978
      pinned   04580b8f154d9330f27b151a7832e938b739ba5583c7ef5a7281f67650bb1341
    protocol/genesis.test.js  regtest and testnet4 network ids match the committed ids

`encodeGameConfig()` writes BLOCK_TICKS into the bytes the genesis config hash is taken over, and the
network id is taken over that. The ids in genesis-ids.js were pinned at 94d9b1c5; c01cc655 - "a round is
three minutes, and the constant is the default a contract overrides" - moved BLOCK_TICKS from 9000 to
10800 afterwards, and nothing re-pinned them. So every node agrees, every round opens, and the Daily has
been holding real stakes under an id that does NOT describe the rules those rounds are played by.

It is the same root cause as the blockTicks fixture family and it is NOT this letter's to take. Re-pinning
changes the network's identity: every contract, bond and donation set already signed under the old id
stops matching, and whether regtest and testnet4 take that now or carry the drift until M4's external
review is a rule question. Listed, not rewritten.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT, when it is somebody's letter: re-pin GENESIS_CONFIG_HASH and both NETWORK_IDs from
`computeGenesisConfigHash()`, then measure that the Daily still opens a paying round, that a bond rebuilt
from the published body and genesis alone still verifies (94d9b1c5's test), and that a contract signed

## Guardian pay, guardian slash, and leaving with notice - close-out check (2026-09-21, 961adcef)

Spec-only: `FEDERATION.md` +15, `multiplayer_p2p.md` +78, no `.js`, no `.mjs`, no `.cs` in
`47cc55f3..961adcef`. Checked against the four ruled points, in the text, on this checkout.

POINT 1 - THE GUARDIAN SHARE OF THE 2%, THREE EQUAL POTS. §22A now reads:

    node_fee = 2.00% of gross_round_volume
    2/3 %   -> GAME/VERIFY pool     (the round's sitting seats)
    2/3 %   -> SETTLEMENT pool      (the round's sitting seats)
    2/3 %   -> GUARDIAN pool        (the seated guardians of the federation
                                     the Round Contract names, §23A) v4.6.4

The 2% total is unchanged. The guardian pool is divided evenly among the guardians SEATED at the round's
FINAL, paid as one payout contract per guardian in the round's settlement transaction to the
`payout_pubkey` of his census advertisement; a gone guardian's share goes pro rata to the seated ones. In
a 7-guardian federation that is `(2/3)% / 7 ~= 0.0952%` of gross volume for the role; in a 2-of-2,
`(2/3)% / 2`.

POINT 2 - THE SLASH, 75/25, WITH THE WITNESSES OUT.

    75%  evenly to every active census node at the slashing transaction's height: bonded and
         eligible (§5A.3), minus the slashed node, and minus every guardian of the federation concerned
    25%  to the donation set of §22A - the developers - by share_bps

Paid as outputs of the slashing transaction itself (§5A.3B), one per recipient, remainders in ascending
`H(txid || node_pubkey)`, so every observer computes the same list from chain state at that height. The
reason the witnesses are excluded is written with it: the abandonment proof is signed by `2f + 1`
guardians of that very federation, and people who attest an absence must not earn from attesting it.

POINT 3 - LEAVING WITH NOTICE KEEPS THE BOND. The departure row now ends "his seat is gone with no offence
and **his bond is untouched**: he stays a bonded census node, keeps sitting as a seat, and may be drawn as
a guardian again". Only the abandonment row slashes - and it still catches "a departure that stops serving
before its `leave_after`", so the notice is a promise, not a formality.

POINT 4 - §5A.3 UNCHANGED. Proven by byte comparison across the commit, not by reading:

    "Slashed bonds are distributed: half to the affected players of that round,
     half burned or to the remaining honest committee members of the round, as
     fixed by the Round Contract."

A round committee has a known victim set and a guardian federation does not; the 75/25 rule is the
guardian-bond rule only and does not reach §5A.3.

## Gate 4 on testnet4: the bond cannot be relayed, and the wallet is locked (2026-09-21, 5ce1934b)

Ruled: the Daily plays for real testnet4 sats, no hybrid, the launcher waits for six real confirmations
instead of `rt.mine(6)`, stake 17701 sat. Two blockers were measured before a sat moved, and neither is
the mining change.

BLOCKER A - THE BOND TRANSACTION IS NON-STANDARD, BY DESIGN, AND SO CANNOT REACH A TESTNET4 BLOCK.

§5A.2 requires the signed advertisement to travel in the bond spend's witness, and `regtest-bond.mjs`
puts it there as a tapscript witness stack item:

    witnesses: [scriptPathWitness({ stack: [schnorr.sign(sighash, carrierSecret), body], ... })]

Measured, with no wallet and nothing spent:

    signed advertisement body, as it goes in the witness stack: 266 bytes
    Bitcoin Core tapscript policy limit per stack item:          80 bytes
    -> NON-STANDARD by 186 bytes

That is exactly what the helper's own comment records - "consensus allows and mempool policy does not
('bad-witness-nonstandard'), so `generateblock` is what measures consensus without asking the mempool".
On regtest `generateblock` puts the transaction straight into a block. testnet4 has no such door: the
transaction has to relay, our node runs standard policy (no `acceptnonstdtxn` in `/mnt/bitcoin/tn4/
bitcoin.conf`), and the blocks are mined by other people at 635 Ph/s who will never see a transaction
their own mempools rejected.

So there is no census bond on testnet4 with the bond format as specified, and with no census there is no
beacon and no round. This is a §5A.2 question - where the advertisement body travels - not a launcher one.

BLOCKER B - THE tn4 WALLET IS ENCRYPTED.

    bitcoin-cli -datadir=/mnt/bitcoin/tn4 sendtoaddress ...
    -> error code -13: "Please enter the wallet passphrase with walletpassphrase first."

Wallet `testnet`, trusted balance 682182 sat, chain testnet4 at 153367, not in IBD. Nothing can be funded
or posted without that passphrase. I did not go looking for it.

WHAT IS MERELY WORK, ONCE A AND B ARE ANSWERED:
  - `fund(spk, '1.0')` funds each bond with 1 BTC and `bondSats` defaults to 50000000 (0.5 BTC). We hold
    682182 sat. The protocol minimum is `bondMinSats` 50000 sat, so both numbers come down.
  - `fund()` calls `mine(1)` to confirm and the census path calls `rt.mine(6)` to bury. Both become waits:
    at the measured 723.3 s a block, six confirmations is about 72 minutes per launcher start.

## The advertisement witness, field by field, and why no field cut reaches 80 (2026-09-21)

`node packages/protocol/tools/advert-layout.mjs` - measured by encoding the prefix 1..n and diffing, not
by reading the struct:

    field                             bytes  running  on-chain?
    type (u8)                            1        1   needed
    protocol version (u16)               2        3   needed
    nodePubkey (32)                     32       35   needed    5A.1: who the bond gives standing to
    operatorId (str)                     6       41   no        5A.13: self-declared, never proof
    protocolVersions (vec u16)           4       45   no        negotiation, not consensus
    roles (vec u8)                       5       50   needed    opt-in: drawn only for what it declared
    endpoint (str)                      22       72   needed    25.1: fixed for the life of the bond
    region (str)                         9       81   no        description
    capacityClass (u8)                   1       82   no        description
    softwareHash (32)                   32      114   no        description; nothing on chain checks it
    settlementCapabilities (u32)         4      118   no        description
    lightningCapabilities (u32)          4      122   no        description
    bondTxid (32)                       32      154   needed    5A.1 MANDATORY
    bondVout (u32)                       4      158   needed    5A.1 MANDATORY
    bondScriptTemplateVersion (u16)      2      160   needed    5A.1 MANDATORY
    payoutPubkey (32)                   32      192   needed    22A: where this node is paid
    guardianOf (vec)                     2      194   needed    23.6 P3
    timestamp (u64)                      8      202   needed    ordering and freshness

    body                                202
      needed on chain                   142
      description                        60
    + BIP-340 signature                  64
    = one witness stack item            266      policy refuses over 80

SO THE ANSWER TO "WHAT CAN LEAVE" IS: 60 of the 266 bytes are description - operatorId, protocolVersions,
region, capacityClass, softwareHash and the two capability words - and dropping every one of them lands at
206, which is still two and a half times the limit. **The signature alone is 64 of the 80.** No cut to the
advertisement's fields can make one stack item standard, and that is arithmetic, not judgement.

WHAT ACTUALLY CUTS IT. The limit is per STACK ITEM, not per witness, so the body travels as several items
of at most 80 bytes with one `OP_DROP` each in the carrier script - 266 bytes is four items. §5A.2's
property is untouched: the whole signed body is still on the chain, still needs nobody to serve it, and
still binds to the bond it rides in. The alternative - drop the body and lean on the 32-byte `advertId`
the bond already carries in its OP_RETURN - would make the census depend on somebody serving the body off
chain, which is the thing 5A.2 exists to avoid.

## The census bond is standard now: 266 bytes in one item became four of at most 80 (2026-09-21)

Measured on the live regtest node, which runs the same standardness policy as testnet4 and mainnet - no
`acceptnonstdtxn` in `/mnt/bitcoin/blwp-2of2/btc/bitcoin.conf` and none on its command line.

BEFORE (d14fbec7's construction):

    prevout scriptPubKey type : witness_v1_taproot        <- P2TR, not P2WSH
    witness item 0:   64 bytes                            signature
    witness item 1:  266 bytes   <- over 80               the signed advertisement
    witness item 2:   35 bytes                            script
    witness item 3:   33 bytes                            control block
    vsize 313 vB, weight 1251 WU, 1 in / 4 out, 1 commitment
    testmempoolaccept allowed=false   reject-reason: bad-witness-nonstandard

That settles the P2WSH question the ruling raised: the spend is TAPROOT, and Bitcoin Core applies its
80-byte limit to a tapscript witness stack item exactly as it does to a P2WSH one. The 266-byte body was
the whole of the refusal.

AFTER (the body in pieces, one `OP_DROP` each, signature still its own item):

    witness item 0:   64 bytes                            signature
    witness item 1:   80 bytes                            body 1/4
    witness item 2:   80 bytes                            body 2/4
    witness item 3:   80 bytes                            body 3/4
    witness item 4:   26 bytes                            body 4/4
    witness item 5:   38 bytes                            script (three more OP_DROPs)
    witness item 6:   33 bytes                            control block
    items 7, largest 80
    vsize 314 vB, weight 1255 WU
    testmempoolaccept allowed=true    reject-reason: (none)
    census can still read the advertisement back: yes, endpoint ws://127.0.0.1:18080

One vbyte more, and the refusal is gone. NOT ONE ADVERTISEMENT FIELD WAS CUT - the body is the same 266
bytes it was, and the signature was never packed in with it.

The reader joins consecutive items (`witnessRunsOf`), singles first so every bond posted before this
resolves unchanged and at the same cost, and a run is believed only when its `advertId` equals a 32-byte
commitment in the transaction's own outputs - so joining bytes that were never one body cannot invent an
advertisement.

SUITES: protocol census-scan + census-resolve + census-minimum + census-root + census-template 51/51;
protocol tx + chain + bond-recognition + bond-script + bond-spend 47/47; protocol advert-witness 3/3 (new);
blwp-node census-chainview + census-derive + census-realblocks + bond-key + bond-spend 45/45.

STILL OPEN, AND IT IS NOT POLICY: the bond cannot be broadcast on testnet4 because that wallet is
encrypted - `sendtoaddress` answers error -13, "Please enter the wallet passphrase with walletpassphrase

## rt.mine(6) becomes rt.bury(6): mine our own chain, wait for anybody else's (2026-09-21)

The round's beacon is the first block after `committee_time`, so an operator who can make blocks on the
round's own chain can make the beacon he wants. On a free regtest round that is nobody's money; on a round
holding real sats it is the whole game. `regtest-bond.mjs` grew `bury(n)`:

    minable = network === 'regtest'
    bury(6)  -> mine(6) on regtest, as before
             -> waitForHeight(height() + 6) on any other chain, saying so every two minutes
    fund()   -> mine(1) on regtest; waitConfirmed(txid) elsewhere

Both waits BLOCK, like everything else in that file - a launcher standing a round up has nothing to do
until its bonds are buried, and making them async would turn every caller inside out.

Measured on the live regtest, so the Daily pays nothing for the change:

    minable: true
    bury(6): 104163 -> 104169 (+6) in 1467 ms
    bond after it: 7 items, largest 80 bytes, testmempoolaccept allowed=true

At testnet4's measured 723.3 s a block, six confirmations is about 72 minutes per launcher start.

census-realblocks + census-chainview + bond-key + roster 46/46.

## The halt case: note holders first, and only then anybody else (2026-09-21)

CORRECTED SAME DAY. I first wrote the halt remainder as BURNED with census nodes and developers at 0%,
on the 17:xx instruction "census nodes and devs get 0% on a halt". `bc05268f` is the accepted law for
this letter and says the remainder goes 75/25 after the claim window, and the ruling that named it
restated that. My v4.6.5 burn was layered on top of bc05268f's 75/25 and left the revision banner saying
both in one sentence. Reverted: the spec, the module and the tests all say 75/25 of the REMAINDER now.

What is load-bearing and what the tests hold is the ORDER, not the recipients: a halted federation is
liquidated note by note BEFORE a node or a developer sees a sat, so the people who run the network are
paid only out of what no player claimed - never out of what a player could still have claimed. A short
escrow goes entirely to the notes, pro rata, and pays nobody else at all.

## (superseded heading kept for the log) The halt case, first attempt (2026-09-21, spec v4.6.5)

§23A.3 already carried the cap as `(f + 1) x the smallest seated bond` and §23A.5 already paid unspent
notes at face value first, with the halt proof already falling back to whoever is left plus the observable
halt. One thing was still wrong and it is the money rule: the remainder after the claim window went
**75% to the census nodes and 25% to the developers**. On a halt it now goes nowhere - it is burned.

    running federation, bond slashed   75% census nodes / 25% developers    (unchanged)
    HALTED federation, liquidation     notes at face value, then BURNED
                                       census nodes 0%, developers 0%

The operator must not profit from a technical freeze. Burning is the only recipient that cannot be gamed:
paying the remaining guardians would pay the witnesses of the very abandonment, and paying the census
would make a freeze worth something to somebody who runs the network.

AND THE RULE IS NOW CODE, not only a paragraph: `packages/protocol/src/federation-slash.js` -
`exposureCap`, `reserveFits`, `slashSplit`, `abandonmentProofNeeds`. Each of the three ways this gets got
wrong turns the suite red, proven by breaking the module and running it:

    cap summed over all ten bonds again      -> 4 pass, 3 fail
    halt paying 75/25 to nodes and devs      -> 6 pass, 1 fail
    halt proof demanding 2f + 1 again        -> 6 pass, 1 fail
    restored                                 -> 7 pass, 0 fail

CAP, MEASURED. Ten guardians at 7 of 10 (`f = 3`), nine bonds of 1 000 000 sat and one of 400 000:

    sum of all ten bonds (the wrong rule)    9 400 000 sat
    (f + 1) x smallest  (the rule)           1 600 000 sat
    the sum is 5.875x the cover that exists if the cheapest four walk out

    testnet 2 of 2, f = 0                    cap = one bond = 50 000 sat
                                             one leaver halts it, his one bond pays every note

A reserve of 9 000 000 sat - which the summing rule would have allowed - is refused, and so is one msat
over 1 600 000.

SUITES: protocol federation-slash 7/7 (new), with genesis + advert-witness + census-resolve 28/28.

## The three halt rules, as code that goes red (2026-09-21, corrected to bc05268f)

`packages/protocol/src/federation-slash.js` - `exposureCap`, `reserveFits`, `slashSplit`,
`abandonmentProofNeeds`. Each way this gets got wrong turns the suite red, proven by putting the old rule
back and running it:

    cap summed over all ten bonds again              -> 4 pass, 3 fail
    nodes paid off the whole bond, notes not first   -> 5 pass, 2 fail
    halt proof demanding 2f + 1 again                -> 6 pass, 1 fail
    restored                                         -> 7 pass, 0 fail

CAP, MEASURED. Ten guardians at 7 of 10 (`f = 3`), nine bonds of 1 000 000 sat and one of 400 000:

    sum of all ten bonds (the wrong rule)    9 400 000 sat
    (f + 1) x smallest  (the rule)           1 600 000 sat   - the sum is 5.875x the real cover
    testnet 2 of 2, f = 0                    cap = one bond = 50 000 sat, one leaver halts it

A reserve of 9 000 000 sat - which the summing rule would have allowed - is refused, and so is one msat
over 1 600 000.

STILL ONLY PROSE, and named rather than assumed: the claim window, the spent-note list, the client
presenting its own unused notes, and the escrow output under the arbitration k-of-m keys. `slashSplit`
computes the split a liquidation would pay; nothing yet opens a window, publishes a list, accepts a claim
or builds that output. No node path pays anything on a halt today because no node path implements a
halt at all - §23A is law with one module under it, not a running system.

## The halt remainder, settled: split, never burned (2026-09-21, HEAD 5578d27f is the law)

I flipped this twice and the ruling settled it: **do not invent a burn of player money.** The law is
5578d27f's - a halt pays every unspent note at face value first, and only the UNCLAIMED remainder is
split 75/25. The burn I wrote at 796cf8d5 was the invention; my 5578d27f revert was right and stands.

What my revert left behind was a broken sentence, because it collided with cd73dc1b's late-claim text:

    then the remainder is
    goes 75% to the nodes and 25% to the developers as above

Repaired, and the late-claim tail is now written where it belongs: a note shown late is still paid from
what is left until two weeks after the halt - the player who was offline for a weekend is not the one the
deadline is for - and only the remainder after THAT is split. "No player's money is ever burned: what is
unclaimed after two weeks is paid out, not destroyed."

AND THE CLOCKS ARE CODE NOW, not a table to remember. `MAINNET_CLOCKS`, `liquidationSchedule`,
`remainderMaySplit`:

    abandon_blocks     288    48 h
    departure_notice   432    72 h
    founding_window    432    72 h
    drain_blocks      2016    14 d   - the drain AND the late-claim tail
    claim_blocks       216    36 h   - the arbitration claim window

The trap this holds shut: the claim window closing is NOT when the nodes get paid. Proven by making the
remainder splittable at `claim_blocks` instead of `drain_blocks` - 8 pass, 1 fail; restored, 9 pass.

SUITES: protocol federation-slash 9/9.

## BURN cannot be minted any more, and the drain tail is four weeks (2026-09-21)

The spec withdrew `slashRemainder: BURN`; the tree still defaulted to it everywhere, and a default that
contradicts the money law gets copied.

BEFORE                                                    AFTER
    SLASH_REMAINDERS = ['BURN', 'COMMITTEE']              ['SPLIT']
    slashRemainder: 'BURN' in tools                 15    0
    slashRemainder: 'BURN' in test fixtures         97    0
    contract-chosen burn branch in slash.js          1    0
    slashRemainderByte('BURN')                  byte 0    refused: "BURN is not one of SPLIT"
    slashRemainderByte('SPLIT')                      -    byte 0

The one `slashRemainder: 'BURN'` left in the tree is the test that asserts the encoder REFUSES it.

`SPLIT` takes byte 0, which `BURN` used to hold, so a contract stored before this reads as SPLIT rather
than as a burn - the safe direction: the money it describes is paid out instead of destroyed. Byte 1, the
old `COMMITTEE`, no longer decodes at all.

In `slash.js` the line that asked the contract where the remainder went is gone: `hand(honestCommittee,
rest, out)` runs unconditionally, so no round can be written that burns its own remainder.

AND THE CLOCKS FOLLOWED HEAD: `drain_blocks` is 4032 (four weeks), not 2016. `MAINNET_CLOCKS` and the
late-claim tail test moved with it.

SUITES: protocol slash-distribution + protocol 40/40; protocol federation-slash + genesis +
advert-witness + census-resolve 30/30; blwp-node custody + round + winnings-door 56/56; blwp-node server +
entry-fee-door with blwp-client page-stake + session-pay 28/28.

STILL BURNING, AND NAMED RATHER THAN QUIETLY FIXED: two burns in `slash.js` are structural, not chosen by
a contract - `hand()` burns when there is nobody at all to pay, and an excluded member's share is burned
rather than spread over the rest (spreading it would pay the honest MORE the more colleagues were
slashed). The spec's new sentence is absolute - "every remainder in this document has a recipient" - so
these two need a recipient naming, and that is a rule call, not a default to flip.

## The federation clocks, all three networks, and what a testnet day actually buys (2026-09-21)

The spec pins three networks at §27A.6; `federation-slash.js` carried only mainnet, so the code could not
have run a testnet federation at all. All three are in it now, and `clocksFor` refuses a network nobody
pinned rather than guessing one.

    parameter           mainnet            testnet            regtest
    abandon_blocks          288 (48 h)          12 (2 h)           10
    departure_notice        432 (72 h)          18 (3 h)           10
    founding_window         432 (72 h)          18 (3 h)           10
    drain_blocks           4032 (28 d)         144 (24 h)         100
    claim_blocks            216 (36 h)           9 (1.5 h)         10

Testnet is 24x / 24x / 24x / 28x / 24x of mainnet - "about a twentieth", and the test holds it between
20x and 28x so a clock cannot drift out of the family unnoticed.

AND THE ONE-DAY CYCLE, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. At ten minutes a block, which is what pinning 12
blocks to 2 h assumes:

    abandonment + founding + drain, one after the other   174 blocks   29 h
    with the founding started at the departure (§23A.5)   156 blocks   26 h
    the drain by itself                                   144 blocks   24 h

So the DRAIN is the day; the cycle around it is not. A guardian who simply vanishes costs 29 h from his
last session to the successor's CLOSED, and 26 h if he gave notice and the succession started at his
departure. Naming it here because the letter was described as a one-day cycle and it is a 26-to-29-hour
one - whether that matters is a ruling, not a number.

## The network id did not commit to the federation clocks (2026-09-21)

Asked of the code, closing out the clocks letter: does anything CALL the clocks, and does the network's
own identity cover them?

    callers of federation-slash.js outside its own test   0
    federation parameters in encodeGenesisParameters      0 of 6

`encodeGenesisParameters` hashed eight fields - chain, the two slot/threshold pairs, censusMinNodes,
censusConfirmations, bondMaturity - and §27A.6 lists six more that it did not: `federation_nominal`,
`abandon_blocks`, `departure_notice`, `founding_window`, `drain_blocks`, `claim_blocks`. That block is
committed in `network_id`, so the id did not commit to them.

What that meant concretely: two networks could share a `network_id` while one drains a federation in 24 h
and the other in 28 d, and a contract naming that id would not say how long its holder's money can be
frozen or how long he has to claim it. Same class as the BLOCK_TICKS gap fixed earlier today at
`9a78ecf1`, on the other half of the genesis.

Fixed: the six are hashed, `testnetShape` carries them, and `genesisFor` gives testnet 2/12/18/18/144/9
and regtest 4/10/10/10/100/10 - they differ per network and used to share one shape. Both ids moved:

    testnet4   e9171215... -> 9715f0c6...
    regtest    06ad7746... -> 66f5caba...

The blast radius was the same one and was handled the same way: both test donation sets carry the network
id in their signed bodies, so they were re-signed by the same two authority keys. No recipient, share or
endpoint moved, and the published vectors are byte-identical - regenerating them changed nothing.

WHERE THE FLAG LIVES, and why it is not a hole: the player's own browser. Clearing it only makes him type

## The verified flag was not bound to the seed it verified (2026-09-21, found by the checklist)

`70c2dd11` shipped an hour old and had a hole the ruling's own checklist named - "notice gone after
refresh". Measured:

    tabSeed({ storage: window.sessionStorage })   mints a FRESH 32 bytes when it finds none
    sessionStorage                                per tab, dies with the tab
    blwp.backup.verified                          localStorage, outlives every tab, bound to nothing

So: verify the phrase in one tab, open a second, and `tabSeed` mints a wallet nobody has ever written
down - while the flag still said verified. `mayDeposit` and `mayPayStake` would both have opened for it.
The gate was answering about a wallet that no longer existed.

FIXED: the flag records `sha256(seed)`, and the gate opens only when the seed in hand hashes to it. A new
seed is unverified however many older ones were not. Proven by restoring the old behaviour - flag present
rather than matching - which fails 1 of 10; bound, 10 of 10.

    verified seed          mayDeposit true
    a different seed       mayDeposit FALSE, mayPayStake FALSE, lobby line back
    a different seed, free mayJoin({paying:false}) still true
    no seed at all         unverified; digestOf(undefined) null, digestOf(8 bytes) null

## The seed is 24 real BIP-39 words now (2026-09-21)

TAKEN, NOT TYPED. The list is bitcoin/bips `bip-0039/english.txt`, copied out of Trezor's
`python-mnemonic` at /usr/local/lib/python3.10/dist-packages/mnemonic/wordlist/english.txt and checked
against a second independent copy - @scure/bip39's `english.js` via ethereum-cryptography. The two agree
word for word:

    sha256 of the newline-separated list   2f5eed53a4727b4bf8880d8f3f199efc90e58503646d9ff8eff3a2ed3b24dbda
    2048 words, "abandon" first, "zoo" last, no duplicates

`bip39-wordlist.js` is generated from that file and the test recomputes the digest from the words
themselves on every run, so a hand edit shows up as a red rather than as a wallet that will not restore.

THE ENCODING IS BIP-39's, NOT OURS. The seed stays the 32 bytes `tabSeed` already mints - nothing was
re-minted. 256 bits of entropy plus an 8-bit checksum, 11 bits a word, is 24 words.

MEASURED:

    BIP-39's own published 256-bit vectors, both ways     4 of 4
      0000...0000 -> "abandon x23 art"
      7f7f...7f7f -> "legal winner thank year ... worth title"
      8080...8080 -> "letter advice cage absurd ... acoustic bless"
      ffff...ffff -> "zoo x23 vote"
    200 arbitrary seeds -> 24 words -> the same 32 bytes  200 of 200
    last word changed (the checksum's own word)           refused, no bytes handed back
    a word outside the list                               refused, names word 5
    twelve words where 24 are wanted                      refused
    a 16-byte seed                                        refused rather than padded

The checksum is why the last word matters: without it a mistyped word gives a different VALID seed and
the player restores an empty wallet with no error anywhere.

SUITES: blwp-client bip39 6/6, backup-gate 10/10 (unchanged by this).

## Step 1's blocker, with numbers: a 4-guardian federation cannot be bonded by a 2-node harness (2026-09-21)

The federation stands up. `FEDERATION_READY`, and the node's own port reads it:

    federation_id  423e010e320b0200d3a72e3fa0a6798263a43f768b50e22aee1d128ade12e563
    guardians      4        threshold  3
    keys           03222650..., 02ca5f41..., 032b495e..., 0218aa3d...
    gateway        http://127.0.0.1:30170, joined, pegged in, vetted
    invite         fed11qgqpw9thwvaz7te3xgmjuvpwxqhrzw3nxqcnyvf0qqqjqs37...

And the bond can now name a guardian (`d353ba08`). What it cannot do is reach the count:

    federationIsBonded wants   threshold = 3 DISTINCT bonded census nodes, each advertising a
                               guardian key of that federation (`nodesTaken` is a Set, one key per node)
    the harness has            2 census nodes - it is the Daily's 2-of-2
    2 < 3                      so the gate cannot be satisfied, however the adverts are filled

The guardian count is not a knob: `federation-hold-probe.sh` line 146 is `for g in 0 1 2 3`, hard-coded
four, threshold three - the rehearsal's shape, not the one the 17:08 HARD names.

THE HARD NAMES THE OTHER SHAPE: "testnet on the 2-of-2 that runs, seated by its two bonded operators",
