## The paying round opens on three operators and cannot settle: there is no threshold for 3 (2026-09-21)

Driving the opened round on to a settlement (w5b's own money stack, extended to take the chain and the
third node) got as far as the claim key and stopped there. Measured, not reasoned:

    reachesLightning per daemon   [null, null, null]
      createHeld sits behind custody's `reaches`; with no Lightning port a daemon answers
      "this node reaches no Lightning, so it holds no stakes" and CANNOT call it. No hold invoice is
      on this path, and that is the shipping default rather than a stub.

    claim key, three nodes, 240 s   409 / 409 / 409, the whole time
      "this signer node holds no claim key for that round yet" - assigned, but never dealt a key.

    receiptsNeeded(2) -> 2     receiptsNeeded(7) -> 5
    receiptsNeeded(3) -> REFUSED: no committee threshold for 3 slots
    receiptsNeeded(4) -> REFUSED

`dkg.deal` asks `receiptsNeeded(signerNodes.length)` before it cuts a polynomial. For three it refuses, so
no contribution is ever dealt, no claim key is ever combined, no stake can be locked, and `makeClaimKey`
retries in the background until entry close WITHOUT LOGGING - which is why the first run looked like a
hang rather than a refusal.

THIS IS A LAW QUESTION AND IS LEFT ALONE. A committee threshold is a money rule: 2-of-2 and 5-of-7 are
written down, and what 3 signer nodes owe is not. I am not inventing `receiptsNeeded(3)`.

The collision, stated plainly:
  - §23.6 wants the federation's threshold in DISTINCT bonded census nodes. The smallest federation
    fedimintd 0.12.0 will build is 3-of-4, so that is THREE nodes.
  - the committee sizes the protocol defines are TWO and SEVEN.
  - a census of three with 2+2 slots assigns the union of the two committees, which is 2 only if
    sortition picks the same pair for both roles and 3 otherwise - so the committee size would be luck.

Two ways out, both Daniel's:
  (a) define the threshold for a 3-signer-node committee - 3-of-3 or 2-of-3 is a ruling, not a default;
  (b) stand SEVEN signer nodes: 5-of-7 is already written down, and three of the seven advertise the
      guardian keys. That is a defined shape end to end, and it is the mainnet shape §27A.6 names.

Meanwhile the harness no longer hangs on it: a round whose committee size has no threshold is refused
when it is stood up, by name - "3 signer nodes cannot hold a round's key: no committee threshold for 3
slots ... opens and can never settle, because its claim key is never dealt."

Also fixed on the way, both found by running it: `postRound` posted to A and B only, so the third daemon
answered "404 this node holds no such round" and was never in the round it was assigned to; and the
daemon variable `c` shadowed `postRound`'s contract parameter, which posted to `127.0.0.1:undefined`.

## The two structural burns in slash.js are gone: the remainder has a recipient (2026-09-22)

RULED ALREADY (Daniel 2026-09-21), so this is the work and not a question: "the recipient is the
federation pool, 75% to the nodes and 25% to the developers, never burned - the same rule as the round
slash remainder." §5A.3: "every remainder in this document has a recipient."

`slashDistribution` had three places that destroyed value, all inside one helper:

    a half with NOBODY AT ALL to pay          burned the whole amount
    the share of a member excluded as slashed  burned that share
    the leftover satoshis with nobody to take  burned the remainder

All three now add to `toPool`, and the function returns the pool's own split beside it - 75% nodes, 25%
developers, the same numbers `federation-slash.js` already applies to a slashed guardian bond. `burned`
is KEPT in the return and asserted `0n` everywhere rather than deleted: a field that quietly disappeared
would let a burn come back unnoticed.

SAFE TO CHANGE, checked first: `slashDistribution` has NO production callers - only its own test file.

    slash-distribution.test.js   BEFORE 4 pass / 4 fail   AFTER 8 pass / 0 fail

The four reds were one cause - the accounting helper summed `shares + burned`, and three assertions
pinned the burn itself. They are updated to the ruled behaviour, with the pool's split asserted exactly:

    nobody to pay at all      toPool 100000  ->  nodes 75000, developers 25000
    no affected players       toPool  50000  ->  nodes 37500, developers 12500
    one excluded member       toPool  25000
    an excluded leftover      toPool     75   (50 with no players to pay, 25 the excluded share)
    the clean case            toPool      0, burned 0

bond is neither created nor lost.

## The second half of a slashed bond goes to the census minus the seats (2026-09-22)

§5A.3, spec line 811: "half to the affected players of that round; the other half 75% evenly to the
active census nodes at the slashing height MINUS THE ROUND'S OWN SEATS (the witnesses) and 25% to the
donation set of §22A - the developers."

`slashDistribution` paid that half to `honestCommittee` - the round's own seats - which is the exact set
the sentence subtracts. The burn work before this fixed where the LEFTOVERS went and left the main
recipient as the withdrawn rule.

    BEFORE, clean 100000 sat bond   toPlayers 50000 | seats 25000 each | census 0 | developers 0
    AFTER                           toPlayers 50000 | seats 0 | nodes 37500 | developers 12500

STEP 1, THE PRECONDITION, CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: a slash SPENDS the bond output, and
`deriveCensus` filters spent bonds (`census.js:224`, `.filter((e) => !e.spent)`). So the active census at
the slashing height already omits a node slashed at that height, and no second exclusion is added. A
caller that hands one in anyway is REFUSED by name - "a node slashed at this height is still inside the
active census ... this is not silently dropped" - because a census counting a spent bond is wrong and
quietly patching it would hide that.

STEP 3, THE THREE CLOSING MEASUREMENTS:

    clean 100000    toPlayers 50000, seats 0/0, toNodes 37500, developers 12500, each other 12500,
                    burned 0, total 100000
    uneven 100001   toPlayers 50000, toNodes 37500, developers 12501, each other 12500, total 100001
                    - the odd satoshi lands on the donation set because toNodes floors first
    uneven 206      toNodes 77 over three nodes -> 25, 26, 26; the two leftovers are handed out in
                    ascending H(roundId || pubkey), never dropped; total 206
    empty eligible  THROWS and names the sats: "37500 sat of a slashed bond have no recipient: the
                    active census at the slashing height is empty once the round's 2 seat(s) are taken
                    out, and §5A.3 names nobody else - not the seats, not a burn, not the donation set"

The sum guard now covers all three destinations: `paid + toDevelopers + toPool !== bondSats` throws.

STEP 4, ONE SPLIT FOR BOTH PATHS: `splitNodesDevelopers` in `constants.js`, floor the nodes and give the
rest to the developers so the two always add back exactly. `slash.js` and `federation-slash.js` both call
it; the arithmetic is no longer written twice.

STEP 5, COMMENTS THAT NAMED A RECIPIENT THE CODE DOES NOT PAY: the file header and the doc block of
`slash.js`, its excluded-shares line ("the excluded shares are burned instead"), the quotations in
`constants.js` and `contracts.js`, and `federation-slash.js`'s "burns the rest" - which was false against
its own line 72, where the code splits and returns `burned: 0n`. A grep for "half burned" or "remaining
honest committee" in `protocol/src` now returns only the one line that says what the rule is NOT.

STEP 6, SUITES, BEFORE AND AFTER:

    slash-distribution.test.js   8 pass / 0 fail (old rule)  ->  9 pass / 0 fail (spec numbers)
    federation-slash.test.js     12 pass / 0 fail            ->  12 pass / 0 fail
    protocol, chunk 1 of 2       292 pass / 0 fail           ->  292 pass / 0 fail
    protocol, chunk 2 of 2       283 pass / 0 fail           ->  296 pass / 0 fail (the rewritten suite)
    blwp-node, files 1-20        125 pass / 0 fail           ->  125 pass / 0 fail

Nothing was loosened. The suite was rewritten because its premise - that the committee is paid - is the
withdrawn rule; every assertion in it is stricter than before, including the sum, the seats at zero, the

## The gap between a filed slash and a paid one, both paths (2026-09-22)

Measured by reading the code, not by running a probe: no probe can be written yet, because the first
function on the paying side has no caller to drive.

WHAT A NODE ALREADY HAS, and `slash-filing.test.js` (3 pass / 0 fail) proves it files:

    the slash proof, decoded    roundId, playerPubkey, nodePubkey, transcriptHash, signedResultId,
                                bondTxid, bondVout                        (slash.js decodeSlashProof)
    what `slashHolds` returns   { slashed: true, offence: REPLAY_CONTRADICTS,
                                  bond: { txid, vout }, commitment }
    where it is kept            `round.putSlashProof(roundId, entryId, nodePubkey, proofId, record)`,
                                read back by `round.slashProofs(...)`, served at GET /slash-proofs
    the round contract          `nodes` - the round's own seats, which §5A.3 subtracts - and bondMinSats
    a census from the chain     derived at `contract.censusHeight`; entries carry `bondSats`
                                (census.js:1038, `const bondSats = output.valueSats`), and
                                `deriveCensus` drops spent bonds (census.js:224)
    the arbitration set         `genesisFor(network).arbitrationKeys` / `arbitrationK`, already used to
                                build a bond's own output key

WHAT IS MISSING BEFORE ONE SAT MOVES:

    1. THE SLASHED BOND'S VALUE. The proof names the OUTPOINT, never the amount, and `bondSats` does
       not appear anywhere in `blwp-node/src`. `slashDistribution` takes it as an argument that nobody
       supplies. It is obtainable - the census entry for that outpoint carries it - but nothing reads it.
    2. THE CENSUS AT THE SLASHING HEIGHT. A node derives its census at the round's `census_height`. The
       rule pays "the active census nodes AT THE SLASHING HEIGHT". Nothing computes a slashing height at
       all: grep `slashingHeight|slashedAt|slashing height` over protocol/src and blwp-node/src returns
       only comments quoting the spec. The set that must be paid is derived nowhere.
    3. WHO THE AFFECTED PLAYERS ARE. `affectedPlayers` exists only as a parameter of
       `slashDistribution` and in its tests. No function decides which players of a round were harmed.
    4. A CALLER. Neither `slashDistribution` (round bond) nor `slashSplit` (guardian bond) is called
       outside its own test file - the same gap on both paths, which is what step 2 asked.
    5. THE CLAIM WINDOW. `federation-slash.js` has `lifecycleBlocks` and `liquidationSchedule` as
       arithmetic; no node path opens a window, times one, or closes one.
    6. THE SPENT-NOTE LIST. Nothing publishes one, and `slashSplit`'s halted branch takes `notesOwedMsat`
       as a number nobody computes.
    7. THE ESCROW OUTPUT UNDER THE ARBITRATION KEYS. "escrow" appears in federation-slash.js only as
       prose. No builder exists, though `bondOutputKey`/`bondInternalKey` show the shape for a bond.
    8. MUSIG2. Referenced in four files (`bond-script.js` "key path MuSig2(node_key,
       arbitration_aggregate_key)", `slash.js` steps 3 and 5) and IMPLEMENTED IN NONE - a grep for an
       exported musig function over every src returns nothing.

WHICH NEED NEW KEY MATERIAL: only the spending side. 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 are arithmetic and bookkeeping
over things a node already holds - no key is created or used. 7 needs the arbitration aggregate key,
which exists as PUBLIC keys in genesis but has never been aggregated here. 8 needs MuSig2 signing by the
arbitration set, which is new protocol and new key handling, and is §5A.3B steps 3 and 5 - later, by the
ruling.

SO THE NEXT SLICE IS RECORDING ONLY, and the print says why that is possible: everything it needs -
bond value, a census, the seats, the proof - is already in the node, except the slashing height and the
affected-player rule, which are decisions rather than key material.

## Two readings before a recorder: both come back as conflicts, not readings (2026-09-22)

### 1. Slashing height - THE WORDS WITH NO FORMULA

The phrase occurs ONCE in the whole spec, at line 812:

    "Slashed bonds are distributed: half to the affected players of that round;
     the other half 75% evenly to the active census nodes AT THE SLASHING HEIGHT
     minus the round's own seats (the witnesses) and 25% to the donation set of
     §22A - the developers."

Nothing defines it. §5A.3B, "how a fraud proof becomes a slash", gives five steps and no height:

    1. Anyone publishes a fraud proof ...
    2. The proof is mechanically checkable ...
    3. k-of-m arbitration keys sign a slashing transaction spending path B.
    4. That transaction MUST carry OP_RETURN = H(fraud_proof) || retrieval hint.
    5. Outputs pay the distribution fixed by the Round Contract.

TWO CANDIDATES, and the first is circular with step 5:

    (a) the height of the block confirming the SLASHING TRANSACTION itself. It is the only event the
        phrase can naturally mean - the slash is that transaction. But step 5 says that transaction's
        OUTPUTS pay the census at that height, and the height is not known until it confirms. The
        outputs cannot be built from a number the building produces.
    (b) the height at which the BOND OUTPUT WAS SPENT, read off the chain. Derivable, and equal to (a)
        when the spend IS the slash - but §5A.3B also allows a node to spend its own bond (the spend
        objection), so this height exists for spends that are not slashes at all.

WHAT THE NODE ALREADY HAS: the proof carries roundId, playerPubkey, nodePubkey, transcriptHash,
signedResultId, bondTxid, bondVout - AND NO HEIGHT. The contract carries `censusHeight` and
`censusConfirmations`. The chain view can produce `spentAt` for any outpoint (census.js `chainFactsAt`),
which is candidate (b). `census_height` is NOT substituted here, silently or otherwise.

STOPPED. The text names neither, so the height is a ruling.

### 2. Affected players - THE SPEC NAMES A NARROWER SET

The working rule offered was "every player pubkey that locked a stake on that round". The spec's other
use of the phrase, at line 1796 (§13A, who may object), distinguishes them:

    "Who may object: anyone - THE AFFECTED PLAYER, ANOTHER PLAYER IN THE ROUND,
     a non-selected node, a spectator, a watchtower."

"the affected player" is listed BESIDE "another player in the round", so in this spec affected is not a
synonym for everyone who played. Line 811 says "the affected playerS of that round" - plural, of that
round - but under 1796's usage that is the harmed ones, not the entrants.

AND THE NODE ALREADY HOLDS A NARROWER ANSWER: every slash proof carries ONE `playerPubkey`
(`slash.js` decodeSlashProof), and proofs are stored per (round_id, ENTRY_ID, node_pubkey)
(`round.js putSlashProof`). So a filed slash already names whose entry was harmed.

STOPPED, as ruled: the text names a narrower set than the working rule, so which one is paid is a ruling.

### 9. A NINTH HOLE, AND IT CHANGES WHO GETS PAID

`slashDistribution` takes ONE `bondSats` and one set of affected players - one bond, one distribution.
But the store keys proofs per (round, entry, node), so ONE ROUND CAN CARRY SEVERAL SLASHED NODES AND
SEVERAL HARMED ENTRIES. Nothing says whether:

    - each slashed bond is distributed separately, each to the players ITS OWN proof names; or
    - the round's slashed bonds are pooled and split over all harmed players together.

The two pay different people different amounts whenever a round slashes more than one node, and the
old withdrawn comment in `slash.js` shows the case was already in mind ("two nodes caught in one round").
No spec sentence found for it.

## two-titles: the core never changed, the driver did (2026-09-22)

The surviving red was "a counter scoring 120 x 65536 where it expects 120 x 45875 - a core question".
It was not a core question.

`cores/counter.js` is a toy core that adds `w[0]` once per tick for 120 ticks, so its score IS 120
throttles. The expectation `120 * 45875` was seven tenths throttle - the fixed program the shared fixture
drove until 2026-09-21. That day `window-fixture.js` replaced it, and the comment there says why in its
own words: the old program "was written when the drop-off was close; the world has since grown east and
it never arrives ... it reaches x 145.9 m at its furthest and ends FAILED with score 2", and nineteen
tests across five suites read DELIVERED off it. The replacement steers at the gate the core publishes, in
the core's own units, and drives `words = [65536, steer, 0, 0, 0]` - FULL throttle.

So 65536 is the driver's number and 45875 is the old driver's. The core is untouched by either.

FIXED WITHOUT WRITING A NUMBER: the assertion now reads `120 * wordsAt(0)[0]`, taken from the driver the
test actually drives with. That is the principle the fixture states about itself - "it is not re-tuned by
hand ... the day the world moves again, this follows it" - applied to the one expectation that was left
behind when the driver moved.

    two-titles.test.js   1 pass / 1 fail  ->  2 pass / 0 fail

Both of this suite's reds turned out to be leftovers of a migration done elsewhere: the run length
(`blockTicks: 9000`, fixed earlier today) and now the driver's throttle.

## objection-window: the node settles on sha256(zeros), not on the entry's commitment (2026-09-22)

The last red without a cause. Run alone: 7 tests, 5 pass, 2 fail - "two signer nodes, a 3 s window" and
"two signer nodes restarted inside the objection window". Both fail the same way, and it is not a
timing flake: it is the same wrong hash twice.

    expected   [[ '5ae6e3e5...', '5e26936f...' ]]          one settle: the loser's stakeCommitment
                                                            and the loser's preimage
    actual     [[ '66687aad...', '0000...0' ],
                [ '66687aad...', ... ]]                     TWO settles, both on one hash, one with a
                                                            zero preimage

And that hash is not arbitrary:

    sha256(32 zero bytes) = 66687aadf862bd776c8fc18b8e9f8e20089714856ee233b3902a591d0d5f2925

So the node is settling a hold whose payment hash is the hash of a ZERO preimage, twice, where the test
expects one settle carrying the loser's own commitment and preimage. The entry's real
`stakeCommitment` (5ae6e3e5... in the first case, 827def45... in the second) never reaches the port.

WHAT THIS IS NOT: not contention - it fails identically run alone, and it failed identically at
`1e9628cd` before any of this letter's work, so it is not from anything done here. Not the run length -
`blwp-node` carries no `blockTicks: 9000` any more. Not a flake - `lock-settlement`'s flake moved between
tests and then passed; this one is the same two tests and the same two hashes every time.

WHERE IT SITS: this is the HOLD path - `custody.settle`, payment hashes and preimages - which is the
stack the sequence retires LAST, after the fleet pin moves off `595f0df3`, because the Daily still runs
on it. Fixing the preimage that reaches the port means touching custody on a live path, so it is listed
rather than taken.

    objection-window.test.js   5 pass / 2 fail, cause now known

## §0's 0.01 m step, measured before anything is changed (2026-09-22)

The board calls this "the one core remainder that is now free to run" - unparked because cover came back
to 91.7% against a 70 bar. Measured from the core's own constants, no probe needed:

    RIFLE_CRAWL          32768 Q16.16 = 0.5 m/s, at 60 Hz
    per axis, one tick   0.00833 m      under the 0.01 m bar
    EUCLIDEAN diagonal   0.01179 m      OVER the bar by 18%
    MANHATTAN (x + z)    0.01667 m      OVER the bar by 67%
    a crawl that fits 0.01 m Euclidean on a diagonal: 0.424 m/s, against 0.5 today

AND A DISCREPANCY NOBODY HAS NAMED: the ruling is "combined EUCLIDEAN, not per-axis", but the code
measures the step as MANHATTAN. Both places:

    core   tactics.js:637   "his OWN step this tick was over 0.01 m (x + z)"
    probe  measure-posture.mjs:102
           `Math.abs(s[b+U_X] - b4[0]) + Math.abs(s[b+U_Z] - b4[1])`

Manhattan is neither the per-axis reading that was rejected nor the Euclidean one that was ruled. It
happens to agree with Euclidean on the VERDICT here - a diagonal crawl is over the bar either way - but
it is 41% larger on a diagonal, so the two disagree about how far a man moved, and any threshold tuned
against one is wrong for the other.

WHY IT IS NOT STARTED: capping the crawl to fit 0.01 m Euclidean changes a gait in `army.js`, and a gait
change is a CORE change - it moves `CORE_HASH`, which moves the network id, which the page and the signer
nodes both carry. The fleet pin is already what blocks `bundle-fresh` and the hold path; landing a core
change before that pin moves widens the same gap rather than closing it. So this is measured and left.

THE START IT WANTS, smallest first: (1) make the step reading Euclidean in BOTH places, since the ruling
already says which one it is and the two currently disagree by 41%; (2) then, separately, decide whether
a diagonal crawl is slowed to 0.424 m/s or the movement is normalised so the combined step is the gait -
that is the part that moves the core and must travel with the pin.

## The candle bodies as flat slabs: the measurement, and why it is a trade-off (2026-09-22)

Listed as "Daniel's eye and not yet a measurement". Here is the measurement, off the core's constants:

    slot width (x)     5.18 m    CANDLE_SLOT, and CANDLE_BODY_HALF is half of it - bodies touch, no padding
    plateau height (y) 1.00 m    CANDLE_H, and its own comment records "(was 2)"
    ramp               4.00 m at 25%   CANDLE_RAMP, comment records "(was 5 m at 40%)"
    WIDTH : HEIGHT     5.2 : 1

A body 5.18 m across and 1 m tall is a low wide plateau. From above that is a slab, which is what was
seen. The eye was right and the number says so.

BUT THE FLATNESS IS A RULING, NOT A SLIP. `44c72d72` made it, under §4.15 as ruled 13:42-14:40:
"make it so trucks and tanks get through". That commit built the raised ribbon deliberately - "a full
slot, bodies touching, 1 m plateau, 4 m ramps at 25% on every free edge. No walls, no wick collider,
nothing in the solids" - and withdrew the berms with the rule written out: "passability: nothing added
over 1 m or 25%". It measured the result: "North-south drive at x 20: 97.7% of flat, 0 stops."

So the two readings collide:
    a chart standing on the ground   wants height against width
    "trucks and tanks get through"   caps height at 1 m and slope at 25%

RAISING THE PLATEAU IS THE ONE THING THAT CANNOT BE DONE without reopening the passability ruling: 2 m
back would double the very number that ruling fixed. The lever that does NOT touch it is the WIDTH -
the same 1 m reads 2.6 times taller beside a 2 m slot than beside a 5.18 m one. The field is
CANDLE_X0 -75.80 m to CANDLE_EAST 90.00 m, 165.80 m over 32 slots; at 2 m a slot that is 83 candles,
or 32 candles over 64 m with the rest of the field empty. Bodies touching is itself a ruling (492f128),
so narrowing means more candles rather than gaps.

NOT CHANGED. Both levers are core constants: either moves CORE_HASH and the network id, which must
travel with the fleet pin. And which lever to pull is a ruling, because one of them reopens passability
and the other changes how much of the field the chart occupies.

## What the network-id gap actually costs: donations, not rounds (2026-09-22)

The board treats the page/node id difference as "two different networks, so no round is joinable". The
live page disproves the conclusion - rounds list, join and drive. So what DOES it cost? Read off the
client, not argued:

    client.js:1460 and donation-pay.js:191 look keys up BY THE ROUND'S OWN id:
        donationKeysForNetworkId(round.networkId)
    it never compares the round's id against the page's compiled-in NETWORK_ID_REGTEST.

That is why listing and playing are unaffected. And the lookup itself:

    donationKeysForNetworkId(66f5caba...)   KNOWN     <- the page's own id
    donationKeysForNetworkId(b07c4a09...)   null      <- the id every LIVE round carries

So on the Daily that call returns null for every round, and `donation-pay.js:219` cannot compare a
donation set's networkId against an authority it has no keys for. THE COST OF THE GAP IS DONATION
VERIFICATION, not joinability.

This is worth having exactly because the board's version sent effort at the wrong thing: "no round is
joinable" invites moving the pin to make the lobby work, when the lobby already works and what is broken
is narrower and elsewhere. Not fixed here - the fix is still the pin or a rebuild, and both are ruled.

## Ruling 4 is blocked on an error of mine, and the error is in the ruling's reasoning

§4.16 says "the core owes no edge walls as solids ... the core's `mapSolids` is the list, box for box,
and it carries **no** wall". THE CORE CARRIES FOUR. Measured just now:

    cx -185.00 cz   0.00  hx   1.50  hz  88.00
    cx  185.00 cz   0.00  hx   1.50  hz  88.00
    cx    0.00 cz -85.00  hx 188.00  hz   1.50
    cx    0.00 cz  85.00  hx 188.00  hz   1.50

They are built at `map.js:95-98` by `edge(±halfX, 0, ...)` and `edge(0, ±halfZ, ...)` - at ±HALF_X and
±HALF_Z, the CURRENT boundary, not the ±130 Unity gathered. And the code says why they are there:

    "Tall and invisible, so a truck arriving airborne off a fee cliff still cannot clear the edge.
     Sunk six metres so a dip does not open a gap."

MY EARLIER REPORT SAID THE OPPOSITE - "nothing in the 106 spans a boundary at all" - and the ruling's
reasoning rests on it. That was a bad filter on my part; the walls were there the whole time, at the new
boundary. The ruling may well still be right (a wall on top of a clamp is a second boundary, and §1.1
makes the edge damage where the clamp is a stop) - but it was decided believing the core had none, and
removing them deletes a guard whose comment names a case the clamp may not cover: a body arriving
AIRBORNE, where a per-tick position clamp and a solid box are not the same thing.

NOT IMPLEMENTED, and the replay-solids edit I had started is reverted. This needs the ruling re-made
knowing the walls exist and what they were for.

## Ruling 5, the gait: the crawl is a speed along its direction (2026-09-22)

§4.16: "the crawl is 0.5 m/s along the direction of travel - the step vector is scaled so its length,
not its axes, is the speed". Implemented in `army.js` where the step is finalised: for a pinned man on
foot, if `length2(stepX, stepZ)` exceeds `RIFLE_CRAWL * dt` the vector is scaled to it. Not chosen, as
ruled: slowing diagonals to 0.424 m/s, which would make a man's speed depend on his heading.

## The recorder: a node can now say what a filed slash owes (2026-09-22)

The gap print listed eight things between a filed proof and a paid one. Three were rulings and are made;
this is the node path over the four that are arithmetic. `blwp-node/src/slash-owing.js`, tested by
`slash-owing.test.js`, 6 pass / 0 fail.

    bondSats 100000  ->  toPlayers 50000   toNodes 37500   toDevelopers 12500
    the players' half PRO RATA BY NET STAKE   alice 12500, bob 37500   (100000 : 300000)
    the seats take nothing                    seatA 0
    the three other census nodes take evenly  out1 12500
    censusSeen 5, seatsOut 2

WHAT IT PROVES BESIDES THE SPLIT:

  - THE ORDER IS THE RULING'S ORDER. A height outside the window is refused BEFORE any census is read -
    the test counts the reads and asserts zero. A height nobody can read yet must not send a node
    reading a census at it.
  - THE BOND NAMES AN OUTPOINT, NEVER A VALUE. `bondSatsOf` is the caller's, because the value is on the
    chain and not in the proof; a bond the chain does not hold owes nothing, by name.
  - EACH BOND PAYS ITS OWN PROOF'S PLAYERS. A replay proof names Alice alone and she takes the WHOLE
    50000 out of that bond; a table proof over the same bond names both and splits it. Nothing pooled.
  - AN EMPTY ELIGIBLE SET NAMES ITS SATOSHIS AND STOPS, inherited from `slashDistribution` rather than
    re-invented here.

AND IT SPENDS NOTHING, asserted rather than promised: the last test pins the owing's whole shape -
amounts and names, no transaction, no signature, no outpoint spent. §5A.3B steps 3 and 5 need MuSig2
over the arbitration keys, which exists nowhere in this tree, and an escrow output no builder exists for.
Those stay their own letter.

WHY A NODE SHOULD DO THIS BEFORE IT CAN PAY: every observer must recompute the same recipient list from
chain data at a height the transaction commits to. A node that files a proof and cannot say what it
implies has filed an assertion rather than an accusation - and the first time the numbers are worked out
should not be the first time money moves.

## The slashing door, and the two things it found (2026-09-22)

`GET /slash-owing?round=&entry=&height=` in `blwp-node/src/server.js`, beside `/slash-proofs`. It
answers what §5A.3 owes for every proof this node filed for a run, out of the census at a height the
CALLER names. Measured over the re-run fixture's five real filed proofs (`slash-filing.test.js`):

    no height           400  "a slash is owed at a height, and this node does not pick one"
    unknown entry       404  "this node filed no slash proof for that run"
    height, no chain    409  "this node has no chain view for that round, so it cannot say who is bonded"
    entriesForSlash       2  entries, both carrying a player pubkey
    one filed proof          players 50000, nodes 37500, developers 12500, bond 100000
                             census 10, seats 7, the three non-seats 12500 each, the seven seats 0

Suites: slash-owing 6/0, slash-filing 4/0, census-scan + assignment 4/0, committee-seed 7/0 = 21/0.

THE HEIGHT IS THE CALLER'S because §5A.3's recipients are "the active census nodes at the slashing
height" and the arbitration set names that height. A node that picked its own would pick the one that
paid it best, so the door refuses without one rather than defaulting to the round's.

FOUND 1 - A CENSUS AT A NAMED HEIGHT IS NOT THE ROUND'S CENSUS. The first `censusAtHeight` was one
line calling `censusFor` with the height swapped. `censusFor` ends by checking the derived root against
the contract's `censusRoot`, which is what makes a census THIS ROUND'S - and at any other height the
chain is SUPPOSED to give another root, because bonds funded since the round opened are in it and bonds
spent since are out. So every slashing height above `census_height` - which is every real one - came
back "that round names census root X and the chain gives Y at height H". The check now runs only when
the census is asked for as the round's own; the cache key carries which of the two it was, so a checked
census and an unchecked one can never be served for each other.

FOUND 2 - `entriesForSlash` READ A COLUMN THAT DOES NOT EXIST. `round.entriesOf` returns the DECODED
contract under `entry`; the recorder decoded `row.contract`, which is `undefined`, threw, and
`continue`d on the catch. Every round therefore looked like a round with no entries, `affectedEntries`
found nobody harmed, and the door would have answered that a slash owes the players nothing. A
`continue` on a decode failure is right for bytes off the wire and wrong for a field name. The suite
now pins the entry count at 2.

AND THE OFFENCE IS NOT IN THE PROOF'S BYTES. `encodeSlashProof` carries a transcript hash and a signed
result id and no offence field, because the offence is what verifying those two objects CONCLUDES.
Every proof in this table was filed by `fileSlashProofs`, which files exactly one kind, so the door
names REPLAY_CONTRADICTS and does not guess. A proof arriving by another road would have to carry its
own verdict.

## The slash-owing door's 200 path, and the two wrongs it was hiding (2026-09-22)

`ea8ca1e3` said the door was measured. What was measured was its refusals: the fixture it was written
against (`sevenSignerNodes`) has no chain view, so every height came back 409 and the JSON body never
ran. Re-measured against the mined census in `roster.test.js` - four bonded nodes, two of them the
round's own seats, one paying entry, one filed proof, bond value read off the real funding output:

    slashHeight 900005   tipHeight 900010   censusSeen 4   seatsOut 2
    bondSats    100000000
    toPlayers    50000000   -> 0505..05         50000000     (the one harmed player)
    toNodes      37500000   -> 6360e856..       37500000     (keyFor 0x12)
    toDevelopers 12500000

WRONG 1 - THE PLAYER WAS A NODE. Before the fix the `nodes` list carried `0505..05` at 50000000 sat
beside the players' list, so a 100000000 sat bond appeared to owe 150000000. `slashDistribution` writes
`hand(affectedPlayers, toPlayers)` and `hand(eligible, toNodes)` into one `shares` map. It cannot be
unpicked afterwards - a node operator's own entry is legitimately in both halves - so the split is made
where it is known: `playerShares` and `nodeShares` are returned beside `shares`, which keeps its exact
old contents and its sum check. `slash-owing.test.js` asserted `nodes.get(SEAT_A)` and `nodes.get(OUT_1)`
one key at a time and never the whole map, which is why it never saw this.

WRONG 2 - THE ACCUSED WAS PAID FROM ITS OWN BOND: 18750000 of 100000000 sat back to keyFor(0x11), the
node the proof accuses. Not an accident of the door. At `slash_height` the bond is unspent - that is
exactly why step 2 can read its value there - so `deriveCensus` counts it and it falls inside "the
active census nodes at the slashing height". `slashDistribution` asserts the opposite in a comment and
throws on a `slashed` node inside the census, a guard meant for a census read AFTER the spend. The two
are each right about their own height, and the ruled window (`census_height <= slash_height <= tip when
they sign`) puts this one before the spend, because the spend IS the slashing transaction. Resolved by
taking the accused out of the census the split is computed over, in `slash-owing.js`: the guard is not
loosened, `slashed` is not passed, and §5A.3's 75% simply divides among the census nodes left. Flagged
on the board as a reading rather than a ruling.

Suites, each alone: slash-distribution + slash-rulings 15/0, slash-owing 7/0 (a seventh test pins the
accused at 0 and the players absent from the nodes' map), slash-filing 4/0, roster 19/0 = 45/0.

FIXTURE NOTE. The door's test opens the round on the store rather than posting it to `/round`: that
door additionally requires `contract.nodes` to be exactly the set the census assigns, and the
assignment is seeded from the round id the node list is part of. Iterating to a fixed point grows the
slot count until every bonded node is a seat and §5A.3 has nobody left to pay, so the fixed point is
the wrong tool here - the door under test reads the seats off the stored contract and never asks who
was assigned.

## Two more holes in the slash-owing door, and one that was not (2026-09-22)

RULING 3 WAS THE DOOR'S OWN SUBJECT AND ITS LOOP WAS UNMEASURED. "Several slashed nodes: nothing
pooled - each bond pays the players its own proof names" is exactly what `/slash-owing` answers, and
every 200-path measurement had used a single filed proof. The census is read ONCE and shared across
the loop while each proof removes its own accused from it, so a second proof is precisely where a
shared list would show the first one's exclusion leaking. Measured with two proofs, two accused nodes,
one run:

    proof against 4f355bdc (0x11)  -> nodes: 6360e856 37500000   players: 0505..05 50000000
    proof against 6360e856 (0x12)  -> nodes: 4f355bdc 37500000   players: 0505..05 50000000

Each answer sums to its own 100000000 sat bond, and the harmed player is paid the players' half out of
BOTH, pooled nowhere - which is the ruling, read back off the door rather than off the library.

THE HEIGHT WAS BOUNDED AFTER THE CENSUS, NOT BEFORE. `slash-owing.test.js` pins the order - "a height
nobody can read yet must not send a node reading a census at it", asserted as `asked === 0` - and that
property held for the recorder and not for the door, which called `censusAtHeight` first and
`slashOwing` (whose step 1 is the bound) second. A height below the round's own census height made the
node scan, resolve and root a whole census before saying the height was never valid. The bound that
can be checked without a chain view is now checked at the door: measured, 409 "899999 is below the
round's census height 900000". The tip bound needs a view and stays where it is.

NOT A HOLE, MEASURED: `toPool`. The door reports toPlayers/toNodes/toDevelopers and never a pool, and
`slashDistribution` does have a `toPool`. It is unreachable on this path - an empty affected set is
refused at step 3 and an empty eligible set throws at step 6 - and `hand()` hands leftover satoshis out
one at a time rather than pooling them. Measured on bonds 100000, 206 and 100001: toPool 0 in all
three, and the three reported numbers sum to the bond exactly. Now asserted per answer at the door's
own test so a later change cannot open a gap in silence.

## A paying entry that hands over no F (2026-09-22) - measured, sized, not started

§23.5 gives the node fee its own lock; on Lightning custody `holdFee` keys it on
`sha256(entry.feePreimage)`. A zeroed F therefore asks for a hold on `66687aad...`, which is every
zero-F entry's hash in every round. Measured on two players of one round, on the node's own store:

    MEASURED custody: THRESHOLD_LN   feeMsat per entry: 2000
    fee holds on A: [ {entry 0fe46ee9cd90, hash 66687aad..., 2000, HELD},
                      {entry 24bda68ef90d, hash 66687aad..., 2000, HELD} ]
    entries: 2   distinct payment hashes: 1      entry ids differ: true

Two players' fees on ONE HTLC, settled afterwards with a preimage anybody can compute. That is the
`objection-window` red: its settle list is [66687aad/zeros, 66687aad/zeros, the loser's own stake]
where one settle was expected.

IT IS NOT A NEW RULE. `join.js:833`: "Measured on the Daily when it was left at zeros: lnd answered
'cannot use hash of all-zeroes preimage' and no fee invoice was ever made, so the 2% went on being
uncollected." The shipped client mints `random(32)` on a paying round.
`stake-lock-signer-node.js:137` refuses the same entry by name on the FEDERATION path. Only the
hold-invoice path accepts it, and only a stub endpoint ever lets it through.

WITH THE RULE IN (holdFee refuses a zeroed F once a fee is owed; settleFees refuses a row stored
before it), each suite alone:

    objection-window   5/2  -> 7/7
    custody           30/5  -> 35/35   (once its own fixture mints a real F)
    custody-daemon    12/1  -> 13/13   (same)
    federation-invoice + hold-two-first 7/7, void-expiry + walk-away-hold 4/4, unpaid-expiry green

And the assertions stop being vacuous: `custody.test.js:305` says "the fee hold is not keyed on the
entry's own feePreimage" and `custody-daemon.test.js:158` says "the fee is not quoted against the
entry's own fee preimage" - both were checking `66687aad...`, which is nobody's own.

WHY IT IS NOT LANDED. `second-closer` is green today at 2/0 and goes red on "A never took the node fees
it served for" - the correct complaint, because an entry with no F has no fee anyone can take. It
builds its own entry at line 145, and **69 fixtures across blwp-node, blwp-client and protocol build a
paying entry with `feePreimage: new Uint8Array(32)`**. That is a sweep of its own, each suite re-run
chunked, not a line inside the federation letter. The tree is left at HEAD - measured back to
second-closer 2/0 and objection-window 5/2 - and the refusal patch is kept out of it.

BOARD CORRECTION. Two lines said objection-window waits on the hold-path retirement, which follows the
fleet pin. It does not: the cause is the zeroed F, and the fix touches neither the custody enum nor
THRESHOLD_LN. Both corrected in PRIORITIES.md.

## The zeroed fee secret, fixed and swept (2026-09-22)

THE RULE. `holdFee` refuses an entry whose `feePreimage` is thirty-two zero bytes once a fee is owed,
and `settleFees` refuses to settle a row stored before that rule. Measured on two players of one round:

    before   2 fee holds, 1 distinct payment hash (66687aad = sha256 of 32 zero bytes)
    after    2 fee holds, 2 distinct payment hashes

THE GUARD ORDER WAS THE REAL RISK, and only a HEAD baseline caught it. The F check first went in BEFORE
`if (!this.reaches)`, so a FEDERATION round's seats - which reach no Lightning by design - were told
"that entry hands over no F" where they used to be told "this node reaches no Lightning". Measured:
lock-settlement 15/15 -> 13/2, both failures naming fee locks. The board lists that suite as
timing-flaky, so those two LOOKED like known noise. Running HEAD first is the only reason they were not
filed as such. The node's own capability is asked first now, then the entry's.

    second-closer.test.js     2/0  -> 2/0       "A never took the node fees it served for" now means it
    window-fixture.js                           new shared `feeSecretOf`, derived from the stake
                                                preimage so entry ids stay deterministic
    objection-window.test.js  5/2  -> 7/7       the red this started from

Two assertions stop being vacuous: custody.test.js:305 "keyed on the entry's OWN feePreimage" and
custody-daemon.test.js:158 "quoted against the entry's own fee preimage" were both checking

## Ruling 4: the map edge is a clamp, not a wall (2026-09-22)

RULED (Daniel, re-stated knowing the walls existed): "the map edge is a clamp, not a wall. The core
owes no wall solids. The client stops drawing walls the core does not build."

WHAT WENT. `rules/map.js` built four boxes at +-halfX / +-halfZ, 3 m thick, 26 m tall, sunk 6 m, whose
own comment said they caught "a truck arriving airborne off a fee cliff". Gone; `MAP_BOXES` 106 -> 102.
`Bootstrap.cs` no longer calls `BuildBoundary` - the method is kept unreferenced with its reasoning,
because a future edge rule has to answer why they were tall and sunk.

## The assaults 10 -> 14 flag, answered by measurement (2026-09-22)

Ruling 5 was recorded DONE with a flag attached: "assaults 10 -> 14 ... If 14 is outside doctrine the
doctrine row is the fix, not the number." Nobody had checked, and the row that would decide it is
reported by `tools/measure-assault.mjs`, which is a TOOL and not a test - so nothing ran it. That is
how a settled ruling kept an open question for two letters.

Re-measured on the current core (rulings 4 and 5 both in), seeds 1-5:

    assaults started 14, target unheld by the attacker at the start 14 of 14
    ended 12: took the objective 9 (75.0%, row 30-70%), failed 3; still running 2
    declared then happens: lane push >= +8 m inside 600 ticks on 1 of 14 (7.1%, row >= 80%)
    lulls: no assault running on 84.1% of ticks (row 25-60%)
    front moves visibly: a forward hull >= 16 m across on 4 of 5 seeds (row: every seed)
    first starts 22.1, 47.7, 32.0, 23.4, 26.8, 28.1 s (rule 20-40 s); none inside 20 s of a side's end

THE COUNT WAS THE WRONG QUESTION. The lull row says there are too FEW assaults, not too many: 84.1% of
ticks with nothing running against a row of 25-60%. Fourteen is not what breaks doctrine.

AND THREE OF THE FOUR REDS ARE ALREADY PARKED. TASKBOOK's own ASSAULT PROBE baseline recorded
"RED: lane push >= +8 m inside 600 ticks on 1 of 20 -> 1 of 19 (row >= 80%); no assault running on
62.1% -> 70.3% of ticks (row 25-60%); a forward hull >= 16 m across on 0 of 5 seeds", with the
conclusion "Needs a ruling: the row or the cadence" - because "a new direction needs two confirmed
readings (10 s) and the §0.1 600-tick row cannot be met under the 20:30 hold cadence". So:

    declared then happens   1/19 -> 1/14    red before, red now, same in kind
    lulls                   70.3% -> 84.1%  red before, drifting further
    front moves visibly     0/5 -> 4/5      BETTER, nearly passing now
    fail/win split          66.7% -> 75.0%  NEWLY outside its row

ONLY THE LAST IS NEW, AND IT IS ONE ASSAULT WIDE. Nine of twelve ended assaults took the objective;
eight of twelve would be 66.7% and inside the row. On a sample of twelve that is noise, not a finding,
and it is not claimed as one. It is also the direction ruling 5's own chain predicts - fewer men read
STAND, fewer are exposed, more live, and survivors are what an assault clock reads.

WHAT THIS CLOSES AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. The flag "is 14 outside doctrine" is answered: no - the count is
not what the rows measure, and the rows that fail were failing before ruling 5 moved it. What remains
is the ruling already parked in that baseline, unchanged by this letter: the 600-tick row or the 20:30
hold cadence. That is Daniel's, and it is not made here.

## RULED (Daniel 2026-09-22): the cadence stays, the 600-tick row yields

THE HOLD CADENCE STAYS AT 21:20. It is not to be reverted to 20:30. Moving the cadence to chase the row
would undo a kept decision in order to satisfy numbers that were already red before the assault count
moved.

THE §4.12 600-TICK ROW IS THE SIDE THAT YIELDS, and is the open rewrite. A new direction needs two
confirmed readings - ten seconds - so that row cannot be met under the cadence that was kept.

THE COUNT FLAG IS CLOSED. 14 is not what breaks doctrine. The count is not to be reopened.

WHAT THE NEW ROW MUST BE WRITTEN AGAINST: declared-to-happens at 1 of 14, and lulls at 84.1% of ticks.
Those two were already red in the ASSAULT PROBE baseline and are the real subject.

NOT SUBJECTS. The fail/win split at 75.0% is one assault wide on a sample of twelve: noise, not a
finding, unless a second sample puts it outside the row on its own. Front movement improved to 4 of 5
and that row is NOT to be loosened to hide the other two.

## The §4.12 rows re-measured at 20 seeds, and the 600-tick row's real shape (2026-09-22)

Under the kept 21:20 cadence, on this tree. Two disjoint 20-seed blocks of `measure-assault.mjs`
(10800 ticks each), plus a read-only window probe kept out of the repo.

    row                     5 seeds      A: seeds 1-20    B: seeds 21-40    row
    fail/win split          75.0% (12)   57.4% (47)       58.7% (46)        30-70%
    declared-then-happens    7.1% (14)    7.5% (53)        6.1% (49)        >= 80%
    lulls                   84.1%        76.9%            77.5%             25-60%
    front moves visibly     4 of 5       13 of 20         14 of 20          every seed

SAMPLE: 53 and 49 assaults started, 47 and 46 ended, 20 seeds x 10800 ticks per block.

WHICH ROWS MOVE WITH SAMPLE SIZE, which is the whole reason for 20 seeds:
  - fail/win split 75.0% -> 57.4 / 58.7%. NOISE, confirmed on a disjoint second sample as ruled.
  - front moves visibly 4 of 5 -> 13/20 and 14/20. THE IMPROVEMENT WAS ALSO NOISE, in the other
    direction. 80% of seeds at n=5 is 65-70% at n=20. Recorded because the ruling rested on it having
    improved; the row is NOT proposed for loosening, and this is not offered as cover for the others.
  - declared-then-happens 5.3 -> 7.5 -> 6.1% and lulls 70.3 -> 76.9 -> 77.5%: STABLE. These two are the
    subject, as ruled.

THE 600-TICK ROW'S REAL SHAPE. `measure-assault.mjs` reports only whether +8 m happened inside 600
ticks, so a separate read-only probe recorded the gain at five windows over seeds 1-20:

    window   n   share>=8m   share>0    mean gain   distinct values seen
      600   42       9.5%      9.5%       0.95 m    0, 8, 16
      900   42      14.3%     14.3%       1.71 m    0, 8, 16
     1200   41      22.0%     22.0%       2.34 m    0, 8, 16
     1800   39      35.9%     35.9%       4.72 m    0, 8, 16, 24
     2400   38      44.7%     44.7%       6.32 m    0, 8, 16, 24

TWO FACTS FALL OUT, AND BOTH BEAR ON HOW THE ROW IS WRITTEN:

1. THE THRESHOLD AND THE PERCENTAGE ARE ONE DIAL. `share >= 8m` EQUALS `share > 0` at every window:
   lane push never lands between 0 and 8, and the observed gains are exactly 0, 8, 16, 24. So "8 m" is
   not a magnitude, it is "at least one step of push". Any threshold in (0, 8] measures the same thing;
   16 would demand two steps. A rewrite that tunes the metres is tuning nothing.

2. THE WINDOW IS NOT THE BINDING CONSTRAINT. At 1800 ticks - the assault's OWN maximum life - 35.9%
   gain a step. At 2400, past the assault entirely, 44.7%. Against a row of >= 80%. Lengthening 600 to
   1800 moves 9.5% to 35.9% and gets nowhere near.

   So the median assault moves its lane by NOTHING within its own life, and that is the finding. The
   mechanism is not established here: gains arriving only in multiples of 8 suggests either a quantised
   push word or that typically one team is on the lane, and `k` was not measured. Named, not claimed.

PROPOSED - NOT ACCEPTED, NOTHING EDITED. Written from the readings above:

    "An assault is declared, then it happens" | tempo §4.12 | within 1800 ticks of an assault's start -
    its own maximum life, so the row asks about the assault and not an arbitrary prefix - the attacking
    side's mean push on the assaulted lane is at least one step (>= 8 m) higher than at the start, on
    >= 30% of assaults.    [measured 35.9%, n=39 over 20 seeds, margin 6 points]

    "Lulls exist" | assault clock §4.12 | on 70% to 85% of ticks no assault is running on either side;
    no assault starts inside 20 s of the previous one on the same side.
                           [measured 76.9% and 77.5%, two disjoint 20-seed blocks; the 20 s clause
                            passes today, 0 violations in 102 assaults]

AND THE HONEST OBJECTION TO BOTH, which is why they are proposed and not written: each bound describes
this tree rather than the intent it replaced. A row passing at 30% lets seven assaults in ten move
nothing visible, and "an assault is declared, then it happens" then means almost nothing. A lull band
of 70-85% blesses a war that is quiet three ticks in four where doctrine wanted it quiet one in two.
If the intent is to be kept, no bound over this tree satisfies it and the finding is about the
simulation, not the row.

## RULED and written (Daniel 2026-09-22): the declared-to-happens window, and nothing else

ONE ROW CHANGED, ONE FIELD OF IT. §4.12's "An assault is declared, then it happens" now reads its push
gain within **1800 ticks** of the assault's start - the assault's own maximum life - where it read 600.
THE BAR IS UNCHANGED at >= 80%.

WHY THE WINDOW AND NOT THE BAR. The rows table already rules this shape four times over on 2026-09-19,
and every restated row carries an incompatibility, never an inconvenient number: §2.6's "Something is
always happening" had "the window was 10 s and that number was arithmetic under the 6-10 s leg this row
was written against ... The window is restated to the leg the doctrine now has ... The bar is still 0
windows." Same case here: a new direction needs two confirmed readings, 10 s, which is the whole of a
600-tick budget, so the row spent its entire window confirming and had none left for the push. The
cadence stays 21:20 and the row yields its window, not its bar.

IT IS STILL RED, AND THAT IS THE POINT. 35.9% on the restated window (n=39, seeds 1-20) against >= 80%.
That red is a simulation finding, not a doctrine problem, and the bar was not moved to meet it.

WITHDRAWN, BY THE SAME PRECEDENT: my own proposals of >= 30% for this row and 70-85% for the lull band.
Both were the bar moving to meet the measurement, which is what keeping the cadence refused.

NOT TOUCHED: lulls stay written at 25-60% and stay red at 76.9 / 77.5% - a row merely unmet is a red,
and no row in that table was ever restated for being unmet. Fail/win stays closed as noise, confirmed
on a disjoint 20-seed block at 58.7%. Front movement stays as written and stays red at 13-14 of 20; it
is not loosened. No core, no C#, no cadence, no new coupling.

## RULED (Daniel 2026-09-23): THRESHOLD_LN disposal - the decoder commit, slice 2, and the store measurement

### Step 1, the decoder commit (not slice 2, never merged with it, never red)

- Byte 0 stays EMPTY. FEDERATION stays byte 1 and is never renumbered onto the freed byte (spec
  `d8eb4158`): renumbering would make every old record decode as FEDERATION, which the 22:59 ruling forbids.
- The name THRESHOLD_LN is deleted. Encoding it throws; decoding byte 0 throws the way a bad length does.
  Not a value, not a reserved slot, not a label.
- In this commit: `packages/protocol` constants and contracts, and the tests that prove the throw and that a
  FEDERATION round still decodes as byte 1.
- STEP 1 DOES NOT SHIP RED. Measured: 95 test files at HEAD encode `custody: 'THRESHOLD_LN'` in code, and
  every one would throw at build time. So, in this same commit:
    - a test that only needs a valid PAYING custody, and whose subject is not the withdrawn custody, moves
      its contract to FEDERATION. That is the new ruling, not the old free-round migration. The 95 are
      judged one by one, not retargeted blindly;
    - a test whose subject IS THRESHOLD_LN, the hold invoice or the threshold branch gets no fake
      FEDERATION pass. Protocol tests of that name assert throw or invalid in step 1; node hold-path tests
      stay for slice 2.
- NOT in step 1: `server.js`; the free-round fixture migration; `run-2of2.mjs` (a tool that still names the
  withdrawn custody is a slice-2 blocker, not a reason to keep the enum or merge the slices).

### Slice 2, one later slice

Retire `custody.js` with the hold-invoice path and the threshold branch, and delete `preflight.js` with it
(the Lightning preflight: "can this lnd hold a round's stakes"). With byte 0 failing at decode, `/round`
answers a byte-0 post with a PARSE refusal - no custody-specific 409, nothing stored. The store treats an
unparseable row as ABSENT on load: not decoded, not replayed, not settled, not listed, not counted. That
is where "past rounds included" is enforced.

Source: the Daily's own stores, `/mnt/bitcoin/blwp-2of2/a.db` and `/mnt/bitcoin/blwp-2of2/b.db`, table
`rounds` (the pinned opener writes `store + '/a.db'` and `'/b.db'`, `round-2of2.mjs:174-175` at
`02eefc04`). Read 2026-09-23 with `sqlite3 -readonly` on `mode=ro` URIs.

## The two-gateway gate, on a federation of our own (RULED Daniel 2026-09-23: hole 1 of 3, first)

§23.6: "deposits and withdrawals through any of at least two gateways ... run by different operators".
A paying FEDERATION round's `POST /round`, on a signer node with a lock port, now counts that round's
federation's gateways through the port - `blwp-stake-lock --mode gateways`: every name the guardians
registered, whether it answered `routing_info`, and the Lightning node key it answered with. Identity is that
key; two names on one key are one gateway, then counted (`federationGatewayCount`, protocol/gateways.js - not
`gatewaysAreIndependent`, whose inbound count and refuse-the-set rule are the operator's, not the door's).
Under two distinct live: refused by name, with the count, BEFORE anything is stored - 404, nothing kept. A port
on another federation than the round names is refused naming both. Inbound is NOT read at the door and not
claimed there: the federation's API does not say it. It is shown only by a deposit that commits through each.

Unit (gateway-gate.test.js, the shared lock fixture): 0, 1, two names on one node, one of two not answering
-> 409 by name, 404, stored 0; two independent, and two plus a second name on one -> 201; a free round is
not refused. 3/3. The two fake ports that reach the door report two gateways (lock-fixture, guardians-bonded).

OWN FEDERATION (the port-shifted federation-hold-probe, SECOND_GATEWAY=1, on 31101..31182; the other session's
probe on 30101 untouched): 4 guardians, threshold 3, federation a9d2f0b8; gateway A 31170 on bob's lnd
022d23b6, gateway B 31180 on carol's 03046818; payer alice with a channel to each. `tools/gateway-probe.mjs`:

    one gateway (B off all 4 guardians' lists)   409 x2 "that round's federation has 1 distinct live gateway(s)
                                                  (1 registered): a paying round needs at least two ..."
                                                  held 404 x2, stored 0 x2
    two gateways (B back on)                     201 x2, held 200 x2, stored 1 x2; lobby: listed, federation-lock
    deposit, B down (the page's own lock client  invoice payee = A's node, paid, Claimed in 4.9 s; the stake lock
      build, no gateway named - it picks)          verified and committed 980000 msat on both signer nodes
    deposit, A down                              payee = B's node, Claimed in 2.3 s; committed 980000 x2

So each distinct live gateway received a deposit that committed - its inbound - and the client fell back to the
live one each time. Pass for this slice. Found on the way: the harness's pids file holds the self-extracting
wrapper, not the gatewayd it runs (killing it stops nothing); the probe stops a gateway by its listening port
and restarts it through the wrapper. Full measure: no red but the baseline; the hole-2 pin its one skip.
Winnings (hole 2's neighbour, "always sent") is the next slice, not started.

## Winnings are always sent, on a FEDERATION round (RULED Daniel 2026-09-23; hole 3 of 3, after the gateway gate)

"Winnings are always sent. There is no Collect" (Daniel 2026-09-21). A qualifier's payout was a pre-expired contract only
the winner's key could move, collected by the page. Now, when the winner named a Lightning address once (POST
/payout-address, signed with the entry's session key), the settlement pays that qualifier by an LNv2 OUTGOING CONTRACT:
  - the gateway: the LOWEST KEY among the round's federation's distinct live gateways (the door's own count);
  - the invoice: fetched from the address for what that gateway's own send fee leaves of the payout, taken only if its
    amount and its LUD-06 description hash (sha256 of the address's metadata) stand - otherwise no payout is built on it;
  - the refund key: the round's COMMITTEE claim key, never the winner's - the winner never acts.
One signer node proposes the plan (the round's lowest key: two proposals fetched two invoices and built two transactions
no signature joined - measured); every other signer node checks it itself before it rebuilds. After the guardians accept,
the committee FROST-signs the invoice's consensus hash (the gateway pays only with the refund key's signature), the gateway
is asked, and the preimage is checked against the invoice and kept on every signer node: one payment row each. Unpaid past
its expiration, the contract is refunded to the committee and re-sent through the next live gateway to a fresh invoice.
A sweep drives it, so nothing of the player's runs. Tool: blwp-stake-lock settle takes invoice payouts and --refunds,
`send` asks a gateway, `gateways` reports each gateway's send terms and the federation's height.

Unit (winnings-sent.test.js, fake lock port and LNURL): pass - one contract to the checked invoice, lowest gateway,
committee refund key, gateway asked once, PAID on both, settling again adds nothing; fail - no qualifier: no output, no
invoice asked; refuse - bad amount, bad description hash: no settlement; expiry - re-sent once through the next gateway,
paid once. 4/4, 114 s.

OWN FEDERATION (a9d2f0b8, 3-of-4; gateway A 31170 on bob's lnd, B 31180 on carol's; the winner's address an https LNURL
on alice's lnd), tools/winnings-probe.mjs, on the committed code:
  PASS    W owed 980000 msat; invoice 70748411.. 970179 msat through A (module 03e63da0), expiration 3404; contract at
          settlement c4e197f5..:2, id 5bcebf3b..; alice SETTLED 970179 msat over her channel to A; preimage sha256 = hash;
          the contract no longer held (the gateway claimed it); L's lock claimed into the pool; PAID on both; address asked 1.
          RESTART both signer nodes, 30 s: address asked 1, alice's settled count 6 -> 6, settlement ACCEPTED, PAID on both.
  FAIL    both runs under min_score, W's address named: only the two fee locks claimed, address asked 0, no rows, both stake
          locks still held (150 blocks left).
  EXPIRY  A live but its node drained below the winning (an ordinary bob->alice payment, after the round's deposits - a
          deposit through A had refilled it, and A paid attempt 0: measured): attempt 0 through A, contract in settlement
          7655d0a6.., the gateway cancelled; alice's first invoice OPEN. Mined to federation height 3533 past 3404. Attempt 1
          through B, funded by the committee's refund 2fc93e87..; alice's second invoice SETTLED 970179 msat; preimage =
          hash; PAID on both; address asked 2.
Why "stop the lowest-key gateway before settling" was realised as a drain: a stopped gateway is not live, so the plan
picks the other one and nothing expires - measured: bob's lnd down, A answered FailedToRequestRoutingInfo.

Known and left: attempt 0's row reads SENDING, not EXPIRED, after its re-send; the proposer is the one that drives sends,
so a proposer down leaves winnings waiting until it is back (restart resumes); in the probe both signer nodes share one
federation client directory, and once a tool call collided on its lock - retried by the next sweep. The page does not yet
ask for the address; the probe names it at the door.
Full suite: no red but the baseline; the hole-2 pin its one skip; winnings-sent and lock-settlement passed.

## The pool: a qualifier who names no address is not paid (RULED Daniel 2026-09-23: (ii), with (iii); never (i))

The rule, on the settlement path (protocol lockSettlement, `addressed`): only a qualifier whose entry named a Lightning
address is paid. An unaddressed qualifier's share stays in the pot and is split over the addressed ones by the payout
table's own weights, renormalised over that set; the msat the division leaves goes to the first addressed row in the
table's order, so the payouts, their fees and the input fees are the whole claimed pot - no remainder for the guardians.
With nobody addressed no loser's stake lock is claimed: each expires back; the fee locks still settle. Nothing is ever
paid to a key-held contract a winner would have to collect: a signed plan with an addressed qualifier and no accepted
send is refused (`requireSends`). Every signer node reads the addressed set from its own stored addresses; a peer
holding another set rebuilds other amounts and refuses the proposer's plan by name (the proposer now hands out an empty
plan too).

NOT RULED, AND TAKEN AS (iii): an addressed qualifier outside the paying ranks has no weight in the table. When every
qualifier with a paying rank is unaddressed, the addressed set's weights sum to nothing, there is no split to renormalise,
and none is invented: no stake lock is claimed, each expires back (stakeWhy says so). Measured on the node: two
qualifiers make one paying rank; the top one unaddressed and the other addressed claimed nothing.

Found and fixed on the way, each measured red first:
  - a peer that refused its own settle while waiting for the plan never settled after taking it (A ACCEPTED, B NONE for
    30 s): it settles as soon as it takes the plan.
  - a peer not yet FINAL refused the plan and nothing offered it again before the 60 s sweep: the proposer offers it
    again every second, at most 120 times.
  - a signer node restarted inside a settlement asked again before it knew its peers and "handed" a new plan to nobody:
    a plan handed to no peer is a refusal.
  - W6 (b)+(c): the fee rule changed between plan and submit, and every rebuild was refused against the old payout. A
    send planned for another amount is refused, and a kept first plan the payout no longer matches is dropped and planned
    again - only while the round is not ACCEPTED and nothing of it was sent. Send planning now runs after the W6 federation
    check, so a plan the money already moved on is never re-planned.

once each, each above its own share, row 3 exactly its renormalised weight, input fees + payouts + output fees = pot,
unspent 0; the dust - pool 294000 over weights 127136:71513, floors 188160 + 105839, 1 msat left - to the first row
(188161). POOL B - nobody addressed: no stake claim, pool/fees/unspent 0, fee locks still claimed. POOL C - all addressed:
every row but the first exactly the pre-ruling split, each a sent contract to the committee key; a missing send refused.

## The page asks a winner once where to send the winnings (RULED Daniel 2026-09-23: the accepted sequence)

THE PAGE (packages/blwp-client/src/winnings.js, index.html, blwp.jslib): on the existing BLWP_RUN_OVER hook, and only when
the page's own core says DELIVERED at or above the contract's min_score, `blwp.winnings.asked.<round>.<entry>` is written
and then ONE window.prompt ("Where should your winnings be sent? Lightning address (name@host)"). The bridge hands the hook
the run (round, entry, the core's word and score, min_score, the round's nodes) and ONE narrow call that signs the
address's UTF-8 bytes with the session key and nothing else: no score, no payout, no round id; the key stays in the
closure. It checks the name@host shape itself (the shipped bundle waits for the pin, so the bridge calls no new bundle
export - ghost-field 6 measured that); the full Lightning-address check is the page's before it signs and every door's
after. An accepted address is kept as `blwp.winnings.addr.<round>.<entry>` (address, signature, the round's nodes, who
answered 201) and POSTed to every signer node on the round's node list, not the gateways. Every load re-posts the same
bytes only to the nodes that did not answer 201, until all have. Empty, cancelled or not an address: nothing kept,
nothing posted. THE DOOR: the first address stands - the same bytes again 201 and nothing changes, another address 409.
The committed dist/template bundle is the pin's and is not rebuilt here; until it is, `askForWinnings` is absent and the
page asks nothing (index.html checks for it).

ON A 5-OF-7 (the measurement's shape, and forced by the federation): fed2 is 3-of-4, so §23.6 refuses a round unless three
distinct bonded signer nodes each vouch for one guardian, and a paying committee is 2 or 7 (`receiptsNeeded`) - measured:
two nodes refused "0 of that federation's 4 guardians are bonded", a 3-node round cannot settle. So seven signer nodes,
bonded on fed2's own regtest chain (standUpRound with rpc; the fixture chain carries two bonds), three vouching.

FOUND BY MEASURING, AND FIXED ON THE SETTLEMENT PATH (each red first):
  - the send plan needed EVERY peer: one signer node that saw the run end differently stalled a 5-of-7. It needs the
    signing threshold.
  - a peer that rebuilt other bytes still committed, and its share would spoil the combined signature: /settle-commit
    names the asker's txid, and a peer that rebuilt another refuses by name.
  - every node that took the plan combined at once; each peer shares over one list only ("keeps no second pair") and no
    combination completed (measured: fee-only round NONE after 240 s). And a single fixed proposer (the lowest key) that
    signed the run FAILED stalled the round for good (measured: 1 of 5 took its plan, 120 tries). RULED ALREADY, applied:
    M3.3-19's takeover - the round's nodes sorted by key, rotated by an index from the round id (`askerOrder`); seat 0
    alone at the close, seat k once the chain is k x TAKEOVER_BLOCKS past the round's beacon; no chain tip, no takeover.
    The others answer, keep the signature they are handed, and ask the federation every 2 s (not the minute's sweep).
  - two askers eligible at once each fetched an invoice; the peers split 4 and 2. An asker now adopts a plan its peers
    keep (GET /settle-sends) if it stands here, and two plans converge on the lower-keyed (payment hashes sorted) while
    nothing is settled or sent. Unpaid extra invoices expire; one is paid.
  - "is it in?" read stored payout contracts, and a sent winning's contract is claimed by the gateway as it pays: a paid
    winning's preimage, held only if it hashes to the invoice, now counts; a SUBMITTING row of other bytes gives way to
    a signature over the bytes the node rebuilds now; "neither" makes an answering node ask again.
  Tests moved with it, each by name: the no-qualifier settlement is polled on the asker (it was a fixed WINDOW+3 s sleep,
  red 1 in 2 on origin; with one asker it was red every time); two W6 checks accept the sent contract claimed; the
