## RULED Daniel 2026-09-23: §10's required window for the run's last mark (the hole 86f52c3b left)

The window is not a new second-count - spec and code never named one, and no timeout constant is invented. It runs from
the checkpoint ask until the settlement is combined in M3.3-19's takeover order. A receipt counts only if it is the SAME
mark already asked, posted again to the signer node that missed it, and it lands before that combine. No second prompt to
the winner; the signature stays the address only. Two-of-two: if that re-offer lands before the combine, both sign
DELIVERED and the winner is paid once to the named address. If the page's tick clock is already closed, or the settlement
already combined, both sign FAILED at the last accepted mark - one payout, and the missing final receipt is not paid.
Five-of-seven uses the same window: the rule is not split so that five-of-seven pays and two-of-two does not. A 7 s outage
fits inside it (ruled). Not coded yet: the game path is not touched until the measurement below is read.

## The run's final mark reaches a signer node that missed its last inputs (RULED Daniel 2026-09-23, the window above)

MEASURED FIRST, on the code as it stood (tools/last-mark-window-probe.mjs: the page's own bundle and blwp.jslib on the
Daily's two-of-two shape, a free round - a paying two-of-two FEDERATION round cannot be stood up: Fedimint 0.12.0 refuses
a federation of 2, one guardian is single custody, and at 4 guardians §23.6 wants three vouching signer nodes). Signer
node B stopped as the core said DELIVERED and was served again 7 s later: `finish` asked for the final mark, `markNow`
held it for every peer, B's feed sat 4 ticks short (1002 of 1006) with its socket closed, and after the existing 10 s
input wait the final mark was SENT TO NOBODY; no pending link, no relink, B's feed never ran again. A signed DELIVERED,
B FAILED - 3 runs of 3 (e.g. A 1126 ticks, B 1122). The page's tick clock was never closed (last post 18-41 ms before
DELIVERED). It was the inputs, not the mark: B lacked the last batch the final mark committed to.

THE RULE, AS BUILT:
  THE PAGE (client.js). `finish` asks for the run's FINAL mark (`markNow(..., { final: true })`): it waits only for this
  client's own node to hold its inputs and goes to the peers that hold them - it has no successor, so no second child of
  its parent can follow it. Every other mark keeps the all-peers wait and its existing timeout. The final mark is the
  pending link and `finalLink`; `#catchUpFinal` re-offers that SAME object once a second (a cadence, not a timeout),
  FEED FIRST - `#relink` runs a behind peer's input feed from the first batch it never answered, through the batch
  ending at the mark's tick, nothing past it - until every signer node has receipted it, the page leaves (`close`), or
  the node answers the settlement combined. Five of seven receipts end the ask, not the catch-up of a node still behind.
  THE SIGNER NODE (round.js, verify.js). At its close, a run that would be signed as a stopped transcript, while the
  close's own receipt pull shows a peer holding a mark this node has not got - read from that peer, session-signed,
  chained on a mark held here, over inputs this node is short of - is HELD BACK: kept in `held_final_ask`, no result
  signed. While held, the batch door takes after the close only batches ending before the mark's tick, then the
  checkpoint door only that mark, byte for byte; anything else is "the round is closed", as is everything for a node
  that holds no such ask. Inputs whole but the mark not yet taken: still held (feed first, then the mark). The node that
  holds the final mark's ask, the run DELIVERED, while the mark is not yet carried (a peer short of its inputs) holds its
  close too, so both sign over the same transcript - measured without it: A signed at its close without the final mark,
  B after its catch-up with it, two transcript hashes, never 2 of 2. Only a DELIVERED run: a player who kept its last
  inputs from one node cannot hold a pair open on a run it lost (§15). The combine ends it: then the stopped result is
  signed and the doors shut. The close retries on the finality cadence it already had; no new timer on the node.

MEASURED ON THE FIX:
  Free two-of-two, B back after 7 s, close the moment B returns (CLOSE_AFTER_BACK_MS=0), 3 runs: both DELIVERED, same
  score, same transcript hash, same ticks (1027/1027, 999/999, 1259/1259), same checkpoints, final mark 2 of 2 -
  3 of 3. Before the hold-back: B FAILED, 4-6 ticks short, "the round is closed" (2 of 2 runs).
  Free two-of-two, close 5 s after B returns, 3 runs: the same - 3 of 3 (and 3 of 3 before the node change).
  Client test (final-mark-catchup.test.js): the final mark goes to A alone, pending at 120; B back: one batch, ticks
  60-119, then the same mark byte for byte (message 2 of 2), receipted after 1 re-offer; 120 ticks and one transcript
  hash at both; no fork proof. Control: a non-final mark with B down waits its 1500 ms bound, is sent to nobody, never
  a final link; the next mark after B returns chains on the head both hold, no fork proof.
  Doors test (held-final-ask.test.js): after the close, no ask - batch and mark refused; with the ask - a batch past the
  tick refused, another mark at the same tick and parent refused, the mark before its inputs refused, then the batch
  (60 ticks) and the mark taken; dropped - refused again.
  fed2, 5-of-7, case W (winnings-page-probe.mjs, B stopped at DELIVERED, back after 7 s):
    close 5 s after B back: all seven DELIVERED 1, final mark 7 of 7 after 8 re-offers, B's inputs whole at +8.3 s;
      combined +60 s; alice SETTLED 970179 msat once; 7 PAID; restart all, 30 s: nothing more; another address 409 x 7.
    close 12 ms after B back: all seven DELIVERED 472; combined +125 s; alice SETTLED once; 7 PAID; restart nothing
      more; 409 x 7. B took the page's batches before its close was processed, so at its close its inputs were whole
      and only the mark was missing: it closed as today (ruled: hold only while the inputs are short) and signed over
      its chain without the final mark; the re-offer then met the closed door; the mark stayed 6 of 7 and the six
      carried the settlement.
  Measuring it needed, on fed2: the federation's height caught up with the chain before a round (after many blocks
  mined, a lock's expiry from the federation's height fell short of the nodes' rule - one run discarded for it), and
  bonds of a run killed mid-stand-up aged out of the 20-block census read (30 blocks mined).
  Full suite (247 files, one per node --test, 180 s cap): the baseline reds - ghost-live 9, replay-solids 2, bundle-fresh
  (the pin), discovery 18, the pin's one skip - and objective-markers timed out at 180 s. That file drives the live
  playtest Chrome on the Beelink (CDP 9351, the deployed Daily page) and touches nothing this slice changed; run from a
  clean worktree of origin's own HEAD it times out the same, 180 s, with the Chrome up and the page open. It passed in
  38 s in the earlier suites: the live page, not this code. Named, not fixed here.

## A DELIVERED signed without the final mark is a failure, not a close (RULED Daniel 2026-09-24)

The pass at 3dc6177b let one 5-of-7 run through that broke the rule: B's batches landed milliseconds before its close,
so at the close it was short only the MARK, did not hold (the hold was only while the inputs were short), and signed
DELIVERED over a transcript without it; the final mark stayed 6 of 7. Measured as a miss, forced every run:
winnings-page-probe.mjs CASE=WF (harness only - the page and the signer node unchanged) stops B at DELIVERED, brings it
back after 7 s, lets the page's batch feed through, sends the close only once B's inputs are whole, and holds back the
final mark's bytes to B until B has applied its close. BEFORE THE FIX: six nodes DELIVERED 328 over one transcript
(69612afc..), 17 checkpoints, 6 receipts of the final mark; B DELIVERED 328 over ANOTHER (d8175c0f..), 16 checkpoints,
0 receipts; the client 6 of 7.

THE FIX: the close holds back also while the node lacks the final mark itself - a peer holds it, session-signed and
chained on a mark held here (the close's pull names it: "a receipt for a mark this node has not got") - not only while
its inputs are short. One check whatever the replay said; the hold is dropped once the mark and its inputs are both in,
and the run is signed over the transcript with it; until the combine, as ruled. While held, the checkpoint door takes
that same mark byte for byte after the close; everything else is "the round is closed". AND the receipt a node issues
for a mark taken after its close is offered at once to every peer over the play socket (§10's receipt exchange): the
peers signed before it existed and pull no more - measured without it: every node agreed on the result, the client
counted 7 of 7, and the six others held 6.

MEASURED ON THE FIX (per node: its OWN signed result, /transcript ticks, /checkpoints, its receipts of the final mark):
  forced WF, 3 runs: all seven DELIVERED 2 / 241 / 98, one transcript hash per run (b8070047.., d1d777ad.., b3330525..),
  1163 / 1004 / 1224 ticks, 20 / 17 / 21 checkpoints at every node, the final mark 7 of 7 at every node and on the
  client; paid once, 7 PAID, restart of all seven adds nothing (same txid), second address 409 x 7 - each run.
  unforced W, close 10 ms and 5 s after B back: the same, all seven one result (DELIVERED 94 / 88), 7 of 7 everywhere,
  paid once, 7 PAID, restart nothing, 409 x 7.
  free two-of-two, 6 runs (3 close at once, 3 at +5 s): both DELIVERED, one score, one transcript hash, the same ticks
  and checkpoints, final mark 2 of 2 - 6 of 6. In one close-at-once run node A had not yet fetched B's (identical)
  signature when the tool stopped at 90 s: past its result window A gathers on a 60 s cadence. Named, not a disagreement.
  Doors test: a node holding back only for the mark, its inputs whole before the close, takes that same mark after it
  and nothing else. Client tests: final-mark-catchup 2/2, checkpoint-quorum 9/9, finish-at-delivered 4/4, backpressure
  21/21.
  Full suite (247 files): the baseline reds (ghost-live 9, replay-solids 2, bundle-fresh the pin, discovery 18, the pin's
  one skip), objective-markers' 180 s timeout on the live Beelink Chrome (origin's own code times out the same, above),
  and first-mark 7 ("late start at close (2)") once. That one is intermittent under a loaded suite and predates this
  slice's code (it failed once in the pool slice's suite, before any final-mark code existed): 3/3 alone, 3/3 as a
  whole file (15/15 each) on this code. Named, not fixed here.

## The combine comes first: the last-mark window closes (RULED Daniel 2026-09-24)

MEASURED AS A MISS FIRST (winnings-page-probe.mjs CASE=WC: B stopped at DELIVERED, kept down until the other six combined
the settlement, then brought back and closed): B held its close for ever - 180 s, no result - with a held-back ask at
tick 1006 and its door taking the final mark ("this node holds this run's inputs only ..."), not "the round is closed".
B had been down across the combine, so its own store held no settlement row and it never learned the window had ended.
And nothing was paid: the harness's loser played one late first mark, which by M3.3-34 waits on every unreachable node,
and with B down past the 3 s result window §13C voided it - no stake to claim.

THE FIX: a node asks whether the settlement is combined of its own row OR of a peer's row whose combined signature
verifies under the round's claim key over the message it names (only a threshold of the round's signer nodes can make
one, so a peer's word alone ends nothing). If the combine came first while a node still lacked the final mark, it signs
the stopped transcript - never a DELIVERED without the mark - and its held ask is dropped, the doors shut. The harness's
loser now plays an on-time first mark at tick 60, then its last - its close depends on nobody.

THE REGRESSION PASS FOUND TWO MISSES IN THE WINNINGS SEND, BOTH FIXED HERE (each red first):
  - a signer node keeping another send plan committed to the send's auth anyway, and its share over its own invoice spoiled
    the combined auth: 34 x "the auth signature does not verify under the claim key", the winner never paid. The send's
    commit now names the plan's payment hash, and a node keeping another refuses - the settlement's own txid guard.
  - after the combine, a later asker's lower-keyed plan still replaced the settled one at three nodes (the convergence rule
    read "settled" as ACCEPTED only): "3 of 5 signer nodes committed to the auth", 165 times, unpaid. A plan no longer gives
    way once this node holds the combined settlement (SUBMITTING or ACCEPTED): signed is settled.

MEASURED ON THE FINAL CODE, fed2 5-of-7:
  WC (combine first), 3 runs: the six DELIVERED 250/288/196 over one transcript each, the final mark 6 of 6 at each; B
  back 0.75 s after the combine (+42 to +95 s), signs FAILED over its own shorter transcript, no held ask, answers the
  final mark "error the round is closed"; the page's catch-up ends "combined", 0 re-offers after; paid once (6 PAID - B
  was down across the send); restart adds nothing; second address 409 x 7. Then again on the final send code, 3 runs:
  the same, each paid (6 PAID), restart nothing, 409 x 7.
  WF (forced short-only-the-mark), 3 runs: all seven one result, one transcript, one tick and checkpoint count, 7 of 7
  receipts at every node and on the client, paid once, 7 PAID, restart nothing, 409 x 7.
  unforced W, close at once and at +5 s: the same, 7 PAID, 7 of 7.
  free two-of-two, 6 runs (3 at once, 3 at +5 s): one result over one transcript each, the final mark 2 of 2.
  Node tests: held-final-ask 3/3, checkpoint 21/21, lock-settlement 9/9, lock-settlement-restart 6/6, winnings-sent 4/4,
  winnings-pool 3/3.
  Full suite (247 files): the baseline reds only (ghost-live 9, replay-solids 2, bundle-fresh the pin, discovery 18, the
  pin's one skip) and objective-markers' live-Chrome timeout (origin's own code the same, above).
The last-mark window is closed: from the ask until the settlement is combined, the same mark, no DELIVERED on a transcript
that lacks it, 7 of 7 after a late mark that lands in time, and the stopped result when the combine comes first.

## FEDERATION: a lock's expiry is checked against the lock's own height, not the verifier's tip + 144 (RULED Daniel 2026-09-24, c4a0eff6 ruling A, option (a))

SEARCHED FIRST: the check was protocol/src/stake-lock.js lockMatchesEntry - refused when expiration < height + 144,
where height is the federation block count at verification (stake-lock-signer-node.js passes st.blockCount, stake lock
and fee lock alike). The page built its locks at count + 144 + LOCK_EXPIRY_MARGIN_BLOCKS (6, W1a's number) only to
survive that off-by-the-wait. The stock federation has no lock height: lnv2 process_output stores
OutgoingContractKey(outpoint) -> OutgoingContract with no creation height, and outgoing_contract_expiration answers only
(contract_id, blocks_left).

THE CUT, option (a): lock_height = the federation-held expiration less stake_expiry_blocks - the expiration the node
already checks equals blockCount + blocksLeft, never the player's number - so expiration >= lock_height + 144 holds by
construction and the check that bites is freshness: refused when lock_height < verify height - 12, i.e. expiration <
verify height + 132. STAKE_LOCK_FRESHNESS_BLOCKS = 12 is in constants.js. The page's margin is deleted, not zeroed:
both locks are built at count + 144. stake-lock-signer-node.js changes only its comment.

MEASURED: stake-lock.test's new case (built at 306, expiration 450) is refused on 458fb47e at 316 ("expires at 450,
before 316 + 144") and counted after, at 316 and 318; at 319 it is refused as stale, the message naming the 12-block
bound. Line 41's refused row moves from HEIGHT + 143 (now valid, 143 >= 132) to HEIGHT + 131 with the lock-height
wording. signer-node-lock:60 (port.height + 100) stays refused, its regex unchanged. page-lock's two pinned deltas are
144. Named suites: stake-lock 5/5 + protocol 32/32, signer-node-lock 5/5, page-lock 27/27.
Full suite (247 files, 1643 pass = 1642 + the new test): the baseline reds only (ghost-live 9, replay-solids 2,
bundle-fresh 1 the pin, discovery 18, pool-outpoint's one skip) and objective-markers' live-Chrome timeout.
Next slice, named not done: c4a0eff6 ruling B, the beacon hash itself is the randomness (the height term dropped).

## FEDERATION: round_randomness is the beacon block's hash itself, no height term (RULED Daniel 2026-09-24, c4a0eff6 ruling B)

SEARCHED FIRST: no computation ever mixed in a height. committeeSeedFrom (protocol/src/beacon.js) hashes
root || root || round_id || round_randomness under TAG.committeeSeed; committeeSeedFromBeacon hands it the block hash
alone; playerSubSeed / seedWordForEntry (seed.js) take the same bytes for the world. beaconFromChain takes
blockHashOf(header) = hash256 of the raw 80-byte header, internal order, never reversed, and beacon-source.js hands those
bytes to main.js's randomnessFor. Height is read only to choose and check the block (beaconIsAfterRound, depth,
beaconIsTheChains) and is returned beside the hash for display and agreement (join.js:192, the server's putBeacon);
all of that stays. The one stale sentence was beacon.js's comment "The spec then takes round_randomness =
H(hash(beacon_block) || height(beacon_block))".

THE CUT: that comment now says round_randomness is hash(beacon_block) in internal order and the callers seed with the
block hash itself; the height only chooses and checks the block. No function body changed.

A PIN, NOT A RED-FIRST TEST: beacon-selection.test's new case passes on 458fb47e and after, because nothing it measures
changed. It fixes the bytes: the mainnet genesis header's internal hash 6fe28c0a...19000000000000, the committee seed
89bcdfa54f3fd95285a230736281bd2e1c78ff0cf1bbeeae2300826787a2fbbd for root b32(2) in both positions and round id
b32(0x11), and the seed from the reversed explorer hash (000000000019d668...8ce26f) is another value, 9c282f0c...39732a.
Named suites: beacon-selection + beacon 16/16. Full suite (247 files, 1644 pass = 1643 + the pin): the baseline reds
only (ghost-live 9, replay-solids 2, bundle-fresh 1 the pin, discovery 18, pool-outpoint's one skip) and
objective-markers' live-Chrome timeout.
Next, named not done: c4a0eff6 ruling C, SUSPENDED ends in at most three windows.

## FEDERATION: a suspended entry ends with its re-run window - §13C at filed + W, and a contract's window is six hours at most (RULED Daniel 2026-09-24, c4a0eff6 ruling C, slice C1)

SEARCHED FIRST: SUSPENDED is recomputed, never stored - objection.js finality() answers it for a valid objection filed
inside the window, and finality.js resultFinality() was the only thing that ended it: 5 of 7 re-runs on one outcome,
posted, made it FINAL. Nothing timed it out ("what 13C does then is timed from the result window, which the contract does
not carry yet"), so four re-runs stayed SUSPENDED forever (rerun.test.js:106 pinned that). The window is the contract's
objection_window_ms, in ms; the result window is the same field (ruled 2026-09-15). contracts.js roundWindowsAreValid
refused only a window <= 0.

THE CUT: resultFinality counts only re-runs stored before rerunEnds = filed + objection_window_ms (filed = this node's
objection seen_ms; the spec's block-timestamped filing is a gap flagged, not fixed), so the answer at that instant is the
answer from then on. No threshold by then is §13C's noQuorumOutcome (payout.js, imported, not edited): FORFEIT when
round.provenTwoFirstMarks, VOID otherwise. settlement.js entriesOnRecord lists a finality FORFEIT as FORFEIT score 0,
like the VOID line above it - no stored §13C record needed; a stored one is still taken once, above, never twice.
MAX_OBJECTION_WINDOW_MS = 21_600_000n in constants.js; roundWindowsAreValid refuses a window over it, naming the cap.
Until C2, a re-run agreed inside the window is FINAL at once with no objection window of its own: short of the spec and
inside its three-window cap. The second objection row (C2) and the settlement's waiting on SUSPENDED (C3) are not here.

MEASURED, W = WINDOW_MS (3000) on the node's own clock stubbed, no sleep: filed + 2999 SUSPENDED; filed + 3000 VOID
("the re-run window closed at ... with 4 of 5 re-runs on one outcome (§13A, §13C)"); filed + 6000 VOID. VOID refunds:
mayRelease refuses, entriesOnRecord lists VOID/0, the forfeit refuses (the lock returns to the player at its expiry).
Proven equivocation at the same instant: FORFEIT; mayRelease { ok, FORFEIT, proven }; entriesOnRecord FORFEIT/0 on the
finality alone (before the settlement line: "nothing is claimed while a run is not final"); with a stored record too it
is listed once. Cap: 21600000 opens, 21600001 and 86400000 refused.
FIXTURES, RULED: the re-runs land 0.66-0.94 s after the filing (measured, three runs and two more at 0.85-0.93), so an
800 ms re-run window was luck. rerun.test and slash-filing use WINDOW_MS; rerun.test:106 flipped to VOID (ruled), and its
test 5 and slash-filing's short-of-five case read at filed + W - 1, assertions unchanged (SUSPENDED, "3 of 5 committee
signer nodes have re-run", no proof filed). objection-window reads at the windows' close, inside the re-run window
(no share, /suspend/), and at filed + W: no share, VOID. result-window.test's "any positive window" list stops at 6 h.
The first full run caught slash-filing (1, 2, 4) and objection-window 1 before those two files moved.
Named suites: rerun 6/6 twice, slash-filing 4/4 twice, objection-window 3/3 twice, result-window 8/8, objection 9/9,
entry-window + no-quorum. Full suite (247 files, 1647 pass = 1644 + 3 new): the baseline reds only (ghost-live 9,
replay-solids 2, bundle-fresh 1 the pin, discovery 18, pool-outpoint's one skip) and objective-markers' live-Chrome timeout.
Next, named not done: C2 (the re-run's own objection window; a second valid objection voids), C3 (the settlement does not
wait on a suspended entry).

## FEDERATION: an agreed re-run gets its own objection window before it is FINAL (RULED Daniel 2026-09-24, ruling C, slice C2a)

THE CUT (finality.js resultFinality): a re-run at the threshold inside the re-run window is PROVISIONALLY_FINAL until its
own objection window closes. The window opens when this node held the re-run at threshold - the seenMs of the record that
first made the count, among the records inside the re-run window - and is objection_window_ms long. That start is before
filed + W, so it closes before filed + 2W and before P + 3W: the three-window cap holds by construction. After it, FINAL,
and only once the re-run's transcript is posted (P2), as before.
OPEN EDGE, NOT A RULE: a re-run transcript still unposted at that close leaves the entry not-FINAL, which can outlive the
cap. The re-run replays the same canonical transcript the objection already needed posted, so it should not happen in
practice; no timeout is added.

MEASURED, rerun.test's new case, W = WINDOW_MS (3000) on the node's own clock stubbed, no sleep: on 1962890c the entry was
FINAL and a share was released at agreed + W - 1; now PROVISIONALLY_FINAL with no share, and FINAL at agreed + W. The
fifth re-run landed 766-859 ms after the filing (three runs). rerun 7/7 twice (cases 1 and 2 at filed + 2W stay FINAL);
slash-filing 4/4 twice, its polls unchanged (proofs are filed once FINAL, now about W later); objection-window 3/3,
result-window, no-quorum, objection. Full suite (247 files, 1648 pass = 1647 + 1): the baseline reds only (ghost-live 9,
replay-solids 2, bundle-fresh 1 the pin, discovery 18, pool-outpoint's one skip) and objective-markers' live-Chrome timeout.
Next, named not done: C2b (a second valid objection inside the re-run's window: a stored row, then VOID), C2c (slash
proofs against the re-run's signers), C3 (the settlement does not wait on a suspended entry).

## FEDERATION: a second valid objection inside the re-run's own window makes the entry VOID (RULED Daniel 2026-09-24, ruling C, slice C2b)

SEARCHED FIRST: POST /objection names a round and an entry; `objections` is one row per (round, entry), INSERT OR IGNORE,
so a second objection answered 200 "already objected" and stored nothing - an agreed re-run could not be objected to.

THE CUT: a new table rerun_objections (round_id, entry_id, seen_ms), the first objection's shape, one per entry - no
column on objections, no migration; Round.objectRerun / rerunObjectedAt mirror object / objectedAt. The intake is one
exported function, server.js objectionIntake, called by the HTTP door and by the test on a stubbed clock: the first
objection as before (201); a second only while this node answers PROVISIONALLY_FINAL on an agreed re-run (201, stored
once); after that window 409 "the re-run's objection window has closed", nothing stored; while still SUSPENDED, or a
third, 200 "already objected"; a missing entry or a round the entry is not in, 404. finality.js: a stored second
objection with agreed <= seen_ms < agreed + W that objectionHolds accepts - the same round, the committee's receipts,
signedResultId the agreed re-run's run id, and this node's own re-run contradicting it - is VOID at once, no third run.
The VOID goes the suspended entry's way to the money; no new money code. FORFEIT, slash proofs against the re-run's
signers (C2c) and the settlement's wait on SUSPENDED (C3) are not here; filing time is still the node's seen_ms.

MEASURED, rerun.test, W = WINDOW_MS (3000), stubbed clock, no sleep. Fixture: five of the other six keys re-run to another
score, so the re-run agrees at 5 of 7 without the holder, whose own re-run keeps the old score. RED FIRST on 559437b4: the
second POST was 200 "already objected" where 201 was asserted, the state PROVISIONALLY_FINAL. After: 201, stored 154 ms
after the agreement (agreed 835 ms after the filing); VOID at agreed + W - 1, at agreed + W and at filed + 3W; mayRelease
refuses (state VOID), entriesOnRecord VOID/0, the forfeit refuses (the lock returns to the player at its expiry); a
third POST 200, the stored time unchanged. Outside: the intake at agreed + W answers 409 and stores nothing; a row
written straight to the store at agreed + W is not counted - FINAL. While SUSPENDED: 200, no second row; missing or
foreign entry 404, this entry unchanged. rerun 10/10 twice; slash-filing + objection-window 7/7; result-window, no-quorum,
objection, rerun-object 25/25. Full suite (247 files, 1651 pass = 1648 + 3): the baseline reds only (ghost-live 9,
replay-solids 2, bundle-fresh 1 the pin, discovery 18, pool-outpoint's one skip) and objective-markers' live-Chrome timeout.
Next, named not done: C2c (slash proofs against the re-run's signers), C3 (the settlement does not wait on a suspended entry).

## FEDERATION: slash proofs against the agreed re-run's signers once a second objection has made the entry VOID (RULED Daniel 2026-09-24, ruling C, slice C2c)

SEARCHED FIRST: the published evidence was a proof plus a signed PLAYER result (joinSlashEvidence, SLASH_EVIDENCE_BYTES),
and slashHolds decodes a player result; a re-run signer signed a RE-RUN result { contradictedRunId, result } over
rerunResultId, which that path cannot carry. slash_proofs is keyed (round, entry, node_pubkey), so a node that signed
both the first result and the re-run would collide. The only filing (fileSlashProofs) ran when a re-run made the entry
FINAL; a VOID filed nothing.

THE CUT: slash.js joinRerunSlashEvidence / splitRerunSlashEvidence (RERUN_SLASH_EVIDENCE_BYTES = proof + signed re-run,
its own size) and slashHoldsOnRerun - offence still REPLAY_CONTRADICTS: on the committee; the accused's own signature
(verify injected) over rerunResultId; this round, this player, the canonical transcript; the agreed re-run's run, not
another outcome; the bond from their own advertisement; and this node's own re-run differing from the agreed one.
Store: rerun_slash_proofs, one row per (round, entry, signer), no migration, no new key on slash_proofs. verify.js
fileRerunSlashProofs mirrors fileSlashProofs: only on a VOID by a second objection; the holder, a stranger, a key whose
re-run is another outcome and a signer with no advertisement refused by name, nothing stored; stored once, published
once. server.js: the 201 that takes the second objection files before it answers; the relay's PUT /slash/<id> keeps
the new shape, checked against the re-run it names. Money does not move: no k-of-m spend. The first result's signers
are not filed against here - that is the next cut, before the settlement wait.

MEASURED, rerun.test on the C2b fixture (W = WINDOW_MS): RED FIRST on 67554344 - the second objection's 201 filed 0
proofs, 5 asserted. After: 5, exactly the agreeing re-run signers, each slashHoldsOnRerun accepts, none against the
holder, 0 rows in slash_proofs, the relay keeps each. On a stubbed clock: nothing filed while SUSPENDED, PROVISIONALLY_FINAL
or a clean FINAL; on the second-objection VOID 4 filed with one advertisement withheld, the holder / stranger / other
outcome / missing advertisement refused by name; that advertisement restored, 1 more; again after the window, none -
publications 4, 1, 0; rows = the 5 committee signers who agreed. Money before and after the proofs identical: VOID,
mayRelease refuses, entriesOnRecord VOID/0, the forfeit refuses (the lock returns at expiry). protocol slash.test: each
refusal of slashHoldsOnRerun by name, and neither evidence shape splits as the other. Named suites: rerun 12/12 twice,
slash 12/12, slash-filing + objection-window 7/7, objection / no-quorum / rerun-object / result-window 36/36. Full suite
(247 files, 1654 pass = 1651 + 3): the baseline reds only (ghost-live 9, replay-solids 2, bundle-fresh 1 the pin,
discovery 18, pool-outpoint's one skip) and objective-markers' live-Chrome timeout.

## FEDERATION: the first result's signers are slashed when the entry ends VOID, or FORFEIT by §13C (RULED Daniel 2026-09-24, ruling C steps 2 and 3)

SEARCHED FIRST: the first-result slash (fileSlashProofs) was filed only when a re-run made the entry FINAL - its verdict
asked for an authoritative re-run - so a second-objection VOID and §13C's VOID or FORFEIT slashed nobody, though ruling C
says "the slashing of the first result's signers stands, because the objection that proved them wrong already exists".
AND A PRODUCTION HOLE: the re-run watch's default budget was the objection plus one window, which stops before §13C
(filed + W) and, since C2a, before the re-run's own window closes; the slash-filing tests only filed because they set
the rerunMs test aid to 8 s.

THE CUT (verify.js, server.js; no protocol, store or settlement change): fileSlashProofs's body is one private helper,
shared; fileFirstResultSlashProofs files through it with the verdict "this node's own replay differs from the contradicted
run", only when this node answers VOID by a second objection, or VOID or FORFEIT with noQuorum - never while SUSPENDED or
PROVISIONALLY_FINAL. Same evidence (joinSlashEvidence), check (slashHolds), table (slash_proofs), dedupe. Named
refusals, nothing stored: the holder ("this node's own result, which is the replay"), a stranger ("... is not on this
round's committee" - now checked before the advertisement), a re-run signer who never signed the first result ("signed
the re-run, not the contradicted result"), a missing advertisement ("no advertisement names its bond"). The 201 that takes
a second objection files these after the re-run proofs, before it answers; the watch files on VOID or FORFEIT with
noQuorum (or a second-objection VOID) and stops. The watch's default budget is filed + 2W and one tick; rerunMs stays a
test aid. A signer of both results has one row in slash_proofs and one in rerun_slash_proofs. Money is untouched.

MEASURED, rerun.test, W = WINDOW_MS: RED FIRST on a5121cd9 - all four new cases 0 proofs. After: the 201 files exactly the
five first-result signers, each slashHolds accepts, each also in rerun_slash_proofs; the sixth key (re-ran to the agreed
outcome, never signed the first) has no first-result row. Stubbed clock: nothing while PROVISIONALLY_FINAL; 4 filed with
one advertisement withheld and the four refusals by name; that advertisement restored, 1; after the window, 0 -
publications 4, 1, 0; money before and after identical (VOID, mayRelease refuses, VOID/0, the forfeit refuses). §13C on
the C1 fixture: nothing while SUSPENDED; FORFEIT with proven equivocation at filed + W files 5, mayRelease identical
before and after; the VOID at the same instant dedupes. Real clock, default budget, no rerunMs: the watch filed the five
about 4.4 s after the filing (after filed + W; poll bounded at filed + 2W + 4 s). RULED FLIP: C2c's firstResultProofs 0
after the 201 is 5 - that 0 marked this cut. rerun 16/16 twice; slash-filing + objection-window 7/7; slash, no-quorum,
rerun-object, result-window, objection 37/37. Full suite (247 files, 1658 pass = 1654 + 4): the baseline reds only
(ghost-live 9, replay-solids 2, bundle-fresh 1 the pin, discovery 18, pool-outpoint's one skip) and objective-markers'
live-Chrome timeout.

## FEDERATION: the round's one settlement no longer waits on an entry still in its re-run window (RULED Daniel 2026-09-24, ruling C, slice C3a)

SEARCHED FIRST: two gates held a round's money on one objected entry. server.js's settle pass called settlements.settle
only when no entry was PROVISIONALLY_FINAL and none SUSPENDED; settlement.js entriesOnRecord refused the whole round
("nothing is claimed while a run is not final") for any entry not FINAL, VOID, FORFEIT or ENTRY_VOID. The finality watch
retried with back-off, so since C1/C2a the round waited for the entry's own decision - up to P + 3W.

THE CUT (settlement.js, server.js; no payout.js, preimage.js, protocol or store change): entriesOnRecord leaves out an
entry SUSPENDED, or PROVISIONALLY_FINAL on a re-run, and names it in `leftOut`; it is not in the payout table and its lock
is neither claimed nor forfeited; the other entries settle as today. The settle gate is server.js settleWaitsOn: only a
run PROVISIONALLY_FINAL inside its first objection window is waited on. No second transaction. LockSettlement
lockAfterSettlement(rid, eid) says what becomes of an entry's lock once the round settled, from what is kept - the claimed
outpoints the round's settlement recorded (lockSettlementMoves) and the entry's finality: claimed there; left out, still
in its re-run window; VOID - nothing acts, the lock returns to the player at its expiry (the forfeit keeps refusing a
§13C VOID; "forfeited to the player on VOID" is the expiry, RULED); FORFEIT, or FINAL and not a qualifier - "claimed in
the round's second settlement, not built yet"; FINAL and a qualifier - its stake back by its own forfeit, stake back
only, no share (RULED: no share, no clawback; the first table stands without that entry).
OPEN EDGE, UNTIL C3b: a left-out lock that later ends FAILED or FORFEIT is not claimed in C3a and returns to its player at
expiry - the same as a round that cannot settle today. C3b, RULED, not built: FORFEIT or FAILED is claimed in a second
transaction; that stake only increases the pool; the difference is paid to the winners already paid; no clawback.

MEASURED, rerun.test, W = WINDOW_MS, stubbed clock; a round with a FINAL loser and one objected entry. RED FIRST on
c893b2f4: the gate waited on the SUSPENDED entry and entriesOnRecord refused the round. (The red test carries today's
gate literally - "PROVISIONALLY_FINAL or SUSPENDED waits" - so it fails on the old code with settleWaitsOn absent.) After:
SUSPENDED - the gate waits on nothing, entriesOnRecord lists only the decided entry, the objected one in leftOut "still in
its re-run window", its forfeit refuses ("no forfeit before the result is final"), mayRelease refuses. PROVISIONALLY_FINAL
on a re-run - left out too; an ordinary PROVISIONALLY_FINAL is still waited on. Then VOID - "VOID: nothing acts, and the
lock returns to the player at its expiry", the forfeit refuses VOID. Then FORFEIT (§13C, proven equivocation), and FINAL
with the replay FAILED - "claimed in the round's second settlement, not built yet". rerun 18/18 twice; lock-settlement
9/9, lock-settlement-restart + pool-settle 17/17, winnings-pool + winnings-sent + daily-paid-federation 9/9, slash-filing +
objection-window + no-quorum 12/12. Full suite (247 files, 1660 pass = 1658 + 2): the baseline reds only (ghost-live 9,
replay-solids 2, bundle-fresh 1 the pin, discovery 18, pool-outpoint's one skip) and objective-markers' live-Chrome timeout.
Next, named not done: C3b (the second settlement for a late FORFEIT or FAILED).

## FEDERATION: a late loser's second settlement - the left-out lock that ends FAILED or FORFEIT, claimed alone and paid to the winners already paid (RULED Daniel 2026-09-24, ruling C, slice C3b-1)

SEARCHED FIRST: the round's settlement is one per round - lock_settlements, lock_settlement_moves and the `built` cache are
keyed by round - and lockSettlement computes one pool from every loser's lock; nothing kept what the first settlement
paid each winner. A lock left out by C3a that ended FAILED or FORFEIT was never claimed and went back at expiry.

THE CUT - PROTOCOL (lock-settlement.js): lockSettlement returns `stakeShares`, what it paid each winner in the table's
order. lateLockSettlement: only a FAILED or FORFEIT late entry (VOID - "not claimed: ... returns to its player at its
expiry"; DELIVERED - "stake back only, no share"); the first settlement paid nobody - nothing claimed; the lock must hold
the net stake. Its net stake less this transaction's input fee is split by the first shares (target = share x spendable /
first pool, the largest payout that pays its own fee, a share too small folded back, the dust to the first row), paid as
pre-expired payout contracts to each winner's own lock key; the late fee lock, where minted, claimed with it and paid to
the sitting signer nodes by §22A, never the pool. Nonce: lateSettlementNonce(round, entry), never the round's.
NODE: store late_lock_settlements (one row per (round, entry), never a second row under the round key) and
lock_settlement_shares (the first settlement's shares, written when it is signed, so a restart splits the same way).
settlement.js lateMessage rebuilds the plan only after the round's settlement is ACCEPTED, for an entry it did not claim
that is no longer in its re-run window, the P opened as for any loser; settleLate combines on the round's asker (M3.3-19
turn), a second attempt on an ACCEPTED row builds nothing, a peer holding a handed signature reads ACCEPTED back from the
federation (claimed lock gone, a payout stored). commit/share/take take an optional entry; lockAfterSettlement says
"claimed in the round's second settlement" once it is ACCEPTED. server.js: /settle-commit|share|signature take &entry=;
a sweep (finality.lateEveryMs, else the back-off) visits the objected entries of ACCEPTED rounds. A TEST AID, named as
such: `finalityOf` (serve option, default resultFinality), because two signer nodes that agree on a run cannot hold a
valid objection against it - the late-settlement tests hand both nodes the "still in its re-run window" and the outcome.
Winners are paid by payout contracts, as the base plan does - no send plans (C3b-2). No payout.js, preimage.js or
winnings-send.js change. The first transaction is never touched: no clawback.

MEASURED. Protocol lock-settlement.test (red first: stakeShares and lateLockSettlement absent): FAILED and FORFEIT split
to the msat under 1000 msat base fees, the stake wholly accounted for (paid + output fees + input fee), the nonce the
entry's; VOID, DELIVERED, a first table that paid nobody and a wrong amount refused by name; a late fee lock pays 1000 +
1000 to the two signer nodes and leaves the winner's amount unchanged. Node late-settlement.test on the lock-round fixture
(red first: the file fails at import on the old src, lateLockSettlement absent): late FAILED - the first settlement
claimed only the on-time loser and left the late lock held; while in its window settleLate refuses and nothing is
submitted; once FAILED the sweep builds the second transaction, both nodes ACCEPTED on one txid, exactly the late stake and
fee lock claimed, the winner paid 98000 msat to its own key (the protocol's arithmetic; the fixture federation charges
no fee), 2 signer nodes paid the fee lock, the first settlement unchanged, 2 submissions, lockAfterSettlement "claimed in
the round's second settlement" at both, a second attempt kept and nothing submitted. Late FORFEIT - the same. Late VOID -
no second transaction, the lock held, refused by name. Late DELIVERED qualifier - in no transaction, no share, its own
forfeit 200. Named suites: late-settlement 4/4 twice, lock-settlement 9/9, lock-settlement-restart + pool-settle 17/17,
winnings-pool + winnings-sent + daily-paid-federation 9/9, rerun 18/18. Full suite (248 files, 1666 pass = 1660 + 6):
the baseline reds only (ghost-live 9, replay-solids 2, bundle-fresh 1 the pin, discovery 18, pool-outpoint's one skip)
and objective-markers' live-Chrome timeout.
Next, named not done: C3b-2 (the late payout by send plans keyed by (round, entry)).

## FEDERATION: the late winners are sent, not collected - send plans per late (round, entry) (RULED Daniel 2026-09-24, ruling C, slice C3b-2a)

SEARCHED FIRST: winnings_sends is keyed (winner entry, attempt), so a winner's late send would share a key with its
first-round send; WinningsSend reaches its rows only through the Round's send methods (putSendPlan, sendAttemptsOf,
sendPlansOf, markSend, dropPlannedSends, putWinnings, lockSettlement).

THE CUT. Protocol: lateLockSettlement takes `sends` and `requireSends` - a winner with an accepted late send is paid by
an outgoing contract to its invoice, refunding to the committee claim key, for exactly the split's payout (a send for
another amount refused by name); with requireSends a winner without one is refused by name; a send needs no winner lock
row. Node: store late_winnings_sends, key (round, late entry, winner entry, attempt) - never winnings_sends. Round
lateSendScope(lateEntry) is the store seen through one late settlement: its send methods read and write that table, its
settlement row is the late one, and putWinnings writes nothing (the first round's winnings row stands). WinningsSend
takes `scopeParam` (`&late=<entry>`) on its peer calls. settlement.js: a late WinningsSend per (round, entry)
(lateWinningsFor); the asker proposes the late plans from the late base plan and hands them to the peers (POST
/settle-sends?late=), each checking them as for the first round (takeLateSends); the late transaction is built with the
sends (requireSends) and commits to their payment hashes; one plan set per late settlement, unreplaceable once it is
SUBMITTING (the scoped lockSettlement); once ACCEPTED the asker sends (sendLate): committee auth over the invoice, the
gateway pays, the preimage checked and kept on every signer node. server.js: /settle-sends, /send-commit, /send-share,
/winnings-paid take `late=`; the late sweep also carries unpaid late sends of ACCEPTED late settlements. Gateway: the
lowest live one, as the first round. A round settled before 6074fbeb has no stored shares: refused, "kept no shares",
its late lock returns at expiry. Amounts exactly lateLockSettlement's; the fee lock still pays the nodes; the first
transaction untouched.
`finalityOf` STAYS A SERVE TEST AID - pinned at the source level: an option only of server.js (default resultFinality,
used by the settle pass and handed to the LockSettlement it makes) and settlement.js (default resultFinality); main.js
never names it; verify.js names it only as its own import alias of resultFinality.

MEASURED. Protocol (red first: no sent payouts): with sends each late payout is `sent` for exactly the base payout's
msat under 1000 msat base fees, refunding to the committee, the fees the same; another amount and a missing send refused
by name. Node late-settlement.test on the lock-round fixture, zero-fee federation (red first on 6074fbeb's src: the late
winner was paid by a contract to its own key 020a0a...): late FAILED and late FORFEIT - the late payout 98000 msat, sent,
payoutPk the committee claim key; invoiceMsat 93440, the largest invoice whose own fee under the lowest gateway's rule
(4000 msat + 6000 ppm) fits in 98000; the late send PAID at attempt 0 with a preimage that hashes to the invoice at both
signer nodes, and the late transaction commits to that hash; the first-round send still PAID at attempt 0; the winner
paid exactly twice, once per transaction; a second sweep adds no second late row. (C3b-1's assertion that the late payout
goes to the winner's own lock key is RULED changed to sent-to-the-committee.) Named suites: late-settlement 5/5 twice,
protocol lock-settlement 24/24, lock-settlement 9/9, lock-settlement-restart + pool-settle 17/17, winnings-pool +
winnings-sent + daily-paid-federation 9/9, rerun 18/18. Full suite (248 files, 1668 pass = 1666 + 2): the baseline reds
only (ghost-live 9, replay-solids 2, bundle-fresh 1 the pin, discovery 18, pool-outpoint's one skip) and objective-markers'
live-Chrome timeout.
Next, named not done: C3b-2b (restart mid-send; the expiry re-send of a late winning).

## FEDERATION: a late winning through a restart, and re-sent after its contract expires (RULED Daniel 2026-09-24, ruling C, slice C3b-2b)

SEARCHED FIRST: /resend-sends took only the round's own sends (winnings.checkResend over settlements.message), so a late
re-send was checked against the first round's rows and refused; a re-send's nonce was sha256 over round, winner entry and
attempt, so a late attempt 1 would share a nonce with that winner's first-round attempt 1.

THE CUT (winnings-send.js, server.js; no settlement.js or store change): resendNonce({ roundId, lateEntryId, entryId,
attempt }) - a late sender (its scoped store names lateEntryId) hashes its late entry in, under its own tag; the first
round's nonce is unchanged. /resend-sends routes `late=` to the late sender and lateMessage; the late routes (/resend-sends,
/send-commit, /send-share, /winnings-paid) refuse by name a `late` naming no late settlement of this round: "no late
settlement for that entry". A re-send is attempt + 1 in late_winnings_sends under the same (round, late entry, winner) -
not a new plan set - through the next live gateway the entry's earlier attempts did not use, to a new invoice from the
address the winner named, refunding to the committee claim key; its payout is largestPayoutMsat(fees, prev - fee(prev)),
the existing re-send rule. A second re-send of the same expired attempt adds no row (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, and the
peer's "not the next attempt"); if attempt 1 also expires, attempt 2 is legitimate.

MEASURED, late-settlement-resend.test (new file, split from late-settlement.test for the 180 s cap), the lock round on
FILE-BACKED stores as lock-settlement-restart.test has them, the late sweep slowed out of the way and each step driven by
the round's asker. RED FIRST on 632293e7's src: the file fails at import (resendNonce absent); run with that import
stubbed, the peer checked the late re-send against its first-round rows ("attempt 0 has not expired here ...") and no
re-send was taken or signed. After:
1. Restart (a), killed after the late plans were proposed and taken, before signing: after the restart the same payment
   hash (the kept plan, no new invoice), the late transaction ACCEPTED, one row per node PAID at attempt 0 with a preimage
   that hashes to the invoice, one late submission, the first-round rows unchanged.
2. Restart (b), killed after ACCEPTED with the send unpaid (SENDING): the txid equal before and after the restart and to
   the rebuilt one, the one row resumed to PAID, one late submission.
3. Expiry (port.gatewayDown on the lowest gateway, port.height past the expiration): attempt 1 through gw-b to a new payment
   hash at the same address, 98000 msat on the zero-fee federation, the re-send refunding to the committee claim key, PAID
   with a preimage that hashes to attempt 1's invoice at both nodes; the late re-send nonce 64f7404c... is not the first
   round's dd81e254... .
4. A second re-send of attempt 0 adds no row: attempts 0 and 1 at both nodes.
5. late= naming the winner's own first-round entry: /resend-sends and /send-commit 409 "no late settlement for that
   entry", nothing stored, the first-round rows unchanged.
6. VOID and a late qualifier still never sent: late-settlement.test 5/5.
7. Under the 1000 msat base fee a 98000 msat expired contract re-sends exactly largestPayoutMsat(fees, 98000 - 1000) =
   96000 msat, PAID.
A HARNESS EFFECT, NAMED: right after both nodes restart on the same ports a peer's first answer can fail at the connection
("fetch failed" - seen in 1 of 3 runs of restart (a)); the daemon's late sweep asks again, and the test drives settleLate
and sendLate as the sweep does, a bounded number of passes, reporting them: restart (a) 1-2 passes, restart (b) 1.
Named suites: late-settlement-resend 4/4 twice (restart cases 3 more times), late-settlement 5/5, winnings-pool +
winnings-sent + daily-paid-federation 9/9, lock-settlement 9/9. Full suite (249 files, 1672 pass = 1668 + 4): the
baseline reds only (ghost-live 9, replay-solids 2, bundle-fresh 1 the pin, discovery 18, pool-outpoint's one skip) and
objective-markers' live-Chrome timeout.
Ruling C (C1, C2a, C2b, C2c, the first-result slash, C3a, C3b-1, C3b-2a, C3b-2b) is on origin with this.

## FEDERATION: the objection windows are blocks at both ends - the ruling locked as a measurement, no src changed (RULED Daniel 2026-09-24)

THE HOLE: every §13A window counted from this node's own receive time (resultFinality: objectedAt's seen_ms, the re-run
records' seenMs, the threshold's and the posting's seenMs), so two honest holders could decide one objected entry
differently.
THE RULING, locked in test/window-blocks.test.js as `ruledWindow`: a window opens at the timestamp of the block its opening
event sits in (the objection's filing; for the re-run's own window, the block where the agreed re-run first sits at
threshold) and ends at the first later block whose timestamp is >= open + objection_window_ms - both ends chain facts, no
receive time an input on either. An event is inside only if its own block timestamp is strictly before the end block's;
a filing in the end block or later is outside. A node without the end block decides nothing (no FINAL, VOID, slash or
claim): tip lag is a wait. Holders with the same blocks through the end block name the same outcome.
WHY NOT "OPEN + W" ON A CLOCK (measured before this ruling, not committed): with each moment moved to its first block at
or after it and the end left at open + W, an objection that arrived inside the window was placed after it - W 3 s on a
10 s chain: the window closed at ...893000, the objection sat at ...900000, and the entry went on to FINAL. And any rule
that maps receive times to blocks per node still splits when a block falls between two holders' arrivals.

MEASURED (two holder daemons: the fixture's holder and a second daemon on a VACUUM INTO copy of its store - the same
holder, its own clock; the fixtures' block clock, one block per second, a block's timestamp its median time past; each
filing assigned ONE block, the first at or after its first sighting at either holder; W = 3000): the objection reached A
at t + 2 and B at t + 1632, the fifth agreeing re-run at t + 3540. TODAY'S ANSWER, the committed local-clock finality at
t + 5000: A VOID, B PROVISIONALLY_FINAL - the split, asserted as measured (the code that follows the ruling turns it).
The ruled window: open ...933000, end ...936000, the fifth's block ...937000 - both holders VOID, "4 of 5 re-runs inside
[open, end), none proves the player: §13C VOID", the same reason; with the fifth moved to a block inside, both
PROVISIONALLY_FINAL for the same reason; a node holding blocks only to end - 1 decides nothing ("does not yet hold the end
block"); a filing in the end block itself outside on both (4 in, 1 out). Three runs, all green; in two the fifth fell in
the end block itself and was outside on both.
Committed: the test and its block-clock helper only. The earlier implementation (moments to their first block, end at
open + W) is not committed; it is kept aside, to be redone to this ruling in the next pass. No settlement edit.

## FEDERATION: the §13A windows are blocks at both ends, and every filing names its block (RULED Daniel 2026-09-24)

THE RULINGS IMPLEMENTED (locked at e460687a): every §13A window is [open block, end block) - the first objection window,
the re-run window, the re-run's own window. The end block is the first later block whose median time past is at or after
open + objection_window_ms (median time past, not a header's own time: it only rises). A filing is assigned to the block
hash IT CARRIES - not a receipt time, not anyone's sighting, and with no "within N below my tip" bound: inside only if that
block is in this chain, at or after the open and strictly before the end block; the end block or later, or a hash not in
the chain once the end block is present, is outside. A node without the block it needs decides nothing - no FINAL, VOID,
slash or claim; tip lag is a wait. The first window opens at the block the POSTING RECORD names - the posting that
completes the threshold, by the chain's order (one signature never marks it).

THE WIRE CHANGE: protocol posting.js - the posting record carries blockHash (POSTING_BYTES 131 -> 163), and
transcriptIsPublished returns the counted postings' blocks; rerun.js - the re-run record carries blockHash (RERUN_BYTES
+32). The objection intake (/objection) requires block=<hash> and keeps it (objections.block_hash, and rerun_objections'
for the second objection; ALTER TABLE for older stores). A node names its chain tip on its own postings and re-runs and
refuses by name without a chain.
THE NODE: finality.js resultFinality reads every window from the node's chain (chainIndex over `round.chainView`: a
block's height by hash and its median time past; windowEnd; place -> inside / outside / pending); `now` no longer decides
a window. server.js sets round.chainView from its own `chainFor`, or from `windowChain` (a harness hands its daemons a
block clock this way without the verifier checking the fixtures' beacon against it); the re-run watch keeps asking while
a block is awaited. No settlement, slash, send or money path was edited: they read finality and follow it.
THE FIXTURES: test/block-clock.js - one block per second, a block's time its median time past; a view is the chain AS OF
the round's own clock (`this.now()`), so a stubbed read sees exactly that moment's blocks; `tipAt`, `mtpOf`, `endAt`.
window-fixture's `opts` carries windowChain, so every fixture daemon reads it; fixture postings, re-runs and objections
name the tip. Tests moved from receive times to block anchors; a few file a block apart where two windows must not end at
one block; tests with 1 ms windows wait for the next block. No assertion loosened; changed expectations are the ruled
outcome.

MEASURED. window-blocks.test (two holder daemons, one a VACUUM INTO copy of the other; the one objection naming one
block, received ~1510 ms apart; W = 3000; three runs green): at t + 5000 both VOID for the same reason (the local-clock
finality measured A VOID / B PROVISIONALLY_FINAL at e460687a); with the end block both VOID, and the locked ruledWindow
agrees; a node holding blocks only to end - 1 decides nothing (SUSPENDED, blockPending); a sixth re-run naming the end
block is outside on both (4 counted); a seventh naming a block inside turns both to FINAL 5 together. Guards: rerun
18/18, slash-filing 4/4, objection-window 3/3 (three runs, two under full-suite load), late-settlement 5/5,
late-settlement-resend 4/4, lock-settlement 9/9, result-window 8/8, no-quorum 5/5, publication-finality 5/5, posting
3/3, rerun-object 3/3, protocol slash 12/12, reconstruct 5/5, verify 9/9, close-retry 3/3, first-mark 15/15. Full suite
(250 files, 1673 pass): the baseline reds only (ghost-live 9, replay-solids 2, bundle-fresh 1 the pin, discovery 18,
pool-outpoint's one skip) and objective-markers' live-Chrome timeout. (A run before objection-window moved to block reads
had it red under load; its timings were sub-block on a one-second clock - fixed in the test, not the rule.)
Next, named not done: THRESHOLD_LN cut 6 (the hold vocabulary in protocol payout.js).

## FEDERATION: §13C's result window is blocks at both ends, opened at the contract end (RULED Daniel 2026-09-24, ruling (a))

THE RULING IMPLEMENTED: the result window opens at the first block at or after roundEndMs(contract) - entry close + 2 x
start deadline + run length, the same instant at every holder - by the same beacon-from-chain ask the other windows use,
and ends at the first later block whose median time past is at or after open + objection_window_ms. No open block or no
end block: no decision. No close record, no closed_ms + W. The clocks at server.js's watches stay polling budgets.
THE NODE: finality.js resultWindow(round, rid, contract) -> { ok, open, end } over the node's chain (chainIndex now also
hands back the headers). The four §13C checks read it: verify.js #unretrievedPastWindow, shortPastWindow and #noQuorum
(a pending decision says it waits for the chain's end block), server.js voidStands. No closed_ms is read to decide
anything (one log line keeps it). No money path, refund, claim or forfeit amount edited; the §13A rules untouched.
THE FIXTURES (harness only): window-fixture presentDay(contract, endMs) moves a round's committee time, start and entry
close so roundEndMs lands at endMs, every interval unchanged; the fixture beacon's time is the round's committee time +
400 (exactly the old 900 on a 1970 round). The §13C rounds of one-signer-node-refused, close-retry, first-mark 5b-5e and
five-of-seven moved to present-day times and wait for the chain's end block, then each node's decision, not W after a

## FEDERATION: §13C's evidence is tied to the block it sits in, and a late closer gets no free stand (RULED Daniel 2026-09-24)

THE RULINGS IMPLEMENTED. Evidence counts when its block is strictly before that window's end block - the open is not a
floor, so play-time first marks, equivocation, refusals and peer refusal answers count; a record in the end block or later
is outside at every holder (filings keep their own open-to-end rule). Each evidence record stores the tip of the node that
records it; a pulled record keeps the block the peer named; a holder places a mark at the earliest block among the records
it holds, pulls peers before it decides, and decides only once the end block is there. A pair counts only if both marks
are before the end block - on the result window and the re-run window alike. No block on the player's mark: core, protocol
and client unchanged. No free stand: past the end block an ENTRY_VOID with no counted pair does not end the close; every
holder writes the same §13C record - VOID, or FORFEIT on a counted pair - and the first-result slash follows it. Amounts
unchanged. Residuals stand as ruled: an unreachable earlier record may still differ; a lying node may name an older block.
THE NODE. store.js: evidence_blocks (entry, mark id, block) - every record kept, the earliest placed; first_mark_offers
gains block_hash (ALTER; a repeated answer keeps its first block). round.js: tipOf, noteEvidenceBlock (stamped on a
checkpoint, an offered mark, a pair's two marks, a late start, the Void's first mark, a refused first mark), evidenceBlocks,
markCounts(entry, mark, chain, end), provenTwoFirstMarks(..., window). finality.js: resultWindow hands back its chain; the
re-run window's §13C reads provenTwoFirstMarks gated by its end block. verify.js: #pullEvidenceBlocks (/evidence-blocks of
each peer) before any §13C decision; #equivocationProven(..., window) counts a pair only when both marks count;
#noQuorum reads the window first - a late start, a pair, a refusal (the offer's block, the refusing node's mark block) count
only before the end block; a Void (its own, or a peer's on-time first-mark Void read at /entry-void by a holder with no
first mark) is decided VOID past the end block even with a peer down; #unretrievedPastWindow and shortPastWindow read the
gated, pulled proof; pullEvidence for the re-run watch. server.js: voidStands no longer ends a close on a Void;
GET /evidence-blocks; the re-run watch pulls the peers' evidence before it reads a §13C outcome and files the slash.
THE FIXTURES (harness only). window-fixture joinAndPlay returns otherFirstMark (the player's second first mark). The
seven-node lock paths start 25 s before their contract end so every mark of the path is play-time evidence, and
lockAfterClose asserts the close came before the end block; the standing-Void shortcut of the last slice is gone. Split to
stay inside the suite's 180 s: five-of-seven-expiry.test.js (the three "down through the lock's expiry" paths),
first-mark-fixture.js + first-mark-late.test.js (5b-5e and the late proof); five-of-seven-receipts-lost's rounds
moved to the present the same way. No assertion changed except the ruled outcomes.

MEASURED, RED FIRST on 6f46b643 (no src changed): (1) late closer, seven nodes, path 2 with signer node 4 (the pair)
down: 0-3 closed before the end block and wrote VOID, 5 and 6 - shown the Void by the doors - closed after it and wrote
nothing (evidence-blocks.test). (2a) late proof, result window: B voided, closed before the end block; the player's late
first mark reached A after it - A FORFEIT, B nothing, its Void standing (first-mark-late). (2b) late pair, re-run window:
the player's second first mark reached holder A after the re-run window's end block - A FORFEIT, B VOID, 5 first-result
slashes at each (window-blocks). (2c) late refusal: A closed before the end block holding nothing, B refused the on-time
first mark after it - A signed FORFEIT/0, B VOID (one-signer-node-refused).
GREEN: (1) all six up write VOID, the same (empty - no first result was signed) slash set; (2a) VOID at both; (2b) VOID
at both, the same 5 slashes - and the same pair made inside the window: FORFEIT at both, the same 5; (2c) FORFEIT/0 at
both, no VOID; a refusal inside the window still VOID at both (refused 1, 8). No holder writes before the end block.
OUTCOMES THAT MOVED, all toward one record at every holder: five-of-seven path 2 - FORFEIT at all seven (5 and 6 wrote
nothing); path 2 with node 4 down - VOID at all six up; receipts-lost's genuine outage-VOID - VOID at all seven (none
wrote anything before: each Void stood). Every refund-door, kept-forfeit and lock-held assertion unchanged.
Guards: first-mark 11/11, first-mark-late 5/5, five-of-seven 3/3, five-of-seven-expiry 3/3, receipts-lost 4/4,

round on an unbonded federation (§23.6): " + federationIsBonded's reason); nothing stored, nothing listed; censusFor takes
the posted contract with no stored row required and the same census; contracts unchanged; assignSignerNodes and the claim
key stay after round.open. Out of this slice: a node with no chain view still counts no guardians and asks no bond check.
MEASURED BEFORE (a probe on guardians-bonded's fixture with the round's clock inside its entry window): under threshold (2 of
4 guardians bonded, threshold 3) and none bonded (0 of 2) were 409 with the round STORED and LISTED - guardiansBonded ran

## FEDERATION: §24A.1's player wallet, and the stake spent from it (RULED Daniel 2026-09-25) - the invariants, before code

The red of rehearsal item 8 (27e1fbb9) is the spec's fault line: page-lock.js fund() paid an lnd invoice into a wallet
keyed by seed AND ROUND. A round is not a federation. The slice builds only the player wallet and the paying-round spend.
THE INVARIANTS (written before any code; the measurement is held to them):
1. ONE WALLET PER SEED AND FEDERATION: its secret is a function of the seed and the federation id only - never of a round
   id - and its store is keyed the same way. Two paying rounds of one federation open the same wallet.
2. THE STAKE LEAVES THAT WALLET: the stake lock and the fee lock are funded from the player wallet's notes, and the page's
   lockStake takes that wallet; it opens no per-round wallet and asks for no deposit.
3. NO LIGHTNING BETWEEN THE PLAYERS: nothing Lightning sits in the per-round stake path. A top-up into the player wallet is
   its own act, before a round's stake and never inside it.
4. THE PER-ROUND LND INVOICE IS NOT THE STAKE SOURCE: a wallet that cannot cover the round's locks refuses the stake by
   name; the stake path never answers a shortfall with an invoice.
5. AFTER THE SPEND THE STAKE SITS IN THE FEDERATION, in its §23 stake lock (a stock OutgoingContract to claim_pk) - not in
   a threshold hold-invoice.
6. A PAYING ROUND WITH NO SUCH WALLET DOES NOT OPEN for this page: no player wallet, no stake, no entry. Free rounds stay
   free - no wallet is opened for them.
NOT IN THIS SLICE: refunds, redeems and payouts still open the per-round wallet (items 9-10 decide where they land); the
Unity C# scripts; THRESHOLD_LN.
BUILT (this slice): page-lock.js - walletSecretFor(seed, federationId) under its own tag (TAG.playerWalletSecret),
walletStoreFor keyed by the federation, playerWallet (the one join), fundPlayerWallet (the top-up: a Lightning deposit
into the player wallet only when it is short of the round's locks, the quote-then-allowance loop the stake used to run),
and lockStake now opening the player wallet and spending the stake and the fee lock from it - no per-round wallet, no
deposit; a short wallet is refused by name. The page (WebGL template index.html) tops the player wallet up first, then
stakes; the bundle and its template copy rebuilt (bundle-fresh 2/2). page-lock 29/29: the five tests that pinned the
per-round deposit moved to the player wallet, two new ones pin the invariants (a short wallet is refused and asks no
deposit; two rounds of one federation open one wallet, another federation or seed another). Every regtest tool that stakes
tops up first. Refunds, redeems and payouts still open the per-round wallet (not this slice).

## FEDERATION REHEARSAL ITEM 9 (a): RED BY DESIGN, FROM THE CODE AND THE EXISTING TESTS - NO RUN (RULED Daniel 2026-09-25)

Item 9 (a), FEDERATION.md: "a payout contract and a forfeit redeemed into the wallet by the client on its own, with no
press". Recorded red against two rulings already in force, measured from the code and the tests that pin them; no harness
built and no regtest run spent (the gate driver wins 6 of 10, which is why a run was refused - not a measurement to chase).
CAUSE ONE - NO PRESS, NO REDEEM: the page redeems nothing on a timer. Its timer lookThePayout (WebGL template
index.html:1486) only calls lookOwed; the collect runs inside the player's Withdraw press (collectAndWithdraw), into the
round's wallet (index.html:994-1010). page-lock.test.js:788 ("the page spends nothing on a timer") pins it. The ruling it
keeps is W4/6d: a closed tab must not collect money it then loses. So nothing is redeemed into the one wallet per seed and
federation without a press.
CAUSE TWO - NO PAYOUT CONTRACT TO REDEEM: under the pool rule (RULED 2026-09-23; settlement.js:462) a winner is paid by an
outgoing Lightning send to the address it named; a qualifier with no address is paid nothing and no stake lock is claimed
(winnings-pool test 2). There is no payout contract for the page to redeem into any wallet.
NOT PATCHED (RULED): the timer, the Withdraw path, the pool send and the settlement stay as they are.

## THE ARRIVAL CARD: THE CORE'S SCORE IS THE PRODUCT OF E, T AND C, AND THE CARD PRINTS THEM - CLOSED (2026-09-26)

RULE. The score is 1000 x E x T x C on the 5-decimal grid: each factor an integer count of 1e-5 formed from the core's
own words (E from S_EXPOSURE over the 320 m reference, T = 3900 over S_ELAPSED held to 2600..15600 ticks, C from the
S_CARGO bed fraction), and the score their product, kept in 1e-5 points (SCORE_SCALE 100000). min_score is in the same
unit and compared with the score directly; the Daily's is 100000 (1 point). The card prints
"load C x danger E x speed T x 1000 = S" with S the core's S_DELIVERED, the same number as the SCORE line.

MEASURES. Lane 0, seed 0: 7.50000 on phase0 (C 0.20000 x E 0.02500 x T 1.50000), 9.91500 on the fleet. The 72-run
arrival set (9 lanes x 8 seeds, all delivered): the product of the printed factors equals S on every run, 0 failures.

LIVE RUN. btc-logistics-core.pages.dev, phone shape: round 14bff641..., entry 194e48a7..., "load 0.70000 x danger

## THE LOAD PATH: ONLY THE NEW LOBBY, THE WALLET IN SETTINGS, A CLOSED ROUND BACK TO THE LOBBY - CLOSED (2026-09-26)

THE MISS. Case (c), a closed round's link with play=1: the page built the entry locally, so its join fallback never ran;
Unity auto-played from the address and opened the cargo chooser; then the node refused the session ("the node refused
the entry: the round is closed"). The bridge dropped its client, but the game's running-session mark stayed set, and
BlwpNetEnded read only the client, so the run looked live forever. The chooser stood there with a players-panel line.

THE FIX (fleet 7dc2e8f9, the same patch here). First patch:
- The bridge's failed open calls the page's BLWP_ENTRY_REFUSED.
- The page takes the join fallback's own steps. The round globals are cleared, the join is recorded refused with the
  node's words, round and play leave the address, and the lobby shows.
- SplashScreen, while hidden with no live session and the chooser open, reads the refused join and closes the chooser
  without rolling out (LoadoutPanel.Dismiss). It then shows the lobby.
First patch measured live: the page side passed, the game side did not come back. Unity reported showing false in 26
of 27 samples, and the chooser was still up in the last screenshot. BlwpNet.Running stayed true after the refusal, so
Live never went false.
Second patch (RULED 2026-09-26): a bridge in error with no client is over (BlwpNetEnded returns 1), so the session is
not live.

MEASURED, LIVE. btc-logistics-core.pages.dev, framework 90d9c9d5, headless Chrome on the Beelink (Vulkan). Each case ran
on a brand-new profile, phone shape 390x844, DPR 3, touch, cache off. Unity's own lobby report was read every 250 ms for
15 s after the loading screen.
(a) Bare root. 35 samples, all lobby, 0 in title mode. Wallet rows (balance, deposit, withdraw, move) hidden. The gear
    opens Settings with the Wallet row; Close hides it; "Back up now" opens Settings with the phrase. PASS.
(b) Bare root, then a reload of the same tab. 36 + 36 samples, all lobby, 0 in title mode. Wallet as in (a). PASS.
(c) Closed round 14bff641... with play=1 (the node said "the round is closed", not an unknown round).
    - 27 of 28 samples lobby. The one before, at 1.2 s, was the run starting from the address.
    - 0 in title mode.
    - Unity reports showing and lobby, with "Not joined: the node refused the entry: the round is closed." drawn in the
      red box and on the hint line.
    - The cargo chooser is gone in the last screenshot.
    - The address keeps node, bond and advert; no round, no play, no round id.
    - The bridge is in error with no client; the join is recorded refused.
    - Wallet rows hidden after load, the Wallet row inside Settings.
    PASS.
EditMode OnlyTheLobbyTests + ResultHold + Timer/Void return + RunStopped: 27 of 27.

THE PAYING ROUND: WHAT IS LOCKED BEFORE THE FIRST testnet4 PAYMENT
- On chain, before the round opens:
  - Each signer node's bond on testnet4. The census reads it, and a paying round opens only when federationIsBonded -
    the four guardian-advertising nodes are bonded.
- Per player, in the federation, before the run: the stake lock (the Daily names 100000 msat, 100 sat) and, beside it,
  the fee lock for the 2% node fee (§22A). Both are made from the player wallet after its deposit, with no Lightning
  payment between. The deposit into the player wallet is the first testnet4 Lightning payment.
- The bond amount: the spec names no fixed amount.
  - §5A.3: bond_min(role) is named in each Round Contract.
  - §5A.10: bond_min is two to four times the largest round pool, and at least max_round_volume per role.
  - The 50,000 sat in round-2of2.mjs is a launcher's choice, not the spec's. This cut does not invent one.

## A walk-away is never a refund, even with no qualifier (RULED Daniel 2026-09-30, destination 1)

Ruling: a walk-away is §15 FORFEIT 0 at the door, never ENTRY_VOID, never a refund. With nobody qualifying, its stake
lock is claimed and paid by the ruled remainder split: 75% to the round's sitting signer nodes (one pre-expired contract
each to its own key, the fee-lock path), 25% to the donation set by share_bps through the Lightning-address send. Other
losers keep the no-qualifier expiry.

BEFORE (door-walkaway-noqualifier.test.js test 1 on 53d97748): door FORFEIT 0 at both, entryVoid null, /forfeit 409;
the close ACCEPTED with the fee lock only (2 payouts to the signer nodes, 1 lock claimed); the walker's stake lock not
among the claims and still held - due to expire back to the walker.

CHANGE:
- settlement.js marks `atTheDoor` on a FORFEIT result this store holds with no first mark, or a first mark recorded
  late (startForfeit). No-quorum and equivocation FORFEITs stay unmarked. It hands lockSettlement the round's signed
  donation set (server.js passes its donationSetFor, one line).
- lock-action.js: nobody qualifying and a door loser present -> the door locks CLAIM, the other losers EXPIRE,
  remainderMsat = what they hold (the pool equality counts it).
- lock-settlement.js remainderSettlement: less the input fees, 75% evenly to the sitting signer nodes (dust to the
  first), 25% splitDonation by share_bps; each recipient paid by a send kept under donationSendId(round, index). The
  signed plan without a recipient's send, or without a held donation set, is refused. Also in the pool's (iii) case
  (qualifiers, none addressed): the door locks are claimed the same way, the others expire.
- winnings-send.js: the donation shares are wanted sends beside the addressed qualifiers - LNURL (bech32) decoded to
  its pay request, proposed, checked by the seats, signed, sent, re-sent if unpaid; a PAID donation writes no winnings
  row. The record: store.js donation_sends (winnings_sends' columns, no entries reference - a recipient is no entry);
  round.js reads both tables.

MEASURED:

  (36750 each), 24500 to the set (16335 + 8165 by 6667/3333 bps), both donation sends PAID, lock gone, /forfeit 409;
  late first mark - recorded FORFEIT at both, claimed; control, FAILED alone - not claimed, held; mixed walker +
  FAILED - only the walker's 98000 claimed, the FAILED lock held.
- protocol walkaway-remainder.test.js 4/4: actions, the split, refusal without a donation send / without a set.
- door-walkaway-settled.test.js (walker beside a winner) stays green.

  PHASE=walkaway; locks by the page's own lock client): door 23 s after the lock, FORFEIT/0 at A and B, entryVoid

## Item 1, hole 1 (a): a donation recipient that does not answer is HELD, and the walk-away still settles (RULED Daniel 2026-09-30)

Before (74abeed7): with the donation set not answering, the plan was refused ("the donation recipient's invoice does not
stand") - no settlement at all, the fee locks not claimed either, and the walker's lock left to expire back: a refund.

Now: the proposer plans an unanswered recipient's share HELD (a send row with no invoice); the seats take it as their own
share of that recipient; the settlement pays it into a pre-expired contract under the committee claim key only - not a
signer fee, not the walker's, never part of the 75%. The proposer's sweep asks the same recipient again; once it answers,
the re-send spends the held contract (the committee's refund) into the Lightning-address send to its invoice. Unpaid, it
stays held for a later send to the same address. Code: lock-settlement.js (kind 'held'), winnings-send.js (propose, check,
sendsFor, contractOf, sendAll), settlement.js (summary heldMsat). No HUD, no core.

MEASURED, fixtures (door-walkaway-held.test.js 2/2, walkaway-remainder.test.js 5/5): 2-of-2, set down - ACCEPTED, the
walker's 98000 claimed, 36750 x2 to the signer nodes, 16335 + 8165 held under the claim key, both HELD, nothing asked of the
set; the set answers - both re-sent (attempt 1) and PAID to the set's two LNURLs, the held contracts spent, no new

## Item 1, the last hole: a donation recipient that answers the proposer and not a seat (inside ruling (a))

Before: the HELD fallback ran only where the PROPOSER could not reach a recipient. A seat that could not read that
recipient's pay request refused the plan - on a 2-of-2, or short of the threshold, nothing settled and the walker's lock
would expire back. Measured (door-walkaway-held test 3 before the fix): 297 invoices asked of the set, no settlement.
Now: the seat names the recipient it cannot reach ("the donation recipient does not answer here: <lnurl>"); the proposer
plans each one named HELD and offers the plan again until the seats agree or name no new one. And an unfunded re-send is
offered to the seats again before it is signed (winnings-send offerResend): a seat that refused a held share's retry while
it could not reach the set takes the same attempt once it can.
Measured: fixture - the set down at the non-proposing seat only: ACCEPTED, the walker's lock claimed, 16335 + 8165 held,
no sent output; the seat reaches the set -> both attempt 1 PAID. door-walkaway-held 3/3, winnings-sent 4/4,
late-settlement-resend 4/4. Private regtest (patched fork, 2 of 2, DONATION_DOWN=1 RESTART=1): both shares HELD, every
signer node restarted on its own store (and port) while held - still HELD; the recipients answer -> attempt 1 PAID at
both, alice SETTLED 158392 and 77195, held contracts spent; walker's lock gone, FAILED lock held, /forfeit 409.
Full suite 280 files, 1726 passing; reds the accepted six, plus rerun (a different test each loaded run - 1, 11, 6;
18/18 alone) and series-doors (a 180 s timeout in the suite; 1/1 alone twice, 14 s).

## The paying runner waits for its own publication before a beacon (Daniel 2026-09-30, pick (b), after fcb15cca)

Measured on testnet4: round fcb15cca's publication 37af92a0 (2 sat/vB, broadcast 21:48:57Z) sat ~3.5 h in the mempool
and confirmed at 154489, after its beacon block (~154477). The runner waited for the beacon alone, posted the round at 6
deep, node 1 (31221) refused it - rightly, "there is no publication transaction to read" - and the runner exited
01:18:32Z; deposit-fcb15cca exited 01:18:47Z (its round never came up). fcb15cca stays dead; 37af92a0 not rebroadcast.

Now (src/publication-wait.js, used by round-2of2.mjs on a chain it does not mine): the publication is replaceable; no
beacon is named and nothing posted until it has confirmed; each block that comes without it raises its fee (bumpfee,
doubling, 100 sat/vB at most); only a beacon strictly above the publication's block counts; a round whose beacon block
came first - unconfirmed, or confirmed at or above it - is dead: never posted, the first round drafted again (new committee
time just past the tip, same windows after it, its own census root and publication; six in a row at most), and a keeper
round not opened (the keeper drafts the next). A node that has not yet read a publication the runner saw confirm is asked
again, not exited on.
