## The testnet4 bitcoind flood, 07:10Z (caused by the series listing) - and its fix

After units 1-4 were restarted on fceca56f holding series 3cfbe516 (~508 rounds each), every listing asked each round's
chain view, keyed by round id and read ~100 blocks at a time, with no guard for a read in flight: the testnet4 bitcoind hit
"Too many open files" at 07:10:27Z, its unit restarted it (07:14:28 shutdown, 07:15:25 up, a new cookie), LND-a shut down at
07:15:13 and LND-b at 07:18:29 (their bitcoind backend gone), the guardians kept the old cookie (bitcoind: "incorrect
password attempt" every few seconds), and unit 6, restarted at 07:14, found no cookie and is up without its guardian.
Fix: main.js chainFor keys a view by what it depends on - census height, committee_time, confirmation depth - so every
round of the series shares one, with one read in flight per key; beacon-source refresh the same (one read per question).
beacon-seed, beacon-source, chain-rpc, main-settings, series-doors, committee-seed 24/24.
Then GET /rounds on node 1 took over 90 s: ~500 series rounds each derived their census from the ~2080-block view past a
64-entry cache keyed by round id. Now roster censusFor keys a series round's census by its series id (one template, one
census), and guardianBondsFor indexes a view's txids once per view. roster, committee-seed, census-derive, series-doors 42/42.
Then no series round drew a committee - two refusals, measured against the testnet4 chain (read-only):
  - the seed check looked only for a round's own publication; a series round has none, its series' is its (3029fc6f,
    154237, below beacon 154268). Now roster takes the series publication for a series round (findSeriesPublication),
    strictly below the beacon.
  - the census root: the series names 726a0b87, derived by the 2026-09-28 runner from a view starting at 154152 (the
    seven bonds at 154172); a node's 2016-block lookback also sees each key's earlier bond at 154120 - fourteen entries,
    root a86ea4e0 - and refused ("names census root ... and the chain gives ..."), re-deriving it for every round (3.4 s
    each). For series 3cfbe516 alone the census is read from 154152, as published (old-series.js) - an extension of the
    pick-B exception to the census root; the committee is the same seven keys either way.
roster, committee-seed, census-derive, series-doors, old-series, series-round 48/48; bundle-fresh, client-hash green.
Then GET /rounds still passed 90 s: each round's chain check (the beacon's block, its proof of work, the series
publication - ~220 ms) was kept per round past a 64-entry cache. Now kept per series, randomness and view extent; the
per-round seed is still derived per round. roster, committee-seed, census-derive, series-doors, beacon-seed 45/45.
Then the page offered no series round: the series writer only opened the rounds (round.open) and never assigned their
signer nodes, so no node listed itself assigned and the page counted 0 agreeing; and the page fetched each of ~450
listed contracts one after another on every paint. Now the writer assigns the rounds starting in the next 2 h (20 a pass;
the claim key is the committee's, made once), and the lobby keeps contracts by id and fetches 16 at a time. lobby 16/16,

notes (ceilNote) and credits whole; Custom too; the rest is the shortfall in whole notes, floor 5 sat -> 5120 msat. The
modal shows exact amounts (e.g. 100.352 sat). Test: a note-model wallet funded by each tab plays exactly N rounds' locks
with no further deposit, N = 1, 2, 5, 10.

WINDOW-10-SPEC, POINTS 1-4 (Daniel 2026-10-01: "Accepted ... Go. Build that plan"; re-run window opens at the previous
window's close, E+600, never at the objection's arrival or block). E = the round's end from its contract (roundEndMs).
1. protocol/src/contracts.js: objectionWindowMs must be exactly 600000n, else invalid (MAX_OBJECTION_WINDOW_MS withdrawn;
   OBJECTION_WINDOW_MS + FINAL_TOLERANCE_MS 5000 in constants.js, windowsOf() in protocol/src/window.js). Node refuses open
   (POST /round 400), list (/rounds skips a held one), entry (Round.enter); the page's fetchRound refuses list and join.
   Measured (window-10.test 1): 0/599999/600001 -> 400 "objection window is N ms: ... exactly 600000ms", 600000 -> 201,
   a pre-rule round in the store not listed, enter refused by name. Client page-lock.test: same three refused by fetchRound.
2. FINAL is a signed record (protocol/src/final-sig.js, TYPE 0x1a: round, entry, run, signer, signed-at). A seat signs from
   its own E+605 s, holding PROVISIONALLY_FINAL, transcript posted, no valid objection received in time; GET /final-sig signs
   fresh, POST /final-sig takes one; each watch gathers the peers' (gatherFinal). Counted only if signed within 5 s of the
   receiver's clock, at/after E+605, by a committee seat; one refused for its time is kept as evidence (final_sig_evidence).
   FINAL = the round's threshold (5 of 7, 2 of 2). finality.js reads no block for any window; settlement/payout wait as before
   on FINAL; the pending line unchanged. §13C result deadline: E+600 (decided from E+605).
   Measured (window-10.test 2): end-open 600000 ms; no block for 30 min and an hour of fast blocks alike: not signable at
   E+604999, signable at E+605000; fixtures' chain heights at open/close 500036/500636 (one block a second, informational);
   holder 409 and five early signatures refused ("before the window's final_after") at E+604 s; 4 signatures not FINAL,
   one 20 s-fast clock not counted (evidence row), the fifth FINAL.
3. Objections count by arrival on the seat's clock (objectedAt), until its E+605 s. Measured (window-10.test 3): received at
   E+604.903 s SUSPENDED, never FINAL with 5 others' signatures; at E+605.1 s PROVISIONALLY_FINAL, lateObjection, FINAL once
   signed, and the holder filed REPLAY_CONTRADICTS against the 5 signers by itself. Replaces the 30 s arrival grace.
4. Re-run window [E+600, E+1200): a re-run counts if signed after the objection was held, arrived before the seat's E+1205,
   signed time within 5 s of arrival (the re-run record carries signedAtMs instead of a block). No threshold by E+1205:
   §13C, written once (no_quorum). With one: own window [E+1200, E+1800), FINAL signed from E+1805; a valid objection to the
   re-run before E+1805 VOID at once, after it 409. Measured (window-10.test 4/4b): objections at E+30 s and E+590 s both
   close their re-run window at E+1200 s; agreed re-run own window 1200000/1800000, final_after 1805000; FINAL at E+1805 s
   on the re-run's run; three re-runs: SUSPENDED at E+1204 s, VOID at E+1205 s; second objection at E+1500 s VOID.
§13C evidence (pairs, refusals) counts if recorded before the decision (E+605 / E+1205), a pulled record by its peer's time;

  (cores.js TRUCK_BEFORE_FORK) - every round before the fork replays as before. Both hashes on the client's known-good list.

  longest, 4922 refused); a round of a series the node no longer holds is not announced.

### /wallet: a payment still in flight is answered as an error (playtest 11:12Z residue) - measured 11:50-11:55Z, no code changed

- Run 2, hash c09c0e43, settled at +120 s - the three readings:
  1. at the timeout: HTTP 400 {"error": "payment is still in flight (TimeoutError)"} after 95.2 s;
  2. the ledger then (+66 s and +100 s): send | pending | 1000 msat | fee reserve 5000 msat; /api/state lists the tx, detail empty;
  3. after the settle (+120 s): LND C SETTLED; the ledger send | succeeded | fee 1000 msat | done 11:54:37Z; /api/state the same.
- So the screen reads an HTTP 400 error for a payment that is still pending and then succeeds - the playtest's "failed" vs "succeeded".
- The timeout is not PAY_TIMEOUT_S (60 s): node.pay reads LND's /v2/router/send stream with a socket timeout of PAY_TIMEOUT_S + 30 (wallet.py:178), and with no_inflight_updates LND sends nothing until the payment is final.
- The writer: /home/daniel/tn4-wallet/wallet.py:421 (`raise WalletError("payment is still in flight ...")`), turned into HTTP 400 by do_POST (wallet.py ~697). Nothing in /tmp/btc-phase0 writes it. That tree belongs to another session - not edited.
- Beside it: in both runs the HTLC needed ~61 s to reach LND C (LND a -> LND B -> LND C) before LND C held it.
- FIXED in /home/daniel/tn4-wallet (no git there; backups wallet.py.pre-inflight-1356, index.html.pre-inflight-1356; tn4-wallet restarted 11:58Z): wallet.py's pay answers a read TimeoutError that leaves the ledger row pending with HTTP 200 {"payment_hash", "status": "pending", "fee_msat", "in_flight": true} - no failure text, no 400 (every other path as before: a WalletError rejection, another exception still pending, the 200 succeeded). index.html shows "Payment in flight - waiting for it to settle. Payment hash ..." and refresh() (every 3 s) follows that row until it is succeeded ("Paid.", ok) or failed ("Payment failed: ...", err). sync_send fails only a payment the node never registered, so a long in-flight payment is not failed by age.
- Re-measured, the three readings (new account df9b0654, faucet 1000 sat, 1 sat hold invoice on LND C, hash ca20654b, released at +120 s): at the old timeout /api/pay answered HTTP 200 {"status": "pending", "in_flight": true, payment_hash ca20654b...} after 95.17 s; the ledger then send | pending | 1000 | fee hold 5000 (+66 s and +100 s); after the release succeeded | fee 1000 | done 12:00:37Z.
- Released inside 90 s (+70 s, hash d6e04041): HTTP 200 {"status": "succeeded"} after 69.51 s, ledger succeeded 12:02:28Z - unchanged.

### A reload in a chained round keeps it (2026-10-03, the hole after e7fc8908) - page 0.0.2492
- Hole: BLWP_RUN_OVER's second call put the lobby's address back after the chained join had set round=, so a reload in a chained round landed in the lobby. Fix 1 (0.0.2490): the run-end handler leaves the address alone while a newer join for another round is in progress.
- Measured on 0.0.2490 (Beelink Chrome, 13:58Z): in chained round 5fe6efa8 the address named it (round= same as BLWP_JOIN.round). A reload 10 s into that join, 84 s before its start, was REFUSED: "already locked and committed to entry c87868b3… the run cannot be resumed after a reload" - the lock was committed to the entry, and the kept entry and session key (0.0.2479, PAID-NIGHT-2155) were only used for an uncommitted lock.
- Fix 2: keptLockUse(kept, { entry, beforeStart }) reuses a committed lock when the tab kept the very entry it was committed to (blwp.entry.<round> + round id + the kept session key's public half, the entry as the bridge sends it) and the round has not started. A started round still stops (mid-run reload stays a ruling for Daniel). 0.0.2491 still refused: page-lock.js imported `entryId as entryIdOf`, and the bundle strips imports, so the alias was undefined there and its try/catch answered "staked" (measured in the tab: the same inputs gave the matching id 43ae364c through BLWPCLIENT.entryId, "staked" through keptLockUse). 0.0.2492 imports entryId by its own name.
- Measured on 0.0.2492 (d4e842cc, Beelink Chrome, 14:12Z): chained round 31cbb091 loaded in 2296 ms; the address named it; reload at 14:12:23 -> "the lock is committed to the entry this tab kept, and the round has not started: the same entry is sent again", "stake lock kept from before the reload", "the entry of this round kept", "the session key of this round kept", joining the same round. No deposit asked. Seats: ONE entry 3acb7026 (joined 14:12:15, before the reload), stake seen by 7 of 7, ticks 4920 at all 7 (the harness's drive injector is not reinstalled by a reload, so the truck stood: MISSED). The page then chained on into 259c7aa5 (925 ms).

### A reload after the round started resumes the run (Daniel 2026-10-03, "That run must not be lost") - page 0.0.2494
- keptLockUse(kept, { entry, beforeStart, beforeClose }): a lock committed to the very entry the tab kept is resumed ('running') until the round closes; without the entry or after the close: staked (collect only). The page names it to the bridge (BLWP_RESUME), starts no funding, and the run-end handler leaves the round's address until that run ends itself or its round closes.
- Bridge (blwp.jslib + framework patch): net.opened with BLWP_RESUME runs client.resumeAfterReload (nothing recorded meanwhile; net.tick returns while resuming), the core enters the same world and catchUpCore steps it through the seats' transcript (events before each tick, as replay.js), net.seen = the next tick, new batches and marks go on from the adopted mark.
- 0.0.2493 measured (round cd2d837a, reload 3 s into the run): resumed at tick 168, run went on to WRECKED 440, but every mark after it was refused "does not follow the chain head": all 7 seats held mark 120 with ONE receipt each (their own; the other six had gone to the closed tab), resume() read only its own node's receipts and adopted mark 60.
- 0.0.2494: resume() also reads each committee peer's /receipts (each verified as before; 5-of-7 unchanged). Measured round 35fb0e3e (Beelink Chrome, reload 3 s in): "resumed at tick 168 ... mark head carried by 7, 56 receipts", run to WRECKED 1005, marks 13 accepted / 0 refused; seats: 1 entry, ticks 0..1004 at all 7, 16 marks (last 1005), 0 refused, 0 equivocations; seats' result FAILED:16977450 (final signatures pending settlement at commit time). MacBook Chrome run 79fffbf9/4abf0907: resumed at tick 234, carried by 7, 2 marks accepted, 0 refused.
- Screen after the resume (MacBook, tick 240): the truck is out of the bay and the core's WRECKED at 360 shows WASTED at once (follows the caught-up state); the HUD's load x0.70000 matches the core's load word 45875. Over the run the cargo chooser panel is up - a baseline without reload (wrecked at 176 before its shot) is still to be taken to tell whether that is the reload.

### Donations in the federation, slice 1: protocol formats (Daniel 2026-10-03, FEDERATION.md 37f4def2/fcaf7568)
- Donation set of keys: TYPE_DONATION_SET_KEYS 0x1b, recipients { recipientPk (33-byte compressed secp256k1), shareBps, label <= 48 chars } in published order; stands only all-keys (never mixed with LNURLs), each key once, sum 10000. splitDonation hands key shares ({ recipientPk, label, amountMsat }), remainder to the first. The signed publication (encodeDonationSetBody) carries it unchanged. Every LNURL set keeps its id (79b7f62a real, 7b128a1b test - asserted).
- Entry Contract: donationOutpoints after claimKeyAttestationRef, written only when non-empty (an empty list on the wire is refused) - every entry without them keeps its bytes and id; with them they are in the id and their order matters.
- donationOutputsExpected(entry, recipients): the pairs a signer node checks - one output per share above 0 msat, in the set's order, { outpoint, recipientPk, amountMsat }; refuses a count mismatch, outputs where nothing is donated, outputs for an LNURL set.
- Tests: donation-keys 9/9 (new); protocol suites donation 26, donation-authority 12, test-donation-sets 2, protocol 32, vectors 8, seed 2, entry-void 2, contract-network 9, lock-settlement 23, walkaway-remainder 6, stake-lock 5, inclusive 7, old-series 2 - all pass; client bundle 5, donation-choice 7, page-lock 55; node donation-set-door 5, donation-resend 1, donation-rotation 3. Page bundle rebuilt (not deployed).
- Next (slice 2, not started): seats check donation outputs with the federation and index them (GET /donations).

### Donations in the federation, slice 2: the seats (Daniel 2026-10-03)
- Store: donation_outputs (outpoint PK - one output is one entry's; entry, round, federation, recipient key, amount, contract id, verified_ms), indexed by key.
- verifyDonationOutputs: for a round whose set pays keys, every output donationOutputsExpected pairs is asked of the federation (status + contract id, as the stake lock) and must be the payout contract to that key for exactly that share (zero hash image, expiration 0, claim = refund = key - the settlement's payout shape, so the node's stake-lock tool's id mode hashes it unchanged). /lock refuses the stake (nothing kept) while any donation output is wrong or missing; when all hold, they are indexed with the stake. The entry door (POST /entry) refuses a wrong count of donation outpoints for the round's set.
- GET /donations?key=<66 hex>[&since=ms] -> { key, donations: [{ outpoint, entryId, roundId, federationId, amountMsat, contractId, verifiedMs }] }, oldest first; any other key 400.
- Tests: donation-outputs 5/5 (new: shape; taken with rows; 8 refusals by name - swapped, nothing held, 1 msat short, one missing, none named, reused by another entry, outputs in an LNURL round, no set held; nothing to check; GET /donations on a daemon). Node suites signer-node-lock 5, lock-client 1, donation-set-door 5, door-walkaway-settled 1, lock-settlement 9, donation-rotation 3 pass.

### Donations in the federation: the dev client, its two instances, and the set of keys (Daniel 2026-10-03)
